name: 0fold-4fold-coding-site-classification
description: Use when you need per-gene, per-population unfolded 0-fold/4-fold SFS counts and divergence counts (mi, Di, m0, D0) from DGN FASTA alignments or 1000GP Phase III VCFs to run McDonald-Kreitman tests with iMKT.

name: 16s-abundance-kmer-filtering
description: Use when building or validating a k-mer detection library for baseLess 16S sequence detection on MinION raw signal, where selected k-mers must maximize Smith–Waterman sequence and dynamic-time-warping squiggle dissimilarity.

name: 16s-amplicon-pipeline-evaluation
description: Use when you need to decide which 16S OTU-retrieval pipeline preserves raw paired-end read information, or when benchmarking merging-free (CD-HIT-OTU-Miseq/CDSnake) against merging-based pipelines (DADA2, deblur) on mock community datasets.

name: 16s-amplicon-profile-correction
description: Use when a 16S rRNA amplicon OTU table (biom, QIIME, GAAS, Unifrac or generic format) with read counts and unaltered Greengenes taxonomic assignments needs GCN bias correction, or when 16S qPCR total abundances must be corrected by community-average GCN.

name: 16s-amplicon-quality-filtering
description: Use when paired-end 16S FASTQ reads show good base quality over an initial stretch (e.g. ~200 bp R1 / 180 bp R2) followed by a sudden quality drop, and reads must be trimmed and length-filtered before OTU clustering.

name: 16s-amplicon-sequence-clustering
description: Use when Illumina MiSeq 16S rRNA amplicon FASTQ data (primer-removed, paired, trimmed to 250 bases) must be de novo clustered into true sequence variants with one-mismatch children assessed against sequencing error.

name: 16s-amplicon-variant-calling
description: Use when calling de novo sequence variants from primer-trimmed, paired Illumina 16S rRNA amplicon FASTQ data (e.g., mock communities like PRJEB24409), especially when a conservative, fast, scalable caller with explicit P values is preferred over DADA2 defaults.

name: 16s-copy-number-estimation
description: Use when inferring gene family content or 16S copy number for unsequenced organisms on a Greengenes/IMG 16S reference tree, or normalizing 16S OTU tables by predicted copy number.

name: 16s-denoising-execution-dada2-deblur
description: Use when demultiplexed, trimmed paired-end 16S reads must be processed through multiple denoising/clustering alternatives (DADA2, Deblur, vsearch open/closed/de novo) and the resulting representative sequence sets compared via pairwise UniFrac distances.

name: 16s-otu-pipeline-performance-ranking
description: Use when wall-clock running times of 16S OTU retrieval pipelines (CDSnake, DADA2, deblur, CD-HIT-OTU-MiSeq utilities) must be ranked per dataset from Table 2-style runtime measurements to verify which pipeline is fastest or slowest.

name: 16s-otu-rarefaction-depth-normalization
description: Use when benchmarking 16S-based metagenome prediction (e.g. PICRUSt KOs) against observed shotgun KO profiles as a function of sequencing depth, to identify the read depth at which prediction equals or exceeds a rarefied metagenome.

name: 16s-otu-table-processing
description: Use when marker-gene (16S) abundance data must be converted into a PICRUSt-compatible closed-reference OTU table as the first step of metagenome prediction, NSTI calculation, or accuracy-vs-NSTI analysis.

name: 16s-phylogenetic-tree-inference
description: Use when raw 16S amplicon reads must be converted into a phylogenetic tree to accompany an OTU/feature table and taxonomy table (e.g., to build a phyloseq object like MiSurv's biom.Rdata example data).

name: 16s-predictive-metagenome-inference
description: Use when input is a PICRUSt-compatible OTU table (BIOM format, closed-reference picked against Greengenes+IMG) and the goal is predicting metagenome/gene family abundance from marker-gene data alone.

name: 16s-reference-database-reformatting
description: Use when preparing an annotated microbial 16S FASTA database (Greengenes or SILVA) as input to the CDSnake/CD-HIT-OTU-Miseq pipeline, whose DATABASE parameter expects the reordered format.

name: 16s-rrna-abundance-threshold-filtering
description: Use when running HashSeq's inferTrueSequences on Illumina 16S rRNA amplicon FASTQ data and a filtering threshold must be set to remove low-abundance parent variants before LOESS-based error modeling and variant calling.

name: 16s-rrna-amplicon-count-comparison
description: Use when assembling overlapping paired-end Illumina 16S rRNA amplicon reads (e.g. 108-base M. capsulatus pairs) and deciding whether lowering the PANDAseq quality threshold from 0.9 to a looser cutoff (e.g. 0.6) recovers more sequences.

name: 16s-rrna-gene-copy-number-inference
description: Use when a 16S rRNA amplicon or qPCR analysis needs GCN estimates for bacterial or archaeal taxa lacking a sequenced genome, and a phylogenetic tree with taxonomy (e.g. Greengenes 99%-identity OTUs) is available.

name: 16s-rrna-insertion-boundary-detection
description: Use when you have curated full-length 16S rRNA gene sequences (e.g. ≥800 bp aligned bases) and need to flag which carry ≥10 bp insertions and report max/mean/sd insertion lengths, or when replicating the Brown et al. 2015 (10.1038/nature14486) CPR insertion statistics.

name: 16s-rrna-kmer-uniqueness-analysis
description: Use when validating that a salient 16S k-mer subset (baseLess read_detection k-mers) can support species detection against an arbitrary genomic background, by quantifying unique-k-mer identifiability across simulated mixture sizes from 1 up to 10,000 constituents.

name: 16s-rrna-multirank-classification-head-design
description: Use when building or reconstructing a 16S rRNA classifier that must predict all seven Linnean ranks (Domain through Species) in a single forward pass, or when verifying that a checkpoint exposes exactly seven per-rank output distributions.

name: 16s-rrna-primer-binding-assessment
description: Use when you have curated 16S rRNA gene sequences (e.g. assembled from metagenomes, ≥800 bp) and need to estimate which taxa a specific primer pair would miss in an amplicon survey.

name: 16s-rrna-similarity-bucket-stratification
description: Use when you have per-sequence species predictions from a 16S rRNA classifier (e.g., DeepTaxa on the Greengenes2 2024.09 69,335-sequence test set) and need to show whether accuracy degrades for test sequences distant from the 277,336-sequence training pool.

name: 16s-rrna-structural-alignment
description: Use when assembled 16S rRNA genes from metagenomes contain large insertion sequences (≥10 bp, e.g. CPR self-splicing introns up to 2,004 bp) that would corrupt a naive sequence alignment, and a reliable domain-level or phyla-level phylogeny is the goal.

name: 16s-rrna-taxonomic-classification
description: Use when 16S rRNA FASTA sequences (full-length ~1,500 bp or in-silico V3–V4 ~420 bp amplicons) need hierarchical taxonomic assignment from domain to species against the Greengenes2 2024.09 reference.

name: 16s-taxonomy-assignment
description: Reference for assigning taxonomy to 16S rRNA representative sequences when comparing multiple reference databases (e.g., Greengenes vs NCBI RefSeq) or when predicted taxonomic abundances are needed for mock-community accuracy assessment.

name: 454-homopolymer-error-modeling
description: Use when gene-finding on 454 metagenomic reads where homopolymer-run artifacts cause frame-disrupting indels, or when simulating/validating 454 read error models against true gene coordinates.

name: abundance-count-tabulation
description: Use when DIAMOND alignment of metatranscriptome reads has produced per-read annotation outfiles and ranked organism/function abundance summaries are needed for downstream DESeq statistics.

name: abundance-error-distance-metrics
description: Use when comparing abundance accuracy of a counting AMQ (e.g. counting Bloom filter) against fimpera and you need overestimation proportions and error-distance statistics on true-positive calls.

name: abundance-estimation-comparison
description: Use when comparing a metagenomic read classifier's genus-level sensitivity and abundance profiles against multiple baselines on mock communities with known ground-truth abundances.

name: abundance-kmer-model-compilation
description: Use when you have genome FASTAs for a target species plus closely related background species and need a model to classify raw MinION fast5 reads (pure samples) by k-mer abundance without basecalling.

name: abundance-l1-norm-error-quantification
description: Use when comparing taxonomic profiling tools on simulated metagenome samples and you need a per-sample abundance estimation error metric (L1-norm) alongside F1-score, from AMBER rank/cumulative results.

name: abundance-quantification-accuracy-assessment
description: Use when benchmarking taxonomic classifiers (e.g. AFS-MetaCache, MetaCacheSpark, CLARK, Kraken2, Kraken2+Bracken) on samples with known ingredient compositions to quantify false-positive rates and abundance-estimation error.

name: abundance-ranked-taxon-matching
description: Use when you need to quantify how much taxonomic assignments of the same OTU representative sequences disagree between 16S reference databases (Greengenes vs SILVA vs NCBI RefSeq), pairwise at each taxonomic level from Phylum to Species.

name: abundance-table-format-validation
description: Use when a PICRUSt2-derived KO or pathway abundance table is about to be transformed or analyzed, and you must confirm rows are features (KO orthologs or KEGG pathways), columns are samples, and post-conversion output preserves sample columns.

name: abundance-threshold-parameter-sweep
description: Use when you need to quantify how fimpera's threshold parameter z controls false positive calls on a counting Bloom filter, e.g. verifying the reported ~0.4%/0.56% FPR at z=3 and near-100% FPR at z=20.

name: accuracy-confidence-interval-reporting
description: Use when reproducing or reporting phenotype-classification accuracy from metagenomic feature tables (16S or WGS MetaPhlAn/QIIME profiles) where both held-out test accuracy and cross-validated accuracy with a 95% CI must be quoted, e.g. against MegaR Table 2 values.

name: accuracy-metrics-computation
description: Use when evaluating phenotype classifiers from cross-validation folds (e.g., Traitar phypat/phypat+PGL over the 67 GIDEON phenotypes) and reporting macroaccuracy alongside overall accuracy.

name: accuracy-vs-completeness-curve-visualization
description: Use when quantifying how genome incompleteness (e.g. metagenomic bins at 60-70% completeness) degrades binary phenotypic trait prediction accuracy, and when visualizing accuracy-vs-completeness curves per trait.

name: adagrad-optimization
description: Use when training a logistic matrix factorization (e.g. ILMF/NRLMF-style) whose latent factors need element-wise adaptive learning rates — e.g. after building virus-host heterogeneous networks with c=5 and K1=K2=5 regularization.

name: adapter-and-contaminant-read-filtering
description: Use when raw Illumina paired-end FASTQ metagenomic reads must be cleaned before assembly — adapters, low-quality bases, PhiX spike-in, or host contamination would degrade downstream MAG assembly and binning.

name: adapter-and-contig-edge-kmer-filtering
description: Use when building a taxonomic k-mer database (e.g., Kraken-GB from GenBank draft microbial genomes) where draft contigs may contain adapter contamination or unreliable terminal sequence, and classification accuracy would suffer if those k-mers were included.

name: adapter-and-quality-trimming
description: Use when raw paired-end RNA-seq/metatranscriptome FASTQ files have been merged (e.g. with PEAR) and still contain adaptor contamination and low-quality bases that would hurt downstream DIAMOND annotation.

name: adapter-sequence-removal-paired-end
description: Use when raw paired-end FASTQ reads enter the ViroProfiler pipeline and need adapter removal, quality trimming, and contaminant stripping before assembly or viral identification; skip only when input reads are already cleaned.

name: adapter-trimming-quality-control
description: Use when raw paired-end Illumina metagenomics reads (e.g. FASTQ/FASTQ.gz such as SRA SRR5381736) must be adapter-trimmed and quality-filtered prior to 16S/18S read extraction with SortMeRNA or BBMap.

name: adaptive-substitution-estimation
description: Use when you have a DAF spectrum plus divergence counts (Ds, Dn, Ps, Pn or mi, Di, m0, D0) for selected (0-fold) and neutral (4-fold) classes and need to estimate α and classify the selection regime for coding genes.

name: adaptive-sum-of-powered-score-testing
description: Use when testing H0: β = 0 for multivariate association between a selected subset of microbial taxa and an outcome in high-dimensional compositional OTU data, where the number of taxa (e.g. 856 OTUs) exceeds the sample size.

name: additive-log-ratio-compositional-transformation
description: Use when longitudinal sequencing count or relative-abundance data are compositional and must be embedded in unconstrained ALR coordinates before modeling trajectories, computing SNR, or interpreting cLV parameters.

name: adjacency-matrix-stacking-and-pca
description: Use when you have interaction/adjacency matrices from many MiCoNE tool-parameter combinations across pipeline steps and need to quantify which step (denoising-clustering, chimera-checking, taxonomy-assignment, OTU-processing, network-inference) drives the total variation among the inferred networks.

name: adjacent-gene-orientation-and-distance-analysis
description: Use when building or reproducing gene-prediction length/start-site models that require the empirical frequencies of adjacent-gene orientations (same-strand vs. opposite-strand categories) and intergenic distance distributions from an annotated prokaryotic genome.

name: admixture-ancestry-estimation
description: Use when genome-wide biallelic SNP data (VCF or PLINK binary) need individual-level ancestry proportions and an objective choice of cluster number K via ADMIXTURE CV-error minimization.

name: admixture-q-matrix-plotting-and-k-selection
description: Use when ADMIXTURE has been run over multiple user-defined K values on PLINK binary (bed/bim/fam) SNP data and the optimal K must be identified via CV error and the Q-matrices visualized interactively.

name: aldex2-compositional-da-testing
description: Use when you have a PICRUSt2-predicted pathway-level (KEGG) abundance table plus sample metadata with a grouping variable, and need to test pathway-level differential abundance between comparison groups.

name: algorithm-correctness-testing
description: Use when an in-place, allocation-free algorithm implementation (e.g. sliding-window minima over fixed windows of size W) must be proven correct against a brute-force oracle and benchmarked before adoption.

name: aligner-benchmarking-f1-throughput
description: Use when comparing accuracy and speed of read classification tools against large, repetitive references (e.g. human pan-genomes) in nanopore depletion or targeted-sequencing scenarios.

name: alignment-free-d2-star-dissimilarity-measurement
description: Use when you have raw whole-genome sequences (e.g. NCBI viral and bacterial genomes) and need virus-virus or host-host similarity without alignment, to seed network-based virus-host prediction methods.
tools: Jie Ren's d2* oligonucleotide frequency tools

name: alignment-free-dissimilarity-computation
description: Use when input is assembled genomic FASTA files or unassembled NGS shotgun reads (.fasta/.fa/.fna) and the goal is a pairwise alignment-free dissimilarity matrix for clustering, PCoA, heatmap or network analysis.

name: alignment-free-genome-distance-computation
description: Use when you need pairwise dissimilarities among whole genomes or unassembled shotgun reads without alignment (e.g. phylogeny recovery, metagenome comparison), especially where background-adjusted k-mer measures are required.

name: alignment-free-read-genome-similarity-scoring
description: Use when you have ebwt/lcp/da files for a combined read+genome fasta and need an alignment-free similarity score of every read against every genome, or when re-implementing LiME's Step 2 scoring with IUPAC-aware symbol matching.

name: alignment-free-sequence-analysis
description: Use when comparing assembled genomic sequences or unassembled NGS shotgun reads without alignments, and the Markov order required by background-adjusted k-mer measures (CVTree, D2star, D2shepp) is unclear to the user.

name: alignment-hits-tabular-output-processing
description: Use when quality-filtered FASTQ shotgun metagenomic reads (MetaLAFFA naming: <sample_id>.<type_id>.fastq.gz) must be aligned to UniRef90 gene sequences and the DIAMOND tabular hits need processing for -hit selection and gene abundance computation.

name: alignment-parameter-tuning
description: Use when building or validating an alignment/annotation pipeline and you need to empirically choose identity-percentage, read-coverage, and e-value cutoffs that maximize true positive mapping without inflating false positives.

name: alignment-quality-filtering
description: Use when quantifying cross-mapping or contamination between sequence databases (e.g., fungal markers vs. a bacterial reference) and strict alignment-quality criteria are needed to call a read 'mapped'.

name: alignment-throughput-measurement
description: Use when comparing resource footprints (peak memory, throughput) of read-decontamination or alignment pipelines across tools, e.g. Hostile vs HRRT on Illumina and ONT FASTQ inputs.

name: alignment-trimming-gap-based-filtering
description: Use when per-locus MAFFT alignments of Patchwork-recovered USCO (near-universal single-copy ortholog) sequences contain gap-rich columns that must be removed before concatenating a supermatrix and inferring a maximum-likelihood phylogeny.

name: alignment-vs-alignment-free-pipeline-performance-comparison
description: Use when replacing or validating an alignment-per-genome pipeline (BWA/Bowtie2/CUSHAW) with an alignment-free classifier and you must quantify speed-up (build time, MR/m query speed) and accuracy trade-offs (Σ FP, Σ Dev) on identical inputs.

name: all-vs-all-comparison-pair-count-analysis
description: Use when you need to characterize how an all-vs-all metagenome comparison tool's runtime scales with input volume, or when validating that Libra's Hadoop MapReduce scoring remains near-linear as sample counts grow despite quadratic pair growth.

name: allele-abundance-estimation
description: Use when you must quantify how accurately an MLST deconvolution pipeline recovers fractional allele composition and complete strain types from simulated mixed reads, and need a baseline comparison against abundance-estimation tools like Kallisto or strainEST.

name: allele-call-accuracy-evaluation-tvd
description: Use when validating an allele-diversity or strain-deconvolution stage against known simulated allele mixtures, and you need per-locus precision/recall and TVD statistics to compare with published baselines.

name: allele-depth-pileup-processing
description: Use when shotgun metagenomic BAMs aligned to a reference gene database must be converted into allele-depth pile-ups (cellSNP VCF), clustered via MetaQuad, and normalized into per-gene nucleotide diversity for group comparisons.

name: allele-diversity-integer-linear-programming
description: Use when WGS reads have been mapped to a curated MLST allele database and you must infer, per locus, which alleles are present and their fractional proportions in mixed (within-host heterogeneous) samples.

name: allele-fasta-sequence-processing
description: Use when you have one FASTA file per locus with all identified alleles from a chewBBACA cg/wgMLST schema and need to assess allelic variability per locus via per-locus MSAs and phylogenetic trees.

name: allele-frequency-density-clustering
description: Use when you have cellsnp-lite AD/DP allele count matrices from shotgun metagenomic samples and need to identify shared informative variants versus background noise based on clustering of sample allele frequencies.

name: allele-frequency-dissimilarity-computation
description: Use when comparing treatment groups (e.g. CLA, LEVO vs OTHERS) at a time point such as T+6W using allele-frequency profiles of shared informative variants from a cellSNP-lite/MetaQuad pipeline on ARG VCF data.

name: allele-frequency-extraction-from-vcf
description: Use when VCF files from low-frequency variant calling on wastewater NGS samples must be matched against a lineage mutation profile (e.g., B.1.1.7 unique mutations via Pangolin rules or outbreak.info) and per-mutation allele frequencies or a non-zero minimum AF are needed.

name: allele-frequency-summary-statistics
description: Use when you have VCF files of SARS-CoV-2 variants (e.g., from freebayes on wastewater NGS data) and need per-lineage abundance metrics such as mean allele frequency and variant counts.

name: allele-frequency-threshold-classification
description: Use when a resistance-calling pipeline must distinguish susceptible, low-frequency (minor), and high-frequency (major) resistant alleles from k-mer depths at mutation sites, and when a frequency threshold for calling resistance must be applied or justified.

name: allele-proportion-error-constraint-modeling
description: Use when reconstructing a multi-sample strain decomposition from per-locus allele distributions (geneX_proportions.csv) where you must minimize previously unobserved strains while respecting allele proportions within a tolerance.

name: allele-proportion-estimation-from-read-mappings
description: Use when processing WGS tick samples (2x76bp read pairs) against the 1726-allele B. burgdorferi MLST database and you need, per locus, the set of alleles and their fractional composition under within-host strain heterogeneity.

name: allelecall-scaling-analysis
description: Use when you need to quantify the computational scaling of chewBBACA AlleleCall (runtime vs CPU count, per-sample seconds-to-minutes behaviour) for a fixed set of draft genome FASTA files on a laptop or HPC cluster.

name: allelic-profile-matrix-generation
description: Use when draft/complete bacterial genome FASTA assemblies must be converted into a gene-by-gene allelic profile matrix against a pre-defined cgMLST/wgMLST schema, e.g. for strain typing or outbreak analysis.

name: alpha-cluster-detection-on-lcp-array
description: Use when classifying metagenomic reads alignment-free with LiME: you have precomputed ebwt, lcp and da files (e.g. built with BCR/egsa and merged with eGap) for a collection S of reads plus reference genomes, and you need the α-cluster blocks that feed the similarity analysis.

name: alpha-diversity-index-calculation
description: Use when you have a rarefied OTU count table per study plus a phylogenetic tree and need per-sample α-diversity summaries (richness, Shannon, Simpson, PD, PE, PQE) to feed downstream regression or meta-analysis.

name: alpha-diversity-index-computation
description: Use when comparing within-sample microbial diversity between treatment groups on a rarefied feature table and you need per-sample alpha-diversity estimates (including phylogenetic indices) plus covariate-adjusted group difference tests.

name: alpha-diversity-index-meta-analysis
description: Use when you have study-by-marker effect estimates and standard errors (no raw data, no a priori marker-by-marker correlations) for multiple related markers such as α-diversity indices and need an overall hypothesis test or pooled estimate.

name: als-radar-predictor-comparison
description: Use when a study provides two alternative remote-sensing predictor sets (e.g. ALS and Sentinel-1 radar) for the same plot-level biodiversity responses and you must quantify and validate their relative predictive power.

name: amber-f1-score-evaluation
description: Reference for reproducing or extending metagenomic taxonomic binning benchmarks that need rank-based F1-scores computed with AMBER over multiple tools, samples, and reference database configurations.

name: amber-metric-evaluation-of-bins
description: Use when binning outputs from competing binners (e.g., CH-Bin, MaxBin2, MetaBAT2, SolidBin) on datasets with known reference genomes (Sim50, Sim100, CAMI2 UG, Sharon) must be compared using purity/completeness/F1 metrics.

name: amber-rank-based-profile-evaluation
description: Use when per-sample taxonomic profiling results (e.g. ganon2, kraken2+bracken, kmcp outputs on simulated CAMI/RefSeq samples) must be scored against ground-truth taxon assignments to compare F1-score by rank and abundance accuracy.

name: ambiguous-nucleotide-kmer-filtering
description: Use when enumerating k-mers from metagenomic reads that contain ambiguous bases ('N'), adapter remnants, or concatenated paired mates, to decide which k-mers contribute LCA taxa to the classification tree.

name: ambiguous-read-re-examination
description: Use when LiME's Classify step labels paired-end reads as Ambiguous (status 'A') in the OutputFile and you need to convert those entries into single-taxon assignments (C/U) before computing species-level SEN/PREC/F1/specificity on datasets such as setA2/setB2.

name: amino-acid-identity-alignment-filtering
description: Use when two non-redundant protein/gene catalogues (e.g. VMGC-90 vs VIRGO-90) must be compared to compute mutual gene coverage and protein-space expansion fractions.

name: amino-acid-recoding-alphabet-selection
description: Use when training Snekmer supervised models or clustering protein families (e.g., nitrogen cycling families or UniProt genomes) and you must choose among the 7 AAR alphabets (sizes 2–20) and k=4–16 via config.yaml sweeps.

name: amino-acid-recoding-kmer-vectorization
description: Use when protein FASTA sequences must be vectorized as reduced-alphabet AAR kmers, or when supervised family-scoring semantics (F_kmer, F'_kmer, S_kmer with values in (-1, 1)) must be reproduced or unit-tested in Python.

name: amino-acid-reduction-encoding
description: Use when protein FASTA sequences (e.g., nitrogen cycling families) must be recoded into AAR k-mer vectors, or when comparing feature-generation runtime/model performance of MIQS-recoded k-mers versus unencoded k-mers at a fixed k.

name: amoa-aob-gene-cluster-analysis
description: Use when a curated set of amoA-AOB (or similar functional gene) reference protein+nucleotide sequences must be clustered into representative clusters and prioritized by abundance/prevalence across environmental metagenomes before primer design.

name: amplicon-assembly-validation
description: Use when you have overlapping paired-end Illumina FASTQ/SAM reads (e.g. 16S rRNA amplicons) and must merge them while probabilistically correcting uncalled or miscalled bases, then filter assemblies by quality score.

name: amplicon-error-background-modeling
description: Use when building or validating a background error model for amplicon variant calling: one-mismatch child abundances (mean/SD per cluster) must be related to parent sequencing depth to justify an abundance threshold.

name: amplicon-metagenome-profile-agreement-analysis
description: Use when paired amplicon (16S) and metagenomic profiles exist for the same mock or known communities and you need to test whether GCN correction (or another bias correction) brings the amplicon profile closer to the metagenomic or expected composition.

name: amplicon-metagenomic-preprocessing
description: Use when raw amplicon FASTQ reads (454 or Illumina 16S/ITS) need primer trimming plus adaptive quality filtering before OTU clustering, and reads exceeding a maximum expected error (EE) budget must be discarded.

name: amplicon-metagenomic-read-simulation
description: Use when a validation study needs communities of known composition to benchmark amplicon profiling or GCN correction — e.g. to test whether CopyRighter-corrected 16S profiles match expected and metagenomic profiles.

name: amplicon-metagenomic-workflow-command-execution
description: Use when you have an OTU representative-sequence FASTA file from MICCA de novo clustering and need an aligned set and phylogenetic tree (Newick) for downstream phylogenetic diversity metrics.

name: amplicon-naive-bayes-taxonomy-assignment
description: Use when OTU representative sequences need taxonomic labels under alternative 16S reference databases (Greengenes, SILVA, NCBI RefSeq) to quantify how database choice affects downstream community-composition inferences.

name: amplicon-otu-clustering-method-comparison
description: Use when demultiplexed 16S amplicon reads must be processed by multiple OTU-assignment/denoising methods and the similarity of the resulting representative sequence sets needs to be quantified with UniFrac distances.

name: amplicon-pipeline-combination-enumeration
description: Use when assessing how alternative tools/parameters at each 16S pipeline step (DC, CC, TA, OP, NI) affect the inferred co-occurrence network, or when quantifying which step contributes most to total network variation.

name: amplicon-rarefaction-depth-analysis
description: Use when validating OTU-count accuracy of a 16S amplicon pipeline against a ground-truth synthetic dataset with known OTU composition, or when comparing de novo OTU-picking pipelines across sequencing depths.

name: amplicon-read-dereplication
description: Use when quality-filtered FASTQ/FASTA amplicon reads must be collapsed to unique sequences with abundance vectors before de novo OTU inference, chimera filtering, or benchmarking dereplication speed.

name: amplicon-read-quality-filtering
description: Use when raw 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing reads (e.g., FASTQ deposited in QIITA) must be quality-filtered in QIIME 2.0 before downstream feature table, taxonomy, and phylogeny generation for MiSurv-style survival analysis.

name: amplicon-sequence-variant-cluster-analysis
description: Use when evaluating or reproducing an inference test on one-mismatch children in HashSeq cluster output (OneMismatchCluster.txt, childrenProperties.txt), e.g. to benchmark Poisson-based variant-calling error models.

name: amplicon-survey-detection-bias-analysis
description: Use when you have curated 16S rRNA gene sequences (e.g. assembled and intron-stripped) and need to estimate which taxa a specific primer pair would fail to amplify in a cultivation-independent amplicon survey.

name: amplicon-template-synthesis
description: Use when you need a simulated paired-end Illumina benchmark with known ground-truth sequences but realistic, experimentally derived per-base error probabilities for validating an assembler.

name: amplicon-variant-count-table-processing
description: Use when raw pre-processed 16S rRNA amplicon FASTQ data (e.g., PRJEB24409 mock communities with primers removed, reads paired, trimmed to 250 bases) must be converted into a filtered variant count table for downstream analyses.

name: ancestral-character-state-inference
description: Use when predicting bacterial phenotypes from Pfam presence/absence profiles and you want to incorporate horizontal gene transfer by augmenting phyletic patterns with ancestral gains/losses inferred on the species tree.

name: ancestral-state-reconstruction-gene-content
description: Use when you must infer gene content (e.g. KO/COG abundances, 16S copy number) for organisms without sequenced reference genomes from a 16S phylogenetic tree plus a gene-by-genome annotation table, as required to build PICRUSt reference files.

name: ani-based-genome-dereplication
description: Use when constructing a de novo source-associated genome database (sourceapp_build.py) where redundant reference genomes and MAGs must be collapsed to 95% ANI species representatives per fecal source category before metagenomic source tracking.

name: ani-based-strain-refinement
description: Use when a MAG-level taxonomy classifier (e.g. kMetaShot) assigns MAGs only to a species/genus because the corresponding mock-community or reference genomes lack strain annotation, and strain-level resolution is required for benchmarking.

name: ani-threshold-strain-sharing-analysis
description: Use when the goal is to decide, from metagenomic read mappings to a set of sub-species genomes, which strains are shared between samples, and to compare strain-sharing calls across ANI thresholds (e.g., 99.999% strain clustering vs. 98% dereplication).

name: annotation-abundance-counting
description: Use when you have raw per-read annotation output files from MG-RAST (or DIAMOND) and need to condense them into abundance summary tables of organism or functional hits before statistical comparison.

name: annotation-table-integration
description: Use when you have protein-coding genes predicted on viral contigs and need per-gene functional hits from multiple databases (EggNOG5, VOGDB) plus auxiliary metabolic gene (AMG) calls merged into one tabular annotation table.

name: anova-variance-partitioning
description: Use when many co-occurrence networks have been generated from all tool/parameter combinations of a multi-step 16S pipeline and you must quantify which pipeline step contributes most to network-to-network variation.

name: antibiotic-resistance-gene-variant-detection
description: Use when you need to detect shared informative variants across a population of shotgun metagenomic samples aligned to a reference gene database (e.g., antibiotic resistance genes), and want to separate shared polymorphic sites from background noise.

name: antimicrobial-resistance-gene-database-curation
description: Use when merging several existing antimicrobial resistance (or biocide/metal resistance) gene catalogs into one non-redundant curated database, and you need reproducible filtering, deduplication, and centroid counts.

name: antimicrobial-resistance-gene-flank-reconstruction
description: Use when short-read metagenomic FASTQ data must yield assembled genomic context (100–5000 bp flanks) around ARGs, but full metagenomic de novo assembly is computationally prohibitive or unnecessary.

name: antimicrobial-resistance-prediction
description: Use when raw reads (Illumina MiSeq/HiSeq or ONT MinION FASTQ) from S. aureus or M. tuberculosis isolates need antibiotic-resistance calls across a drug panel, without assembly or phenotype testing.

name: approximate-membership-query-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing an Approximate Membership Query data structure (e.g., a counting Bloom filter) against its fimpera-wrapped version on abundance queries, to quantify false-positive rate, overestimation score, space, and query time.

name: approximate-membership-query-false-positive-handling
description: Use when building an approximate membership query index over k-mer abundances where false positive k-mer calls or overestimated abundances must be reduced without memory overhead.

name: apss-aggregation-and-subsampling
description: Use when you have SynTracker's raw synteny_scores_per_region.csv output and need APSS values per pair of samples or genomes, with subsampled or all-region aggregation for comparisons or cutoff-based strain designation (e.g., APSS 0.95).

name: architectural-ablation-model-training
description: Use when you need to isolate the contribution of individual model pathways (CNN vs transformer vs input tokenization) by training variant architectures on the same data/schedule and comparing species-level top-1 accuracy and F1.

name: architecture-variant-benchmarking
description: Use when choosing among candidate DNN architectures for classifying short metagenomic sequencing reads and you need head-to-head read-level precision/recall on held-out genomes to justify the selection.

name: arg-scaffold-matching-with-kma
description: Use when you have assembled scaffolds (targeted ARGextender or full SPAdes) from metagenomic reads and need to identify which ARG database sequences are present and count ARG-scaffolds per sample.

name: ass2ref-confidence-filtering
description: Use when classifying MAGs with kMetaShot and you need to discard unreliable strain- or species-level assignments: apply the -a/ass2ref filter to the classifier output so only classifications whose minimizer support meets the ratio threshold are retained.

name: assemblathon-benchmark-assembly
description: Use when evaluating or benchmarking a short-read de novo assembler against published baselines on the Assemblathon1 dataset, or when reproducing reported N50 and error-rate reductions (e.g. 90.12% structural error reduction).

name: assembled-contig-fasta-handling
description: Use when input is long reads or already-assembled contigs to supply via -A, or when short reads must be assembled by SPAdes, metaSPAdes, or MEGAHIT with the assembly chosen by N50.

name: assembled-contig-length-and-count-qc
description: Use when you have newly generated contig FASTA files from one or more short-read assemblers and must verify they fall within expected total-length and contig-count ranges for a known-size genome before deeper evaluation.

name: assembler-comparison-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing metaMDBG, metaflye and hifiasm-meta on the same HiFi read set of a taxonomically rich metagenome to quantify uncaptured diversity (unaligned bases) and bases aligned to medium-or-better bins.

name: assembler-comparison-table-compilation
description: Use when benchmarking de novo short-read assemblers on datasets with known reference genomes (GAGE Staphylococcus aureus, Rhodobacter sphaeroides, human chr14; Assemblathon1) and you need a quantitative improvement table versus a predecessor or competing assembler.

name: assembler-output-comparison-across-assemblies
description: Use when several de novo assembly contig sets in FASTA format (e.g. ABySS, Velvet, SPAdes, MEGAHIT output) must be compared without a reference genome to select the most contiguous, complete assembly.

name: assembler-output-comparison-against-reference-variants
description: Use when shotgun metagenomic reads from a mock/defined community have been processed through several SSU extraction and reference-targeted assembly combinations and you must decide which combination recovers the most known 16S rRNA variants.

name: assembler-parameter-recipe-execution
description: Use when reproducing the four E. coli K-12 MG1655 sample assemblies from trimmed paired-end FASTQ reads (SRA ERR008613) as input for WebQUAST/QUAST assembly evaluation, or when comparing short-read assemblers under their citation-standard parameter settings.

name: assembler-resource-usage-extraction
description: Use when you have deposited LMAS benchmark output (e.g. Zenodo/GigaDB deposit for giac122) for repeated runs and need per-assembler runtime, CPU/hour, memory, and data read/written statistics, or must justify excluding assemblers on resource grounds.

name: assembler-runtime-and-contig-count-profiling
description: Use when comparing the computational cost and assembly output (wall-clock time, total contigs, contigs >50 Kb) of a targeted assembly pipeline against complete metagenomic assembly or alternative assemblers on identical raw sequencing reads.

name: assembly-based-variant-concordance-assessment
description: Use when you have de novo diploid assemblies (e.g. Supernova2 output from 10x Linked-Read data) and need to quantify how accurately their variant calls agree with reference-based call sets and GIAB benchmarks.

name: assembly-benchmark-comparison-against-reference
description: Use when validating that a targeted assembly tool recovers comparable gene-containing scaffolds and gene diversity to full de novo assembly on the same samples, at lower computational cost.

name: assembly-benchmarking-metrics-preparation
description: Use when preparing assembler contigs (e.g. from results/assembly/<assembler>/) for reference-based benchmarking in LMAS: contigs must be length-filtered and mapped to a multi-FASTA of reference replicons before computing global and replicon-specific metrics.

name: assembly-contig-alignment-metrics
description: Use when benchmarking metagenomic assemblers against a known mock community with reference replicons, and you need a per-replicon contiguity fraction (LSA) from contig-vs-reference alignments.

name: assembly-contig-sd-representation-quantification
description: Use when comparing how completely two de novo genome assembly versions represent annotated repeat/segmental duplication sequences, or when auditing whether an assembler upgrade improved recovery of known genomic sequence.

name: assembly-contiguity-assessment
description: Use when planning or evaluating de novo diploid genome assembly from 10x Chromium Linked-Read data, especially to choose fragment length (Mu_F) or physical coverage (CF) parameters and predict contig N50 outcomes at a fixed total coverage such as C = 56x.

name: assembly-contiguity-metric-computation
description: Use when FASTA assemblies (contigs/scaffolds) from metagenome assemblers must be scored against a known reference to compare contiguity (NGA50), misassemblies, and base-level accuracy across tools or ablation modes.

name: assembly-contiguity-metric-computation
description: Use when comparing multiple assemblies of the same genome (e.g. outputs from different assemblers such as SPAdes, Velvet, ABySS, MEGAHIT) and you need contiguity statistics like N50, N90, auN, or largest contig length to rank them.

name: assembly-contiguity-metrics-computation
description: Reference for evaluating and comparing de novo short-read assemblies (e.g., SOAPdenovo2 vs SOAPdenovo1.05) on benchmark datasets such as GAGE (S. aureus, R. sphaeroides, human chr14) or Assemblathon1 using N50, correct assembly length, and error counts.

name: assembly-contiguity-n50-evaluation
description: Use when short-read metagenomic FASTQ inputs are being assembled within virMine and no single assembler is obviously appropriate, so contiguity (N50) should decide which assembly proceeds to annotation and viral scoring.

name: assembly-contiguity-n50-evaluation
description: Use when de novo assembled 10x Linked-Read (Supernova2) assemblies must be compared across parameter settings (total coverage C, physical coverage CF, read coverage per CR) using N50 and NA50 contiguity/accuracy metrics.

name: assembly-contiguity-ng50-evaluation
description: Use when a strain-separated assembly (e.g. assembly.scaffolds.fa from Strainberry) must be scored against known reference genomes to quantify contiguity (NG50), base accuracy (ANI), and redundancy (duplication ratio).

name: assembly-contiguity-nx-plot-comparison
description: Use when multiple metagenome assemblers have been run on matched ONT long-read + Illumina paired-end samples and you need to quantify contiguity differences via Nx-length plots and scaffold categories.

name: assembly-contiguity-quality-assessment
description: Use when short-read and/or long-read metagenome samples have been assembled (short-read-only, long-read-only, or hybrid) and you must compare assembly contiguity across assemblers or dispatch modes before binning.

name: assembly-contiguity-statistics
description: Use when you have contigs from a MetaCortex (or similar de Bruijn graph) metagenomic assembly and need to quantify assembly quality as contig counts, N50 and maximum contig length after a length cutoff.

name: assembly-continuity-metric-tabulation
description: Use when comparing contiguity and binning yield of metagenome assemblies produced under different read-type (short vs hybrid) or grouping (sample-wise vs co-assembly) settings, using CAMISIM-style simulated time-series reads.

name: assembly-deposit-retrieval
description: Use when a published genome assembly paper reports assembly statistics (N50, coverage) and you need to download the deposited FASTA files and independently reproduce those metrics.

name: assembly-error-classification-and-counting
description: Use when comparing de novo assembler releases (e.g., SOAPdenovo2 vs SOAPdenovo1.05) on GAGE-style benchmark datasets (S. aureus, R. sphaeroides, human chr14) and you need per-error-type counts and correct assembly length metrics.

name: assembly-error-rate-quantification
description: Use when comparing de novo assembler versions or assemblies on a reference-backed benchmark and you need continuity (N50) plus per-error-class rates (structural, substitution, copy number) to claim improvement.

name: assembly-filter-ablation-comparison
description: Use when you must quantify how an assembly-stage filter (e.g. Plass's --filter-proteins neural network) changes the retained sequence set, by comparing filtered vs unfiltered candidate ORFs.

name: assembly-genome-fraction-evaluation
description: Use when comparing de novo metagenomic assemblers on a community with known reference genomes and you need quantitative genome recovery (genome fraction %) and contiguity metrics to rank assemblers.

name: assembly-graph-variation-representation
description: Use when assembling metagenomic or mock-community sequence data (e.g. the Mock B 12-virus community from SRR961514) where strain-level diversity should be preserved and evaluated against alternative assemblers such as MEGAHIT or Ray Meta.

name: assembly-metric-interpretation
description: Use when comparing genome assemblies with QUAST/WebQUAST against a true or close reference genome (e.g., E. coli K-12 MG1655 vs W3110) and you must interpret misassemblies, NGA50, genome fraction, or duplication ratio to select the assembly.

name: assembly-misassembly-quantification
description: Use when a metagenomic assembly attributes many misassembled blocks to a genome sequenced at ultra-high coverage (>1000x) and you need to test whether excess coverage, not biology, caused the errors.

name: assembly-peak-memory-profiling
description: Use when comparing memory consumption of genome assembler graph-construction modes on a fixed read set, or when quantifying the assembly (N50) tradeoff introduced by a memory-saving algorithm such as the sparse de Bruijn graph.

name: assembly-quality-assessment
description: Use when preprocessed paired-end metagenomic reads must be de novo assembled and the resulting contigs must be quality-checked via contig count, total length (bp), and N50, e.g. to reproduce VIRGO's assembly cohort statistics.

name: assembly-quality-assessment-metrics
description: Use when assemblies from multiple de novo assemblers must be scored per contig against known reference replicons, requiring a Phred-like quality metric derived from alignment identity rather than raw sequence features.

name: assembly-quality-score-geometric-mean-aggregation
description: Use when scoring assembled Illumina paired-end (FASTQ, PHRED/CASAVA qualities) sequences by overlap base agreement and filtering them against a quality threshold such as p = 0.9 or p = 0.6.

name: assembly-quality-score-thresholding
description: Use when PANDAseq has assembled Illumina overlapping paired-end (e.g. 16S rRNA amplicon) reads and you must choose how many low-confidence assemblies to retain or discard via the assembly quality score cutoff.

name: assembly-quality-threshold-filtering
description: Use when paired-end Illumina FASTQ reads have been assembled (or must be filtered) and you need to set an accept/discard cutoff on the PANDAseq assembly quality score to control sequence recovery, as for the 673 845-read M. capsulatus 16S rRNA library.

name: assembly-reference-coverage-ani-assessment
description: Use when evaluating a de novo (strain-resolved or strain-oblivious) metagenome assembly against known reference genomes, needing per-contig reference coverage percentages and nucleotide identity to judge strain separation quality.

name: assembly-runtime-benchmarking
description: Use when a newly proposed assembly or gene-targeting pipeline needs quantitative comparison of runtimes and contig outputs against a standard complete-assembly baseline on identical sequencing datasets.

name: assembly-source-attribution
description: Use when building or extending a non-redundant gene catalog from mixed inputs (e.g., vaginal metagenome assemblies plus urogenital isolate genomes) and you need predicted CDS counts and per-gene lengths attributed to each assembly source.

name: assembly-statistics-interpretation
description: Use when binned contig FASTA files (MAGs) have been produced by a binning step and you must judge per-bin assembly quality before downstream taxonomic or functional annotation.

name: assembly-throughput-benchmarking
description: Use when you need to measure how fast a paired-end assembler processes a large Illumina FASTQ dataset and what fraction of input read pairs it recovers, e.g. to compare PANDAseq against alternative assemblers.

name: association-rule-feature-selection-cpar
description: Use when reproducing or benchmarking the CPAR2SVM pipeline of PICA — association-rule-based feature selection of COG profiles followed by libSVM — for phenotypic trait prediction on ten example traits such as aerobe, motile, or therm.

name: asv-abundance-table-processing
description: Use when the input is a marker-gene (16S rDNA) ASV abundance table with its corresponding sequence FASTA and the goal is to predict metagenome functional profiles from that marker-gene input.

name: auxiliary-metabolic-gene-identification
description: Use when you have a set of predicted viral contigs (post VirSorter2/VIBRANT) and need to annotate their genes and flag which encode auxiliary metabolic genes (AMGs).

name: average-nucleotide-identity-clustering
description: Use when a quality-controlled collection of prokaryotic genome FASTAs (MAGs plus isolates) must be dereplicated into species-level bins at 95% ANI, or when reproducing a published species count such as the VMGC's 786 SGBs.

name: average-nucleotide-identity-computation
description: Use when MAG or genome FASTA assemblies must be assigned species labels relative to a reference genome database via closest-relative search plus AQ/ANI alignment thresholds.

name: average-nucleotide-identity-filtering
description: Use when constructing a non-redundant pan-genome gene database from many reference genomes, or when assigning metagenomic contigs to species-level pan-genomes by BLASTn of predicted genes using ANI thresholds.

name: bacterial-community-read-simulation
description: Use when you need to reproduce or extend a simulated-community assembly benchmark: you have reference genomes and want to generate in silico metagenomic reads (CAMISIM) and rank assemblers by genome fraction and contiguity.

name: bacterial-genome-allelic-profiling
description: Use when you have draft/complete genome FASTA files (e.g. S. agalactiae assemblies) and a cgMLST/wgMLST schema seed, and need to determine allelic profiles or measure how AlleleCall runtime scales with CPU count.

name: bacterial-isolate-genomics-read-processing
description: Use when raw paired-end Illumina FASTQ reads from bacterial isolate genomes (e.g., CDC & FDA Antibiotic Resistance Isolate Bank isolates) need quality trimming, adapter removal, contaminant read removal, and merging of overlapping mates before targeted assembly or annotation.

name: bacterial-phenotype-prediction
description: Use when you have tens or hundreds of bacterial genome sequences (nucleotide or protein FASTAs) and need trait calls for any of Traitar's 67 phenotypes, or when benchmarking genotype-to-phenotype classifiers against curated phenotype labels such as GIDEON or Bergey's Manual entries.

name: bacterial-trait-prediction-from-genome-sequence
description: Use when starting from bacterial nucleotide (or protein) FASTA files for tens to hundreds of genomes and a genotype-to-phenotype assignment across the 67 Traitar trait labels is needed without wet-lab phenotyping.

name: balanced-accuracy-evaluation
description: Use when comparing SVM kernels or training-set variants for binary phenotypic trait prediction (e.g. gram-negative status, spore-forming, phototrophy) on COG presence/absence matrices and you need a class-imbalance-robust performance metric.

name: bam-file-parsing-and-read-pair-joining
description: Use when a metagenomic read-mapping .bam file must be filtered before profile coverage/SNV analysis and paired-end read structure (orientation, insert size, mapQ) should drive filtering.

name: barcode-aware-pcr-duplicate-removal
description: Use when raw 10x Chromium Linked-Read paired-end FASTQs must be deduplicated before fragment inference or subsampling to a target CR — e.g., building comparable Linked-Read sets (Rid) with matched per-fragment read coverage across libraries.

name: barcoded-paired-end-fastq-simulation
description: Use when generating synthetic 10x Chromium Linked-Read FASTQ data for testing de novo assembly (Supernova2) or variant pipelines (Long Ranger), or when exploring parameter combinations such as CF, CR, Mu_F, and N_FP before real library preparation.

name: basecalling-alignment-pipeline-throughput-comparison
description: Use when comparing inference speed of nanopore raw-signal classifiers or basecalling pipelines across low-powered single-board computers and desktop hardware, and kbp/s throughput per tool is the target metric.

name: baseline-ranking-trend-verification
description: Use when a paper claims a model has more balanced per-class performance (e.g. lowest per-status F1 variance) and you need to verify that claim by computing and ranking F1 variance across models and datasets.

name: batch-file-workflow-orchestration
description: Use when you hold a set of per-locus FASTA files (one per schema locus, each containing all identified alleles) and need a per-locus MSA and neighbour-joining tree to assess locus-level allelic diversity.

name: bayesian-core-genome-partitioning
description: Use when computing a core genome from genome sets containing incomplete MAGs/SAGs of mixed quality (e.g. 45–95% complete), where standard pangenome tools like Roary are sensitive to missing genes.

name: bayesian-core-trait-likelihood-partitioning
description: Use when estimating core genomes from genome sets (MAGs, SAGs, or complete genomes) of highly variable or low completeness, where presence/absence patterns of gene-encoded traits must be evaluated against a completeness prior instead of simple occurrence thresholds.

name: bayesian-information-criterion-model-selection
description: Use when running CAFE's background-adjusted k-mer measures (CVtree, D2star, D2shepp) on FASTA sequences and the appropriate Markov order encoding the sequence model is unclear to the user.

name: bayesian-map-model-selection
description: Use when you have Mykrobe predictor JSON output for an M. tuberculosis sample and need to reproduce or audit the susceptible/minor/major genotype logic behind each resistance call.

name: bayesian-presence-absence-likelihood-estimation
description: Use when computing core-genome partitioning for a set of closely related genomes of mixed quality (complete genomes plus incomplete/contaminated MAGs, SAGs, SUBs) from presence/absence patterns of gene clusters.

name: bayesian-variable-selection-mcmc-inference
description: Use when relating a covariate matrix (e.g., dietary or clinical variables) to compositional taxa count data that have a known phylogenetic tree, and the goal is sparse branch-by-covariate association selection with uncertainty quantification.

name: bbmap-read-assignment-counting
description: Use when you have reconstructed full-length SSU sequences (e.g. metagenome_SSU_sequences.fasta) from a metagenomic pipeline and need per-sequence relative abundance from the original high-quality reads before 97% clustering and taxonomic classification.

name: bbmap-read-count-summarization
description: Use when you have multiple reconstructed SSU sequences (from EMIRGE and MetaRib) with per-sequence read counts and need de-redundant cluster representatives with combined abundances for downstream taxonomic profiling.

name: benchmark-accuracy-table-compilation
description: Use when MAGs from CAMI II mock community datasets have been classified by multiple taxonomic tools and you need a ranked accuracy comparison (sensitivity, precision, BA, F1, FPR) at strain/species/genus levels against the CAMI gold standard.

name: benchmark-aggregate-gap-analysis
description: Use when a set of real DNA FASTA datasets with ground-truth cluster labels needs a head-to-head accuracy comparison between a deep-learning clustering method and classical or DNA-specialized baselines, with aggregate gap reporting.

name: benchmark-assembly-evaluation
description: Use when a new genome assembly (contigs/scaffolds from a de Bruijn graph assembler such as SOAPdenovo2) must be benchmarked against a predecessor or competitor on a reference-backed dataset.

name: benchmark-count-table-reproduction
description: Use when the goal is to validate a gene predictor's real-read performance by reproducing published BLAST-hit count tables from 454 metagenomic reads, e.g. the TS28/TS50 human gut twin-study samples.

name: benchmark-dataset-assembly-execution
description: Use when you need to produce de novo assemblies from benchmark Illumina short-read datasets to compare assembler versions or tools on N50, error counts, and correct assembly length.

name: benchmark-error-profile-reproduction
description: Use when two sequence-classification tools must be compared on fragments with known chromosomal/plasmid origin, and you need per-tool error rates (FPR, FNR) plus a concordance fraction between their predictions.

name: benchmark-figure-reproduction
description: Use when reproducing or re-evaluating a published classifier benchmark figure — specifically false-positive behavior on reads simulated from species absent from reference databases — using the DeepMicrobes Figure 4 design.

name: benchmark-figure-reproduction
description: Use when reproducing a taxonomic-classifier benchmark with genome exclusion, or regenerating sensitivity/precision comparison figures for reads stratified by number of reference genomes per genus.

name: benchmark-performance-tabulation
description: Use when you need to reproduce or audit per-assembler computational cost from deposited LMAS benchmark outputs — e.g. comparing runtime, memory, CPU/hour, and data read/written across assemblers or checking consistency across repeated runs of the same mock community sample.

name: benchmark-read-count-comparison
description: Decision support for choosing a 16S paired-end read processing pipeline when you have raw paired-end FASTQ data and want to compare how many total reads (and OTUs) each candidate pipeline (merging-free CD-HIT-based vs merging-based) retains across benchmark datasets.

name: benchmark-result-reproducibility-analysis
description: Use when validating or reproducing published computational-efficiency claims for a metagenomic gene-prediction pipeline — specifically wall-clock timing on a fixed-length test sequence, time-in-scan profiling, and database size reduction factors.

name: benchmark-result-table-compilation
description: Use when several metagenome assemblers have been run on the same sample (e.g. MetaPlatanus vs metaFlye, OPERA-MS, MEGAHIT) and the goal is to tabulate scaffold counts, CheckM completeness/contamination, and reference-alignment edge error rates per assembler.

name: benchmark-results-tabulation
description: Use when comparing runtime, CPU usage, and peak memory of MAG taxonomy classifiers across the same benchmark datasets, especially when one tool's cost is dominated by reference loading (e.g. kMetaShot's ~22Gb HDF5 matrix requiring ≥32Gb RAM).

name: benchmark-table-compilation
description: Use when two or more assembly versions (or assemblers) must be compared under identical settings and the results tabulated, e.g. contig/scaffold N50, coverage percentages, or per-sequence representation rates of a reference set.

name: benchmark-table-value-extraction
description: Reference for extracting per-pipeline OTU counts, total read counts, and annotation/correct-annotation values from benchmark tables that compare CD-HIT-OTU-Miseq-based CDSnake against QIIME2 DADA2 and deblur on mock communities.

name: benchmark-throughput-ratio-computation
description: Use when comparing read-classification tools' benchmark tables (bases/second throughput, index size, peak RSS) and you need quantitative advantage ratios across references of increasing repetitiveness, e.g. single-genome vs many-strain pan-genome indexes.

name: benchmarking-log-parsing
description: Use when deposited assembler benchmark logs (e.g. Zenodo record 7996690) contain per-run timing/memory records across thread counts and you must reproduce or re-aggregate speed claims such as the 3- to 10-fold Plassembler vs Unicycler improvement.

name: benchmarking-read-preprocessing
description: Use when raw paired-end Illumina FASTQ pairs (e.g. Acinetobacter_baumannii_1.fastq.gz/_2.fastq.gz from Zenodo 7996690) must be adapter-trimmed and quality-filtered before hybrid plasmid assembly with Plassembler.

name: benjamini-hochberg-fdr-correction
description: Use when comparing case-control metagenomic feature tables (e.g. healthy vs adenoma vs carcinoma CSS-normalized abundance at five annotation levels) and you need per-feature P-values corrected for multiple testing.

name: benjamini-hochberg-fdr-correction
description: Use when evaluating one-mismatch children from HashSeq's OneMismatchCluster.txt against a background error rate with poisson.test, and per-child P values must be multiple-hypothesis corrected with BH at 5% FDR before writing InferenceTestSignificantChildren.txt.

name: benjamini-hochberg-fdr-multiple-testing-correction
description: Use when hundreds/thousands of taxa (phylum through genus) each yield a raw P-value from group-comparison regression and a family-wise-error-controlled, FDR-adjusted significance list is needed.

name: berger-parker-dominance-estimation
description: Use when amplicon OTU tables (e.g. Greengenes-based twin gut cohort profiles) are being corrected with CopyRighter and you must verify that per-sample dominance changes fall in a reported range (0-23.3%) or summarize community dominance shifts.

name: bernoulli-read-carrier-mutation-injection
description: Use when you need simulated longitudinal metagenomic reads carrying within-strain mutations with user-specified allele-frequency trajectories across timepoints, to benchmark mutation-detection tools.

name: best-e-value-hit-selection
description: Use when processing per-sample DIAMAND tabular alignment output during metagenomic read mapping and you must reduce many-to-many read-gene hits to matches before gene counting.

name: best-hit-model-assignment-per-sequence
description: Use when post-processing hmmsearch output against a profile HMM library where one input sequence may match several models and a single, -supported profile assignment per sequence is required.

name: beta-diversity-distance-analysis
description: Use when comparing gut microbial community composition between treatment groups (e.g., control vs tylosin) from a 16S feature table with taxonomic annotations and a phylogenetic tree, and you need distance matrices plus covariate-adjusted MiRKAT beta-diversity p-values.

name: beta-diversity-permanova-testing
description: Use when OMARU profiling tables for shotgun metagenomes (e.g., T2D n=171 or SCZ n=344 case-control cohorts) are available and the goal is to test whether between-sample community composition (beta-diversity) differs between cases and controls.

name: bi-directed-weighted-string-graph-construction
description: Use when you already have strain-separated contigs plus long-read alignments to them and need to order/connect contigs into scaffolds via a read-supported string graph rather than a contig graph.

name: bidirectional-lstm-sequence-modeling
description: Use when encoding variable-length DNA sequencing reads (e.g. FASTQ/FASTA metagenomic reads) as dense neural representations where oligonucleotide order and context matter for downstream taxonomic classification.

name: bin-completeness-and-strain-heterogeneity-assessment
description: Use when you have a set of metagenomic bins clustered from assembled contigs and need per-bin completeness and strain heterogeneity estimates to judge which bins represent near-complete organisms.

name: bin-quality-categorization-from-checkm
description: Use when evaluating a HiFi long-read metagenome assembly that has been binned (e.g. MetaBAT2 bins scored by CheckM2) and you need read/base mapping ratios split by bin quality category instead of a single aggregate alignment ratio.

name: bin-quality-scatter-visualization
description: Use when a CheckM2 quality_report.tsv of metagenomic bins (completeness/contamination columns) is available and a visual, per-bin completeness-vs-contamination overview is needed alongside the quality category counts.

name: bin-quality-stratified-mapping-analysis
description: Use when evaluating a HiFi metagenome assembly by aligning raw reads to contigs with minimap2 and breaking down mapping ratios by CheckM2 bin quality to benchmark assemblies (e.g. Mock vs Gut vs Deadwood).

name: binary-classification-f1-scoring
description: Use when comparing read classifiers on nanopore reads where a gold standard must be derived from minimap2 alignments (MAPQ >= 30) and classification accuracy must be reported as F1 on target vs non-target calls.

name: binary-classification-metric-computation
description: Use when profiler outputs (KMA with mOTUs/Silva/genomic databases, MetaPhlAn 4, mOTUs 3, Bracken 2.8 on Kraken2) on CAMI in silico datasets must be scored per taxonomic rank against ground truth to compare binary classification performance.

name: binary-presence-absence-taxon-modeling
description: Use when microbial abundance is treated as a binary presence/absence trait and you need to estimate the relationship of one taxon to one SNP (genotype) across a large sample cohort.

name: binary-search-range-query
description: Use when reconstructing, reimplementing, or validating a minimizer-indexed k-mer database (e.g., Kraken-style k-mer/LCA store) and you need exact per-k-mer lookup via index-offset range retrieval plus binary search.

name: bioconda-environment-management
description: Use when a workflow requires multiple short-read genome assemblers (ABySS, MEGAHIT, SPAdes, Velvet) or QUAST, and tool installation via Bioconda into a conda environment is needed before running assembly or quality assessment.

name: biodiversity-alpha-beta-phylogenetic-metrics
description: Use when plot-level taxon occurrence/abundance data across multiple trophic groups must be converted into α, β (NMDS composition axes), and phylogenetic diversity response tables for modelling against remote-sensing predictors.

name: biodiversity-diversity-metric-modelling
description: Use when biodiversity response variables (taxonomic/phylogenetic alpha- and beta-diversity) are modelled against ALS or Sentinel-1 radar plot predictors and you must quantify the explained-variance loss after accounting for forest region as a random effect.

name: bioinformatics-tool-benchmark-tabulation
description: Use when a paper reports per-tool benchmark numbers (bases/second throughput, index size, peak RSS) in tables and you need to compute and verify cross-tool performance ratios across experiments.

name: biological-versus-technical-zero-classification
description: Use when longitudinal sequencing count data (OTU table, taxa by samples over time) contain many observed zeros and you need posterior probabilities distinguishing biological zeros from technical/sampling zeros.

name: biological-zero-posterior-inference
description: Use when longitudinal count data contain many zeros and the analysis must decide whether a taxon is truly extinct from the community or merely under the sequencing detection threshold.

name: biomass-trend-significance-testing
description: Use when you have qPCR-derived total microbial abundance estimates for paired samples (e.g., day 27 vs day 362 anaerobic digester biomass) and need to test temporal trends before and after GCN correction.

name: biosample-taxonomy-classification
description: Use when you have positive genome hits (e.g. from COBS queries against a compact index of ENA bacterial genomes) mapped to BioSample accessions and need to classify them by isolate taxonomy and count distinct known genera and species.

name: biosynthetic-gene-cluster-detection
description: Use when comparing metagenome assemblies by biologically meaningful content — counting BGCs (alongside Swiss-Prot CDSs, viral sequences, and CheckM/Prokka scaffold categories) recovered per assembler per sample.

name: biosynthetic-gene-cluster-genome-mining
description: Use when you have complete strain genomes (e.g. RefSeq FASTA) and need per-genome counts of BGCs, RiPP-encoding clusters, and short ORF candidates under motif-ORF vs all-ORF mining modes to benchmark mining sensitivity.

name: biosynthetic-gene-cluster-window-construction
description: Use when assembled nucleotide contigs must be partitioned into putative RiPP-encoding BGC regions, by anchoring fixed-size (10 kbp) windows on HMMer-detected modification enzyme hits before candidate ORF extraction.

name: bit-score-best-hit-selection
description: Use when you have a set of inferred amplicon sequence variants (e.g., HashSeq sequences.fasta) and need to confirm they match previously observed references by BLASTing against SILVA132 and keeping the top bit-score hit per variant.

name: bits-per-base-alignment-scoring
description: Use when assigning taxonomy to reconstructed viral contigs from metagenomic assemblies using combined nucleotide (BBMap) and translated/protein (DIAMOND) alignments, especially for low-coverage or divergent viruses that defeat read- or kmer-based classifiers.

name: bitvector-computation-kmin-kright-localmin
description: Use when the input is an eBWT file (e.g. reads.fasta.bwt built with BCR_LCP_GSA) of raw sequencing reads and reference-free SNP/INDEL detection requires positional clustering without storing LCP or gSA arrays.

name: bitwise-hash-packing-of-quantized-events
description: Use when building a RawHash-style index or mapping pipeline in which quantized raw-signal event means must be converted into 32-bit hash values for storage in or querying against a hash table.

name: blast-all-against-all-identity-computation
description: Use when auditing a sequence clustering's sensitivity at a fixed identity threshold (e.g., 50%): you need a BLAST-derived reference of clusterable sequence pairs (≥90% coverage of the shorter sequence) to compute per-tool false-negative fractions.

name: blast-based-reference-database-filtering
description: Use when a real metagenomic sample must be reduced to reads mappable to known references before benchmarking classifiers, and when a customized reference database with per-genome taxonomy must be derived from those BLAST hits.

name: blast-based-sequence-similarity-verification
description: Use when a kmer-signature classifier (e.g. PlasFlow) has binned assembly contigs as plasmids and you need sequence-level confirmation against known, manually curated plasmid references.

name: blast-based-taxonomic-classification
description: Use when OTU representative sequences need taxonomic labels via sequence-similarity search against NCBI RefSeq, or when comparing assignment consistency across 16S reference databases (Greengenes vs SILVA vs NCBI RefSeq).

name: blast-contig-verification-against-viral-references
description: Use when extended or seed contigs from viral metagenomic assembly must be validated — after ContigExtender extension, to confirm non-chimeric, accurate sequence and assign the correct reference virus.

name: blast-database-construction
description: Use when running SynTracker's first stage: you have per-sample metagenomic assemblies or isolate genomes in a target directory and need them indexed as a BLAST database for homologous-region retrieval against reference genome fragments.

name: blast-database-construction
description: Use when a pipeline needs a searchable nucleotide reference from a large multi-genome FASTA (e.g. the GeneMark-HM pan-genome) for similarity-based contig-to-pan-genome assignment or gene-to-reference matching.

name: blast-evalue-threshold-interpretation
description: Use when a set of nucleotide sequences (e.g. a FASTA catalogue of ISs) must be classified against a reference database and the goal is a reproducible strict/loose/novel homology split based on BLAST e-value thresholds.

name: blast-hit-flanking-sequence-extraction
description: Use when homologous genomic regions must be recovered from per-sample assemblies via BLASTn against a fragmented reference, and each hit needs flanking context for synteny block detection.

name: blast-homology-validation-against-nr
description: Use when raw 454 metagenomic reads (e.g. human gut microbiome samples TS28/TS50) have gene predictions from multiple callers and an independent, database-grounded estimate of prediction correctness is needed for tool comparison.

name: blast-identity-coverage-filtering
description: Use when running SynTracker strain-tracking analyses and you need to filter BLASTn hits of reference central regions against target assemblies/genomes by identity and coverage thresholds, or when reproducing sensitivity tests over these parameters.

name: blast-reciprocal-best-hit-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating whether an HMM-based protein assignment tool (e.g. DiSCo on Dsr proteins) outperforms blast-based baselines on curated genome or metagenome test sets.

name: blast-score-ratio-allele-inference
description: Use when allele calling draft/complete bacterial genome assemblies against a cg/wgMLST schema FASTA and each CDS must be classified as exact match, inferred (BSR-based), size-deviant (ASM/ALM), paralogous (NIPH), contig-tip (PLOT) or LNF.

name: blast-score-ratio-loci-merging
description: Use when constructing a novel wg/cgMLST schema seed from a set of draft or complete genome assemblies and you need to define distinct loci from predicted CDSs via BSR-based similarity clustering.

name: blast-scored-graph-path-walking
description: Use when a metagenomic assembly graph (GFA from MetaCortex MC mode) contains unresolved branches from strain-level variation, and consensus contigs must be resolved into strain-specific sequences for per-strain validation.

name: blast-search-parameter-configuration
description: Use when running SynTracker on metagenomic assemblies or genomes to detect conspecific strain sharing, and the BLAST identity/coverage, region length, and subsampling seed must be set for reproducible APSS computation.

name: blastn-all-vs-all-genome-comparison
description: Use when a set of viral genomes (e.g. CheckV-quality-filtered FASTAs from metagenomic assembly) must be dereplicated into species-level vOTUs, or when vOTU representatives need to be screened against external virome databases.

name: blastn-database-scanning-profiling
description: Use when benchmarking GeneMark-HM run-time on a real metagenome FASTA (~45 Mb) with one CPU, quantifying the BLASTn fraction of wall-clock time against the pan database, or measuring the volume/memory reduction of species-level pan-genomes vs. the non-redundant SGB/tCluster gene set.

name: blastn-homology-search-configuration
description: Use when metagenomic contigs from human microbiome assemblies must be assigned to species-level reference pan-genomes so that taxa-specific GeneMark.hmm-2 gene prediction models can be selected.

name: blastn-similarity-search-against-pangenome
description: Use when annotating human microbiome metagenomic contigs where species-specific gene-finding parameters cannot be self-trained from short sequence and the contig must instead be assigned to a reference pan-genome by sequence similarity.

name: blastp-all-against-all-sequence-clustering
description: Use when building a novel wg/cgMLST schema seed from a set of draft or complete genome assemblies and loci must be defined de novo by sequence-similarity clustering of predicted CDSs.

name: blastp-ground-truth-validation
description: Use when a profile-HMM screen (e.g., KEMET --hmm_mode onebm) yields candidate missing-KO hits that need independent verification against a reference database, or when the HMM score threshold must be tuned to balance sensitivity against false positives.

name: blastx-alignment-threshold-optimization
description: Use when calibrating translated-DNA alignment cutoffs (identity %, read coverage %, e-value) for a functional protein database against simulated or mock-community metagenomic reads.

name: blastx-tabular-hit-parsing
description: Use when DNA query contigs (or reads) have been searched against protein reference sequences with DIAMOND and tabular BLASTX hits must be grouped per reference and ordered for merging into continuous marker sequences.

name: block-tridiagonal-matrix-inference
description: Use when reconstructing latent relative-abundance trajectories from longitudinal OTU/count tables (taxa by samples) where sequencing noise causes technical zeros, and you need efficient posterior inference plus biological-vs-technical zero discrimination.

name: blosum62-alignment-scoring
description: Use when implementing or tuning inexact protein-level search that extends exact seed matches with amino acid substitutions and needs a substitution-matrix score (BLOSUM62) to rank and filter candidate matches.

name: blosum62-substitution-matrix-scoring
description: Use when trimming stitched DIAMOND BLASTX alignments of noncoding stretches, or when computing gap-excluded identity-based query-reference distances per window for coding-sequence cleanup in phylogenetic marker retrieval.

name: bonferroni-multiple-testing-correction
description: Use when comparing abundances of many predicted functional modules (e.g. KEGG modules M00009, M00240) between sample groups and need family-wise error control over the resulting battery of statistical tests.

name: boosted-gam-model-fitting
description: Use when tabular plot-level predictor sets (e.g., Sentinel-1 gamma_0 time-series statistics vs ALS structural metrics) must be compared for modelling biodiversity responses such as NMDS axes, species richness, or phylogenetic diversity with cross-validated regression.

name: bootstrap-confidence-interval-estimation
description: Use when a gene set (e.g. selected by recombination rate bins or chromosome localization) needs a confidence interval on alpha rather than a single point estimate, and when homogeneity of selection across genes must be statistically assessed.

name: bootstrap-consensus-tree-construction
description: Use when you need to infer population relationships and migration events from a filtered VCF of biallelic SNPs, with bootstrapped support and a consensus tree across bootstrap replicates.

name: bootstrap-false-positive-rate-estimation
description: Use when a core-genome prediction from incomplete genomes (MAGs/SAGs) needs a quality estimate — e.g. to flag problematic genome combinations or to validate a bootstrapped core call against an empirical 'true' core.

name: bootstrap-pvalue-network-filtering
description: Use when converting a bootstrapped interaction/correlation matrix from a network inference method (sparcc, propr, spieceasi, flashweave, cozine, harmonies, spring, mldm) into a significant co-occurrence network via Resample bootstraps, per-edge p-values, and threshold filtering.

name: bowtie2-alignment-based-read-classification
