description: Use when paired or single-end Illumina FASTQ reads from a microbial sample must be screened for human origin: aligning to a host reference index is needed to remove human contamination while retaining bacterial reads.

name: bowtie2-score-min-parameter-sweep
description: Use when aligning metagenomic reads against a partial or remotely related viral reference (e.g. bat coronavirus NC_014470.1) and you need to choose the read-mapping scoring that yields the richest seed set for overlap-based recruitment.

name: bowtie2-short-read-alignment
description: Use when decontaminating paired or single short reads (e.g. Illumina 2x150bp) from microbial samples by removing human host reads with Hostile's Bowtie2 mode, or when benchmarking retention of bacterial reads versus human read removal.

name: bpe-sequence-tokenization
description: Use when deep-learning classification of 16S rRNA (or other nucleotide) sequences requires fixed-size tokenized inputs for a transformer trained on the DNABERT-2 BPE vocabulary, e.g. before HybridCNNBERTClassifier inference or training on Greengenes2 FASTA data.

name: bray-curtis-abundance-distance-calculation
description: Use when you need an abundance-based all-vs-all distance matrix over sequencing samples (reads or assembled contigs) to benchmark abundance-ignoring methods like Mash or normalization-limited methods like Simka.

name: bray-curtis-dissimilarity-computation
description: Use when mock-community 16S data have been taxonomically assigned with alternative reference databases/classifiers and you need a single [0,1] dissimilarity metric per taxonomic level to compare assignment accuracy against a known expected composition.

name: bray-curtis-dissimilarity-computation
description: Use when you have a ground-truth presence-absence species composition matrix (plots × species) grouped into taxonomic/functional groups and need assemblage-composition response variables (β-diversity axes) for downstream modelling.

name: broad-category-cluster-visualization-comparison
description: Use when evaluating whether a k-mer MinHash tool's clustering resolution on 16S amplicon metagenomes is adequate by comparing its sample-cluster visualization against a full k-mer abundance cosine-similarity method.

name: busco-automated-lineage-selection
description: Use when binned contig FASTA files (MAGs) from metagenome binning need per-bin completeness and contamination estimates and assembly QC metrics (contig count, total length, N50).

name: busco-quality-threshold-filtering
description: Decision support for routing metagenome-assembled genome (MAG) FASTA bins between GTDB-Tk and CAT/BAT during the taxonomic annotation stage of nf-core/mag, using BUSCO quality summaries as the gate.

name: busco-single-copy-ortholog-profiling
description: Use when you need to profile completeness of MAGs via universal single-copy orthologs, or detect systematic absence of USCO genes (e.g. purine biosynthesis) across a clade of genomes.

name: bwa-mismatch-penalty-tuning
description: Use when reads must be recruited to a target virus via a distant reference genome and you need to sweep BWA mismatch penalties (e.g., -B 1/2/4/8) to build seed-read sets for overlap-based recruitment.

name: bwt-backward-search-context-extraction
description: Use when the input is an eBWT file (e.g. reads.fasta.bwt) of a raw-read collection and candidate variant intervals have been found, and read contexts flanking each variant must be extracted for variant-fragment assembly without aligning to a reference genome.

name: bwt-backwards-search-mem
description: Use when classifying high-throughput sequencing reads (Illumina or Roche/454) against a protein reference database at taxon level, especially when nucleotide-level k-mer classifiers miss divergent organisms.

name: bwt-based-overlap-read-recruitment
description: Use when you have a SAM file of reads aligned to a partial or remotely related viral reference (e.g. bat coronavirus NC_014470.1) and need to recruit reads of the true target virus (e.g. SARS-CoV haplotypes) for strain assembly.

name: bwt-construction-of-read-collections
description: Use when raw NGS reads (FASTA/FASTQ) need to be indexed for reference-free, alignment-free variant discovery, and the downstream tool (ebwt2InDel) consumes a .bwt file as input.

name: bwt-construction-runtime-profiling
description: Use when benchmarking BWT-based read-analysis pipelines on raw FASTA/FASTQ read sets and you must report wall-clock split between index construction (BCR/eBWT) and downstream SNP/INDEL detection.

name: bwt-fm-index-alignment
description: Use when classifying high-throughput sequencing reads (FASTQ/FASTA, Illumina or Roche/454) to NCBI taxa at the protein level, especially when k-mer classifiers like Kraken or Clark would need 65–78 GB of RAM but only a standard PC is available.

name: bwt-fm-index-construction-for-reads
description: Use when a SAM seed alignment and a FASTA read set must be searched for read–read overlaps via an FM-index, e.g. to expand a small seed set before de novo haplotype assembly with TAR-VIR/PEHaplo.

name: bwwtp-multi-omics-dataset-loading
description: Use when a task requires loading the built-in Example 1 BWWTP time-series multi-meta-omics data (metagenomics, metaproteomics, metatranscriptomics, metabolomics, physico-chemical) into MOVIS for downstream sanitizing, filtering, analysis, or visualization.

name: cached-query-range-optimization
description: Use when reimplementing or tuning Kraken-style exact k-mer/LCA lookup over a minimizer-partitioned database and you classify consecutive k-mers of a read, so the prior query's range can be searched before recomputing the M=15 minimizer.

name: cam-simulated-read-taxonomic-classification
description: Use when benchmarking taxonomic profiling tools (e.g. ganon2, kraken2+bracken, kmcp) on simulated read sets such as the 16 CAMI-derived samples, needing AMBER rank-based metrics and runtime comparisons.

name: cami-mock-community-benchmarking
description: Use when a taxonomy classifier must be evaluated on MAGs from simulated multi-sample communities (e.g. CAMI II GI-Illumina, GI-PacBio, Air-Illumina, Air-PacBio) against an expected taxonomy at strain/species/genus rank.

name: cami-simulated-metagenome-evaluation
description: Decision support for choosing a taxonomic profiler or reference database: when in silico CAMI datasets with known ground truth are available and candidate tools such as KMA-mOTUs, KMA-Silva, KMA-genomic, MetaPhlAn, mOTUs, or Bracken must be compared quantitatively.

name: camisim-output-parsing
description: Use when the input is a CAMISIM output directory of simulated longitudinal metagenomic reads and a downstream tool needs the community reads plus a genome_id-to-FASTA mapping table.

name: canonical-correlation-analysis
description: Use when two sets of standardized continuous variables describing the same sampling units (e.g., radar-derived vs. ALS-derived forest structural metrics per 1-ha plot) must be compared via multivariate correlation to find significant shared axes.

name: canonical-kmer-representation-xor-scrambling
description: Reference for implementing or reproducing Kraken-style minimizer indexing: when building a k-mer/LCA database that groups k-mers by 15-bp minimizers and needs a fast index-lookup-plus-binary-search query path.

name: capture-probe-set-comparative-evaluation
description: Use when multiple probe design strategies must be compared on identical target genomes (e.g., 56 RefSeq coronaviruses) and you need a quantitative efficiency metric — average distinct genomes hit per probe — to trade off probe count versus breadth.

name: capture-probe-set-statistics
description: Use when a HUBDesign-style probe design run has completed and you need to report compactness (probe count), percent of input nucleotides covered, capture depth, and efficiency as in Table 1 of the Cell Reports Methods paper.

name: cas-operon-annotation-verification
description: Use when assembled contigs from targeted (CasCollect) or complete assembly runs must be validated to confirm all known cas genes are recovered and cas operons/CRISPR arrays are correctly assembled and annotated.

name: cas-operon-targeted-assembly
description: Use when raw paired-end Illumina FASTQ reads (isolates or metagenomes) must be screened for CRISPR arrays and cas operons without performing a complete de novo genome assembly, e.g. for phage-susceptibility assessment.

name: case-control-mwas-covariate-correction
description: Use when QCed FASTQ-derived clade/gene abundance tables (QCed3_sample_list.txt) from shotgun metagenomic data must be tested for case-control association with hidden confounding correction.

name: casp-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when a contact prediction model must be benchmarked on standard CASP target domains, or when accuracy gains (e.g., from features, ensembling, or MSA depth) must be quantified at top L/5, L/2, and L on held-out CASP sets.

name: casp-target-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when a trained contact or secondary-structure predictor must be compared against existing methods on fixed CASP11/CASP12 domain sets, with precision at top L/10-L and accuracy tables reproduced.

name: catbat-bin-taxonomic-classification
description: Use when assigning taxonomy to MAG FASTA bins, especially bins that fail BUSCO-derived completeness/contamination quality thresholds and therefore cannot be processed with GTDB-Tk's marker-gene-based classification.

name: cbar-chromosomal-plasmid-classification
description: Use when benchmarking plasmid-identification tools: you have chromosome/plasmid validation fragments of known origin (e.g. RefSeq-derived) and need cBar's error rates and its agreement with PlasFlow predictions.

name: cbf-vs-fimpera-comparison-analysis
description: Use when comparing abundance accuracy of a counting Bloom filter queried directly versus via fimpera on identically sized cBF indexes, and you need overestimation rates and error-distance metrics.

name: ccmpred-precision-matrix-execution
description: Use when you need to benchmark contact-prediction runtime: you hold pre-computed MSAs for the 150 PSICOV proteins and must time CCMpred precision-matrix optimization against a DNN-based predictor on identical inputs.

name: cd-hit-nucleotide-sequence-clustering
description: Use when you have a large set of extracted marker-gene or coding nucleotide sequences (FASTA) from many genomes and need a non-redundant reference catalog that keeps strain-level resolution (high identity cutoff like 99%).

name: cd-hit-parameter-tuning
description: Use when building a non-redundant gene catalog from a large set of predicted coding sequences (FASTA) and a near-duplicate collapse at a defined nucleotide identity/coverage threshold is required.

name: cd-hit-similarity-threshold-parameterization
description: Use when building a nonredundant representative set from a curated functional-gene protein FASTA (e.g., amoA-AOB) and you need a data-driven similarity threshold rather than an arbitrary one.

name: cds-allele-calling-classification
description: Use when draft or complete genome FASTA assemblies must be assigned allele identifiers or classification tags (EXC, INF, ASM, ALM, NIPH, NIPHEM, PLOT, LNF) against a pre-defined cg/wgMLST schema to build strain allelic profiles.

name: cds-coordinate-parsing
description: Use when assembling a gene catalog from metagenomic contigs and/or isolate genomes and you need per-gene CDS coordinates, lengths, and source provenance after running a gene caller such as MetaGeneMark.

name: cds-deduplication-and-length-filtering
description: Use when constructing a wg/cgMLST schema from draft or complete genome assemblies and you need to clean Prodigal-predicted CDSs prior to all-against-all BLASTP clustering, or when adapting/validating external schemas that must contain only translating, non-redundant alleles.

name: cds-prediction-from-genome-assemblies
description: Use when the input is draft or complete genome assemblies (FASTA from de novo assemblers) and the goal is to define target loci for a novel wg/cgMLST schema from scratch, requiring CDS prediction rather than allele calling against an existing schema.

name: cds-protein-call-tiling-onto-nucleotide-scaffolds
description: Use when reconstructing virus-like genomes from metagenomic reads where translated (DIAMOND) and nucleotide (BBMap) alignments must be merged per genome into one super-scaffold with nucleotide precedence over protein calls.

name: cell-dimension-value-extraction
description: Use when processing natural-language prokaryotic taxonomic descriptions to populate a taxon-by-character matrix with cell dimension (diameter, width, length) measurement states and units.

name: censored-time-to-event-data-handling
description: Use when the outcome is right-censored time-to-event data (survival time plus event/censor indicator) and the goal is comparing treatment groups with or without covariate adjustment via a Cox model.

name: cgmlst-allele-calling
description: Use when you have draft/complete genome FASTA assemblies and a defined MLST schema (schema_seed) and need to determine allelic profiles, identify known/novel alleles, or scale calling to hundreds/thousands of assemblies.

name: cgmlst-core-locus-selection
description: Use when you have a chewBBACA allelic profile matrix (results_alleles.tsv) over draft or complete assemblies and must reduce the wgMLST schema to loci present in ≥95% (or 95-99%) of strains for core-genome typing.

name: cgmlst-schema-evaluation
description: Use when a chewBBACA schema (per-locus FASTA files with full allelic diversity) must be assessed locus-by-locus, e.g. to inspect allele variability before using the schema for cg/wgMLST strain identification.

name: cgmlst-schema-locus-matching
description: Use when calling alleles of query-genome CDSs against a pre-defined cg/wgMLST schema and interpreting classification tags (EXC, INF, ASM, ALM, NIPH, NIPHEM, PLOT, LNF) in the allelic profile.

name: checkm-completeness-contamination-estimation
description: Use when benchmarking metagenome assemblies of a target species and extracted scaffold sets (e.g. B. longum 51A scaffolds from MetaPlatanus vs metaFlye/OPERA-MS/MEGAHIT) need completeness and contamination estimates to confirm which assembler produced a single near-complete bin.

name: checkm-completeness-file-parsing
description: Use when running mOTUpan on MAGs/SAGs of varying quality and you have (or can produce) a CheckM output file to supply completeness and contamination priors per genome.

name: checkm2-completeness-contamination-parsing
description: Use when you have CheckM2 quality_report.tsv output for binned HiFi metagenome assemblies (e.g. Deadwood or Mock community bins) and need to reproduce Mapler's near complete / high / medium / low quality counts.

name: checkpoint-based-model-inference
description: Use when you need to classify 16S rRNA sequences into seven taxonomic ranks (Domain–Species) with an existing published DeepTaxa checkpoint, without retraining, e.g. on the 69,335-sequence Greengenes2 2024.09 test FASTA.

name: checkv-quality-class-interpretation
description: Use when a viral metagenomic contig library must be screened for viral sequences and CheckV quality-class output should be merged with VirSorter2, VIBRANT, DeepVirFinder, and MMseqs2 hits into a per-contig confidence label.

name: chewbbaca-extractcgmlst-execution
description: Use when you have a chewBBACA AlleleCall results_alleles.tsv matrix (optionally paralog-filtered) and need to select the core-genome loci at a chosen presence threshold to define a cgMLST schema.

name: chimera-detection-removal
description: Use when processing raw 16S rRNA amplicon reads (e.g., V4 regions from QIITA studies) into taxonomic annotations, and chimeric PCR artifacts must be filtered out before building the taxonomy table.

name: chimera-retention-quantification
description: Use when comparing OTU pipelines on datasets with known ground-truth chimera content (e.g., 454 error-model simulations with 20% chimeras) and you need to measure how many chimeric reads each pipeline retains after filtering and chimera detection.

name: chimera-sequence-filtering
description: Use when processing raw 16S/ITS amplicon reads (e.g. 454 or Illumina FASTQ) into OTU tables and the dataset may contain chimeric sequences — e.g. synthetic benchmark sets with 20% chimeras — so chimeras must be excluded before clustering.

name: chimeric-bin-taxonomic-discordance-filtering
description: Use when a MAG catalogue (e.g., 19,542 VMGC prokaryotic FASTA genomes) has per-genome CheckM2 Completeness/Contamination estimates and bins must be screened for taxonomic discordance (chimerism) prior to quality classification.

name: chromosomal-read-removal
description: Use when a hybrid bacterial plasmid assembly pipeline needs to exclude chromosomal reads from FASTQ inputs after a long-read-only assembly has been produced, to cut compute cost and avoid chromosomal contigs in plasmid output.

name: cigar-string-parsing
description: Use when scoring suffix-prefix overlaps between NGS reads aligned with Minimap2 all-vs-all mode, where overlap quality must be derived from the CIGAR string rather than re-assessed across the full overlap length.

name: circular-scaffold-detection
description: Use when preparing viral scaffold FASTAs (e.g., VIBRANT/VirSorter predictions) as input to vRhyme binning, to flag complete circular viral genomes before binning and dereplication.

name: clade-exclusion-database-masking
description: Use when evaluating a k-mer LCA classifier on reads from novel organisms: reads simulated with Mason (2% average mismatch) from RefSeq genomes whose clade of origin (species through phylum) is excluded from the classification database.

name: classical-vs-specialized-algorithm-comparison
description: Use when you need to quantify how much a new DNA sequence clustering method improves over classical (k-means++, GMM) and DNA-specialized (MeShClust v3.0, DeLUCS) baselines on labeled real sequence datasets.

name: classification-accuracy-comparison
description: Use when comparing two read-classification or aligner tools on the same read set and you must verify that a faster method (e.g. PML-based streaming) does not degrade classification accuracy relative to a batch baseline.

name: classification-accuracy-metrics-evaluation
description: Use when you have per-read classification labels (C/U/A/H plus TaxID and maxSim) from LiME or a comparable classifier on simulated metagenomes with known ground-truth taxonomic provenance, and you need SEN/PREC/F1/specificity at a fixed taxonomic rank (species).

name: classification-concordance-analysis
description: Use when raw mycobacterial sequencing reads must be classified as MTBC vs non-tuberculous mycobacteria and lineage-typed, and the accuracy of those calls (vs KvarQ or expected labels) must be quantified.

name: classification-error-discrimination-analysis
description: Decision support for choosing a minimum match length (or similar score cutoff) so that random short spurious matches are excluded while classification sensitivity is preserved.

name: classification-metric-aggregation
description: Use when comparing multiple classifiers (e.g., PM-CNN, RF) on multi-class microbiome datasets (3–5 status labels) and you need to verify a claim that one model has more balanced per-class performance via per-status F1 dispersion.

name: classification-metric-benchmarking-across-assemblers
description: Decision support for claims that a MAG taxonomy classifier is robust to upstream assembly choices; triggered when the same read set can be assembled with two or more meta-assemblers (e.g. metaSPAdes v3.15.2 vs MegaHIT v1.2.9) and classifier metrics must be compared.

name: classification-metric-computation
description: Use when comparing taxonomic classification tools on MAGs or genomes with a known ground-truth taxonomy (e.g., CAMI II expected taxonomies, real mock community composition), and you need per-rank accuracy metrics.

name: classification-metric-computation-precision-recall
description: Use when a new protein/sequence classifier must be benchmarked on a curated test set against baseline methods, and per-method and per-protein precision/recall/accuracy/FDR values are needed to demonstrate ity.

name: classification-metrics-computation
description: Reference for comparing a classifier's per-read calls (e.g., SPUMONI PML/MS reports) against an aligner's mappings (minimap2) using accuracy, precision, recall, F1, throughput, peak RSS, and index size.

name: classification-metrics-evaluation
description: Use when a taxonomic classifier (e.g., kMetaShot vs GTDBtk vs CAMITAX) has been run on genomes with known expected labels and you need rank-level (strain/species/genus) performance metrics.

name: classification-performance-metrics-computation
description: Use when evaluating a taxonomic classifier against ground-truth community composition (e.g. a mock community or simulated human gut dataset) and you need genus/species-level precision, recall, F-measure and runtime comparisons.

name: classification-rate-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing how many reads different metagenomic classifiers (e.g. Kaiju MEM/Greedy-5 vs Kraken k=31) assign on the same real FASTQ metagenomes, or when quantifying overlap and merged classification totals.

name: classification-runtime-measurement
description: Use when comparing the RAM and runtime footprint of metagenomic classifiers (LiME vs Magic-BLAST, TaxMaps, CLARK-S, Centrifuge, Kraken 2) on the same read sample, e.g. the simulated setA2 dataset.

name: classification-sensitivity-f1-evaluation
description: Use when a simulated metagenome benchmark (e.g. setA2, setB2 with known read provenance) has been classified by LiME and you must quantify classification accuracy via sensitivity, precision and F1, or reproduce reported values like SEN 95.55%/F1 97.66% on setA2.

name: classification-tree-path-scoring
description: Use when reconstructing or re-implementing Kraken's taxonomic label assignment for metagenomic DNA reads, or when scoring query sequences against a k-mer LCA database built with Jellyfish and the NCBI taxonomy tree.

name: classifier-accuracy-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating a plasmid/chromosome classifier's accuracy on known-label fragment data, or when deciding which probability threshold balances accuracy against the fraction of unclassified sequences.

name: classifier-accuracy-evaluation
description: Use when a trained genotype-to-phenotype classifier must be validated on independent test genomes, e.g. GIDEON II held-out species or Bergey's Manual bacteria, to compute accuracy and macroaccuracy.

name: classifier-comparison-maximum-selection
description: Use when a paper reports aggregate counts of samples/phenotypes exceeding a performance threshold across multiple classifiers, and a supplementary table gives per-classifier metrics per row that must be reconciled.

name: classifier-performance-comparison
description: Use when you have pooled cross-validation prediction tables from two competing phenotype classifiers and need per-taxon (e.g. NCBI phylum) accuracy comparison to quantify where a phylogeny-aware model outperforms phyletic-pattern-only prediction.

name: classifier-precision-recall-evaluation
description: Use when multiple taxonomic classification model architectures must be compared on short shotgun metagenomic reads to select the one with the read-level precision and recall before deploying it for profiling.

name: classifier-runtime-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing prediction quality and computational cost of a simplified classifier (e.g. SVM-only) against a feature-selection-then-classifier pipeline (e.g. CPAR2SVM) over repeated cross-validation runs.

name: classifier-sensitivity-precision-comparison
description: Use when comparing read classifiers on datasets of known composition (mock communities or simulated reads) where genus- or phylum-level sensitivity and precision must be quantified per tool.

name: classifier-speed-comparison-analysis
description: Use when you need to quantify and reproduce a classifier's wall-clock throughput (reads per minute) on specific metagenome read sets, comparing Kraken against Megablast (or MetaPhlAn) with a documented OS-cache priming protocol.

name: classifier-throughput-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing taxonomic classifiers on speed and memory: you have identical simulated FASTQ read sets (multiple read lengths, single/paired-end), 25 threads available, and need r.p.s. plus peak-RAM figures per tool/mode.

name: classifier-throughput-measurement
description: Use when reproducing or verifying reads-per-minute throughput claims for a metagenomic classifier, or when comparing classifier speed on HiSeq/MiSeq/simBA-5 read sets.

name: cli-hyperparameter-configuration
description: Use when invoking the idelucs CLI on a DNA FASTA dataset and you must choose valid hyperparameter values (k in [4,5,6], n_clusters 2-199, epochs 50-150, batch_sz a multiple of n_mimics).

name: closed-reference-otu-picking
description: Use when a 16S rRNA OTU table must be built against a fixed reference (Greengenes+IMG) so downstream PICRUSt metagenome prediction can map OTUs to reference genomes.

name: cloud-scale-metagenomic-pipeline-execution
description: Use when a reproduction target requires executing a multi-component metagenomic pipeline (VirMAP/MEGAHIT/BBMap/DIAMOND) over many SRA samples, with resource provisioning and cohort-level metric computation such as average reconstructed genome segments per sample.

name: clr-compositional-data-transformation
description: Use when OTU/feature count tables (e.g., otu.tab.txt from the MiSurv Data folder) must be compositionally normalized before linear-regression differential abundance or Cox proportional hazards models that relate taxon abundance to survival outcomes.

name: clr-compositional-taxa-transform
description: Use when raw genus/OTU count data (e.g. biom.Rdata or otu.tab.txt from the MiSurv Data folder) must be converted to compositional predictors before survival prediction modeling, such as feeding random survival forests in MiSurv Module 4.

name: cluster-assignment-table-formatting
description: Use when you have run Minimap2 overlap scoring plus StrainXpress single-linkage clustering on metagenomic short reads and need to write or validate a per-read cluster assignment TSV as the deliverable of the 'Clustering Reads' stage.

name: cluster-count-verification
description: Use when a claimed clustering outcome (e.g. Metaclust's 424 million clusters) must be independently reproduced or validated from a published FASTA and reported Linclust parameters.

name: cluster-count-verification-against-reported-results
description: Use when a published pipeline reports a specific number of sequence clusters at a stated identity threshold and you must independently reproduce and validate that cluster count from the same curated input set.

name: cluster-quality-metric-rank-correlation-analysis
description: Use when you have per-algorithm, per-dataset clustering results from DNA-sequence clustering tools (iDeLUCS, DeLUCS, MeShClust v3.0) plus ground-truth cluster_id assignments, and need to decide whether unsupervised intrinsic metrics reliably track label-based clustering accuracy.

name: cluster-representative-sequence-selection
description: Use when a reference gene set (FASTA protein sequences with matching nucleotides) must be reduced to non-redundant representative clusters before aligning to metagenomes or designing primers, and a similarity threshold must be chosen.

name: cluster-resource-allocation
description: Decision support for allocating cluster CPUs and per-task memory before running SAMSA2/DIAMOND annotation jobs, or when estimating annotation wall-clock time from input FASTQ size.

name: cluster-statistics-computation
description: Use when you have ≥2 clusterings of the same sequence set (e.g., Linclust at m=20 vs m=80 and a UCLUST reference at 50% identity) and need summary statistics to judge which clustering recovered more sensitivity and at what runtime cost.

name: cluster-timeout-handling-for-batch-jobs
description: Use when comparing computationally expensive R tools for longitudinal high-dimensional data on an HPC cluster and you need per-replicate runtime/memory statistics under a fixed timeout (e.g. 96 h).

name: clustering-accuracy-label-matching
description: Use when comparing cluster assignments from unsupervised methods (e.g., iDeLUCS, k-means++, GMM, DeLUCS, MeShClust v3.0) against ground-truth TSV labels, since predicted cluster IDs need optimal matching before accuracy can be aggregated.

name: clustering-benchmark-metric-computation
description: Use when comparing clustering algorithms on labeled FASTA datasets with TSV ground-truth files, to produce a per-method × per-dataset table of intrinsic and external clustering evaluation metrics.

name: clustering-ensemble-aggregation
description: Use when multiple trained networks have emitted cluster assignments for the same DNA sequence set (e.g. iDeLUCS mimic-based training with n_mimics augmentations) and a single final consensus cluster label per sequence is required.

name: clustering-method-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when two protein clustering methods (e.g. Snekmer AAR-kmer clustering vs MMseqs2 easy-cluster) have been run on the same protein FASTA set and you must benchmark them via V-scores and quantify overlap/union coverage of assigned proteins.

name: clustering-result-count-validation
description: Use when a spectral networking/clustering step has produced a spectrum-to-cluster assignment and you must verify the number of distinct clusters (e.g. 8,071 families from ~10M spectra) before downstream interpretation.

name: clustering-sensitivity-runtime-tradeoff-analysis
description: Use when clustering large protein sequence sets at ~50% sequence identity and Linclust's default m=20 k-mers per sequence yields more (smaller) clusters than a reference tool like UCLUST, prompting a test of whether --kmer-per-seq 80 closes the sensitivity gap at acceptable runtime.

name: clustering-tool-command-line-parameterization
description: Use when clustering a protein or nucleotide FASTA set to a target sequence identity (e.g. 50%, 70%, 90%) and the tool invocation parameters must be specified, tuned, and logged for reproducible runtime or cluster-quality comparisons.

name: clustering-vscore-annotation-evaluation
description: Use when comparing de novo protein clusterings against reference functional annotations (GO, Pfam, InterPro, TIGRFAMs, COG) using V-scores, or when selecting AAR/kmer parameterizations by clustering quality.

name: cmh-heterogeneity-testing
description: Use when the analysis goal is to assess adaptation (alpha) for a whole gene set — e.g. genes grouped by recombination rate bins or chromosome localization — rather than gene-by-gene, and to test heterogeneity of selection among those genes.

name: co-abundance-correlation-ranking
description: Use when estimating abundances of de novo MAG clusters from shotgun metagenomics and needing to pick cluster-specific signature genes from a non-redundant gene count matrix before read-based abundance computation.

name: co-abundance-genome-binning
description: Use when you have assembled metagenomic contigs plus short reads from multiple samples grouped by the user and need to bin contigs into MAGs exploiting sample-wise co-abundance, or to estimate per-sample MAG abundances.

name: co-assembly-sample-grouping
description: Use when multiple related metagenomic samples (e.g. a time series) should be assembled jointly per group rather than sample-wise, and assembly size, N50, or MAG counts are the target metrics.

name: co-occurrence-network-inference
description: Use when starting from a genus-level OTU/counts table (otu_table.tsv with obs_metadata.tsv) and the goal is to infer interaction networks and quantify how much inferred edges/nodes agree across different NI methods.

name: cobs-compact-index-querying
description: Use when you need to predict the isolate origins of novel insertion sequences (or other query sequences) by screening them against a large set of microbial genomes, and when you must attach ENA BioSample metadata and taxonomy to the hits.

name: cobs-hit-table-parsing
description: Use when you have COBS query results (per-IS genome hit lists) against the 661,405 microbial isolate genomes and need to quantify how widely each IS is shared across genera/species or identify ISfinder coverage gaps.

name: coefficient-of-determination-model-assessment
description: Use when a fitted model (e.g. radar fixed-effects NMDS1 models) must be validated on independent external plots, and predicted-vs-observed agreement needs to be quantified as R² per taxon.

name: cog-database-category-filtering
description: Use when preparing the -nv (nonviral) and -v (viral) protein FASTA inputs for virMine 2.0, or when a bacterial-only protein reference with viral-origin sequences excluded is needed.

name: cog-feature-matrix-handling
description: Use when training or validating SVM phenotype predictors from comparative-genomics data: inputs are complete/partial bacterial genomes or COG presence/absence tables plus trait labels, and features must be assembled and completeness-screened.

name: cog-feature-sign-interpretation
description: Use when a trained PICA/libSVM linear-kernel phenotype model must be explained by ranking its COG features by signed weight, e.g. to test whether gene absence dominates a genome-reduction trait.

name: cog-profile-feature-filtering
description: Use when applying a trained phenotype model (e.g. obligate intracellular prediction) to new species whose genomes are summarized as COG presence/absence profiles, and the model expects only its specific universal marker COG features (e.g. the 39/40 marker COGs) rather than the full eggNOG 4.

name: cog-profile-perturbation
description: Use when assessing the robustness of COG/SVM-based phenotypic trait predictors to genome incompleteness, e.g. before applying trait models to incomplete metagenomic bins.

name: cohort-stratified-sample-subsetting
description: Use when you have sample-level metadata (continent, country, sample source, disease status) plus paired fungal and bacterial taxonomic profiles and need to isolate a specific cohort before per-cohort modeling or network analysis.

name: colinear-seed-chaining
description: Use when raw nanopore signal seed matches (hash-table lookup hits) must be converted into a single mapping position for a read, i.e., when reconstructing the RawHash mapping step over seed matches from a hash index like ref.ind.

name: colorectal-cancer-metagenome-phenotype-comparison
description: Use when comparing metagenomic sample groups (e.g., healthy vs adenoma vs carcinoma) to identify taxa, genes, KOs, EC numbers, or reactions that differ significantly across phenotypes in a mapping-based analysis.

name: colored-de-bruijn-graph-construction
description: Use when building a compact pangenome/colored de Bruijn graph from a panel of highly similar FASTA sequences (e.g., the 12 human mitogenomes, or 5k/20k simulated panels) as the input substrate for cSupB decomposition and variant detection.

name: colored-superbubble-decomposition
description: Use when a colored de Bruijn graph built from highly similar sequences (e.g., mitochondrial pangenomes) must be decomposed into nested, population-specific superbubble structures to enable coordinate assignment or variant detection.

name: colored-superbubble-matching
description: Use when a VARI-merge constructed colored de Bruijn graph (.dbg + .colors.sd_vector) must be decomposed into sample-specific colored superbubbles and organized into a tree to support a tri-tuple coordinate system or nested variant detection.

name: combinatorial-scenario-enumeration
description: Use when a two-group microbiome abundance table must be tested for association robustness across progressively mixed label permutations rather than a single global permutation test.

name: command-line-bioinformatics-pipeline-execution
description: Use when a workflow step requires running a repository-hosted command-line tool (e.g. PICRUSt2/MinPath) on a KO abundance table to produce a pathway abundance table.

name: command-line-flag-configuration
description: Use when running CasCollect on raw Illumina FASTQ reads and you must decide which flags to enable (e.g. --trim, --clean, --noprot, --nucl, --seed -define) and set parameters like -match and -cycle for a targeted CRISPR/Cas or custom gene-set run.

name: command-line-pipeline-execution
description: Use when a large FASTA protein set (thousands to >190,000 (meta)genomic records) must be screened from the command line against an HMM library, with configurable output separator, prefixes, threads, and sequence extraction.

name: command-line-pipeline-execution
description: Use when raw metatranscriptome FASTQ files must be processed through preprocessing, annotation, and aggregation on a cluster with local databases, or when benchmarking DIAMOND resource allocation (RAM sweep at fixed CPUs).

name: command-line-pipeline-execution
description: Use when you need to phenotype bacterial genome assemblies (nucleotide or protein FASTA) from the command line with Traitar, e.g. to reproduce present/absent calls for metagenome-recovered population genomes like unClos_1 and unFirm_1.

name: command-line-pipeline-execution
description: Use when a task requires running the STEMSim simulator end-to-end from the command line, or reproducing its reported throughput benchmark (~1 million reads in ~3 minutes on a 2.40 GHz server CPU).

name: command-line-r-script-development
description: Use when building reproducible R analysis scripts that consume ranked abundance summary tables and must emit statistical result tables (p-value, log2FoldChange) plus graphical outputs, invoked via Rscript from a shell.

name: comparative-assembly-table-compilation
description: Use when several de novo assemblers (e.g. PEHaplo, SPAdes, SAVAGE, SGA) have been run on the same input reads and their contigs must be benchmarked against known reference haplotypes with MetaQUAST.

name: comparative-genomics-cog-profile-classification
description: Use when predicting biological phenotypes or ecological roles of uncharacterized microbial genomes or metagenomic bins from COG presence/absence profiles, or when benchmarking SVM-only vs CPAR2SVM phenotype classifiers.

name: comparative-rna-structural-alignment
description: Use when placing 16S/SSU rRNA sequences (e.g. assembled metagenome contigs or SILVA records) into a reference structural alignment, detecting insertions as alignment gaps, or preparing intron-stripped rRNA sequences for phylogeny.

name: comparator-tool-performance-evaluation
description: Use when a new host-depletion or filtering tool must be validated against an existing comparator on identical inputs, and retention/precision metrics such as microbial reads retained must be quantified and compared.

name: completeness-estimation-from-mags
description: Use when computing core genomes from MAGs/SAGs of diverse completeness: completeness priors must be supplied so the Bayesian estimator can weigh presence/absence patterns per genome.

name: completeness-prior-iterative-refinement
description: Use when estimating core genomes from genome sets of mixed or low quality (e.g. CheckM-estimated MAG completeness along a completeness scale) and you need the completeness prior refined from the data rather than fixed.

name: composite-likelihood-ratio-sweep-detection
description: Use when phased, filtered biallelic SNP VCFs split by chromosome are available and you need single-population selective-sweep scans that complement haplotype-based iHS/XP-EHH analyses.

name: compositional-correlation-network-construction
description: Use when you have a genus-level OTU/counts table and need to compare networks inferred by multiple compositional-aware inference methods, e.g. to quantify shared vs. unique nodes and edges (UpSet overlap) across methods.

name: compositional-count-data-tool-comparison
description: Use when selecting or validating a longitudinal differential-abundance method for high-dimensional microbiome count data with multiple covariates, and you need empirical runtime/memory/accuracy comparisons against ANCOM, lgpr, ZIBR or MaAsLin2.

name: compositional-data-correlation-estimation
description: Use when you have two compositional taxonomic abundance tables (e.g. fungal profiles from FunOMIC-T and bacterial profiles from MetaPhlAn) over matched samples and need statistically filtered cross-kingdom correlation edges.

name: compositional-data-css-normalization
description: Use when metagenomic count data (taxa or gene-level abundance tables from case-control studies) is sparse and compositional, and differential abundance markers must be comparable or reproducible across independent datasets.

name: compositional-data-normalization
description: Use when KO-level read-count or relative-abundance tables from shotgun metagenomic annotation must be converted to compositionally meaningful per-genome copy numbers before downstream functional comparisons.

name: compositional-microbiome-data-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking a variable-selection or mediation-selection method for compositional count data and you need simulated data with known truth (e.g., which taxa, covariates, or balances are truly active) to score sensitivity/specificity of the selection.

name: compositional-microbiome-regression
description: Use when regressing genus-level OTU/taxon counts (compositional data with or without a known phylogenetic tree) on covariates such as FFQ dietary variables, and you need Bayesian sparse variable selection with FDR control at the branch level.

name: compositional-tss-normalization-fpr-benchmarking
description: Use when benchmarking normalization/model choices on longitudinal microbiome count data with simulated or real depth bias, specifically to measure false positive rates on truly-null (zero effect size) features under rarefaction vs TSS normalization.

name: computation-benchmark-timing
description: Use when you need to empirically quantify how an amino acid recoding alphabet changes the compute cost of kmer vectorization, e.g. verifying the near-4x speedup of MIQS-recoded 4-mers over unencoded 4-mers on nitrogen cycling protein FASTA inputs.

name: computational-cost-metrics-aggregation
description: Use when per-assembler computational cost (runtime, CPU/hour, max memory, data read/written) must be extracted from deposited LMAS run outputs and compared for consistency across repeated runs on the same sample.

name: computational-performance-benchmarking
description: Use when you need to verify claims that a sequence-analysis tool runs efficiently on commodity hardware, i.e. quantify wall-clock seconds and peak RAM per input record.

name: computational-performance-comparison
description: Use when comparing memory footprint and throughput of hash-based raw signal mappers on large genomes (e.g., human NA12878/D5), or when validating claimed speedups such as RawHash2 minimizer seeding (~3X).

name: computational-resource-profiling
description: Use when comparing the CPU time, runtime, and peak memory of genome taxonomy classifiers on the same MAG sets, or when planning hardware needs such as the ~22Gb HDF5 kMetaShot reference load.

name: computational-resource-profiling
description: Use when you need to quantify throughput (Gbp/h) and per-rule wall-clock time, peak memory, or CPU-hours of a Snakemake metagenomic workflow to judge its cost/energy feasibility.

name: confidence-interval-coverage-comparison
description: Use when you have progressive-permutation outputs from binary-outcome microbiome data and need to decide which top hits are real discoveries by comparing observed p-values against the fully permuted data's 95% quantile intervals.

name: confidence-interval-reporting-for-hic-contact-ratios
description: Use when Hi-C library quality must be reported with uncertainty — e.g. inter-contig 3D ratios from qc3C k-mer mode across multiple metagenomic Hi-C datasets that must be reconciled against published values.

name: confusion-matrix-metric-computation
description: Use when evaluating genome-based resistance predictions (e.g. Mykrobe JSON calls) against phenotypic DST labels by building per-drug confusion matrices and computing overall and per-drug sensitivity/specificity on a validation set.

name: confusion-matrix-metric-computation
description: Use when benchmarking a protein-type prediction method (e.g. DiSCo Dsr-dependent dissimilatory sulphur metabolism assignments) against baseline assignments on genomes with curated reference labels, to quantify precision, recall, accuracy, balanced accuracy and FDR.

name: conjugate-gradient-optimization
description: Use when estimating latent relative abundances from longitudinal microbiome count data (OTU tables such as cdiff-counts.csv) via LUMINATE's coordinate ascent VI, specifically when solving the inner optimization for noisy realizations z_1:T.

name: connected-component-graph-analysis
description: Use when a pairwise protein-protein correlation/distance matrix (e.g., Snekmer cluster mode with save_matrix) must be binarized at a threshold like 0.5 and decomposed into connected components to verify family-level subnetwork separation.

name: consensus-network-construction
description: Use when you have association/interaction matrices (plus pvalue matrices) from multiple network inference methods on the same taxa and need to merge them into a single robust consensus network.

name: contact-restraint-selection-top-2l
description: Use when you have ranked residue-pair contact predictions and secondary-structure predictions for a protein domain and need distance restraints for ab initio 3D model reconstruction and TMscore-based quality evaluation.

name: containerized-bioinformatics-deployment
description: Use when a population genomic analysis on biallelic SNP data (VCF or PLINK binary) must be run reproducibly on a local Linux machine or HPC cluster without manually installing each analysis tool or lacking HPC admin privileges.

name: containerized-bioinformatics-execution
description: Use when the goal is to execute the CAMAMED pipeline (taxonomic/functional profiling of metagenomic FASTQ data) without manually installing its dependencies — i.e., when Docker is available and the camamed Docker images can be pulled from hub.docker.com.

name: containerized-bioinformatics-pipeline
description: Use when benchmarking multiple de novo metagenomic assemblers on a defined mock community (e.g. BMock12 SRX4901583) and reproducibility across platforms via containerization is required.

name: contamination-detection-and-abundance-estimation
description: Use when raw nanopore signal reads (FAST5/POD5/SLOW5/BLOW5) from a sample with possible mixed organisms must be assigned to source genomes and per-organism relative abundances or contamination levels must be quantified from the mapped reads.

name: contig-accuracy-blast-verification
description: Use when you have assembled or contig-extension output (e.g. ContigExtender output/contigs.fasta from viral metagenomics seed contigs) and need to verify each contig matches its reference genome before comparing tools or reporting lengths.

name: contig-alignment-identity-metric-implementation
description: Use when you have contig-to-reference alignment results (identity per aligned contig ≥1000 bp mapping to known reference replicons) and need per-contig Phred-like assembly quality scores for assembler benchmarking.

name: contig-circularity-annotation
description: Use when assembled plasmid contigs (e.g. Unicycler FASTA output from Plassembler) need per-contig circularity and known-plasmid similarity annotation against PLSDB, summarized into a plasmid_summary.tsv table.

name: contig-length-classification
description: Use when a long-read-only assembly (e.g. Flye nanopore assembly of a bacterial isolate) must be split into chromosome and putative-plasmid contigs before chromosomal read removal or plasmid read extraction.

name: contig-length-filtering
description: Use when assembler output contigs must be length-filtered before computing reference-based assembly quality metrics, or when comparing assemblers fairly after removing very short contigs.

name: contig-length-filtering
description: Use when preparing metagenomic or isolate assembly contigs/scaffolds (e.g. SPAdes output) as input for PlasFlow or other kmer-signature classifiers that perform poorly on short sequences.

name: contig-length-filtering
description: Use when per-sample contigs assembled by metaSPAdes ('--meta' mode) must be merged and length-filtered prior to CheckV assessment and ANI-based dereplication into the nrclib in ViroProfiler.

name: contig-n50-benchmark-computation
description: Use when comparing two or more assembly runs (e.g. sparse_pregraph vs pregraph builds) and you need a single continuity metric such as contig N50 to quantify how a graph-construction choice affects assembly length.

name: contig-scaffold-path-tracing-with-median-gap-estimation
description: Use when a strain-oblivious long-read metagenome assembly (FASTA) and a coordinate-sorted long-read alignment (BAM) exist and strain-separated contigs must be joined into longer, more complete strain scaffolds.

name: contig-statistics-calculation
description: Use when you have assembled contigs (e.g., a FASTA like contigs.fa from IDBA-UD) and must report assembly quality metrics such as contig count, total length, and N50.

name: contig-tip-truncation-detection
description: Use when calling alleles on draft (multi-contig) assemblies with chewBBACA AlleleCall and you must distinguish genuine size-divergent alleles (ASM/ALM) from apparently truncated matches caused by contig boundaries (PLOT) before building the allelic profile matrix.

name: contig-viral-origin-scoring
description: Use when you have assembled contigs (or virMine assembly output) and need to classify which contigs are likely viral using gene-content origin scoring rather than homology alone.

name: contingency-matrix-construction
description: Use when benchmarking a protein-type predictor (e.g. DiSCo HMM hits) against comparator similarity-search methods on a curated test set and you need TP/FP/TN/FN matrices and derived PR/RC/AC/BA/FDR metrics.

name: continuous-outcome-progressive-permutation
description: Use when the grouping/clinical variable is continuous (not binary) and you want to gauge the overall strength of the microbiome-outcome association and rank feature robustness via a progressive-permutation U-curve.

name: continuous-time-covariate-modeling
description: Use when you have a longitudinal master table (metadata + feature table) with a continuous time variable such as 'Day' and count or continuous feature data, and need to detect features changing significantly over time while disentangling covariate effects.

name: continuous-time-treatment-effect-detection
description: Use when the input is a longitudinal master table (count data) with a continuous time variable (e.g. Day) and the goal is to identify features whose abundance changes significantly over time while detecting covariate effects.

name: contrastive-consistency-training-of-clustering-networks
description: Use when clustering unlabeled DNA sequences alignment-free with a deep learning model, needing mimic-based augmentation pairs and a contrastive consistency term to reduce variance before a clustering ensemble aggregates assignments.

name: contrastive-deep-learning-clustering
description: Use when the goal is unsupervised clustering of unlabeled DNA sequences in a single FASTA file without alignment or taxonomic identifiers, especially for large, diverse, or unbalanced datasets (e.g. simulated metagenomic reads).

name: control-library-benchmarking
description: Use when quantifying how many more assembled sequences an error-correcting paired-end assembler recovers than a strict perfect-match baseline on a control library with known composition.

name: convex-combination-mixing-proportion-estimation
description: Use when a sink microbial community must be decomposed into contributions from many candidate source environments (hundreds), and sparsity is needed to identify the truly contributing sources while discounting noncontributing ones.

name: convex-hull-distance-clustering
description: Use when contigs are represented by high-dimensional feature vectors (concatenated oligonucleotide composition, e.g. k=5,6 k-mer frequencies, plus coverage) and you need clustering where Euclidean/Manhattan distances become unreliable.

name: cooccurrence-association-matrix-aggregation
description: Use when several network inference tools (e.g., sparcc, spieceasi, flashweave, harmonies, spring, mldm, propr) have each produced interaction and pvalue matrices and one robust consensus network is needed.

name: coordinated-noun-phrase-expansion
description: Use when extracting character values from taxonomic description sentences where coordinated noun phrases (e.g. conjoined descriptors) may contain terms absent from the curated per-character Term Lists.

name: cophenetic-distance-computation-ape
description: Use when you have a phylogenetic tree in NEWICK format (from FastTree/Mafft or user-supplied) covering all OTUs/species of a microbial feature table and need a pairwise phylogenetic distance matrix before correlation transformation and hierarchical clustering.

name: core-gene-recovery-analysis
description: Use when you need to quantify how genome incompleteness (e.g. CheckM completeness of MAGs) influences mOTUpan core-genome predictions, including false-positive and recall behaviour under bootstrap estimation.

name: core-genome-estimation-across-completeness-gradient
description: Use when comparing core-genome estimates from Roary, PPanGGOLiN, and mOTUpan over genome sets of varying (e.g. CheckM-estimated) completeness to locate where the tools' relative ordering reverses.

name: core-genome-partition-inference
description: Use when you need a core-genome partitioning for a set of genomes or MAGs/SAGs of varying and possibly low completeness, and you can supply proteomes (.faa) plus a completeness prior such as CheckM output.

name: core-size-trend-comparison-across-tools
description: Use when benchmarking core-genome estimation tools on genome sets of varying (especially low) completeness, to characterize how each tool's core estimate degrades along a completeness scale.

name: coronavirus-genome-taxon-reconciliation
description: Use when a deposited HUBDesign probe set (e.g., probes/Coronavirus FASTA plus a GenomeInfo.tab of taxon IDs) must be reconciled against its source genomes to check per-taxon probe counts and single- vs multi-virus specificity fractions.

name: correction-fraction-tabulation
description: Use when auditing PANDAseq output from an Illumina paired-end run: you have per-correction records with overlapping conflicting bases and their PHRED quality strings, and you want to quantify what fraction of corrections involved quality-masked (end-of-read, lowest-score) bases in zero, one, or.

name: correlation-distance-hierarchical-clustering
description: Use when you have labeled or unlabeled protein FASTA families and want to test whether AAR-kmer similarity recovers known family structure (e.g., nitrogen cycling families) without training supervised models.

name: correlation-distance-network-construction
description: Use when Snekmer cluster mode (unsupervised AAR-kmer clustering) has produced a saved pairwise protein-protein correlation/distance matrix and you need to verify, at a chosen correlation threshold, that known protein families form unconnected subnetworks.

name: correlation-matrix-trimming-and-rendering
description: Use when you have a rho-value correlation table (taxa × SNP) produced by mbQTL and need to trim/visualize it as a heatmap to spot LD-linked SNV clusters.

name: correlation-significance-threshold-filtering
description: Use when you have a dense pairwise correlation matrix (e.g. SparCC output over fungal and bacterial taxa) and must retain only significant edges — here p < 0.001 and |rho| > 0.05 — to build a sparse inter-kingdom network.

name: cosine-distance-similarity-computation
description: Use when viral scaffold FASTA sequences must be compared pairwise by nucleotide composition (tetranucleotide frequencies, codon usage, GC content, CpG, GC skew) to build distance features for vMAG binning.

name: cosine-similarity-kmer-abundance-scoring
description: Use when you need all-vs-all distance matrices between FASTA/FASTQ metagenomic samples that retain both genetic-distance and abundance signal, e.g. for clustering 16S rRNA or WGS datasets at high resolution.

name: cosine-similarity-metagenome-distance-computation
description: Use when an all-vs-all distance matrix must be computed across many metagenome samples from full k-mer abundance vectors (no sketching or presence/absence reduction), and scale demands a single-pass, MapReduce-based sweep over an inverted k-mer index.

name: count-data-normalization-and-multiple-testing-correction
description: Use when you have raw MG-RAST or DIAMOND-derived abundance summary counts (organism or functional category files) from ≥2 sample groups and need normalized differential transcript-activity calls with corrected p-values.

name: count-data-normalization-and-rarefaction
description: Use when running longitudinal differential-abundance benchmarks on genus-level stool count (amplicon/metagenomic abundance) tables where the comparison across tools must be controlled by applying each normalization/rarefaction method consistently to every tool's input.

name: count-data-randomized-control-testing
description: Use when running longdat_cont() or longdat_disc() with data_type = "count" on longitudinal abundance tables (e.g. species counts from a fasting MetS cohort) and reproducible, per-feature control testing is needed.

name: counting-bloom-filter-abundance-querying
description: Use when you need per-k-mer abundance queries from large read sets (e.g. metagenomic fastq) against a counting Bloom filter index, and want reduced false positives via the s-mer amplification parameter z.

name: counting-bloom-filter-construction
description: Use when building a counting Approximate Membership Query (cAMQ) index from k-mer abundance files (e.g. KMC output) where k-mers must be indexed as s-mers with counts, typically with k=31 or 35, b=5, and z=3.

name: counting-bloom-filter-false-positive-analysis
description: Use when comparing an AMQ-with-counts index (fimpera) against a raw counting Bloom filter on abundance query accuracy, or when sizing a filter to hit a target overestimation score within a space budget.

name: covariance-model-alignment-gap-analysis
description: Use when screening assembled or database 16S rRNA gene sequences (e.g. SILVA 115 records or metagenome assemblies) for large insertion sequences, introns, or insertion-encoded ORFs whose boundaries must be located relative to a structural rRNA alignment.

name: covariate-adjusted-linear-regression
description: Use when comparing treatment groups on a continuous microbiome outcome (alpha-diversity index or CLR-transformed abundance) while adjusting for covariates such as Sex, as in MiSurv Module 2.

name: covariate-adjusted-longitudinal-modeling
description: Use when the input is a longitudinal master table (features x samples over repeated time points, e.g. genus-level fasting stool data with a Day or Time_point variable) and time effects must be separated from covariate effects in count, proportion, binary, ordinal or continuous data.

name: covariate-adjusted-mirkat-s-analysis
description: Use when you have an OTU/feature table with matched survival times, censoring/event status, and covariates, and need a kernel-based beta-diversity-vs-survival association test (MiRKAT-S), optionally within a treatment-group subgroup.

name: covariate-adjusted-regression-modeling
description: Use when testing host genetic variants (SNVs/SNPs) for association with microbial taxon abundances across a sample cohort and covariates (e.g., covariates.txt/CovFile) must be adjusted for in the regression model.

name: covariate-confounding-benchmark-design
description: Use when benchmarking longitudinal microbiome differential-abundance tools under covariate-time confounding, or when deciding whether a tool's FDR/TPR is robust to increasing numbers of dummy covariates.

name: covariate-effect-success-rate-evaluation
description: Use when comparing longitudinal differential-abundance tools (e.g. LongDat vs MaAsLin2) on simulated multi-covariate data and you need to quantify whether covariate control keeps FDR stable and covariate-effect success rate near 0.95.

name: covariate-reducibility-classification
description: Use when analyzing longitudinal high-dimensional data (e.g. gut microbial abundance over Day or Time_point) where a significant time effect on a feature must be checked against potentially confounding covariates before being declared a treatment effect.

name: covariate-taxon-association-extraction-from-mppi
description: Use when you have MCMC posterior samples from a Dirichlet-multinomial (DM) regression fit in MicroBVS and need to declare which covariate-taxon associations are selected, e.g. against a simulated ground truth.

name: coverage-and-error-rate-parameterization
description: Use when benchmarking a contig extension or assembly tool on known viral reference genomes (e.g. BASV, BKV, HIV-1) and you need controlled variation in read length, sequencing error rate, coverage depth, and coverage unevenness.

name: coverage-cohen-d-effect-size-computation
description: Use when binning viral scaffolds with vRhyme and read coverage abundance must be converted into pairwise scaffold effect-size distances (vRhyme_machine_distances.tsv) from FASTQ reads or a pre-computed coverage table.

name: coverage-dependent-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when validating an HGT/structural-variant detection method on WGSIM-simulated metagenomic reads where Reconstruction Accuracy must be compared against a baseline tool across coverage levels to confirm a coverage-dependent performance trend.

name: coverage-effect-size-edge-weighting
description: Use when binning predicted viral scaffolds from metagenomes into vMAGs and classified scaffold pairs plus coverage effect-size values (vRhyme_machine_distances.tsv) must be converted into refined, redundancy-scored genome bins.

name: coverage-metrics-tabulation-across-assemblers
description: Use when comparing strain-level genome coverage recovered by a strain-resolved assembly against a strain-oblivious assembly, to compute missing percentages and additional genomic material per reference strain.

name: coverage-progression-benchmark-analysis
description: Use when quantifying whether iterative seed-expansion cycles (CasCollect -cycle 0..N) progressively close coverage gaps on a reference contig, and when a full-dataset baseline coverage comparison is needed.

name: coverage-sensitivity-benchmarking
description: Use when a genome in a simulated or real metagenomic community is assembled at extreme coverage (e.g. >1000x) and shows a high number of misassembled blocks, and you need to test whether coverage rather than assembler or sequence properties caused the errors.

name: coverage-series-benchmarking-and-tabulation
description: Use when you have a series of metagenome datasets that differ only in the sequencing coverage of known spike-in strains (e.g. Salmonella at 5x-40x) and need to quantify how coverage affects strain-aware assembly accuracy against a known ground truth.

name: coverage-variance-effect-size-comparison
description: Use when binning predicted viral scaffolds into vMAGs from multi-sample metagenomes where scaffolds share similar sequence features but differ in read-coverage abundance across samples, and sorted BAM mappings are available.

name: cox-proportional-hazards-survival-analysis
description: Use when input is a phyloseq object (biom.Rdata) or its four component files with survival time, censoring indicator, treatment, and covariate columns, and the goal is a covariate-adjusted Cox model of treatment or CLR-transformed microbial abundance on survival.

name: cplex-optimization-solving
description: Use when inferring strain-type mixtures or allele compositions from MLST allele distributions requires solving an NP-hard optimization (ADP or SDP) with mixed integer linear programming, and when solver gap/time limits must be configured to balance accuracy against runtime.

name: cpr-lineage-16s-divergence-interpretation
description: Use when a metagenomic or 16S amplicon study asks which bacterial lineages would be missed by common 16S primers (e.g. 515F/806R), especially for divergent CPR phyla like Microgenomates, Saccharibacteria, WWE3, or WS6.

name: cpr-monophyly-tree-validation
description: Use when bacterial 16S rRNA gene sequences contain large insertions (≥10 bp) that would corrupt multiple sequence alignment, and the goal is a defensible phylogeny to test whether CPR lineages form a monophyletic group.

name: cpu-parallelization-runtime-benchmarking
description: Use when you need to quantify parallel-scaling behaviour of a CPU-parallelized bioinformatics tool (e.g. chewBBACA AlleleCall) by wall-clock timing the same workload across several --cpu values and identifying an I/O bottleneck.

name: crispr-array-annotation
description: Use when assembled contigs (e.g. SPAdes output from seed-expanded read subsets) must be annotated to locate CRISPR arrays and cas genes, or when validating that a CRISPR/Cas detection pipeline identified cas operons.

name: crispr-cas-targeted-read-capture
description: Use when raw unassembled FASTQ reads must be recruited around known seed reads (HMM-derived or user-provided FASTA seeds) to capture a complete CRISPR/Cas operon for targeted assembly without assembling the full dataset.

name: crispr-repeat-nucleotide-identity-matching
description: Use when raw unassembled FASTQ reads must be searched for CRISPR array repeat sequences by nucleotide identity to seed targeted assembly, especially where repeat-only arrays without cas genes would be missed by protein HMM screening.

name: crispr-spacer-prediction-from-viral-contigs
description: Use when a metagenomic Hi-C pipeline (e.g. ViralCC + HiCBin) has produced draft viral bins and host MAGs, and you need sequence-level CRISPR spacer evidence to validate the inferred virus-host pairs or build an infection-spectrum summary like Fig. 6b.

name: cross-analysis-color-consistency-assignment
description: Use when rendering multiple interactive plots from different sub-workflow outputs (PCA, ADMIXTURE Q-matrices, IBS/FST trees, TreeMix) of the same sample set and the population-to-color mapping must be identical across all figures.

name: cross-assembler-assembly-comparison
description: Use when evaluating a new or candidate metagenomic assembler and you need reproducible genome fraction and misassembly comparisons against established assemblers on the same simulated or mock community reads.

name: cross-assembler-n50-metrics-comparison
description: Use when a task requires comparing de novo assembler performance on identical short-read input using continuity (N50) and accuracy (structural/substitution/copy number error) metrics against published baseline numbers.

name: cross-assembler-performance-tabulation
description: Use when comparing de novo metagenome assemblers on the same read sets and you need a consolidated table of Quast metrics (genome fraction, N50, identity) per assembler-dataset combination.

name: cross-assembly-completeness-comparison
description: Use when two assembly versions of the same genome exist and you need a head-to-head completeness metric against a curated reference sequence set, such as segmental duplications, to quantify assembly improvement.

name: cross-assembly-diploid-overlap-analysis
description: Use when multiple Supernova2 assemblies exist for the same sample and you need per-assembly diploid/hemizygous/uncovered fractions plus cross-assembly diploid overlap percentages.

name: cross-caller-variant-performance-comparison
description: Use when comparing two or more 16S rRNA gene variant callers on the same data set and you need to show their variant tables give near-equivalent supervised classification/association performance against metadata variables.

name: cross-catalogue-gene-overlap-analysis
description: Use when a newly built gene catalogue must be benchmarked against a published catalogue by reciprocal gene-level similarity search, to report directional coverage percentages and catalogue expansion.

name: cross-classifier-benchmark-table-construction
description: Use when multiple metagenomic classifiers have been run on admixture/quantification samples containing cross-reacting species pairs, and you need to extract per-tool false-positive percentages and compute relative FP-reduction factors.

name: cross-database-taxonomic-similarity-analysis
description: Use when the same OTU representative sequences have been taxonomically assigned with multiple reference databases and you need to quantify assignment concordance per taxonomic level (Phylum through Species).

name: cross-database-virome-overlap-analysis
description: Use when a newly assembled viral genome catalogue (e.g. 14,224 quality-filtered genomes >=50% CheckV completeness) must be dereplicated into vOTUs and its novelty estimated against existing virome reference databases.

name: cross-dataset-biomarker-reproducibility-assessment
description: Use when a biomarker-discovery pipeline (e.g. CAMAMED with cumulative sum-scaling and metagenomeSeq) has produced case-control marker taxa/genes from one metagenome dataset and an independent dataset from the same study context is available to test whether the markers reproduce.

name: cross-deposit-output-comparison
description: Use when a pipeline's paper or documentation points to a deposited output archive (e.g., figshare doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.20424705) and you need to verify that your rerun reproduces the reference report structure and figures.

name: cross-environment-profiler-comparison-analysis
description: Decision support for choosing a taxonomic profiling tool and reference database when in silico ground-truth data (e.g. CAMI) are available and per-tool performance must be compared across multiple environments or sampling groups.

name: cross-habitat-microbiome-validation-comparison
description: Use when you have closed-reference 16S OTU tables from multiple habitat types (e.g. mammal gut, soil, hypersaline mat) plus matched shotgun metagenomes, and need to test whether prediction accuracy decays with phylogenetic distance to reference genomes.

name: cross-method-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when a sink community's origins must be quantified and validated by benchmarking a new source tracking method (STENSL) against a baseline (SourceTracker2) on the exact same candidate source set, e.g., 88 HMP individuals across 15 body sites.

name: cross-method-benchmark-recomputation
description: Use when a binning/clustering tool must be benchmarked against published baselines on mock data with known per-contig genome labels, requiring recomputation of metrics (F-score, ARI, NMI, homogeneity) and vMAG quality counts.

name: cross-method-clustering-comparison
description: Use when evaluating a new unsupervised DNA sequence clustering tool and you need a fair, like-for-like accuracy comparison against specialized (DeLUCS, MeShClust v3.0) and classical (k-means++) baselines on unbalanced multi-genome datasets.

name: cross-method-diagnostic-comparison
description: Use when two genotype-based antibiotic-resistance prediction tools must be compared on the same isolates and phenotypic DST labels, e.g. per-drug sensitivity of Mykrobe vs. KvarQ on first-line TB drugs.

name: cross-method-network-comparison
description: Use when several co-occurrence networks (e.g., SparCC, propr, SpiecEasi, FlashWeave, COZINE, HARMONIES, SPRING, mLDM) have been inferred from the same abundance table and you need to quantify shared vs. unique nodes/edges to reveal method-driven rewiring.

name: cross-model-capability-comparison
description: Use when you have reconstructed GSMMs from MAGs and matched complete genomes and need to quantify whether annotation expansion (e.g. KEMET-recovered KOs) closes the metabolic-capability gap between draft and reference models.

name: cross-pipeline-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when two or more 16S OTU-calling pipelines must be compared on the same mock community FASTQ data, and you need to report OTU counts, total counts, and runtime rankings per dataset.

name: cross-pipeline-top-otu-extraction
description: Use when a synthetic amplicon dataset with known composition is available and multiple pipelines' OTU tables must be ranked by accuracy of top-OTU relative abundance estimates.

name: cross-platform-resistance-call-concordance-analysis
description: Use when the same clinical isolate has raw reads from both a high-error single-molecule platform (e.g. MinION) and a short-read platform (e.g. MiSeq) and you need to verify that genotypic resistance predictions agree across platforms.

name: cross-polarization-metric-calculation
description: Use when terrain-corrected Sentinel-1 gamma_0 stacks for VV and VH plus an acquisition-dates table (e.g., ALB_acquisition_dates.csv) are available and per-pixel cross-polarization difference/ratio rasters are needed as radar habitat-structure predictors.

name: cross-source-protein-sequence-integration
description: Use when constructing a reference protein database from coding genes of collected genomes plus curated entries (e.g. UniProt fungal subset), and redundancy and annotation quality must be controlled.

name: cross-species-genome-discrimination
description: Use when raw ONT MinION fast5 reads must be assigned to one of several closely related species (e.g., Poeciliidae guppies) using only genome FASTAs, on inexpensive hardware without basecalling.

name: cross-species-viral-genome-comparison
description: Use when choosing or defending an overlap/identity cutoff for viral read recruitment or strain separation: you need to know how much sequence two viral genomes or a virus and another microbe can share by chance before setting the threshold.

name: cross-study-classification-agreement-correlation
description: Use when a mock-community or benchmark sample has both a newly computed per-lineage classification profile and published reference proportions from another study, and you need a single agreement statistic (e.g., R²) to validate the new method's quantitative accuracy.

name: cross-study-microbiome-pooled-effect-estimation
description: Use when you have comparable per-study differential abundance result tables (estimates + standard errors from GAMLSS-BEZI taxa.compare on the same taxa levels) and need pooled effects, heterogeneity, and FDR-adjusted p-values across studies.

name: cross-tool-ani-accuracy-comparison
description: Use when you need to quantitatively validate or compare ANI/strain-comparison accuracy of inStrain versus other tools (dRep, MIDAS, StrainPhlAn) using simulated genomes with known ground-truth ANI values.

name: cross-tool-benchmark-reproduction
description: Use when a study requires reproducing a published tool-benchmark (same input dataset, multiple strain-comparison tools) with ROC/AUC and detection-count metrics, e.g. validating SynTracker's reported AUC 0.93 and 112 strain pairs.

name: cross-tool-binning-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when multiple viral binning tools must be compared on identical scaffold inputs with sorted BAM coverage, and a reproducible metrics table (F1, precision, redundant-protein counts) is the deliverable.

name: cross-tool-classification-agreement-analysis
description: Use when you have per-read classification files from several metagenomic classifiers run on the same read set and need to measure pairwise or reference-based agreement (e.g. Jaccard-based rates) rather than accuracy against ground truth.

name: cross-tool-comparative-performance-evaluation
description: Use when choosing among metagenomic fecal source tracking tools or claiming a new tool outperforms existing ones: run all candidates on the same benchmark samples with known source mixing proportions and tabulate sensitivity/specificity.

name: cross-tool-comparison-intersection
description: Use when per-sample metagenomic assemblies have been profiled by both SynTracker (APSS) and inStrain (popANI), and the goal is to detect species whose within-species diversity is preferentially point-mutation- or structurally-driven.

name: cross-tool-computational-performance-comparison
description: Use when reproducing or extending a runtime/speedup claim, e.g. quantifying how much faster a parallel pipeline is than its sequential version and whether it matches a tool's runtime on the same input dataset.

name: cross-tool-core-genome-comparison
description: Use when comparing pangenome/core-genome predictions from multiple tools (mOTUpan, Roary, PPanGGOLiN) on the same genome sets, especially MAGs spanning a wide completeness range.

name: cross-tool-detection-performance-comparison
description: Use when comparing detection performance (FDR, TPR) of longitudinal high-dimensional tools like LongDat and MaAsLin2 across varying numbers of covariates on simulated microbiome count data.

name: cross-tool-metagenomic-distance-normalization
description: Use when comparing multiple metagenome distance tools (Libra, Mash, Simka) on the same sample set to assess how data reduction, read-count normalization, or presence/absence metrics distort clustering by a known metadata factor such as body site.

name: cross-tool-performance-ratio-analysis
description: Use when comparing mapping throughput/speed of raw-signal nanopore mappers across tools on the same FAST5 datasets and reference genomes, e.g., verifying whether each tool exceeds nanopore sequencing throughput on the human genome.

name: cross-tool-prediction-comparison
description: Use when two plasmid-prediction tools have been run on identical contig/fragment sets and you must quantify error rates, agreement, and plasmid:chromosome separation ratios to decide which classifier to trust.

name: cross-tool-retention-comparison
description: Use when you need to quantify and compare false-removal rates (off-target loss of bacterial reads) of host-decontamination tools such as Hostile vs HRRT on simulated bacterial Illumina data.

name: cross-tool-runtime-profiling-on-hpc
description: Use when benchmarking multiple phylogenomic marker-mining tools (e.g. Patchwork vs ALiBaSeq vs aTRAM 2) for both accuracy and runtime across a sequencing-coverage gradient on a Slurm-managed HPC cluster.

name: cross-tool-significance-overlap-quantification
description: Decision support for choosing between longitudinal differential-abundance tools when multiple covariates (e.g. medications) may confound a time/treatment effect in high-dimensional microbiome data.

name: cross-tool-taxonomic-benchmarking
