description: Use when a newly proposed MAG/prokaryotic genome taxonomy classifier must be validated against established gold standards (GTDBtk, CAMITAX) on a common benchmark set with known NCBI taxonomic labels.

name: cross-validated-hyperparameter-grid-search
description: Use when fitting a regularized (L1/Lasso) mixture model — e.g., STENSL source selection with sink profile x vs. Y^T*α — and the sparsity level must be chosen from data rather than fixed arbitrarily.

name: cross-validated-phenotype-trait-prediction
description: Use when predicting phenotypic traits (e.g. aerobe, anaerobe, gramneg, thermophile) from comparative-genomics feature matrices (COG/eggNOG presence-absence profiles) and need cross-validated, kernel-comparable SVM accuracy and runtime figures.

name: cross-validation-fold-count-comparison
description: Use when evaluating whether combining models from k-fold cross-validation splits raises protein contact prediction accuracy over a single model, and when comparing accuracy across fold counts (e.g., 3/5/7/10) on CASP-style benchmark sets.

name: cross-validation-k-selection
description: Use when inferring population structure from genome-wide biallelic SNP data (VCF- or PLINK-derived BED files) and the number of ancestral populations (K) is unknown and must be estimated.

name: cross-validation-model-evaluation
description: Use when benchmarking supervised protein family classifiers built on amino acid recoding kmer vectors, and you need cross-validated ROC AUC/PR AUC to compare alphabets and kmer lengths.

name: cross-validation-model-evaluation
description: Use when reproducing or verifying the Character Predictor of MicroPIE: trained SVM models over labelled taxonomic-description sentences must be evaluated with k-fold cross validation and compared to reported precision/recall.

name: cross-validation-of-metagenomic-models
description: Use when a trained metagenomic classification model (e.g. random forest on DIABIMMUNE T1D profiles) needs robustness verification beyond a single train/test split, or when overfitting/bias must be ruled out before reporting accuracies.

name: cross-validation-performance-table-parsing
description: Use when a paper reports aggregate performance counts over a phenotype/class table and you must recompute those counts from a supplementary per-class accuracy table to verify the claim.

name: cross-validation-prediction-pooling
description: Use when you have nested cross-validation predictions with true phenotype labels and need to summarize classifier accuracy per taxon (e.g., bacterial phylum with at least five species), as done for Traitar's Figure 4.

name: csupb-tree-hierarchy-navigation
description: Use when a pangenome graph (e.g., from 12 human mitogenomes built with VARI-merge, k=22) must be navigated structurally — ordering/nesting colored superbubbles, resolving cycles, or mapping linear-reference coordinates and annotations onto graph nodes.

name: csv-structured-output-formatting
description: Use when a paper reports a multi-condition benchmark table (e.g. OTU counts and total counts for CDSnake, DADA2, and deblur on Balanced, HMP, and Extreme mock datasets) that must be transcribed into a structured CSV for downstream comparison.

name: cumulative-abundance-rank-thresholding
description: Use when many clustered gene representatives (e.g., 60 amoA-AOB clusters from 96% CD-HIT clustering) must be prioritized by environmental abundance/prevalence so only a minimal, high-coverage subset is carried forward to primer design.

name: cumulative-identity-distribution-analysis
description: Use when benchmarking sequence clustering tools (Linclust, MMseqs2, CD-HIT, UCLUST) on huge sets and you need to quantify clustering quality (false negatives) without exhaustively comparing all pairs.

name: cumulative-sum-scaling-implementation
description: Use when a sparse high-throughput marker-gene survey count matrix must be normalized for under-sampling before differential abundance analysis with metagenomeSeq, and the scaling factors must be computed and applied outside (but consistent with) the package's own routine.

name: cumulative-sum-scaling-normalization
description: Use when shotgun metagenome read-mapping produced gene frequency counts across samples and differential analysis must be composition-aware (sparse, zero-inflated data spanning taxa, gene, KO, EC and reaction levels).

name: curved-data-extraction-to-csv
description: Use when a sweep of counting Bloom filter sizes has been indexed with fimpera over the TARA dataset and the raw FPR-vs-memory values (e.g. 2.98e9 bits at 2% FPR) must be tabulated into a CSV curve file for comparison with a no-fimpera baseline.

name: custom-fasta-database-header-parsing
description: Use when metatranscriptome reads (FASTQ, already preprocessed) must be assigned organism and function annotations against a custom or RefSeq protein FASTA where header fields (ID, function, organism) must be translated into a per-read annotation table, without MG-RAST or any web service.

name: custom-index-hostile-read-depletion
description: Use when Hostile-cleaned retained reads still show non-human representation (e.g. EBV in human read retention figures) and those contaminant reads must be subtracted to obtain adjusted retention metrics.

name: dada2-taxonomy-assignment
description: Use when reproducing or comparing species-level taxonomic classification benchmarks of full-length 16S rRNA sequences against DADA2, QIIME 2, SINTAX, Kraken 2, or DeepTaxa on the same held-out reference test set.

name: daf-divergence-table-manipulation
description: Use when DGN/PopFly FASTA variation and D. melanogaster–D. simulans divergence data must be converted into tab-delimited DAF and divergence tables (0-fold/4-fold classes) for MKT-based alpha estimation or gene-set comparisons.

name: daf-spectrum-processing
description: Use when input is a tab-delimited DAF spectrum plus divergence counts (Ps, Pn, Ds, Dn) per gene and the goal is to correct alpha estimates for slightly deleterious rare variants via a user-specified frequency cutoff (eMKT/FWWMKT-style exclusion).

name: database-build-runtime-profiling
description: Use when benchmarking how much time and RAM metagenomic classifiers need to build indexing databases from growing reference genome collections (e.g., bacterial-only vs. all-kingdom food-seq databases), to select a tool that fits a fixed-memory workstation or cluster.

name: database-partitioning-scalability-benchmarking
description: Use when a reference genome database (e.g. AFS31RS90, ~135 GB in RAM) exceeds single-node or single-executor memory and you need to quantify the time/memory/speed trade-off of splitting it into partitions or distributing it over Spark executors.

name: database-shrinking-record-subsampling
description: Use when a Kraken database (e.g., the ~70-GB standard RefSeq build) exceeds available RAM and a reduced-memory variant must be created by record subsampling, and the resulting sensitivity/precision deltas need to be measured.

name: dbscan-breakpoint-cluster-analysis
description: Use when paired-end shotgun NGS reads mapped with BWA yield junction read pairs whose two sides map to two different references, and candidate HGT breakpoint pairs must be generated before split-read refinement.

name: de-bruijn-graph-baseline-variant-calling
description: Use when benchmarking a reference-free variant caller against the de Bruijn graph on simulated or real WGS reads, needing an independent baseline call set for hap.py validation.

name: de-bruijn-graph-construction
description: Use when assembling Illumina short reads de novo and peak memory during de Bruijn graph construction is limiting, or when benchmarking sparse-vs-dense DBG memory tradeoffs.

name: de-bruijn-graph-contig-scaffolding
description: Use when assembling Illumina GA short reads (FASTA/FASTQ/BAM, paired-end or mate-pair libraries) into a de novo draft genome for large plant/animal or human-sized genomes and you need scaffold N50 and error metrics comparable to SOAPdenovo1, ALLPATHS-LG, or Assemblathon1/GAGE benchmarks.

name: de-bruijn-graph-genotype-calling
description: Use when raw FASTQ reads (Illumina MiSeq or high-error-rate ONT MinION) from S. aureus or M. tuberculosis isolates must be converted directly into an antibiotic-resistance call set without assembly or SNP-calling pipelines.

name: de-bruijn-graph-kmer-parameterization
description: Use when assembling metagenomic (environmental) FASTQ reads with MetaCortex and a maximum k-mer size must be chosen and baked in at compile time before building the de Bruijn graph.

name: de-bruijn-graph-metagenomic-assembly
description: Use when assembling metagenomic (environmental) FASTQ reads from samples with high strain-level diversity — e.g. viral mock communities, HIV lab mixes, or gut microbiomes — and both a consensus contig set and per-strain graph paths are needed.

name: de-bruijn-graph-postorder-traversal
description: Use when you must decompose a colored (multi-sample) de Bruijn graph into sample-specific superbubbles, assign offset values per node, and build the cSupB tree used for graph coordinates and variant detection.

name: de-bruijn-graph-probe-matching
description: Use when raw FASTQ reads from mycobacterial or staphylococcal isolates need rapid phylo_group, species, and lineage calls — e.g. distinguishing MTBC from NTM or concordance-checking lineage assignments against a reference caller.

name: de-novo-assembly-quality-assessment
description: Use when subsampled low-coverage WGS read sets (e.g. 1x–40x) must be assembled de novo to create query contigs, and assembly quality must be verified before marker retrieval.

name: de-novo-genome-assembly
description: Use when paired-end gzipped FASTQ from 10x Chromium Linked-Read libraries (real or LRTK-SIM simulated) must be assembled de novo and contiguity/accuracy compared across coverage (C, CF, CR) or fragment-length conditions.

name: de-novo-metagenome-assembly
description: Use when input is raw paired-end metagenomic (or spiked-in isolate) Illumina FASTQ reads and the goal is to recover cas operons/CRISPR arrays while measuring runtime against a complete-assembly baseline.

name: de-novo-metagenomic-assembly-with-spades
description: Use when short paired-end metagenomic reads contain ARGs (pre-screened via KMA against PanRes) and you need the surrounding genomic context assembled without assembling the entire metagenome.

name: de-novo-short-read-genome-assembly
description: Use when you have trimmed paired-end Illumina reads from an isolate genome (e.g., E. coli K-12 MG1655, ~4.6-4.8 Mb) and need de novo contig assemblies from several widely-cited short-read assemblers for downstream quality comparison.

name: deep-learning-baseline-algorithm-comparison
description: Use when evaluating a deep unsupervised clustering tool for unlabeled DNA sequences (e.g. FASTA mitochondrial genomes) against k-means++, GMM, DeLUCS, and MeShClust v3.0 with ground-truth cluster_id TSV labels available for posthoc scoring.

name: deep-learning-baseline-output-layer-adaptation
description: Use when benchmarking a multi-status microbiome classifier (e.g. 3 oral labels Control/Periodontitis/Gingivitis or 5 gut labels) and needing convolution-based deep learning baselines that were originally designed for a different output task.

name: deep-neural-network-contact-prediction-training
description: Use when reproducing or extending the DeepECA Feature Added Model for long-range contact prediction from MSAs, particularly to test whether sequential features improve accuracy when homologous sequence depth is small.

name: deep-neural-network-training-on-genomes
description: Use when labeled whole-genome sequences (FASTA with training labels in sequence IDs) must be turned into a DNN read classifier and architecture variants (one-hot CNN, hybrid, LSTM, self-attention) need to be compared by read-level precision and recall.

name: deep-residual-network-training
description: Use when training a DNN to predict protein contacts and secondary structure from raw MSAs end-to-end, rather than from precomputed covariance or precision-matrix features.

name: deepvirfinder-score-thresholding
description: Use when classifying assembled metagenomic contigs as viral in ViroProfiler, specifically to apply DeepVirFinder's score/p-value threshold as one of the per-tool detection criteria.

name: degenerate-primer-design
description: Use when aligned nucleotide sequences of target functional genes (e.g., amoA-AOB FASTA from ranked/clustered gene sets) must be converted into a minimal set of primer pairs that captures maximal diversity of a reference gene set.

name: delong-correlated-roc-comparison
description: Use when two DA methods have been applied to the same samples with known ground-truth labels and you need a statistically valid paired comparison of their ROC AUCs (e.g., 800 simulated bacterial species, 400 null / 400 differential).

name: dem-based-sar-geocoding
description: Reference for reproducing the Sentinel-1 GRDH-to-gamma0 chain when input is uncalibrated DN in slant-range coordinates and output must be calibrated, terrain-normalized gamma_0 at 10 m pixel spacing.

name: denoising-clustering-method-benchmarking
description: Use when amplicon ASV/OTU inference must be compared across DC tools against ground-truth mock community data (e.g., mockrobiota mock4/mock12/mock16) using a phylogenetic metric such as weighted UniFrac.

name: density-based-variant-clustering
description: Use when cellsnp-lite AD/DP pileups are available for ≥10 shotgun metagenomic samples and you must separate shared informative variants (num_of_clusters >= 2) from non-polymorphic background sites.

name: depth-dependent-variant-detection-evaluation
description: Use when comparing metagenomic variant-caller performance across sequencing depths on simulated data with a known ground-truth variant set.

name: descriptive-association-metric-quantification
description: Use when multiple binary clinical/grouping factors are available for the same microbiome feature table and the goal is a quantitative, comparable measure (AUMC/AOI) of which factor identifies differences in microbial communities.

name: detection-curve-visualization
description: Use when you need to determine how many raw MinION reads are required before a baseLess abundance-mode classifier's MSRD plateau is reached, e.g. plotting MSRD-vs-reads curves for multiple target species on a single figure.

name: detection-limit-threshold-filtering
description: Use when calling fecal source presence/absence in short-read metagenomes from SourceApp's genome-equivalent-normalized cell fraction estimates, where spurious low-level signal must be filtered before computing apportionment portions.

name: detection-power-evaluation
description: Use when estimating the minimum detectable minor-population frequency for a genotype-based resistance or species caller on Illumina data, e.g. benchmarking mecA or plasmid-borne tetracycline/erythromycin detection in in silico S. aureus/CoNS mixtures.

name: diamond-aligner-benchmarking
description: Use when you need to predict or budget DIAMOND annotation compute time for metatranscriptome samples by measuring how SAMSA2's DIAMOND runtime scales with the number of input sequences under a fixed CPU/memory allocation.

name: diamond-alignment-output-parsing
description: Use when you have DIAMOND tabular alignment hits of shotgun metagenomic reads against a microbial gene database (e.g. UniRef90) and must refine them to hits per read for gene abundance estimation.

name: diamond-alignment-parameter-tuning
description: Use when DIAMOND-based retrieval of phylogenetic markers yields low query coverage, particularly with low-coverage read data as query, and masking or sensitivity settings may be limiting alignments.

name: diamond-protein-database-alignment
description: Use when raw FASTQ metatranscriptome reads need organism or functional annotation against a local protein database, and speed or reproducibility rules out BLAST or web services such as MG-RAST.

name: dietary-group-separation-analysis-of-metagenomes
description: Use when you have unassembled NGS shotgun-read FASTA metagenomes (extensions '.fasta', '.fa' or '.fna') with host diet or phenotype metadata and want to test whether alignment-free d2S distances recapitulate those groups.

name: differential-abundance-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing phenotype-enrichment methods for species/pathway abundance tables (16S or metagenomic), especially with limited cohort sizes, or when reproducing the VTwins-vs-conventional sensitivity/10-fold-sample-size benchmark.

name: differential-abundance-method-benchmarking
description: Use when you need to quantitatively compare two or more differential abundance testing methods on simulated microbiome relative abundance data with known differential/null species labels, to decide which method has detection power.

name: differential-abundance-results-plotting
description: Use when you have a differential abundance results table for KEGG pathways from PICRUSt2 output plus the pathway abundance table and sample metadata, and you need a publication figure showing between-group differences.

name: differential-abundance-statistics-analysis
description: Use when ranked abundance summary tables from aggregated metatranscriptome annotations are available and the goal is to find features with significant abundance differences between control and experimental groups.

name: differential-abundance-tool-benchmarking
description: Use when you must reproduce or verify that metagenomeSeq improves differential abundance calling on sparse, undersampled marker-gene survey data relative to default DESeq, edgeR, Metastats, and LEfSe workflows.

name: differential-gene-expression-analysis
description: Use when you have a raw bulk RNA-seq count matrix (csv/txt) plus optional sample metadata and need per-gene differential expression results (log2FoldChange, Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p-values) without scripting R/DESeq2 directly.

name: digital-normalization-of-reads
description: Use when preparing metagenomic/virome FASTQ reads for de-novo assembly where read depth is uneven and deep coverage would inflate assembly time or contig composition, e.g. prior to Virmap.pl or MEGAHIT.

name: diploid-genome-assembly
description: Use when the goal is to assemble a diploid genome from 10x Chromium Linked-Read libraries, or to test how source-genome features (repeats, heterozygous variation, sequencing error) or library parameters (CF, CR, mu_FL) affect Supernova2 diploid assembly quality.

name: diploid-reference-generation-from-vcf
description: Use when simulating diploid 10x Linked-Read libraries (LRTK-SIM Hap=2) that require two haploid reference sequences derived from a reference genome plus known variants, or when a gold standard for diploid assembly accuracy is needed.

name: diploid-reference-variant-injection
description: Use when preparing diploid in silico reference genomes for Linked-Read read simulation, e.g. to reproduce assembly-accuracy (NA50) benchmarks from real NA12878/NA24385-style data.

name: diploid-region-window-classification
description: Use when you need to measure what fraction of the genome a 10x Linked-Read de novo assembly (Supernova2) recovers in a diploid (both-homologs-covered) state, rather than a haploid contiguity metric such as N50.

name: dirichlet-multinomial-microbiome-count-simulation
description: Use when you need to evaluate or benchmark microbiome meta-analysis methods (mMeta, aMeta, marker-specific meta-analysis) under known association scenarios using simulated multi-study count data and α-diversity indices.

name: dirichlet-process-read-clustering
description: Use when you have an alignment of short NGS reads (BAM/CRAM or FASTA MSA) from a genetically heterogeneous sample and need error correction plus local haplotype reconstruction before global assembly or frequency estimation.

name: dirichlet-tree-multinomial-regression
description: Use when the input is compositional count data (e.g., microbiome taxa) paired with covariates, and the goal is variable selection of covariate-by-branch associations while respecting a known or unknown phylogenetic/graph structure.

name: discordant-read-pair-junction-selection
description: Use when paired-end shotgun NGS reads have been uniquely mapped to metagenomic reference genomes with BWA and junction pairs spanning two different references must be grouped into candidate HGT breakpoints.

name: dissimilarity-to-similarity-transformation
description: Use when d2* oligonucleotide-frequency dissimilarity values have been computed with Jie Ren's tools but the downstream model (ILMF-VH on the virus-host heterogeneous network, or SNF host network fusion) requires similarity matrices instead.

name: distance-correlation-computation
description: Use when performing feature screening for microbiome multivariate association testing: given a high-dimensional OTU count matrix (e.g. 856 taxa) and an adjusted response, decide which taxa enter the testing subset.

name: distance-metric-resolution-benchmarking
description: Use when choosing among metagenome comparison tools/metrics and you need evidence on which metric preserves body-site or community-composition structure rather than collapsing resolution.

name: distance-metric-runtime-comparison
description: Use when you must reproduce or verify runtime-scaling claims for an all-vs-all metagenome comparison tool, or quantify the per-metric runtime share of Libra's scoring algorithms across increasing input volumes.

name: dn-ds-calculation-from-metagenomic-snvs
description: Use when inStrain has called SNVs on read pairs mapped to a reference genome and you need per-gene synonymous/nonsynonymous classification and dN/dS to compare variation within versus between hosts.

name: dna-bpe-tokenization
description: Use when a FASTA of 16S rRNA sequences (full-length ~1,500 bp or in-silico amplicons such as ~420 bp V3-V4) must be converted into fixed-length token inputs for a DNABERT-2-vocabulary transformer classifier.

name: dna-kmer-signature-encoding
description: Use when raw DNA reads or sequences in FASTA must be converted to numeric signatures for unsupervised alignment-free clustering (e.g. iDeLUCS, DeLUCS, k-means++), with ground truth reserved for post-hoc scoring.

name: dna-rna-processing-metadata-annotation
description: Use when building or extending a sample metadata table for metagenomic lab workflows that must capture DNA/RNA extraction and processing status per sample before sequencing, especially when labs need custom fields beyond a generic schema.

name: dna-sequence-clustering-benchmark-evaluation
description: Decision support for choosing a clustering-quality metric when ground-truth labels are unavailable: apply when benchmark tables exist for multiple clustering algorithms/datasets and you need to know if silhouette or Davies-Bouldin can proxy ACC.

name: docker-based-pipeline-execution
description: Use when a user wants to execute the full CAMAMED workflow (quality-controlled reads → MetaPhlAn2/MOSAIK → KEGG KO/EC/reaction annotation) without installing software dependencies, or when reproducible containerized execution is required.

name: docker-container-resource-monitoring
description: Use when benchmarking the computational requirements (job runtime, CPU usage, peak memory) of tools executed inside Docker containers or through Nextflow pipelines, where measuring the orchestrator process would underestimate actual resource use.

name: dockerized-bioinformatics-pipeline-execution
description: Use when a tool's README states Docker is the only prerequisite and all other dependencies (e.g., Python 3.9, BBMap, SPAdes, MEGAHIT) are handled by the Dockerfile, and you need to execute the full pipeline end-to-end.

name: draft-viral-bin-export-and-validation
description: Use when ViralCC's inputs (final.contigs.fa, name-sorted MAP_SORTED.bam, viral_contigs.txt) are ready and you must cluster G_int with Leiden to produce draft vMAG bins and validate the exported clustering files against the Test dataset reference.

name: drosophila-population-data-handling
description: Use when estimating alpha or selection regimes (adaptive, neutral, strongly/weakly deleterious) for D. melanogaster protein-coding genes from polymorphism/divergence data, e.g. comparing gene sets such as high-recombination regions against the whole genome.

name: drosophila-population-genomics-data-processing
description: Use when raw D. melanogaster DGN/PopFly FASTA alignments and divergence data must be converted into per-gene DAF spectra (0-fold/4-fold classes) and divergence counts for MKT-based estimation of alpha.

name: dsr-sulphur-metabolism-protein-typing
description: Use when you have user-supplied protein sequences in FASTA format (complete genomes or metagenomic assemblies) and need to detect Dsr proteins and predict enzyme direction/type automatically, without phylogenetic tree reconstruction.

name: dtm-mcmc-variable-selection
description: Use when you have genus-level OTU/ASV count data with a known phylogenetic tree and covariates (e.g., FFQ dietary variables) and need to identify which covariates associate with taxa branches via Bayesian variable selection in a DTM model.

name: dual-assembler-metagenome-assembly
description: Use when comparing whether a MAG taxonomic classifier's accuracy depends on the choice of meta-assembler, using independently reconstructed MAG sets from the same read dataset.

name: dynamic-neighbor-joining-distance-clustering
description: Use when tuning pairwise sequence-distance parameters (e.g. Mash sketch size, k-mer size) so that replicate or same-source samples cluster apart from distinct samples in a distance-matrix analysis.

name: dynamic-time-warping-squiggle-dissimilarity-scoring
description: Use when selecting k-mers for a Nanopore signal-detection library (e.g. baseLess 16S detection) and you need to verify that candidate k-mers produce electrically distinguishable squiggles, not just sequence-dissimilar ones.

name: ebwt-data-structure-preprocessing
description: Use when preparing inputs for the LiME metagenomic classifier: FASTA files of paired-end reads (e.g. setB2_1.fasta/setB2_2.fasta, 100 bp) and a reference database (e.g. Refs.fasta, 930 genomes) must be converted into ebwt, lcp and da files before ClusterLCP/ClusterBWT_DA/Classify can run.

name: ebwt-index-preprocessing-merge
description: Use when preparing ebwt/lcp/da data structures for LiME classification, i.e. when a FASTA collection of paired-end reads (e.g. setA2/setB2, SRR1804065) and a reference genome set (e.g. Refs.fasta, 930 genomes) must be merged into ebwt(S), lcp(S), da(S).

name: ebwt-lcp-da-construction
description: Use when preparing inputs for LiME's ClusterLCP/ClusterBWT_DA steps: you need ebwt(S), lcp(S), and da(S) for a fasta collection of paired-end reads plus reference genomes.

name: ebwt-suffix-tree-simulation
description: Use when the input is only the eBWT file (reads.fasta.bwt) of raw reads and you need to detect eBWT clusters / local LCP minima for reference-free SNP/INDEL discovery under tight memory, without suffix-array structures.

name: edge-weight-ranked-neighbor-traversal
description: Use when vConTACT2 outputs (genome_by_genome_overview.csv, c1.ntw) must be converted into a direct per-vOTU taxonomy table instead of manual network inspection.

name: edit-distance-haplotype-evaluation
description: Use when evaluating deconvolved allele or strain-type calls against known ground truth, especially when called sequences may be near-misses (novel strains differing by a few SNPs) rather than exact matches.

name: em-frequency-estimation-execution
description: Use when error-corrected reads and reconstructed haplotypes from ShoRAH windows (e.g., HIV-1 pol pyrosequencing data) must be quantified into per-haplotype population frequencies via the EM-based freqEst step of the shorah.py workflow.

name: embedding-extraction-from-hybrid-cnn-bert-model
description: Use when you need internal representations — not just class predictions — from DeepTaxa's published HybridCNNBERT checkpoints, e.g. to test whether 16S rRNA embeddings from 69,335 Greengenes2 2024.09 test sequences cluster by species or phylum.

name: embedding-vocabulary-design-for-dna-models
description: Use when preparing a DNA/embedding layer for a deep-learning taxonomic classifier: you need a fixed, canonical, index-mapped k-mer vocabulary before training the embedding.

name: emirge-iterative-candidate-merging
description: Use when adapter-trimmed Illumina (meta)genomic reads must be turned into full-length/nearly full-length SSU rRNA gene sequences for species-level taxonomy, and a reference-targeted, iterative assembler with candidate merging is wanted.

name: emkt-alpha-statistics-computation
description: Use when polymorphism/divergence tables (DAF, Pi, P0, mi, Di, m0, D0) are available for D. melanogaster genes and you need alpha estimates per gene or per gene set, e.g. comparing high-recombination regions against all genes in a population such as ZI.

name: empirical-bonferroni-threshold-calculation
description: Use when performing OMARU phylogenetic or gene-level MWAS association testing and a multiple-testing correction threshold is needed that controls type I error better than the standard Bonferroni cutoff.

name: empirical-cumulative-distribution-modeling
description: Use when scaffolding metagenomic contigs with paired long-range links and you need to detect links joining contigs from different species using coverage depth and k-mer composition evidence.

name: empirical-power-analysis
description: Use when validating that a new microbiome multivariate association test (AMAT, aMiSPU, OMiRKAT, OMiAT, LDM, MiHC) controls type I error at the nominal 0.05 level and to compare empirical power across signal densities and effect sizes.

name: empirical-type-i-error-estimation
description: Use when comparing the statistical power and type I error of multivariate microbiome association tests on simulated OTU count data (e.g. Dirichlet-multinomial simulations with known null and alternative scenarios) and you need empirical error rates at alpha=0.05.

name: ena-dataset-retrieval
description: Use when the analysis requires raw short-read FASTQ data for a published study identified only by ENA/SRA accessions (BioProject/Study, e.g. PRJEB40798, ERP015409) and no local FASTQ files exist yet.

name: ena-read-data-retrieval
description: Use when starting a large-scale metagenomic analysis from publicly archived sequencing runs: an ENA/SRA accession (BioProject, Biosample, Experiment, or Run) must be converted into local FASTQ files before downstream QC, alignment, or assembly steps.

name: ensemble-feature-fusion-classification
description: Use when classifying microbiome samples into multiple disease/status labels from OTU or species abundance tables, after features have been phylogenetically organized into multi-layer clustering groups by PM-CNN's Step 3.

name: enterotype-clustering-classification
description: Use when you need to cluster genus-level gut microbiome profiles (e.g. a twin/mother cohort) into enterotypes and test whether CopyRighter GCN correction changes sample-to-enterotype assignment.

name: euclidean-distance-error-computation
description: Use when relative abundance estimates per reference genome (values in [0,1]) have been produced from mapped-read counts and must be scored against known mock-community mixing proportions by Euclidean distance.

name: evolutionary-model-based-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating a strain-composition or haplotype-reconstruction method on simulated samples where ground-truth strain type distributions and mutation/recombination events must be generated under defined evolutionary models.

name: exact-string-matching-sequence-collapsing
description: Use when a quality-filtered FASTQ/FNA amplicon dataset must be dereplicated before OTU inference and you need a deterministic exact-match collapse (or a fast runtime baseline to benchmark against VSEARCH-style dereplication).

name: exclusion-based-nonviral-data-filtering
description: Decision support for identifying viral contigs from assembled sequences when direct homology to known viruses is insufficient, e.g., novel phages in metagenomic assemblies needing gene-content-based viral classification.

name: expectation-maximization-frequency-estimation
description: Use when you have globally reconstructed viral haplotypes (e.g., from ShoRAH's mm.py) and need maximum-likelihood estimates of their population frequencies, including low-frequency variants.

name: expectation-maximization-mixing-proportion-inference
description: Use when an m-by-n microbiome count matrix (rows = SampleID, taxa as columns) plus 3-column metadata (Env, SourceSink, id) must be decomposed into per-sink source contributions, especially with many noncontributing sources or an unknown source.

name: expectation-maximization-sparse-source-selection
description: Use when a microbial source tracking sink must be decomposed against many candidate sources (e.g., hundreds of environments from public repositories like HMP or EMP), where prior methods add considerable error and only a small subset of sources truly contribute.

name: expected-breadth-coverage-modeling
description: Use when profiling metagenomic read mappings against a reference .fasta and you need to distinguish low breadth caused by low coverage from breadth loss caused by strain absence or contamination.

name: expected-calibration-error-estimation
description: Use when evaluating a probabilistic 16S rRNA taxonomic classifier whose confidence must be verified against reported calibration numbers — e.g. reproducing DeepTaxa's per-rank ECE (domain 0.0002 → species 0.0242) on the 69,335-sequence Greengenes2 2024.09 test set.

name: explained-variance-loss-quantification
description: Use when you need to know how much of a predictor set's (e.g., ALS vs Sentinel-1 radar) explanatory power for many response variables depends on between-region variation rather than within-region structure.

name: extended-haplotype-homozygosity-selection-scanning
description: Use when scanning phased biallelic SNP VCF (or PLINK binary) data, split by chromosome and indexed with tabix, for single-population (iHS) and pairwise population-comparison (XP-EHH) haplotype-based signals of selection.

name: extensible-omics-analysis-function-development
description: Use when a tabular time-series omic data set does not fit any of MOVIS's five supported omic-types and you need to add omic-specific functionality to the analysis core rather than preprocess the data externally.

name: external-validation-of-species-composition-models
description: Use when testing whether a fitted radar (Sentinel-1 gamma_0) assemblage-composition model generalizes to independent, georeferenced field plots outside the training regions, e.g. bird or saproxylic beetle NMDS1 scores.

name: extreme-quantile-correlation-filtering
description: Use when running mbQTL's Approach B: you have estimated taxa-taxa correlation (R) values with coringTaxa and need to retain only the most extreme pairwise correlations before estimating taxa-SNP rho values with taxaSnpCor.

name: f1-and-false-positive-rate-computation
description: Use when benchmarking variant callers on simulated shotgun metagenomic datasets and you need per-method, per-depth F1, true positive rate, and false positive counts against a known ground-truth variant set.

name: f1-score-computation
description: Use when benchmarking read classifiers in a mock-community depletion setting: you have per-read target/non-target calls from SPUMONI or minimap2 over multiple index strategies and need F1 scores comparable to the paper's Table 1.

name: f1-score-model-evaluation
description: Use when training or tuning baseLess 1D CNN k-mer detectors on raw MinION squiggle signal and you need a held-out-test-read F1 score, or when comparing hyperparameter candidates under a size-penalized loss.

name: fallback-feature-selection-logic
description: Use when implementing a distance-correlation-based feature screening step for microbiome multivariate association testing and you need a guaranteed non-empty selected feature subset S from an OTU matrix and adjusted response.

name: false-discovery-rate-and-true-positive-rate-estimation
description: Use when head-to-head benchmarking of differential-abundance or longitudinal methods on simulated data with known ground truth is needed, and FDR/TPR trajectories must be quantified as covariate count or confounding strength varies.

name: false-negative-fraction-estimation
description: Use when you need to quantify the sensitivity (false-negative fraction) of a sequence-clustering run at a given identity threshold (e.g. 50%, 70%, 90%) by comparing it against a BLAST-based reference of homologous pairs.

name: false-positive-false-negative-rate-quantification
description: Use when benchmarking plasmid/chromosome classification tools (e.g. cBar vs PlasFlow) on fragments of known origin and you need error rates plus percent agreement between tools.

name: false-positive-rate-analysis
description: Use when choosing k-mer lengths for baseLess's composite k-mer detection networks: run the Section 4.2 analytical Poisson FPR sweep over candidate k values against non-target (30/50 kb) and target (0.6/1.5/30 kb) length combinations.

name: false-positive-rate-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing metagenomic classifiers on samples with known ground-truth ingredient composition, to quantify false positives and abundance-estimation accuracy per tool.

name: false-positive-rate-benchmarking
description: Use when validating a longitudinal association pipeline on microbiome count data by measuring false-positive rates against a permuted-time null in which all true time-feature associations are eliminated.

name: false-positive-rate-measurement
description: Use when benchmarking how a counting AMQ (e.g., a counting Bloom filter built with fimpera) calls k-mers/reads incorrectly, or when quantifying the FPR gain or space savings from wrapping a cBF with fimpera at a given z threshold.

name: false-positive-rate-quantification
description: Use when validating that a taxonomic marker-gene database (e.g., fungal FunOMIC-T) does not erroneously map sequences from off-target organisms, by measuring bacterial mapping rate and specificity on simulated mock-community reads.

name: false-positive-reduction-factor-computation
description: Use when comparing false-positive rates of metagenomic classifiers on admixed food samples containing closely related species pairs (e.g. buffalo/cattle, goat/sheep), where quantification outputs must be cross-parsed and converted to FP-reduction factors.

name: family-composition-tabulation-across-datasets
description: Use when you have draft vMAG FASTA files from ViralCC VIRAL_BIN output for multiple datasets and need to quantify family-level purity (single-family vs mixed-family bins) and per-family composition.

name: fasta-contig-output-generation
description: Use when the goal is to combine cluster-specific contigs (haplotigs) from a strain-aware metagenomic assembly into final master contigs using an overlap graph and emit them as a FASTA output file.

name: fasta-record-parsing
description: Use when a FASTA reference database of annotated microbial 16S sequences must be reformatted for CD-HIT-OTU-Miseq/CDSnake, i.e., when headers embed taxonomy lineages and record order must reflect annotation specificity.

name: fasta-sequence-binning-and-export
description: Use when a PlasFlow predictions TSV assigns contigs to plasmid/chromosome/unclassified classes and you need per-class FASTA bins plus sequence-count and length-fraction summaries per sample.

name: fasta-sequence-file-processing
description: Use when the input is a user-supplied protein multi-FASTA file (e.g. .faa from complete genomes or metagenomes) that must be screened against a curated HMM library and assigned protein-family/type predictions.

name: fasta-sequence-filtering
description: Use when a large FASTA of predicted CDSs (e.g. ~5.5 million from assembled vaginal metagenomes) must be collapsed to a non-redundant gene set before annotation or read mapping.

name: fasta-sequence-manipulation
description: Use when a metagenomic assembly needs coverage-based edge correction of contigs — e.g. FASTA contigs plus a k-mer depth table where terminal regions of suspected interspecies misjoins show coverage deviating from the contig median.

name: fasta-sequence-output-writing
description: Use when merging overlapping DIAMOND BLASTX hits into continuous per-reference sequences or trimming noncoding regions, and the resulting marker sequences must be emitted as FASTA for phylogenetic use.

name: fasta-sequence-parsing
description: Use when the input is archived raw FASTA files (genomics or proteomics omic-type) that must be parsed into individual sequences before embedding, vectorization, or tabular conversion in a time-series multi-omics pipeline.

name: fastq-adaptor-trimming
description: Use when raw paired-end FASTQ metatranscriptome reads contain adaptor contamination or low-quality bases and must be trimmed and mate-joined before annotation, e.g. preparing 100 bp paired-end stool RNA-seq files for MG-RAST submission.

name: fastq-quality-control
description: Use when raw paired-end RNA-seq/metatranscriptome FASTQ files must be cleaned before annotation: mates need merging, low-quality bases and adapters removed, and rRNA reads filtered to speed up annotation.

name: fastq-quality-trimming
description: Use when shotgun metagenomic FASTQs (host-filtered paired and singleton .fastq.gz) must be quality-trimmed before read mapping, and low-quality bases at read ends and overly short reads need removal.

name: fastq-read-count-summary-statistics
description: Use when you have run a MetaLAFFA QC step (e.g., Bowtie 2 host filtering against the hs37d5 reference) and need per-sample read counts plus average read length and base-quality summaries to document how many reads were removed.

name: fastq-read-length-distribution-modeling
description: Use when simulating ONT-like sequencing datasets to benchmark mutation detection, requiring FASTQ read-length and base-quality distributions (e.g. 1020–3968 bp, Q10–Q42) matched to the study's Methods parameters.

name: fastq-read-pair-handling
description: Use when reconstructing StrainXpress's read-overlap scoring: you have an interleaved FASTQ of Illumina-type short reads and Minimap2 all-vs-all alignments with CIGAR strings, and need per-pair scores D with >=30 bp / >=0.9 identity filtering.

name: fastq-read-pair-processing
description: Use when input is paired-end Illumina FASTQ (or CASAVA/QSEQ) reads whose forward and reverse mates overlap an amplicon (e.g. 16S rRNA hypervariable regions) and reads are being discarded (~40%) due to uncalled or miscalled bases under naive perfect-match merging.

name: fastq-read-subset-management
description: Use when you have a small FASTA/FASTQ seed read set (e.g. cas-gene or CRISPR-repeat matches) and a large raw FASTQ dataset, and you need to recruit neighboring reads to prime targeted assembly without assembling the whole dataset.

name: fastq-record-length-and-phred-thresholding
description: Use when raw pooled/subsampled ONT long-read FASTQs (e.g. .fastq.gz from a MinION run) must be quality-trimmed before plasmid assembly, and every retained record must meet a length and Q-score cutoff.

name: fastq-to-tfrecord-conversion
description: Use when feeding FASTQ or FASTA metagenomic reads (e.g. simulated gut-MAG reads or iHMP gut metagenomes) into DeepMicrobes for training or prediction, since the LSTM/embedding models only consume TFRecord input.

name: fastqc-quality-reporting
description: Use when raw Illumina metagenomic FASTQ/fastq.gz reads enter a QC stage and per-file FastQC reports plus a consolidated MultiQC summary are needed before and after adapter/quality trimming with bbduk.

name: fastqc-report-interpretation
description: Use when running or validating the short-read pre-processing module of nf-core/mag and you must judge, from FastQC reports, whether raw Illumina paired-end FASTQ files were adequately trimmed and contaminant-filtered before assembly.

name: fda-argos-reference-genome-handling
description: Use when benchmarking host-decontamination precision on known bacterial content: you need reference-grade complete bacterial assemblies (FDA-ARGOS, BioProject 231221) to simulate reads or to mask a human index against bacterial sequence.

name: fdr-estimation-across-simulation-replicates
description: Use when comparing longitudinal differential-abundance tools on simulated count data and you need per-setting FDR, TPR, and accuracy aggregated over replicate simulations with known ground truth.

name: fdr-estimation-from-psm-p-values
description: Use when tandem mass spectra must be searched against predicted RiPP structures and an FDR estimate is needed at a given p-value threshold via a target-decoy strategy.

name: fdr-multiple-hypothesis-correction
description: Use when interpreting HashSeq's per-variant inference-test P values (e.g. deciding which one-mismatch children are true variants) and you need FDR-adjusted significance across many clusters tested simultaneously.

name: fdr-multiple-testing-correction
description: Use when testing differential relative abundances of many taxa (phylum to genus level, e.g. l2/l5/l6 tables) or pooling taxa estimates across studies, and raw p-values must be FDR-adjusted before calling significant taxa.

name: feature-abundance-heatmap-rendering
description: Use when abundance summary tables from DIAMOND_analysis_counter.py have already been tested with DESeq in the SAMSA2 pipeline and a heatmap of top significantly differing features is needed.

name: feature-table-taxonomy-preprocessing
description: Use when a raw 16S OTU count table (e.g. otu.tab.txt) and taxonomy table (tax.tab.txt) must be quality-controlled before survival-response microbiome analysis and the MiSurv default QC criteria need to be reproduced.

name: fecal-source-apportionment-estimation
description: Use when gzipped shotgun metagenomic FASTQ reads (e.g., from impaired waterways) must be attributed to and apportioned among fecal source categories (human, sewage, septage, cow, dog, bird) using a curated source-associated genome database.

name: fecal-source-cell-fraction-estimation
description: Use when metagenomic read-mapping counts against source-associated genome databases must be converted into cell-fraction-like abundance units (genome equivalents) for fecal source attribution/apportionment.

name: fecal-source-tracking-read-mapping
description: Use when assigning short-read shotgun metagenomic reads (e.g., 2 × 150-bp Illumina NovaSeq 6000) from waterway samples to curated genome databases with known source-associations to quantify fecal signal per source category.

name: fisher-exact-contingency-analysis
description: Use when both an OMARU MWAS pathway enrichment file (sumstats_*_annot.txt) and a PASCAL-derived GWAS pathway enrichment file (<Phenotype>_GWAS_<Pathway_reference>.txt) exist for the same phenotype and you must quantify their pathway-level overlap.

name: flagellar-motility-gene-verification
description: Use when validating that a trained Traitar phenotype model links the correct Pfam families to flagellar motility, nitrate reduction, or l-arabinose phenotypes, e.g. reproducing Table 3 accessions from Table S6 rankings.

name: flux-variability-analysis-phenotype-prediction
description: Use when you have draft GSMMs/GEMs (e.g. from MAGs via CarveMe or gapseq) and need to quantify metabolic capabilities via exchange-reaction flux ranges, or to measure how annotation expansion closes the phenotype-prediction gap toward complete-genome models.

name: food-ingredient-admixture-percentage-parsing
description: Use when quantifying ingredient percentages in food admixture samples and you need to compare false-positive cross-classification rates between closely related species across metagenomic classifiers.

name: forest-structural-metric-comparison-radar-vs-als
description: Use when you have plot-mean structural metrics from two remote-sensing sources (e.g. VH/VV gamma_0 temporal stacks vs ALS point clouds) and need to test whether the cheaper/spaceborne dataset captures the same forest-structure information.

name: fpkm-abundance-file-parsing
description: Use when the input consists of multiple per-sample gene abundance/FPKM files (e.g., Cufflinks-style tabular gene output) that must be aligned by gene identifier and merged into one samples-and-genes matrix for downstream differential expression analysis.

name: fractional-gene-counting
description: Use when building per-gene abundance tables from hit-filtered DIAMOND read-to-gene alignments ( e-value hits per read) and you need MetaLAFFA-compatible fractional counts for reads tied across multiple genes.

name: fractional-ortholog-abundance-counting
description: Use when starting from a per-sample, gene-length-normalized gene abundance table plus a many-to-many gene-to-ortholog mapping, and the goal is a KO-level functional profile.

name: frequency-cutoff-filtering-of-polymorphisms
description: Use when estimating the fraction of adaptive substitutions (α) from DAF/polymorphism and divergence counts and slightly deleterious rare variants must be excluded to avoid biasing α downward.

name: functional-category-differential-abundance-analysis
description: Use when aggregated functional-category summary files exist for multiple metatranscriptome samples in control vs. experimental groups and you need to identify significantly differing functions with adjusted p-values and fold changes.

name: functional-frequency-aggregation-across-samples
description: Use when you have a per-sample gene frequency table and KO assignments for the gene catalog, and need per-sample counts aggregated at KO, EC number, and reaction levels for downstream compositional analysis.

name: functional-gene-reference-set-evaluation
description: Use when a curated reference gene set (e.g., amoA-AOB from Fungene v9.6) and candidate primer pairs exist, and you must quantify which subset size achieves maximum in silico amplification coverage relative to published primers.

name: functional-group-community-ordination
description: Use when presence-absence species composition data are available for multiple plots and per-plot community-composition response variables (e.g. NMDS1/NMDS2 site scores) are needed for taxa or functional groups.

name: functional-hierarchy-annotation-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating or comparing annotation accuracy of metatranscriptome pipelines on simulated data with known ground-truth organism and function labels, e.g. reproducing SAMSA2's ~95% genus-level accuracy benchmark vs SAMSA 1.0.

name: functional-profile-table-generation
description: Use when a MetaLAFFA (or similar KO-based) analysis needs corrected KO abundances rolled up into higher-level KEGG functional categories and written as final TSV functional profile tables.

name: fungal-abundance-association-analysis
description: Use when you have a fungal taxonomic or functional abundance feature table (e.g., FunOMIC-T/FunOMIC-P profiles) joined to sample metadata and need to find which species associate with variables like country, body site, or disease cohort.

name: fungal-bacterial-taxonomic-profile-harmonization
description: Use when paired fungal and bacterial taxonomic abundance tables (e.g. FunOMIC-T output and MetaPhlAn profiles) from the same metagenomes must be subset to matched cohorts and combined for inter-kingdom correlation analysis.

name: fungal-database-specificity-assessment
description: Use when validating that a fungal marker-gene database does not falsely map bacterial sequencing reads — i.e., you need a specificity metric for a taxonomic profiler before applying it to mixed metagenomic samples.

name: fungal-detection-rate-summary-statistics
description: Use when profiling fungal taxonomic presence across a large cohort of human shotgun metagenomes and you need cohort-level detection rates and per-species prevalence tables (e.g. prevalence of S. cerevisiae across thousands of samples).

name: fungal-functional-profiling
description: Use when performing fungal functional profiling of shotgun metagenomic reads against the FunOMIC-P protein database, especially when distinguishing fungal signal from dominant bacterial backgrounds.

name: fungal-marker-gene-read-mapping
description: Use when shotgun metagenomic FASTQ samples need fungal taxonomic profiling (species detection rates, prevalence, abundance tables) via read mapping to a curated fungal marker-gene database rather than ITS amplicon-style analysis.

name: fungal-protein-database-alignment
description: Use when metagenomic sequencing reads must be assigned fungal functions via a fungal protein database, and the Diamond blastx threshold combination (identity, read coverage, e-value) needs to be selected or applied for fungal functional profiling.

name: fungal-single-copy-marker-gene-identification
description: Use when constructing a fungal taxonomic marker-gene database from a pool of assembled, quality-filtered fungal genomes (e.g., ~4,839 NCBI/JGI MycoCosm genomes) and you need per-genome single-copy ortholog extraction and redundancy removal.

name: fungal-taxonomic-database-construction
description: Use when building a strain/species-level fungal taxonomic reference database for read-mapping mycobiome profiling from NCBI/JGI fungal genome assemblies.

name: gamlss-bezi-differential-abundance-testing
description: Use when testing between-group differences in microbiome taxon relative abundances (phylum–genus levels) from compositional data with many zeros, especially with covariate adjustment and repeated-measures/longitudinal designs.

name: gamlss-bezi-longitudinal-modeling
description: Use when testing differential relative abundances of taxa between groups (e.g. diarrhea vs. no diarrhea, breastfeeding status, gender) in microbiome relative abundance tables with covariate adjustment and repeated samples per subject.

name: gamma-distribution-maximum-likelihood-fitting
description: Use when building or reproducing the Glimmer-MG gene-length model: you have annotated ORF lengths (e.g. from a GenBank/FASTA genome annotation) and need a blended coding/non-coding length distribution to score ORF lengths, especially for truncated genes on short metagenomic reads.

name: gapped-local-sequence-alignment
description: Use when clustering protein sequence sets at thresholds like --min-seq-id 0.9 --cov-mode 1 -c 0.9 and survivors of the k-mer, Hamming, and ungapped filters must be verified with exact gapped local alignments before greedy incremental clustering.

name: gc-content-and-uncalled-base-interpretation
description: Use when comparing de novo assemblies (e.g. ABySS, Velvet, SPAdes, MEGAHIT contigs in FASTA) and QUAST's report.tsv G+C content or # N's per 100 kbp columns are needed to detect contamination, divergence from the expected organismal G+C range, or uncalled-base problems.

name: gene-absence-confidence-statistics
description: Use when a presence/absence analysis calls a gene absent in lineages represented mainly by draft bins — especially when completeness estimates (e.g. ≥75% single-copy genes, ≤1.125 copies) are available and you must decide if the absence call is trustworthy.

name: gene-abundance-and-prevalence-quantification
description: Use when a set of clustered gene representatives must be prioritized by how abundant and how widespread they are across a defined collection of metagenomes, e.g. to select representative amoA-AOB clusters from soil metagenomes for primer design.

name: gene-based-similarity-screening
description: Use when constructing a non-redundant species pan-genome reference from predicted genes, or when assigning human-microbiome metagenomic contigs to reference taxa by -match gene similarity to pick a gene prediction model.

name: gene-by-gene-allele-profile-filtering
description: Use when you have a chewBBACA AlleleCall results_alleles.tsv profile matrix over a strain collection and need to define the core-genome (cgMLST) locus set at a presence threshold such as 95%.

name: gene-catalogue-expansion-quantification
description: Use when comparing a newly built non-redundant gene catalogue against a published one (e.g. VMGC-90 vs VIRGO-90) to report bidirectional coverage fractions and protein-space expansion.

name: gene-catalogue-mapping-rate-quantification
description: Use when benchmarking the read-capture efficiency of a gene catalogue (e.g., VMGC-90 vs VIRGO) by aligning clean metagenomic reads and computing per-sample mapping rates.

name: gene-cluster-adjacency-graph-construction
description: Use when you have VAMB-derived gene cluster assignments plus ORF sequences retaining per-contig gene ordering, and you want to group gene clusters into synteny clusters based on genomic adjacency to infer shared pathways.

name: gene-cluster-coverage-quantification
description: Use when you need to benchmark primer-set sensitivity against a curated reference gene set, e.g., recomputing the 94% (MetaFunPrimer) vs 49% (published) amoA-AOB coverage or per-cluster coverage like cluster 3 at 96% vs 19%.

name: gene-content-prediction-accuracy-assessment
description: Use when validating phylogeny-based gene-family prediction accuracy on genomes with known annotations, e.g. measuring per-genome and per-functional-category accuracy of PICRUSt predictions from a KO/COG reference table and a 16S marker-gene tree.

name: gene-copy-number-correction
description: Use when amplicon (16S/18S rRNA) or microarray profiles in biom, QIIME, GAAS, Unifrac, or generic tabular format with read counts and unaltered Greengenes taxonomic assignments must be corrected for GCN bias, or when qPCR total abundances need correction.

name: gene-copy-number-tree-annotation
description: Use when you have GCN trait estimates for Greengenes OTUs/taxa plus the Greengenes phylogeny or taxonomy, and need to quantify how strongly GCN tracks phylogeny (e.g. Pagel's lambda) before inferring GCN for unsequenced lineages.

name: gene-count-matrix-merging
description: Use when you hold one two-column gene abundance file per sample (gene identifier + raw count, or gene identifier + FPKM) and need a single merged matrix to feed differential expression tools like DESeq2Shiny.

name: gene-count-qc-verification
description: Use when reproducing or validating gene catalog construction counts — e.g. after running MetaGeneMark CDS prediction or after BLASTP/Jaccard de-redundification — to check totals and per-source partitions against published VIRGO values.

name: gene-database-inclusion-filtering
description: Use when combining multiple reference gene collections (e.g. ResFinder, CARD, MegaRes, AMRFinderPlus, ARGANNOT, ResFinderFG) into one non-redundant database and you need reproducible source-specific inclusion filters plus identity/coverage-based clustering.

name: gene-family-abundance-inference
description: Use when you have an ASV/OTU abundance table plus a FASTA of marker-gene study sequences and need inferred functional profiles (EC gene families, MetaCyc pathways) without shotgun metagenomics data.

name: gene-family-content-prediction
description: Use when a workflow needs predicted gene family content for unsequenced taxa on a 16S marker gene reference tree, e.g. preparing the pre-calculated PICRUSt gene content file before metagenome inference.

name: gene-identifier-alignment-across-samples
description: Use when you have one tabular gene abundance file per sample (FPKM or count files with genes in the first column) and need a single merged csv matrix keyed on gene identifiers for downstream bulk RNA-seq analysis.

name: gene-identifier-key-joining
description: Use when you hold multiple per-sample two-column gene count files (gene identifier, raw count) that must be combined into one gene x sample matrix before downstream RNA-seq analysis.

name: gene-length-annotation
description: Use when building or extending the VIRGO non-redundant gene catalog and you need per-gene CDS predictions and gene lengths in bp from assembled metagenomic contigs or isolate genome sequences.

name: gene-length-normalization
description: Use when a mapped gene frequency count table (reads per gene across samples) is the input and gene-level abundances must be compared across samples; long genes systematically accumulate more reads, biasing downstream normalization.

name: gene-length-normalization
description: Reference for computing per-gene abundances from read-to-gene alignment hits when reads may match multiple genes equally well, and when gene-length bias in shotgun metagenomic count data must be corrected.

name: gene-level-microdiversity-profiling
description: Use when mapping metagenomic reads of a co-occurring strain (e.g. phage 482_10.ph) back to its own reference and you need per-gene coverage, SNP types, and dN/dS to test whether within-individual diversity overlaps between-individual variation.

name: gene-level-versus-functional-level-differential-analysis
description: Decision support for choosing annotation level (gene vs KO/EC/reaction) when reporting differential abundance results from case-control metagenomic count data.

name: gene-list-over-representation-analysis
description: Use when you have a list of differentially expressed genes (e.g. DESeq2 output with gene name/id, log2 fold change, and p-adjusted values) and want to test whether GO terms or KEGG pathways are over-represented, with multiple-testing correction.

name: gene-ontology-annotation-similarity-computation
description: Use when you need to assess the functional coherence of protein sequence clusters (e.g., produced by Linclust, UCLUST, CD-HIT) via GO or Pfam annotation agreement.

name: gene-prediction-accuracy-evaluation
description: Use when comparing gene caller output (e.g., Glimmer-MG predictions) to known gene coordinates from GenBank reference genomes or simulated metagenomes, to quantify sensitivity and precision per tool, read length, or error rate.

name: gene-prediction-accuracy-evaluation
description: Use when you need to quantify and compare gene prediction accuracy across gene finders on metagenome assemblies, using a reference annotation to count missed genes, start-site errors, or nucleotide Sn/Sp.

name: gene-prediction-error-counting
description: Use when benchmarking a new gene prediction tool's start-codon accuracy against reference GeneMarkS-2 annotations and you need per-group error counts split by regulatory signal class (canonical RBS, non-canonical RBS, leaderless).

name: gene-prediction-model-selection
description: Use when annotating assembled human microbiome metagenome contigs and you must choose gene prediction parameters per contig, assigning contigs to species-level pan-genomes or routing unmatched contigs to fallback algorithms.

name: gene-prediction-open-reading-frame-calling
description: Use when assembled contigs or long-read sequences must be annotated with predicted ORFs before exclusion-based viral classification, e.g., after SPAdes/metaSPAdes/MEGAHIT assembly or when loading contigs via virMine's -A option.

name: gene-prediction-runtime-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing computational cost or database footprint of gene finders on metagenomic contigs, or when reproducing the GeneMark-HM efficiency results (12 min on 45 Mb, ~80% in BLASTn, 15x pan-genome reduction).

name: gene-presence-absence-feature-modeling
description: Use when the goal is to predict microbial phenotypic traits (e.g. gram-negative status, spore formation, phototrophy) from COG presence/absence profiles, especially for incomplete metagenomic genome bins rather than finished reference genomes.

name: gene-sequence-truncation-simulation
description: Use when you need to benchmark HMM-based annotation-recovery tools (e.g. KEMET with --hmm_mode onebm) against fragmented or partial gene sequences that mimic gapped metagenome-assembled genome (MAG) assemblies.

name: gene-set-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when analyzing PICRUSt2 KO/predicted functional abundance tables and pathway-set (KEGG pathway) level enrichment signals are more appropriate than single-feature differential abundance testing.

name: gene-set-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when a researcher has a differential gene expression table (e.g. DESeq2 output with gene id, log2 fold change, adjusted p-value) and needs to identify enriched GO terms or KEGG pathways without writing R code.

name: gene-start-annotation-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating gene start prediction accuracy of metagenomic gene finders on complete genomes and you need error counts stratified by the translation initiation signal (canonical RBS, non-canonical RBS, leaderless) identified upstream of reference starts.

name: gene-synteny-cluster-inference-from-contig-adjacency
description: Use when you have VAMB clusters.tsv, assembled contigs and reads from a metagenomics run and want to group genes into synteny clusters by contig adjacency, then attach eggNOG-mapper KEGG/GO/Pfam annotations to assess intra-cluster functional agreement.

name: gene-taxa-link-analysis
description: Use when a case-control gene association test has flagged disease-associated genes (e.g. from KEGG/UniRef90-based gene analysis of SCZ metagenomes) and you need a gene-to-taxon attribution by tracing sequencing reads back to source organisms.

name: generalization-evaluation-on-unseen-labels
description: Use when quantifying how a hierarchical taxonomic classifier generalizes to species labels absent from its training vocabulary — e.g., after training on Greengenes2 2024.09 and evaluating on the 69,335-sequence held-out test set.

name: generalized-linear-model-association-testing
description: Use when testing association between a microbial taxa-set (e.g. ≥5 taxa at genus/family/order/class/phylum level) and a continuous or binary outcome, where most taxa in the clade are noise and a data-adaptive multivariate GLM test with permutation calibration is needed.

name: generalized-suffix-array-lcp-construction
description: Use when a reference-free variant-discovery workflow (e.g. ebwt2snp-style positional clustering) requires the LCP array and generalized Suffix Array of a FASTA/FASTQ read collection, or when benchmarking disk/RAM footprint of GSA+LCP pipelines against BWT-only ones.

name: genome-annotation-parsing-with-biopython
description: Use when the input is a complete genome annotation (GenBank .gbff/.gbk plus FASTA, e.g. Deinococcus radiodurans R1) and the goal is to extract all annotated CDS/ORF lengths or adjacent-gene features for fitting a gene-length distribution model.

name: genome-assembly-gap-statistics
description: Use when a draft assembly contains N-wildcard gaps between contigs in scaffold sequences and the goal is to close them with short-read data (e.g. GAGE PE datasets) and quantify remaining gap content.

name: genome-assembly-n50-calculation
description: Use when a released genome assembly (contig/scaffold FASTA files) needs its reported statistics — contig N50, scaffold N50, and coverage against a reference genome — independently reproduced and validated.

name: genome-assembly-quality-assessment
description: Use when FASTA contig files from one or more genome assemblers need multifaceted quality assessment and comparison, with or without a reference genome, as in the four E. coli K-12 MG1655 assembly evaluation.

name: genome-catalog-metrics-extraction
description: Use when a metagenomic binning study reports genome yields (e.g. complete vs draft counts) and you need to reproduce or extract the per-category, per-phylum breakdown from abstract text, tables, or supplementary tables.

name: genome-cluster-count-validation
description: Use when a paper reports a species-level genome bin count (e.g. 786 SGBs from 19,542 prokaryotic genomes at 95% ANI) and you must reproduce the clustering from the deposited genome FASTAs to verify it.

name: genome-completeness-categorization-checkm-prokka
description: Use when final cleaned scaffold FASTAs from hybrid metagenome assemblies (e.g. MetaPlatanus, metaFlye, MEGAHIT, OPERA-MS on 18 human gut samples with >1 Gbp ONT plus Illumina paired-end reads) must be categorized as over-half or near-complete bacterial genomes for assembler benchmarking.

name: genome-completeness-contamination-estimation
description: Use when you have a set of metagenome-assembled genomes (FASTA files) and need per-genome completeness/contamination estimates plus a defensible quality-tier classification (e.g. medium/high/near-complete) before downstream analyses.

name: genome-completeness-marker-filtering
description: Use when a COG presence/absence feature matrix (e.g. 97 genomes x 30,455 COGs) is being prepared for trait-prediction training and each genome must pass a marker-COG completeness screen before model fitting.

name: genome-completeness-prior-simulation
description: Use when you need to benchmark or stress-test a core-genome estimator (e.g. mOTUpan) against simulated MAG/SAG incompleteness, or quantify how low-completeness genomes bias core-gene calls and bootstrap false-positive rates.

name: genome-completeness-rarefaction
description: Use when you need to validate a core-genome prediction made on genomes of heterogeneous completeness (e.g. MAGs with CheckM completeness priors) by simulating synthetic genomes degraded to match the incompleteness of the real input set.

name: genome-completeness-simulation
description: Use when metagenomic bins or otherwise incomplete genomes must be scored with trait classifiers, and you need to quantify how much balanced accuracy degrades as genome completeness drops before trusting predictions on partial input.

name: genome-cover-recurrence-modeling
description: Use when sam alignments against the WoL reference database contain low-coverage hits that may be reference-overlap artifacts, and you need a model-predicted versus observed genome cover comparison to judge whether hits are true contaminants or spurious.

name: genome-cover-thresholding
description: Use when short shotgun reads spuriously map to short common motifs or transposable elements against a large reference (e.g., Web of Life), creating ambiguous low-coverage false positives that per-sample coverage cannot resolve because shotgun sequencing is shallow.

name: genome-coverage-profile-computation-from-assigned-reads
description: Use when metagenomic reads (e.g., paired-end FASTQ such as KLyo_C) have been classified against a reference database and you need per-genome window coverage profiles to identify false-positive candidate genomes before final taxonomic assignment.

name: genome-database-construction
description: Use when you have FASTA genome files (public references plus MAGs) with a table of source associations (e.g., cow, pig, dog, sewage) and need a formatted database to run sourceapp.py for metagenomic fecal source tracking.

name: genome-de-novo-assembly
description: Use when you have Illumina short reads (FASTA/FASTQ/BAM, paired-end or mate-pair) from a genome project and need a draft assembly (contigs and scaffold sequences) evaluated by N50 and error rates.

name: genome-equivalent-abundance-normalization
description: Use when per-genome mapped read counts/sequence depths (e.g. CoverM genome-mode output against source-associated genome databases) must be converted into genome-equivalent cell fractions for metagenomic fecal source tracking or apportionment.

name: genome-equivalent-cell-fraction-estimation
description: Use when shotgun metagenomic reads from water samples must be converted into per-source cell-fraction estimates for fecal source attribution and apportionment, and genome-equivalent normalization is needed to compare summed sequence depth across source categories.

name: genome-exclusion-benchmark-database-construction
description: Use when benchmarking taxonomic classifiers on genera underrepresented in reference databases via leave-one-genome-out protein/k-mer databases and simulated reads (Illumina/Roche-454).

name: genome-fraction-and-duplication-ratio-computation
description: Use when one or more genome assemblies (FASTA contigs) must be scored against a known reference genome to quantify how much of the reference is covered and whether contigs redundantly cover the same regions.

name: genome-fraction-benchmark-analysis
description: Use when a Quast/metaQuast genome-fraction table comparing StrainXpress against IDBA-UD, SPAdes, Minia3 and MEGAHIT across benchmark metagenome data sets must be turned into per-dataset and aggregate gain statistics.

name: genome-fraction-misassembly-quantification
description: Use when comparing metagenomic assembler outputs (FASTA contigs from tools like MetaCortex, MEGAHIT, metaSPAdes, Ray Meta) and you need per-reference genome fraction and misassembly counts to rank assemblers quantitatively.

name: genome-graph-scalability-benchmarking
description: Use when you need to quantify how a graph-based pangenome pipeline scales with panel size, e.g. testing whether graph construction and traversal tools remain tractable at 5,000–20,000 genome scale.

name: genome-lineage-phylogenetic-assignment
description: Use when genome bins (draft or complete, e.g., CPR/TM6) must be assigned to lineages via 16S rRNA gene or rp16 concatenated ribosomal protein phylogeny, especially before building lineage-level presence/absence matrices.

name: genome-mutation-simulation-with-known-ani
description: Use when benchmarking ANI/strain-comparison tools (inStrain popANI, dRep, MIDAS, StrainPhlAn) on synthetic data where the ground-truth ANI between genomes is known by construction.

name: genome-quality-filtering
description: Use when curating a set of reference genomes (e.g., NCBI/JGI assemblies) prior to extracting marker genes, to discard assemblies that are too fragmented or too incomplete to yield reliable single-copy markers.

name: genome-region-binning-and-indexing
description: Use when a pipeline needs homologous genomic regions extracted per sample from metagenomic assemblies relative to a reference genome, prior to pairwise synteny or strain-comparison scoring.

name: genome-scale-metabolic-model-reconstruction
description: Use when draft GSMMs built from metagenome-assembled genomes underpredict metabolic phenotypes (e.g. missing exchange reactions) and you want to recover missing KOs with HMM searches and evidence-based gapfilling before flux analysis.

name: genome-scale-sequence-screening
description: Use when you must detect and type Dsr-dependent dissimilatory sulphur metabolism proteins across thousands of complete genomes or (meta)genomic protein records on a personal computer, without reconstructing phylogenies or running blast-based marker searches.

name: genome-signature-characterization
description: Use when characterizing plasmid vs. chromosome sequence sets by %G+C content and length (e.g. reproducing PlasFlow's RefSeq training-set statistics) or checking whether a nucleotide FASTA dataset matches reported composition properties.

name: genome-signature-plasmid-prediction
description: Use when metagenomic or genome assembly contigs (ideally >1000 bp, FASTA) must be labelled plasmid vs chromosome without prior knowledge of sample taxonomic composition, e.g. plasmidome profiling of environmental assemblies.

name: genome-size-metric-recording
description: Use when reproducing or reporting genome yield tables (complete vs draft bin counts) and per-phylum distributions of curated genomes from metagenomic binning results.

name: genome-skimming-marker-retrieval
description: Use when you need to mine single-copy nuclear markers (e.g., OrthoDB USCOs) for phylogenomics from genome-skimming (LC-WGS) data provided as Illumina short reads or de novo contigs, especially at coverages of 1x–40x.

name: genome-wide-alpha-distribution-comparison
description: Use when you need to test whether a biologically defined subset of protein-coding genes (e.g. by recombination rate bin or chromosome localization) shows a different alpha than the genome-wide gene set, using DAF and divergence tables.

name: genome-wide-orf-counting-acquisition-modes
description: Use when benchmarking genome-mining candidate generation on a genome set (e.g., 36 ACTI RefSeq FASTA assemblies) where you need per-genome BGC and RiPP counts from antiSMASH plus short-ORF candidate counts under both motif-ORF and all-ORF modes.

name: genome-wide-scaffold-aggregation
description: Use when you have inStrain profile output per sample (computed against concatenated representative sub-species .fasta references) and need per-sub-species genome-level microdiversity metrics (e.g. nucleotide diversity of Klebsiella) for group-level comparison such as birth mode.

name: genomic-epidemiology-reporting
description: Use when in-silico virulence/typing gene calls from sequencing reads must be validated against PCR or another phenotypic reference across a clinical isolate cohort, with per-isolate concordance reported.

name: genomic-overlap-merging
description: Use when a viral scaffold FASTA may contain redundant/overlapping sequences from fragmented genome assemblies and a dereplicated representative set is required before binning.

name: genomic-reference-library-processing
description: Use when building a Kraken-compatible taxonomy database from NCBI RefSeq complete microbial genomes so that exact k-mer lookups resolve to specific taxon IDs for metagenomic classification.

name: genomic-region-sequence-handling
description: Use when you need per-region pairwise comparisons of homologous sequences (e.g., BLAST-derived region bins from metagenomic assemblies) quantified as synteny scores rather than SNP distances.

name: genomic-sequence-composition-analysis
description: Use when designing k-mer-based sequence detectors and you need to choose the k-mer length k: sweep k over a candidate range and compute the analytical false-positive rate of spurious k-mer occurrence for given target/non-target sequence lengths.

name: genomic-sequence-preprocessing
description: Use when computing background-adjusted alignment-free measures (CVtree, D2star, D2shepp) on genomic FASTA files or NGS shotgun reads and the Markov model order encoding the sequence is unknown to the user.

name: genomic-sequence-retrieval-ncbi
description: Use when a downstream analysis (e.g. LCS cross-contamination ROC curves or Bowtie2 alignment for read recruitment) requires the exact NCBI RefSeq viral genomes cited by accession, such as NC_003977.2 or NC_004102.1.

name: genomic-vs-metagenomic-assembler-group-comparison
description: Use when LMAS global/per-reference metric tables from mock metagenomic communities (e.g. ZymoBIOMICS evenly/logarithmically distributed, in silico or real) are available and the goal is to test whether assembler branding predicts performance.

name: genotype-file-format-conversion
description: Use when input genotype data are VCF files (chromosome-split and tabix-indexed) but the target analysis requires PLINK binary BED format, or when chromosome IDs must be recoded to integers for tools like ADMIXTURE and Eigensoft smartpca.

name: genotype-phenotype-association-interpretation
