description: Use when a trained Traitar phenotype model (phypat or phypat+PGL) yields a ranked list of phenotype-relevant Pfam families and you need to assign biological meaning, accessions, and phenotype-to-family mappings for a trait of interest.

name: genotype-phenotype-concordance-analysis
description: Use when you have per-sample predicted resistance calls in JSON from Mykrobe predictor plus phenotypic DST labels and need sensitivity/specificity per antibiotic, or when reproducing error tables like St_B1's 99.1%/99.6% or minor-allele sensitivity deltas.

name: genotype-phenotype-inference-assessment
description: Use when you need to assess the accuracy of phenotype prediction from bacterial genomes, e.g., computing per-phylum accuracies of phypat vs. phypat+PGL on pooled GIDEON cross-validation predictions for phyla covered by at least five species.

name: genus-level-sensitivity-precision-evaluation
description: Use when comparing metagenomic sequence classifiers on the same read sets and you need genus-level sensitivity/precision tables, or when quantifying accuracy loss from a reduced Kraken database such as MiniKraken 4-GB or Kraken-GB.

name: genus-level-taxonomic-aggregation
description: Use when benchmarking a metagenomic read classifier on genome-exclusion simulations where the true source genome is known, and per-read calls must be summarized into genus-/phylum-level sensitivity and precision stratified by reference-genome availability.

name: genus-level-taxonomic-aggregation
description: Use when OTU-level networks inferred from a genus-annotatable counts table show unstable node identities across methods, and the analysis goal is to quantify shared nodes/edges (e.g., UpSet intersections) at a coarser taxonomic rank.

name: genus-variable-importance-ranking
description: Use when a survival (time-to-event) analysis needs genus-level predictors ranked by predictive influence, e.g., identifying which gut microbial genera most strongly predict time-to-T1D-onset in a treatment subgroup.

name: giab-variant-benchmarking
description: Use when you have variant calls (VCF) from multiple strategies — e.g. FreeBayes/SvABA on Illumina BAMs, Long Ranger on 10x Linked-Reads, or calling directly from Supernova2 assemblies — and need to score them against GIAB truth sets.

name: gibbs-sampler-clustering-of-sequencing-reads
description: Use when error-prone shotgun or amplicon NGS reads (e.g. 454 Titanium pyrosequencing of HIV-1 pol) aligned to a reference must be partitioned into local-haplotype clusters to correct sequencing errors before quantifying genetic diversity.

name: gibbs-sampler-convergence-tuning
description: Use when running diri_sampler-based error correction on overlapping windows of a read alignment (BAM/CRAM or MSA) and you must set sampler iterations and the Dirichlet hyperparameter alpha to achieve proper mixing for haplotype reconstruction.

name: glcm-texture-feature-extraction
description: Use when Sentinel-1 gamma_0 backscatter stacks (e.g. ALB_gamma0_VH.tif / ALB_gamma0_VV.tif) must be converted into spatial-heterogeneity texture predictor variables for habitat-structure or biodiversity modelling on a 10 m grid.

name: global-assembly-metrics-computation
description: Use when you have paired-end metagenomic FASTQ reads from a defined mock community plus reference replicons, and need comparable global assembly quality metrics across multiple assemblers.

name: glv-network-simulation
description: Use when a ground-truth interaction network is required to score co-occurrence inference — e.g. simulating synthetic abundance tables with seqtime gLV or Klemm-Eguiluz dynamics before running MiCoNE network inference or consensus methods.

name: glv-trajectory-simulation
description: Use when you need synthetic ground-truth longitudinal trajectories of taxa abundances (e.g., 16 taxa over 56 days or 17 taxa over 65 days) on which to overlay sequencing noise for benchmarking reconstruction methods.

name: gnps-dataset-acquisition-and-curation
description: Use when reproducing or extending the MetaMiner peptidogenomics pipeline and you need to identify which GNPS MSVxxxxxx accessions have paired genomic/metagenomic data (e.g. MSV000079506, MSV000079622, MSV000078839, MSV000078604, MSV000078552, MSV000080102) and stage them for RiPP search.

name: gnps-molecular-networking-job-configuration
description: Use when a large collection of tandem mass spectra (e.g., ~10M MS/MS spectra across eight GNPS datasets such as MSV000079506 or MSV000080102) must be clustered into spectral families via pairwise spectral similarity before or after spectral library searches.
tools: GNPS (Global Natural Products Social molecular networking)

name: go-term-enrichment-annotation
description: Use when a differential expression result (e.g., a DESeq2 output table with gene name/id, log2 fold change, and padj) needs functional interpretation via enriched GO terms and KEGG pathways.

name: gold-standard-matrix-scoring
description: Use when evaluating a text-mining extraction system that outputs a taxon-by-character matrix over a fixed character set (e.g. the 42 MicroPIE phenotypic characters) and a curated gold standard matrix is available.

name: goodness-of-fit-measure-computation
description: Reference for computing pairwise taxa–taxa correlation strength (R) and per-taxa goodness-of-fit (R²) from a taxa-by-sample 16S abundance data frame, before estimating rho for taxa–SNP correlation in mbQTL.

name: goodness-of-fit-statistics-computation
description: Use when benchmark timing data must be characterized by a scaling law — e.g. verifying claimed algorithmic complexity (O(n^2) vs O(n)) from measured runtimes of CATHAI graph generation.

name: gpt-batch-graph-configuration
description: Use when raw Sentinel-1 GRDH IW products (uncalibrated DN in slant-range coordinates) must be converted to comparable gamma0 backscatter rasters, and a reproducible SNAP batch configuration file is provided.

name: gpu-checkpoint-inference-pytorch
description: Use when you need to extract internal fused embeddings or predictions from a published DeepTaxa .pt checkpoint with PyTorch, e.g., for embedding-space visualization or quantitative cluster-structure analysis.

name: gpu-mixed-precision-inference
description: Use when classifying 16S rRNA FASTA sequences (full-length ~1,500 bp or in-silico V3–V4 ~420 bp amplicons) with a released DeepTaxa checkpoint on a CUDA GPU, where per-rank predictions and accuracy/F1/ECE metrics are required.

name: gpu-versus-cpu-inference-timing
description: Use when comparing wall-clock inference/prediction runtime of a DNN contact predictor against an ECA baseline (CCMpred) across CPU and GPU on a fixed, pre-computed-MSA protein set such as the 150 PSICOV proteins.

name: graph-clustering-coefficient-analysis
description: Use when metagenomic viral scaffolds have already been pair-classified by machine learning (vRhyme_machine_distances.tsv with distance/effect-size values) and you need to convert those pairs into unrefined weighted-network bins and refine them into vMAGs.

name: greedy-incremental-sequence-clustering
description: Use when you need to partition a large protein sequence set (e.g. UniProt-scale, hundreds of millions of sequences) into redundancy-reduced clusters after a k-mer prefilter and alignment steps have produced verified edges.

name: greedy-inexact-match-classification-tuning
description: Use when classifying FASTQ/FASTA metagenomic reads with Kaiju's Greedy mode and you must tune mismatch allowance, match length/score cutoffs, or E-value filtering to balance sensitivity and precision against k-mer classifiers like Kraken (k=31).

name: greedy-seed-extension-algorithm-design
description: Use when implementing or modifying inexact-match search in a BWT/FM-index-based metagenomic classifier, specifically seeding with exact MEMs and extending with BLOSUM62-scored substitutions at match ends under a score threshold.

name: greengenes-lineage-data-parsing
description: Use when an OTU or taxon table needs lineage-specific 16S rRNA GCN values attached from CopyRighter's Greengenes data files, or when Greengenes taxstrings/IDs must be parsed to look up trait values.

name: greengenes-taxonomy-otu-profiling
description: Use when building OTU/taxonomic abundance profiles from 16S amplicon data (biom, QIIME, GAAS, Unifrac or generic site-by-species tables of read counts) that will subsequently undergo lineage-specific GCN correction with CopyRighter.

name: greengenes2-test-set-analysis
description: Use when you have DeepTaxa (or any 16S rRNA classifier) species predictions on a held-out test set plus the training FASTA, and you need to diagnose whether low species-level scores are driven by low similarity to training sequences rather than model failure.

name: ground-truth-accuracy-evaluation
description: Use when you need to quantify clustering accuracy (ACC) of iDeLUCS output against known cluster labels, e.g. reproducing the 98.5% (given k) or 97.3% (HDBSCAN auto-k) synthetic-dataset results or benchmarking excluded regimes.

name: ground-truth-cell-fraction-comparison
description: Use when you have SourceApp attribution outputs for spike-in mesocosms of known composition and need to score per-source sensitivity/specificity against Table S1 ground truth cellular fractions, e.g. to reproduce the finding that cow is the worst-performing source.

name: ground-truth-posthoc-label-evaluation
description: Use when you have clustered unlabeled DNA sequences from a FASTA file and possess a ground-truth TSV with 'cluster_id' labels that must be used only for posthoc scoring of intrinsic and external clustering metrics.

name: ground-truth-precision-sensitivity-evaluation
description: Use when you have synthetic abundance tables with known ground-truth interaction networks and need to quantify how precisely an inference or consensus method (e.g., MiCoNE scaled_sum) recovers true associations.

name: group-diversity-comparison-visualization
description: Use when comparing microbial composition between treatment groups (e.g., control vs tylosin) with covariate adjustment — computing multiple alpha/beta diversity metrics on a rarefied feature table and rendering group-comparison figures.

name: group-level-statistical-aggregation
description: Use when LMAS per-reference metric tables (Contiguity, Multiplicity, Validity, Parsimony, Identity, Breadth of coverage, Lx, NAx, NGx) must be collapsed from individual-assembler to assembler-group level to test group-level performance claims.

name: group-permutation-null-distribution-generation
description: Use when performing adaptive multi-marker meta-analysis (aMeta) on effect estimates and standard errors from multiple related markers across studies, and a null distribution for the minimum p-value statistic must be generated without prior marker-by-marker correlations.

name: group-permutation-sign-flipping-pvalue-estimation
description: Use when combining multiple studies (>=10) across related markers from effect estimates and standard errors only, with no a priori marker-by-marker correlations, and a semi-parametric null is preferred over parametric asymptotic normality.

name: grouped-frequency-table-statistics
description: Use when you have normalized five-level frequency tables (taxon, gene, KO, EC number, reaction) from CAMAMED's med_pipeline and need to find features that differ significantly across two or more sample groups.

name: gsc-mag-quality-criteria-application
description: Use when you have a CheckM2 quality_report.tsv for metagenomic bins and need to assign each bin a GSC-based quality label (near complete/high/medium/low) and summarize counts per category.

name: gtdb-to-ncbi-taxonomy-conversion
description: Use when GTDBtk (v1.0.2) classifications of MAGs or genomes must be compared against NCBI-taxonomy-based ground truth (e.g., HMP genome labels or CAMI taxonomies), because GTDBtk outputs use GTDB taxonomy.

name: gtdbtk-genome-taxonomy-assignment
description: Use when you have assembled and binned MAG FASTA files with BUSCO quality summaries and need GTDB lineage assignments per bin, with a fallback classifier for bins that fail quality gates.

name: gtf-annotation-coordinate-projection
description: Use when a GTF/GFF annotation built on a linear reference genome must be lifted onto a pangenome graph (constructed with VARI-merge, k=22) so gene regions can be located via cSupB bubble coordinates.

name: gwas-summary-statistics-pathway-enrichment
description: Use when GWAS summary statistics are available and the goal is pathway-level enrichment (PASCAL) followed by overlap testing against disease metagenome (MWAS) pathway enrichment at P<0.05.

name: gyra-resistance-snp-interpretation
description: Use when raw FASTQ reads (Illumina MiSeq or ONT MinION 2D) from the same bacterial isolate must yield comparable drug-resistance calls, and a single known SNP (gyrA S84L) is expected as the resistance determinant.

name: gzip-fastq-stream-processing
description: Use when raw or pooled long-read (ONT/PacBio) FASTQ.gz files must be filtered for minimum read length and average Phred quality before assembly or benchmarking, e.g. pre-processing ONT reads for Plassembler.

name: hadoop-mapreduce-job-benchmarking
description: Use when you must verify that a MapReduce-based analysis tool's runtime scales acceptably (linearly) with input volume, or when you need a per-metric/per-mode runtime breakdown to identify the most expensive computation.

name: hadoop-mapreduce-metagenomic-scoring
description: Use when you need an all-vs-all distance/similarity matrix across many metagenomic FASTA/FASTQ read sets where data reduction or presence/absence metrics (e.g., Mash sketches, Simka Jaccard-ab) lose clustering resolution by community composition and abundance.

name: hadoop-mapreduce-pipeline-execution
description: Use when you must run Libra's Hadoop indexing (preprocess) and scoring (core) stages on large FASTA/FASTQ metagenome collections to produce an all-vs-all cosine-similarity matrix, e.g., global-ocean virome comparisons.

name: hamming-distance-sequence-preclustering
description: Use when clustering large protein sequence sets (e.g., UniProt-scale FASTA) with Linclust/MMseqs2 and needing a fast, SIMD-vectorized exact-distance filter to prune center–member pairs after exact k-mer matching but before gapped alignment.

name: haplotype-phasing-snp-vcf
description: Use when downstream EHH-based scans (iHS, XP-EHH, SweepFinder2 inputs) require phased haplotypes but the input is unphased chromosome-split VCF files from biallelic SNP data.

name: harrell-davis-bootstrap-confidence-intervals
description: Use when performing multiple testing correction in metagenome-wide case-control association tests where an empirical null distribution of minimum P-values is built by permuting binary phenotype labels and the uncertainty of the resulting Psig threshold must be quantified.

name: hash-table-index-lookup
description: Use when converting matching seed hash values between a raw nanopore signal (FAST5/POD5/SLOW5/BLOW5) and a reference genome into a mapped region via hash-table lookup followed by colinear chaining of seed matches.

name: hashmap-based-sequence-clustering
description: Use when Illumina 16S rRNA amplicon FASTQ reads (primer-trimmed, paired, trimmed to 250 bases) need de novo variant calling, and one-mismatch child sequences must be grouped with abundant parents before error-rate modeling.

name: hazard-ratio-interpretation-microbiome-survival
description: Use when a time-to-event (survival) outcome must be associated with taxon-level microbial abundances (e.g., phylum CLR values), optionally covariate-adjusted and subgroup-stratified, yielding per-taxon hazard ratios.

name: hdf5-reference-matrix-querying
description: Use when finished MAG FASTA bins (or a multi-fasta with one header per MAG) need NCBI-taxonomic classification up to strain level without alignment, by matching their k-mer/minimizer profiles against an HDF5 reference storage matrix.

name: hdfs-data-management
description: Use when running MetaCacheSpark build or query jobs on a Hadoop/Spark cluster and the reference database or classification results must be shared across Spark executors via HDFS rather than a workstation-local filesystem.

name: hdfs-distributed-sequence-partitioning
description: Use when reference genome collections are too large for a single-machine k-mer/minhash database build and input FASTA sequences plus taxonomy already reside in HDFS on a Hadoop cluster with Spark 2.

name: heatmap-forest-plot-visualization
description: Use when pooled random-effects meta-analysis results (e.g. genderMale comparison of gut taxa across four studies) need to be visualized as side-by-side heatmaps of effect estimates and forest plots at phylum (level='main') or family/genus (level='sub') levels.

name: held-out-test-set-evaluation
description: Use when trained phenotype classifiers must be assessed on genomes that were held out from model training, to confirm cross-validation accuracy estimates (e.g. Traitar's 85.3%/86.7% macroaccuracy) generalize.

name: hellinger-distance-computation
description: Use when an observed 16S rRNA amplicon profile (uncorrected or CopyRighter-corrected) must be quantitatively compared to a mock community of known composition via Hellinger and euclidean distances to decide whether GCN correction improved accuracy.

name: heterogeneity-variance-estimation-random-effects-meta-analysis
description: Decision support for choosing and implementing the heterogeneity variance estimator (SJ vs DL) when meta-analyzing study-specific effect estimates and standard errors across multiple related markers, e.g. alpha-diversity indices.

name: heterogeneity-variance-estimation-sj
description: Use when combining multiple studies across multiple related markers (e.g., 6 α-diversity indices across 15 HIV microbiome studies) from study-by-marker effect estimates and standard errors, requiring a random effects heterogeneity variance estimator with no prior marker-by-marker correlations.

name: heterozygosity-and-titv-statistics-computation
description: Use when a filtered biallelic SNP dataset (VCF or PLINK BED) needs per-sample heterozygosity/homozygosity counts, Ti/Tv ratios, or population-level MAF and Ho/He summary statistics in defined genomic windows.

name: hg19-annotation-retrieval
description: Use when an analysis requires a curated set of human segmental duplication sequences from hg19, e.g. to measure how completely a de novo assembly represents published SD sequences.

name: hgt-breakpoint-detection
description: Use when paired-end shotgun metagenomics reads (e.g., HMP IBD data) are aligned against a bacterial reference set and the goal is to identify horizontal gene transfer breakpoint pairs before local strain reconstruction.

name: hgt-breakpoint-pair-position-matching
description: Use when candidate transferred segments from reconstructed HGT local strains must be scored against reference segments to compute segment similarity, breakpoint-match flags, and reconstruction accuracy (RAi in [0,1]).

name: hhblits-msa-construction
description: Use when a DNN contact-prediction or multitask pipeline (e.g. DeepECA) requires input MSAs for training or test proteins, or when constructing deliberately noisy MSAs to test robustness to metagenomic sequences.

name: hhblits-msa-generation
description: Use when a target protein is given as a FASTA sequence and a downstream covariance-matrix-based contact predictor (e.g. DeepECA) requires one MSA per protein as input.

name: hhblits-parameter-configuration
description: Use when a target protein FASTA must be converted into a high-quality MSA as input to covariance-matrix-based contact prediction, and HHblits run parameters (iterations, E-value, coverage, database path) need to be set.

name: hi-c-alignment-filtering
description: Use when raw Hi-C paired-end reads have been aligned to assembled contigs (BAM available) and downstream binning or graph construction requires a curated set of high-confidence inter-contig contact pairs.

name: hi-c-contact-graph-construction
description: Use when you have Hi-C paired-end read alignments (BAM sorted by name) to assembled contigs plus a list of identified viral contigs, and you need to bin viral contigs using virus-host proximity structure.

name: hic-alignment-contact-processing
description: Use when raw Hi-C paired-end and shotgun FASTQ reads must be converted into a name-sorted, filtered BAM aligned to assembled contigs before running a Hi-C-based binning pipeline such as ViralCC.

name: hic-contact-graph-construction
description: Use when assembling draft viral genomes (vMAGs) from metagenomic Hi-C data: you have assembled contigs (FASTA), a name-sorted Hi-C alignment BAM, and a viral contig list, and need contact/proximity graphs for binning.

name: hic-read-alignment-and-filtering
description: Use when raw paired-end metagenomic Hi-C FASTQ files must be preprocessed and aligned to assembled contigs to produce a name-sorted BAM for Hi-C-based binning.

name: hic-read-cleaning-with-bbduk-and-clumpify
description: Use when raw metagenomic Hi-C paired-end FASTQ reads must be cleaned before assembly/alignment or before Hi-C library quality assessment such as qc3C 3D-ratio estimation.

name: hidden-markov-model-forward-backward-inference
description: Use when longitudinal sequencing count data contain observed zeros and you need posterior probabilities distinguishing biological zeros (extinct taxa) from technical zeros (below detection threshold), e.g. in a state-space/variational inference model of community composition.

name: hierarchical-bubble-tree-organization
description: Use when a colored de Bruijn graph (directed, acyclic, nondegenerate, unique start/end nodes, node color sets per sample) must be decomposed into colored superbubbles and arranged into a parent-child tree that supports tri-tuple coordinates.

name: hierarchical-clustering-of-metagenome-samples
description: Use when you have raw 16S rRNA or WGS metagenome reads for a sample set and need to cluster samples by community composition and abundance, or to compare how different distance metrics (Libra cosine, Mash MinHash, Simka) resolve sample groupings.

name: hierarchical-section-component-instantiation
description: Use when a YAML report config must be turned into instantiated section/subsection/component objects — e.g., implementing or extending VueGen's report generators (Streamlit, notebook, document) for bioinformatics outputs like plots, tables, networks, Markdown, and HTML.

name: hifi-long-read-metagenome-assembly
description: Use when HiFi long reads (FASTQ) from a metagenomic sample must be de novo assembled with multiple assemblers to compare assembly strategies or feed downstream binning/quality evaluation.

name: high-dimensional-data-clustering
description: Use when binning assembled metagenomic contigs whose feature vectors are too high-dimensional for reliable Euclidean/Manhattan metrics — e.g. composition vectors built from multiple k-mer sizes — and hull-based assignment is preferred.

name: high-dimensional-feature-screening
description: Use when the feature matrix is high-dimensional relative to the sample size (e.g. hundreds of standardized OTUs vs tens of samples) and most taxa are expected to be noise, so the multivariate association test must operate on a selected subset S of taxa.

name: high-throughput-genome-scalability-testing
description: Use when you need to verify that a core-genome estimation pipeline (mOTUpan/mOTUlizer with mmseqs2 gene clustering) scales to thousands of MAGs/genomes before committing to a full production run, or to reproduce the published resource benchmarks.

name: highest-scoring-segment-pair-selection
description: Use when multiple overlapping or adjacent DIAMOND (tabular BLASTX) hits map to the same reference protein and must be merged into a single continuous sequence while resolving overlaps by HSP score.

name: hit-filtering-sensitivity-specificity-tradeoff-analysis
description: Use when choosing or configuring a hit-filtering strategy for DIAMOND alignment output in read-based functional annotation, or when reasoning about sensitivity/specificity trade-offs from multi-match reads.

name: hit-stitching-overlap-merging
description: Use when reconstructing Patchwork's hit-stitching phase: DIAMOND tabular BLASTX hits against protein references must be merged into a single continuous sequence per reference for marker retrieval.

name: hit-stitching-parameter-configuration
description: Use when retrieving phylogenetic markers (e.g. USCOs/near-USCOs) from fragmented WGS assemblies or reads with Patchwork, and DIAMOND search sensitivity, frameshift, or tantan masking parameters must be set to maximize retrieval and coverage.

name: hiv-amplicon-read-processing
description: Use when benchmarking ShoRAH's error-correction (diri_sampler) and frequency-estimation (freqEst) stages on large HIV-1 amplicon/pyrosequencing read sets, or when validating reported runtimes against the paper's hardware configuration.

name: hmm-based-cas-protein-search
description: Use when raw paired-end genomic FASTQ reads (isolate or metagenome) should be scanned for cas genes/CRISPR arrays without a complete assembly, e.g. phage-therapy susceptibility screening or novel CRISPR/Cas discovery.

name: hmm-based-genome-annotation
description: Use when starting from nucleotide (or already gene-predicted) bacterial genome FASTAs and you need Pfam protein family presence/absence profiles as features for trait prediction or comparative genomics, following Traitar's Prodigal + HMMER/Pfam 27.0 workflow.

name: hmm-based-modification-enzyme-annotation
description: Use when mining nucleotide genomes (FASTA contigs or assemblies) for RiPP-encoding BGCs and you need to locate modification enzyme homologs to define candidate precursor peptide regions before spectra matching.

name: hmm-based-protein-classification
description: Use when input is a protein sequence set in FASTA format and the goal is automatic detection and enzyme-type prediction of proteins belonging to known paralogous families, where blast-based or phylogenetic assignment is too slow or error-prone.

name: hmm-based-rrna-gene-identification
description: Use when you need to detect SSU rRNA genes within large sequence collections (e.g. non-redundant SILVA releases or metagenome assemblies) so that structural features such as ≥10 bp insertion boundaries can be located from alignment gaps.

name: hmm-hit-precision-sensitivity-calculation
description: Use when KEMET --hmm_mode onebm HMM hits on MAGs must be validated against the same HMM search on corresponding NCBI/PATRIC complete isolate genomes, and precision/sensitivity of recovered missing KOs is needed.

name: hmm-hit-threshold-filtering
description: Use when KEMET HMM-search (--hmm_mode onebm/module/kos) output must be filtered so only KOs whose HMM profile score passes the quality cutoff (default 0.43) count as recovered annotations, e.g. in truncation or KO-removal recovery tests.

name: hmm-profile-annotation-against-pfam
description: Use when starting from nucleotide FASTA genomes (or already-predicted ORFs) and you need Pfam-A protein family profiles as features for Traitar phenotype prediction across tens or hundreds of bacterial samples.

name: hmm-profile-leave-one-out-validation
description: Use when a curated HMM-based classifier (e.g. the DsrABCMK model set behind DiSCo) needs its stability tested against training-set composition, i.e. checking whether model assignments or type predictions change when single training sequences are dropped.

name: hmm-profile-ortholog-recovery
description: Use when eggNOG-mapper/.emapper.annotations or similar KO annotations are suspected incomplete (e.g. fragmented MAG assemblies or truncated genes) and missing KOs from KEGG Modules need evidence-backed recovery via HMM profile search.

name: hmm-profile-protein-family-detection
description: Use when building protein-family inventories or presence/absence matrices from predicted ORFs whose sequence divergence defeats keyword-based annotation — e.g. surveying ribosomal protein L30, L9, L1 absence across divergent lineages such as CPR and TM6.

name: hmm-profile-search-annotation-recovery
description: Use when MAG or draft-genome eggNOG/KAAS/KofamKoala KO annotations leave KEGG Modules incomplete and unannotated genes (including partially truncated sequences) need evidence-based KO recovery via profile HMMs.

name: hmm-profile-threshold-calibration
description: Use when running KEMET's HMM-based missing-KEGG-ortholog search (--hmm_mode onebm) and you need to tune or justify the nhmmer score-per-length cutoff against verified reference hits rather than accepting the 0.43 default.

name: hmm-protein-homology-search-of-reads
description: Use when raw, unassembled Illumina FASTQ reads must be screened for remote protein homologs (e.g. cas genes) and individual matching reads are needed as seeds, rather than assembled contigs.

name: hmm-search-threshold-filtering
description: Use when you need to identify and type-classify Dsr-dependent dissimilatory sulphur metabolism proteins from FASTA protein data using profile HMMs with model-specific score and E-value cut-offs rather than phylogenetic assignment.

name: hmmer-profile-hmm-construction
description: Use when candidate KO annotations are missing from a MAG/genome annotation table (eggNOG, KAAS, KOFAMkoala) and you want to recover them via profile HMM searches against taxonomically relevant KEGG GENES ortholog subsets.

name: hmmsearch-hit-filtering-evalue-cutoffs
description: Use when assigning HMM library hits to input protein sequences after hmmsearch and you must apply model-specific score/E-value cutoffs and keep only the -scoring model per sequence.

name: hmp-body-site-clustering-evaluation
description: Use when evaluating how k-mer distance metrics (Cosine Similarity, Bray-Curtis, MinHash, Simka) cluster metagenomic samples by body site, especially to test whether analysis of assembled contigs instead of reads degrades separation.

name: hmp-genome-dataset-retrieval
description: Use when a benchmark requires the HMP prokaryotic genome set with trusted NCBI-taxonomy labels — e.g. evaluating a MAG taxonomy classifier where strain-level assignments are needed and GTDB-based tools cannot provide them.

name: homology-based-offtarget-probe-filtration
description: Use when a candidate bait-region table (CandidateBaitRegions.tab) from the identification stage must be purged of probes with homologous hits to host or contaminant reference sequences before final probe selection.

name: homology-search-against-viral-refseq
description: Use when viral contigs (>10 kbp, already identified as viral) need reference-backed taxonomy, and you want homology-based calls against NCBI viral RefSeq to complement clustering-based assignment.

name: homopolymer-kmer-rejection
description: Use when generating custom k-mer detection networks with baseLess run_production_pipeline and you need to purge homopolymeric candidate k-mers from the evolutionary pool so only signal-distinguishable 16S k-mers survive.

name: horizontal-gene-transfer-aware-classifier-evaluation
description: Use when comparing phenotype classifiers built from Pfam profiles where one model adds maximum-likelihood ancestral character-state inference on the species phylogeny, and you need held-out-set macroaccuracy/accuracy to quantify the HGT-aware benefit.

name: horizontal-gene-transfer-evidence-analysis
description: Use when you have a catalogue of putative ISs (e.g. the 879-sequence ISC FASTA) and need to identify their isolate origins, taxonomic sharing breadth, and whether cross-genera or cross-class sharing implies horizontal transfer.

name: horizontal-gene-transfer-strain-reconstruction-evaluation
description: Use when comparing reconstruction accuracy (RA) of HGT/transferred-segment detection methods on WGSIM-simulated shotgun NGS data across sequencing coverages (e.g., 5X vs 30X), to test whether a graph-based method outperforms a breakpoint-only tool.

name: host-proximity-graph-linkage
description: Use when binning metagenomic viral contigs from a Hi-C experiment where the Hi-C interaction graph alone is too sparse, and assembled prokaryotic contigs are available to infer virus-host proximity links.

name: host-read-alignment-against-human-genome
description: Use when raw paired-end FASTQ files from ribodepleted or poly(A)-enriched stool metatranscriptomes must be screened for human-derived reads, e.g. to test whether host transcriptomes are recoverable or to quantify host contamination.

name: host-read-decontamination-benchmarking
description: Use when microbial FASTQ (short-read Illumina or ONT long-read) data must be decontaminated of human host sequences, or when comparing Hostile vs HRRT on human removal, microbial retention, throughput, and memory.

name: host-read-filtering
description: Use when raw shotgun metagenomic FASTQs contain host contamination (e.g. human gut samples) and host-derived reads must be removed before gene mapping and functional annotation.

name: host-read-filtering-against-reference-genome-index
description: Use when RNA-seq FASTQ reads from a host organism must be separated from microbial (bacterial, archaeal, viral) content before taxonomic classification or metagenomic reporting.

name: host-read-filtering-rnaseq
description: Use when RNA-seq FASTQ data must be stripped of host-organism reads before microbial taxonomic characterization, e.g. paired-end SSc skin RNA-seq against Mus_musculus.GRCm38.

name: host-similarity-matrix-construction
description: Use when you have two complementary host similarity sources (e.g., genome k-mer ONF similarity and GIP kernel similarity from known virus-host associations) and need a single square host-host similarity matrix to feed a heterogeneous virus-host network model.
tools: Jie Ren's d2* oligonucleotide frequency tools

name: hotspot-bed-configuration-parsing
description: Use when preparing inputs for Nano2NGS-Muta: a hotspot panel must be encoded as a BED-style configure file plus a complete check-hotspot.list before running nano2ngs-muta.pl on nanopore FASTQ reads.

name: hpv-type-assignment-by-l1-sequence-similarity
description: Use when you have Papillomavirus (Papillomaviridae) genomes — e.g. from the VMGC's 627 genomes in 61 vOTUs — and need L1-based type/species/genus classification plus a phylogeny of human vaginal papillomaviruses.

name: htseq-count-file-parsing
description: Use when the input consists of multiple per-sample HTSeq output count files that must be combined into one matrix of samples and corresponding gene counts before differential expression or enrichment analysis.

name: human-and-rrna-read-depletion
description: Use when raw metagenomic FASTQ read sets (e.g., the 264 vaginal metagenomes used to build VIRGO) must be cleaned of human-derived reads and rRNA sequences prior to assembly, CDS prediction, or mapping-based profiling.

name: human-population-genomic-variant-analysis
description: Use when you have human population VCF-derived unfolded SFS / MKT count tables (e.g. 1000GP populations like CEU or YRI) and need to estimate α or compare selection regimes between a candidate gene set and the genome-wide distribution.

name: hybrid-assembly-accuracy-evaluation
description: Use when comparing plasmid recovery accuracy of assemblers (e.g. Plassembler vs Unicycler) on real or subsampled Nanopore/Illumina read sets, where a manually curated ground truth exists and QUAST-based accuracy metrics are needed.

name: hybrid-assembly-configuration-short-and-long-reads
description: Use when you have paired short-read FASTQ plus matching long-read FASTQ/FASTA from the same metagenomic samples (e.g. CAMISIM-simulated mouse-gut time-series data) and want to improve assembly N50, size, and MAG recovery.

name: hybrid-cnn-bert-parallel-fusion-architecture
description: Use when a task requires capturing both local sequence motifs and long-range dependencies of 16S rRNA sequences for hierarchical taxonomic prediction across domain-through-species ranks, or when reimplementing/verifying the DeepTaxa architecture.

name: hybrid-cnn-bert-variant-training
description: Use when you need to attribute DeepTaxa's species-level performance to its components by training ablation variants (CNN pathway only, BERT pathway only, or DNABERT-2 BPE tokenization replaced by one-hot encodings) and comparing species F1 to the full hybrid baseline.

name: hybrid-metagenome-assembly-execution
description: Use when you have Illumina paired-end metagenomic reads plus at least one long-range library (ONT or PacBio long reads, mate pairs, or 10x linked reads) and need de novo scaffolds with high contiguity and few interspecies misassemblies.

name: hybrid-neural-network-extra-trees-probability-classification
description: Use when classifying pairs of viral scaffolds/fragments as same or different genome origin from sequence-feature distances (k-mer/tetranucleotide frequencies, GC content), or when retraining/loading vRhyme's .sav ML models.

name: hybridization-probe-design
description: Use when you have annotated genomes (e.g., PROKKA GFFs) and NCBI taxon-ids for a diverse pathogen group and need a bounded, tiled bait set that captures known plus up-to-20%-divergent related sequences.

name: hypergeometric-enrichment-testing
description: Use when two independent strain-similarity metrics (e.g. APSS from SynTracker and popANI from inStrain) have been computed on the same sample pairs and you must identify species whose within-species diversity arises preferentially from point mutations versus structural differences.

name: hyperopt-bayesian-hyperparameter-optimization
description: Use when training small neural networks (e.g., per-k-mer 1D CNNs on MinION squiggle segments) and you need Bayesian hyperparameter search that trades off predictive F1 against model size rather than grid/random search.

name: hyperparameter-sensitivity-analysis
description: Use when a model such as ILMF-VH has multiple tunable parameters (k, alpha, beta, lambda, gamma, K) and you must sweep each while fixing the others, scoring every setting by mean AUPR under five-fold cross-validation.
tools: Jie Ren's oligonucleotide frequency dissimilarity tools

name: ibd-microbiome-biomarker-interpretation
description: Use when reanalyzing gut metagenomes (e.g. 106 iHMP / PRJNA398089 samples) from IBD cohorts (CD, UC, healthy) to find differentially abundant uncultured metagenomic species as disease biomarkers.

name: illumina-adapter-trimming-bbduk
description: Use when raw paired-end or single-end Illumina FASTQ reads (fastq/fastq.gz) enter a metagenomic pipeline and must be stripped of Illumina adapters and low-quality bases before SSU rRNA filtering or assembly.

name: illumina-phred-quality-decoding
description: Use when you need to characterize which reads PANDAseq's error corrections come from — e.g. testing whether uncertain corrections concentrate in reads with many low-quality (CASAVA-masked) bases rather than high-quality positions.

name: illumina-quality-probability-scoring
description: Decision support for setting PANDAseq assembly quality-score thresholds when recovering more overlapping Illumina paired-end reads matters more than maximum stringency, e.g. 16S rRNA amplicon libraries with many low-quality tail bases.

name: illumina-read-simulation-from-mutated-genomes
description: Use when benchmarking ANI/strain-comparison methods on metagenomic data and you need synthetic read sets with known ground-truth ANI values derived from genomes mutated at controlled rates.

name: illumina-short-read-error-correction
description: Use when deep-sequencing reads (BAM/CRAM aligned to a reference such as HIV-1 subtype B pol) from a genetically heterogeneous mixed sample must be error-corrected and rare variants down to 0.1% frequency quantified.

name: illumina-short-read-simulation
description: Use when you need a known-composition paired-end Illumina FASTQ set from reference bacterial assemblies to quantify what fraction of true bacterial reads a decontamination tool retains or incorrectly removes.

name: imbalanced-metagenomic-cluster-benchmarking
description: Use when reproducing the simulated metagenomic reads benchmark comparing iDeLUCS, DeLUCS, and k-means++ clustering accuracy on unbalanced multi-genome DNA read datasets.

name: in-silico-genome-evolution-simulation
description: Use when you need to benchmark a strain-tracking or genome-comparison tool's sensitivity to specific mutation types (SNPs vs indels) by simulating controlled in silico evolution and comparing pairwise score distributions across mutation regimes.

name: in-silico-mutagenesis-strain-generation
description: Use when benchmarking strain-variant discovery (e.g. MetaQuad) and you need simulated shotgun metagenomic samples with known strain composition, planted substitutions, and controlled mean depths instead of real clinical reads.

name: in-silico-pcr-primer-matching
description: Use when a set of primer pairs (designed or published) must be scored for detection of a curated reference gene set — e.g., computing what fraction of 720 amoA-AOB target genes are amplified in silico, or comparing coverage between two primer sets.

name: in-silico-read-abundance-mixing
description: Use when benchmarking metagenomic assembly of strain-diverse viral communities requires a controlled ground truth: target-organism reads must be spiked into a complex background at a known abundance before assembly.

name: in-silico-read-mixture-simulation
description: Use when you need to quantify how reliably an AMP-based predictor (Mykrobe) detects a low-frequency contaminant or resistant subpopulation in NGS reads, e.g. down to 0.5–2% minor-population frequency.

name: in-silico-read-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking a metagenomic assembler or contig extender and a ground-truth-controlled read set is needed spanning known read lengths, error rates, coverage depths, and uneven coverage profiles.

name: indel-error-modeling-in-gene-prediction
description: Use when predicting protein-coding genes in error-prone sequencing reads (especially 454 reads with homopolymer-run indel artifacts and per-base quality values) where indel errors shift the reading frame and truncate ORFs.

name: indel-mismatch-rate-normalization-per-100kbp
description: Use when comparing small-plasmid assembly accuracy across tools on simulated reads, and you need length-normalized error rates (indels/100 kbp, mismatches/100 kbp) plus genome fraction from QUAST alignments to a curated ground truth.

name: indel-prediction-accuracy-assessment
description: Use when benchmarking gene-prediction tools on raw error-prone metagenomic reads (e.g. 454 homopolymer indels) and you need nucleotide-level sensitivity/precision, including indel-position accuracy, against known truth.

name: index-size-memory-footprint-comparison
description: Use when comparing read-classification or alignment tools on repetitive references and you need to quantify how index size, peak RSS, and bases/second scale with reference repetitiveness.

name: infant-strain-sharing-jaccard-similarity-analysis
description: Use when metagenomic samples from related individuals (e.g. NICU infants, twin pairs) have inStrain profiles and the goal is to quantify and statistically test which pairs share microbial strains.

name: infant-virome-temporal-comparison
description: Use when a vOTU count table from a longitudinal infant virome (e.g., Liang et al. VLP metagenomes sampled at 0-4 days, 1 month, and 4 months) must be compared across sampling-time groups to test whether virome diversity increases with age.

name: influenza-segment-reconstruction-from-metagenomic-reads
description: Use when paired-end metagenomic FASTQ from influenza-positive respiratory samples must be assembled into contiguous genome segments and per-sample segment counts compared against the VirMAP reference results.

name: information-based-robinson-foulds-tree-comparison
description: Use when you must quantify, with an empirical P-value, how well a tree built from your own distance data (e.g., UPGMA trees from APSS-based synteny distances at a given subsampling depth n) agrees with an independently published reference tree over the same taxa.

name: information-extraction-performance-evaluation
description: Use when an NLP-based extractor produces structured outputs (e.g., taxon-by-character matrices) from text and you must quantify its accuracy against a manually curated gold standard or compare it with human annotators.

name: informative-variant-filtering
description: Use when you have a cellsnp-lite output folder (cellSNP) with per-sample AD/DP allele counts from shotgun metagenomic samples and need to distinguish shared informative variants from non-polymorphic sites or sequencing-error noise.

name: insertion-length-summary-statistics
description: Use when you have an rRNA insertion catalog keyed to 16S rRNA genes and need to quantify what fraction of genes carry large (≥10 bp) insertions and the max/mean/s.d. of insertion lengths.

name: insertion-sequence-candidate-filtering
description: Use when you have FASTA files of candidate ITR and flanking IS-region sequences from an upstream maximal-exact-match step and need to call high-confidence insertion sequences via ITR cluster concordance and reverse-complement checks.

name: insertion-sequence-catalogue-search
description: Use when you have FASTA sequences of insertion sequences (e.g. from ISC) and need to find which isolate genomes contain them and infer their taxonomic origins via compact index search.

name: insertion-sequence-database-benchmarking
description: Reference for quantifying the fraction of a newly built IS catalogue with known homologs, e.g. after running Palidis on metagenomes and producing a non-redundant FASTA of insertion sequences to be annotated against ISfinder.

name: insertion-sequence-discovery-from-metagenomes
description: Use when the input is paired-end short-read metagenomic FASTQ.GZ data from mixed microbial communities (e.g. HMP oral/stool samples) and the goal is to detect ISs and build a non-redundant IS catalogue with novel transposase annotation.

name: insilico-mock-community-design
description: Use when validating an amplicon profile correction method (e.g., GCN correction) and you need simulated communities with known ground truth, plus matched amplicon and metagenomic read datasets from the same underlying composition.

name: inter-contig-3d-ratio-estimation
description: Use when you have cleaned Hi-C paired-end FASTQ reads (e.g. quality- and adapter-trimmed with bbduk, duplicates removed with clumpify.sh) and need a reference-free metric of Hi-C ligation quality before binning.

name: interactive-html-report-rendering
description: Use when a genome/metagenome assembly evaluation pipeline (QUAST, WebQUAST, MetaQUAST) has computed quality metrics and plots and they must be merged into one interactive HTML file with an Icarus viewer menu for the user.

name: interactive-html-report-structure-validation
description: Use when a MetaPhage Nextflow run has completed and you must confirm the interactive HTML report was generated with all expected sections (miner comparison, taxonomy, diversity) before comparing against the deposited reference.

name: interactive-manhattan-plot-visualization
description: Use when signatures-of-selection scan results (iHS, XP-EHH, SweepFinder2 CLR values) from scalepopgen need to be visualized as interactive per-population Manhattan plots to inspect candidate regions under selection.

name: interactive-population-structure-visualization
description: Use when a Nextflow population-genomics pipeline has produced analysis outputs (PCA variance/coordinates, ADMIXTURE logs and Q-matrices, IBS and FST distance matrices, TreeMix tree files) and the user needs combined, interactive plots to interpret population structure immediately.

name: interactive-subnetwork-visualization
description: Use when you need to visually justify or audit taxonomic assignments of vOTUs within a vConTACT2 network, e.g. inspecting which INPHARED reference genomes neighbor each vOTU in its cluster.

name: interkingdom-correlation-analysis
description: Use when paired fungal and bacterial taxonomic abundance tables plus sample metadata are available and the goal is to count or rank significant inter-kingdom correlations within defined healthy cohorts (e.g., Danish vs Spanish gut).

name: interleaved-fastq-read-processing
description: Use when the input is paired-end metagenome sequencing data that must be converted to interleaved FASTQ and assembled de novo at strain resolution with StrainXpress, or when reproducing StrainXpress benchmark workflows.

name: interspecies-misasassembly-quantification
description: Use when comparing metagenome assemblers (e.g. MetaPlatanus, metaSPAdes, OPERA-MS, metaFlye) on a mock community whose bacterial reference genomes are known, and misassembly/NGA50 counts must be extracted with metaQUAST.

name: intra-vs-inter-sample-variant-classification
description: Use when mapping-based SNV calls from inStrain profiles across multiple samples must be partitioned into within-host vs between-host variants and analyzed for selection (dN/dS) at the gene level.

name: intracellular-lifestyle-classification
description: Use when predicting the obligate intracellular lifestyle of bacterial genomes from comparative-genomics COG presence/absence profiles, or reproducing the 0.997 ± 0.010 accuracy benchmark on complete genomes.

name: intraspecies-diversity-cluster-validation
description: Use when VIRGO mapping outputs (summary.Count.txt, summary.Abundance.txt) are available for vaginal metagenomes and the goal is to confirm that ward-linkage clustering of Jaccard distances over species-assigned gene content recovers the reported number of MG-subspecies.

name: intraspecies-gene-content-comparison
description: Use when metagenomic reads (single-end merged FASTQ) can be mapped to a reference gene catalog and you want to test whether within-community intraspecies strain co-occurrence inflates per-sample gene counts beyond isolate pangenomes.

name: inverted-terminal-repeat-palindrome-detection
description: Use when input is paired-end, short-read metagenomic FASTQ.GZ data (or mixed microbial genomes) and the goal is to discover novel insertion sequences via their inverted terminal repeats, e.g. to build or query an IS catalogue.

name: is-sharing-across-taxa-aggregation
description: Use when a COBS sample-hits table of ISC insertion sequences queried against 661,405 isolate genomes must be joined to genus/species metadata to identify the most widely shared IS and ISfinder coverage gaps.

name: isfinder-novelty-cross-referencing
description: Use when a set of predicted insertion sequence IDs (e.g. ISC entries like IS_length_1391-IPR001207_495_804) needs known/novel status resolved against ISfinder before ranking or reporting.

name: isoform-abundance-quantification-comparison
description: Use when you have simulated read sets mapped to a known allele database and need to validate fractional allele composition calls against an established isoform/abundance quantification baseline such as Kallisto.

name: isolate-genome-gene-prediction
description: Use when building a non-redundant gene catalog from pooled sources and you need gene predictions from complete/draft isolate genomes (e.g., 308 urogenital isolates) to complement CDSs predicted from per-sample metagenomic assemblies.

name: isolate-genome-hit-parsing
description: Use when you have COBS query results against the 661k ENA compact index and need to resolve genome hits to BioSamples and taxonomic identities for IS origin tracing.

name: isolate-genome-pairwise-scores-extraction
description: Use when isolate or assembly genome pairs have been compared with SynTracker and inStrain and you need per-pair APSS and popANI values to build same/different-strain classification tables.

name: iterated-genome-model-training
description: Use when predicting protein-coding genes in assembled prokaryotic genomes or metagenomic contigs/read sets with Glimmer/Glimmer-MG and you need to boot-strap and retrain IMM models on initial predictions before final calls.

name: iterative-contig-merging-reassembly
description: Decision support for refining assembled metagenomic contigs down to a purely viral set: use when contigs from a mapping-assembly stage must be merged, filtered against Genbank, and rebuilt until convergence.

name: iterative-scaffold-extension-loop-implementation
description: Use when de novo assembly of genomic flanking regions around target genes (e.g. ARGs) is needed from short-read metagenomic FASTQ data but full metagenomic de novo assembly is too computationally expensive.

name: iterative-seed-expansion-implementation
description: Use when raw Illumina FASTQ reads contain a small seed set (HMM- or repeat-derived) and neighboring reads must be recruited for targeted assembly without assembling the whole dataset.

name: iterative-strain-separation-control-loop
description: Use when running Strainberry on a strain-oblivious long-read assembly plus indexed BAM alignment and you must decide how many separation iterations to run, when to stop, and how to organize per-iteration outputs (strainberry_n2/, strainberry_n3/, ...).

name: itr-position-based-read-filtering
description: Use when you have read-level inverted terminal repeat (ITR) calls with LCoord/RCoord positions and paired assemblies, and need to keep only reads where repeat positions imply an IS within a plausible size range.

name: itr-sequence-clustering
description: Use when you have FASTA files of candidate ITR and IS-region sequences from an upstream Palidis maximal-exact-match step and need to filter them into high-confidence IS predictions via cluster concordance and reverse-complement checks.

name: iupac-ambiguity-code-matching
description: Use when computing read-to-genome similarity with LiME's eBWT-based symbol-matching strategy and reference genomes or reads contain IUPAC ambiguity codes that must contribute matches rather than being discarded.

name: iupac-degenerate-primer-matching
description: Use when raw amplicon FASTQ reads (16S/ITS/18S/28S) still carry primer sequences that contain degenerate IUPAC bases, and primers must be removed before quality filtering or OTU clustering.

name: jaccard-distance-agglomerative-clustering
description: Use when protein sequences (e.g. a multi-genome UniProt/SwissProt FASTA set) must be grouped into families without labels, using amino-acid-reduced kmer sets rather than sequence alignment.

name: jaccard-distance-genomic-read-set-filtering
description: Use when reads have been assigned to viral genomes from nucleotide and translated alignments against Genbank gbvrl/gbphage and a genome's read set shows high non-unique read membership relative to larger sets, causing cross-genome ambiguity that would corrupt per-genome pileup assembly.

name: jaccard-similarity-computation-on-read-sets
description: Use when you need to quantify concordance between two or more read-level metagenomic classifiers by comparing their classified-read sets with Jaccard similarity and per-tool missed-read tallies.

name: jellyfish-kmer-frequency-profiling
description: Use when preparing the embedding input vocabulary for DeepMicrobes training — i.e. you have training genome FASTA files (e.g. the 2,505 gut microbiota species repertoire) and need a k-mer-to-index mapping file.

name: jensen-shannon-beta-diversity-pcoa-ordination
description: Use when you have two or more compositional taxa abundance matrices (e.g. a reference MetaPhlAn2 profile and a de novo MAG-based profile) for the same samples with binary metadata (IBD vs control) and need to quantify whether one resolution better separates the groups via beta diversity.

name: junction-read-preservation-for-breakpoint-detection
description: Use when paired-end shotgun metagenomic reads must be mapped against many reference genomes while preserving discordant/junction read pairs spanning two references as input for HGT breakpoint detection.

name: jupyter-notebook-pipeline-execution
description: Use when raw population variation data (DGN FASTA alignments or 1000GP Phase III VCFs) must be converted into per-gene, per-population SFS and divergence tables for MKT analyses, and pre-computed server tables are insufficient.

name: k-mer-abundance-profiling
description: Use when diagnosing why HiFi reads failed to map to a metagenome assembly: compare k-mer abundance histograms of mapped vs unmapped read fractions to test the low-abundance hypothesis.

name: k-mer-assembly-parameterization
description: Use when building or reproducing a body-site gene catalog from raw paired-end metagenomic reads that requires de novo contig assembly with a broad k-mer sweep and reported assembly statistics (contigs, total bp, N50).

name: kbp-s-speed-metric-computation
description: Use when comparing processing speed (kilo-bases per second) of baseLess or competing MinION read-classification pipelines across low-power single-board hardware (Jetson Nano) and desktop configurations.

name: kegg-api-database-retrieval
description: Use when a workflow needs a curated, non-redundant set of KEGG ortholog sequences for HMM profile building (KEMET --hmm_mode onebm/module/kos) or when refreshing a stale local KEGG GENES copy via the KEGG API.

name: kegg-brite-hierarchy-usage
description: Use when you have a corrected KEGG orthology group (KO) abundance table and need higher-level KEGG module and pathway abundance profiles, or need to interpret KOs within the KEGG BRITE hierarchy.

name: kegg-functional-annotation-mapping
description: Use when shotgun metagenome reads have been mapped to a non-redundant gene catalog (e.g. IGC) and per-sample gene frequencies must be translated into KO, EC number and reaction level functional abundance tables for case-control biomarker analysis.

name: kegg-module-abundance-quantification
description: Use when PICRUSt-predicted KO metagenome tables from 16S data must be aggregated to KEGG module abundances and statistically compared between sample groups (e.g., supragingival vs subgingival plaque, menses vs rest of cycle).

name: kegg-module-block-partitioning-comparison
description: Use when evaluating microbial genome or MAG functional potential via KEGG Modules and needing to compare block-level Module completeness across KEMET, KEGG Mapper, and METABOLIC v4.0.

name: kegg-module-brite-functional-category-mapping
description: Use when predicted or observed gene family annotations (KOs, COGs) must be aggregated into higher-level functional categories via KEGG Modules or BRITE, or when per-category accuracy of gene-content predictions is required.

name: kegg-module-completeness-evaluation
description: Use when you have a FASTA genome/MAG plus a KEGG KO annotation file (eggNOG/kaas/kofamkoala format) and need Module-level completeness tables or a comparison of Module block partitioning across KEMET, KEGG Mapper, and METABOLIC.

name: kegg-ortholog-annotation-removal
description: Use when you need to quantitatively validate an annotation-expansion tool (e.g., KEMET) by removing known KOs from eggNOG-mapper .emapper.annotations files and measuring recovery rates from FASTA sequences.

name: kegg-ortholog-ec-reaction-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when mapping-based metagenomic count data (case-control design) has genes mapped to KEGG KO groups, EC numbers, and reactions, and you need to decide whether functional-level differential analysis outperforms gene-level testing at a fixed significance threshold.

name: kegg-ortholog-hmm-search
description: Use when a MAG or genome FASTA has incomplete KEGG Module blocks and unannotated genes that may be genuine KOs recoverable by profile HMM searches, especially for partial/truncated gene sequences.

name: kegg-ortholog-pathway-aggregation
description: Use when you have a corrected KO abundance table from shotgun metagenomes and need higher-level KEGG pathway/module functional profiles rather than ortholog-level abundances.

name: kegg-ortholog-to-reaction-mapping
description: Use when a MAG or isolate genome has KEGG KO annotations (eggNOG/KAAS/KofamKOALA format) and you need to convert them into metabolic reactions for GSMM reconstruction or evidence-based gapfilling, especially after HMM-based KO recovery.

name: kegg-orthology-annotation
description: Use when you have a per-sample gene abundance table and a many-to-many gene-to-KEGG-KO (or other ortholog) mapping file, and need a KO-level functional profile without double-counting multiply-annotated genes.

name: kegg-orthology-annotation-of-mapped-genes
description: Use when a non-redundant gene catalog has already been read-mapped to produce per-sample gene frequencies, and the analysis goal is functional profiling beyond the gene level at KO, EC number and reaction levels.

name: kegg-orthology-annotation-processing
description: Use when you already have KO-annotated genes for a genome or MAG in eggnog/kaas/kofamkoala format and need KEGG Module completeness summaries, or need the KEGG-Mapper INCOMPLETE convention (Modules with <3 blocks) for cross-tool comparison.

name: kegg-pathway-annotation
description: Use when a ggpicrust2 differential abundance (DA) results table carries KO-level or raw KEGG pathway identifiers and needs pathway_name, pathway_description, pathway_class, and pathway_map joined from the KEGG database.

name: kegg-pathway-set-construction
description: Use when you have PICRUSt2 KO abundance features and need pathway-level gene sets (e.g. for ggpicrust2 pathway_gsea()) rather than single-feature differential abundance testing.

name: kegg-pathway-visualization
description: Use when a DESeq2 differential expression table or ranked gene list has produced significant KEGG pathways via ClusterProfShinyORA or ClusterProfShinyGSEA and the next step is to visualize those enriched pathways as KEGG pathway plots.

name: kegg-reference-database-mapping
description: Use when DA result tables from ggpicrust2::pathway_daa() carry KO-level or unannotated feature IDs and need KEGG pathway names, descriptions, and classes joined on before visualization or reporting.

name: kernel-density-smoothing-of-length-histograms

description: Use when you need synthetic longitudinal count benchmarks with known ground-truth trajectories to evaluate compositional denoising or trajectory-reconstruction methods such as LUMINATE, TGP-CODA, or MALLARD.

name: longitudinal-covariate-adjustment
description: Use when comparing microbiome taxon relative abundances between groups using longitudinal cohort data (multiple samples per infant, e.g. Bangladesh cohort ≤6 months), where a covariate such as infant age at sample collection must be adjusted for in the model.

name: longitudinal-glmm-null-model-testing
description: Use when a longitudinal dataset (count, proportion, binary, ordinal or continuous features over time points) must be tested for significant change of features over time (proxy for treatments) while simultaneously detecting and controlling for potentially many covariates.

name: longitudinal-menses-abundance-change-detection
description: Use when you have a longitudinal 16S OTU table (e.g. a vaginal time course) with per-sample metadata marking menses, and want to test whether PICRUSt-predicted KEGG module abundances change significantly during menses versus other cycle phases.

name: longitudinal-microbiome-data-simulation
description: Use when evaluating longitudinal differential-abundance methods on data with known true positives — simulate count datasets across sample sizes, effect sizes and covariate counts to compute accuracy, TPR and FDR.

name: longitudinal-microbiome-differential-abundance-analysis
description: Use when analyzing longitudinal (repeated-measures) microbiome or other high-dimensional count/continuous/binary/ordinal feature data where abundance change over time (treatment proxy) must be disentangled from multiple covariates such as medications.

name: longitudinal-microbiome-signal-interpretation
description: Use when you have longitudinal multivariable data (count, proportion, binary, ordinal or continuous) with a time/treatment variable and potentially many covariates, and need covariate-sensitive biomarker detection.

name: longitudinal-microbiome-taxa-comparison
description: Use when testing differential taxa relative abundances (phylum to genus, taxtab levels l2–l6) between two groups in longitudinal/repeated-measures microbiome relative abundance data with many zeros.

name: longitudinal-mixed-model-microbiome-testing
description: Use when relative abundance taxa tables (phylum-to-genus, e.g. l2/l5/l6 levels) come from longitudinal stool sampling with repeated measures per subject and you need between-group differential abundance testing with proper type I error control.

name: longitudinal-negative-binomial-type-i-error-evaluation
description: Use when validating a longitudinal microbiome pipeline's false positive rate on negative-control data where sequencing depth varies systematically across time points but all features are truly null (zero effect size).

name: longitudinal-sample-mutation-modeling
description: Use when evaluating tools that detect short-term within-strain evolutionary mutations in longitudinal metagenomic data, or when ground-truth mutated reads with a known mutation VCF are needed for simulated time-series communities.

name: low-abundance-feature-threshold-filtering
description: Use when a merged MetaPhlAn (or QIIME/BIOM) taxonomic profile table must be preprocessed for ML classification and sparse low-abundance taxa need removal prior to RF/SVM/GLM model building.

name: low-frequency-clone-detection-in-mixed-samples
description: Use when quantifying genetic diversity of a mixed NGS sample (e.g. 454 Titanium reads from an HIV-1 pol amplicon mixture) and you need to recover individual haplotypes/clone frequencies as low as 0.1% despite error-prone reads.

name: low-quality-base-trimming
description: Use when raw paired-end metatranscriptome FASTQ files show adaptor contamination or low-quality bases and must be cleaned before read joining (FLASH) and submission to an annotation server such as MG-RAST.

name: lowest-common-ancestor-assignment
description: Use when building or interpreting an exact k-mer-to-taxon database for metagenomic classification, e.g. deciding which taxonomic ID a shared 31-mer should carry when it appears in multiple genomes.

name: lowest-common-ancestor-taxonomy-resolution
description: Decision support for assigning taxonomy to filtered viral contigs (>10 kbp) from ViroProfiler when combining clustering-based (vConTACT2) and homology-based (MMseqs2) evidence.

name: mafft-multiple-sequence-alignment
description: Use when a set of candidate ortholog sequences for target KOs must be aligned into a non-redundant MSA so a profile HMM can be built and searched against protein sequences of a MAG/genome to recover missing KEGG orthologs.

name: mag-abundance-profiling-from-shotgun-reads
description: Use when you have VAMB bins (clusters.tsv), their contigs FASTA, and the original paired-end FASTQ reads, and need accurate per-MAG-cluster abundance estimates plus subspecies-level phylogenetic stratification rather than a marker-gene-only profile.

name: mag-abundance-quantification
description: Use when you have assembled metagenomic contigs from multiple samples in a group and need MetaBAT2 binning plus a per-sample MAG abundance table, e.g. on CAMISIM simulated reads from Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.5155395.

name: mag-annotation-expansion-gsmm-gapfilling
description: Use when you have a MAG FASTA with an existing KEGG KO annotation (eggNOG/KAAS/KofamKOALA format) and need to recover missing KOs and improve MAG-derived GSMM metabolic capability predictions.

name: mag-binning-and-classification
description: Use when shotgun metagenomic paired-end reads need to be assembled, binned into MAGs, and taxonomically classified, or when testing whether MAG classification accuracy (sensitivity, precision, FDR, balanced accuracy, F1) is robust to assembler choice.

name: mag-cluster-taxonomic-annotation
description: Use when you have VAMB clusters.tsv plus assembled contigs and need taxonomic labels and MGS grouping of MAG clusters before abundance estimation, signature gene identification, or strain-level analysis with MAGinator.

name: mag-functional-annotation
description: Use when you have MAG or complete-genome FASTA files and need KEGG KO-level functional annotation plus Module completeness recap tables, especially for fragmented MAG assemblies where standard annotation tools miss orthologs.

name: mag-quality-filtering-checkm2
description: Use when building a de novo SourceApp source-associated genome database from mixed FASTA inputs (reference genomes plus MAGs) and low-quality or fragmented genome drafts must be excluded before ANI dereplication.

name: mag-reconstruction-counting-from-binning
description: Use when benchmarking metagenome assembly pipelines on simulated (e.g. CAMISIM) short and long reads and you need to quantify how hybrid assembly and co-assembly change N50, assembly size, and the number of recovered MAGs.

name: mag-reference-genome-concordance-analysis
description: Use when you have paired MAG and matching complete isolate genomes (e.g. from NCBI/PATRIC) with KEGG KO annotations and need to benchmark HMM-recovered missing KOs against a complete-genome reference.

name: mag-taxonomic-classification
description: Use when you have binned MAG FASTA files (from MetaBAT2 or similar) and need NCBI-taxonomy assignments up to strain level, comparing tools or benchmarking classification accuracy.

name: mag-taxonomic-classification
description: Use when assigning taxonomy to metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) produced by nf-core/mag or similar binning workflows, especially when bins have heterogeneous quality and a BUSCO-gated GTDB-Tk plus CAT/BAT fallback is appropriate.

name: manual-metabolic-reconstruction-comparison
description: Use when draft metagenome-assembled genomes (e.g. estimated 91% and 60% complete) need automated phenotype predictions that are validated against an existing expert metabolic reconstruction.

name: many-to-many-mapping-table-parsing
description: Use when you have a gene-length-normalized gene abundance TSV plus a tab-separated gene-to-ortholog map (ortholog ID in column 1, gene ID in column 2) and need KO-level functional profiles.

name: map-reduce-key-count-merging
description: Use when building a distributed metagenomics reference database on Spark from minhash sketches stored in per-executor hash tables and the counts must be merged globally before writing to HDFS.

name: mapped-unmapped-read-fraction-comparison
description: Use when a significant proportion of long (HiFi) metagenomic reads remain unmapped to an assembly and you need to determine whether low abundance (e.g. median k-mer abundance of 1), read length, or read quality explains the unassembled fraction.

name: mapping-accuracy-evaluation-against-minimap2
description: Use when a raw nanopore signal mapper (e.g., RawHash) has produced mapping.paf and its mapping positions must be validated against sequence-level ground truth before downstream analysis.

name: mapping-assembly-super-scaffold-construction
description: Use when reconstructing full-length viral genome segments (e.g. influenza's 8 segments) from low-coverage metagenomic FASTQ data where de-novo assembly alone yields fragmented contigs.

name: mapping-quality-based-read-pair-filtering
description: Use when processing a mapped metagenomic .bam file for microdiversity or strain-level analysis and you need to remove un-paired reads and apply pair-level filters (orientation, insert size, mapQ, nucleotide identity) before downstream profiling.

name: mapping-rate-quantification
description: Use when you must quantify how much of a newly built sequence database cross-maps to an independent reference catalog (e.g. checking a fungal marker database for bacterial contamination), or when computing a defensible mapping-rate summary for a large sequence set.

name: mapping-tool-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when comparing raw nanopore signal mappers for adaptive-sampling benefits: PAF mappings from multiple tools (e.g., RawHash, UNCALLED, Sigmap) are available on the same FAST5 datasets and you need per-tool averages of read prefix length or chunks consumed per mapped read.

name: mapreduce-distributed-pairwise-scoring
description: Use when you need an all-vs-all distance matrix between many (FASTA/FASTQ) metagenomic samples at scale, and a per-pair loop is infeasible; a k-mer index directory already exists or can be built.

name: marker-gene-based-genome-recovery-assessment
description: Use when you have binned contigs (e.g. MetaBAT2 bins from a HiFi metagenome assembly) and need to grade MAG recovery into quality categories from marker-gene completeness/contamination estimates.

name: marker-gene-completeness-contamination-estimation
description: Use when binned contig FASTA files (MAGs) have been produced by a binning step and you need per-bin completeness/contamination estimates plus assembly statistics to judge bin quality.

name: marker-gene-tree-formatting-and-pruning
description: Use when building a PICRUSt-style reference pipeline: a marker gene phylogeny (e.g. Greengenes 16S tree) must be aligned with a gene-by-genome KO/COG table before ancestral state reconstruction or tip gene content prediction.

name: marker-recovery-accuracy-evaluation
description: Use when you need to quantify marker-retrieval accuracy of a phylogenomic mining tool (e.g. Patchwork) against a divergent reference species, using recovery counts, unique reciprocal alignments, percent identity, and query coverage as validation metrics.

name: markov-background-model-estimation
description: Use when computing background-adjusted alignment-free distances (CVtree, D2star, D2shepp) in CAFE and the sequence's Markov order is unknown — the default '-1' triggers automatic BIC-based inference.

name: markov-order-background-adjusted-kmer-statistics
description: Use when computing background-adjusted k-mer dissimilarities (D2star, D2shepp, CVtree) in CAFE and the Markov background order must be chosen or auto-inferred per sequence set.

name: markov-order-model-selection
description: Use when running CAFE background-adjusted measures (CVtree, D2star, D2shepp) on genomes or NGS shotgun reads and the appropriate Markov order is unclear to the user.

name: mash-distance-screening
description: Use when you have assembled plasmid contigs (e.g. from Unicycler within Plassembler) and need to annotate each contig with its closest PLSDB plasmid match using Mash distance.

name: mash-distance-tree-pruning
description: Use when you have a large published phylogenetic tree (e.g., a Mash distance tree over >10,000 genomes supplied as a newick file) and a smaller subset of analyzed genomes, and need a pruned reference tree to quantify agreement with trees built from your own distance matrix.

name: mash-minhash-distance-computation
description: Use when computing fast all-vs-all pairwise distances between many metagenomic FASTA/FASTQ samples where sketching unique k-mers is acceptable, or when benchmarking abundance-aware k-mer metrics against Mash.

name: masked-base-probability-scoring
description: Use when auditing which overlap mismatches PANDAseq corrected probabilistically, to quantify whether uncertain corrections are driven by low-quality (masked) bases flagged by upstream Illumina processing.

name: masked-reference-index-selection
description: Use when cleaning microbial FASTQ reads against a human host reference and microbial retention (not just host removal) is a priority, e.g. bacterial Illumina or ONT metagenomic reads that are being over-removed by the unmasked human-t2t-hla index.

name: mass-spectra-similarity-network-construction
description: Use when thousands-to-millions of tandem MS/MS spectra from LC-MS/MS datasets (e.g. GNPS MSV datasets) must be grouped by fragmentation-pattern similarity, either to propagate peptide/spectrum identifications across related spectra or to estimate true chemical diversity.
tools: GNPS (Global Natural Products Social molecular networking)

name: match-length-distribution-analysis
description: Use when choosing or validating a minimum match length (or similar alignment-length) cutoff for a classifier by comparing match-length distributions on real versus shuffled reference databases.

name: matching-statistics-hypothesis-testing
description: Use when classifying basecalled nanopore reads as target vs non-target against a repetitive pan-genomic reference for targeted sequencing/depletion, especially when alignment tools like minimap2 are too slow or memory-heavy.

name: mate-pair-scaffolding
description: Use when assembling metagenome mock or real communities from Illumina paired-end reads plus mate-pair libraries (e.g. 4 kbp/8 kbp jumping libraries), and NGA50 contiguity versus short-read-only assemblers must be quantified.

name: matrix-pivot-transformation
description: Use when per-taxon natural-language extraction records (character and character-state values from prokaryotic taxonomic descriptions) must be pivoted into a standard taxon-by-character matrix usable by phylogenetic analysis software.

name: maximum-likelihood-model-comparison
description: Use when a continuous trait measured across taxa (e.g., 16S rRNA gene copy number estimates from CopyRighter's Greengenes files) must be tested for phylogenetic signal on a tree, and the strength of that signal needs to be compared between a phylogeny and a taxonomic tree.

name: maximum-likelihood-phylogenetic-inference
description: Use when you already have per-locus marker sequences (e.g. Patchwork-recovered near-USCOs) and need a well-supported phylogenomic tree via alignment, trimming, concatenation, and ML tree inference.

name: maximum-weight-matching-optimization
description: Use when error-corrected local haplotypes from ShoRAH windows must be stitched into full-genome haplotypes and their frequencies estimated from deep sequencing of a mixed sample.

name: maxinfo-criterion-trim-calculation
description: Use when quality-controlled paired/singleton FASTQs (e.g. host-filtered <sample_id>.<type_id>.fastq.gz files) still contain low-quality read ends and short reads that must be trimmed before read-to-gene mapping.

name: mcdonald-kreitman-adaptation-estimation
description: Use when estimating adaptive evolution (alpha) from DAF and divergence tables for coding genes, or when comparing selective regimes of a user-selected gene set (e.g. recombination-rate bins) against a genome-wide distribution.

name: mcl-weighted-graph-clustering
description: Use when you have gene cluster assignments plus per-contig ORF ordering (all_genes_cluster.tsv + all_genes.fna) and want to group co-localized genes into synteny clusters for pathway-level functional insight.

name: mcmc-hyperparameter-and-burnin-tuning
description: Use when fitting a Bayesian DTM regression on compositional microbiome data (e.g. genus-level OTU counts) and you must choose inclusion-prior hyperparameters, MCMC run length/burn-in, and association-selection cutoffs before comparing variable-selection counts across methods.

name: mcmc-posterior-inference
