description: Use when posterior samples of covariate-taxon or mediation-effect inclusion are needed from compositional count data via MicroBVS MCMC (DMbvs_R, MCMC_Med) before applying selected_DM or Selection_Med1/Med2.

name: mds-ordination-visualization
description: Use when assessing case-control beta-diversity of metagenome abundance profiles (taxonomic levels L2-L7 or gene abundance) and you need ordination plots plus a significance test of sample grouping (e.g. T2D vs controls).

name: median-iqr-summary-tabulation
description: Use when you have per-iteration error rates (e.g. proportion of taxa with p < 0.05 under 1000 artificial case/control splits) and need a compact median (IQR) summary table per method and taxonomic level (phylum l2, family l5).

name: medication-covariate-adjustment
description: Use when reanalyzing longitudinal gut-microbiome data (e.g. the Maifeld et al. 2021 fasting MetS cohort) where medication use is a confounder and the goal is to identify which time-associated species are reducible to medication covariates.

name: mem-mode-taxonomic-classification
description: Use when classifying Illumina or Roche/454 metagenomic sequencing reads against a protein reference database (e.g. NCBI nr microbial subset) and maximum exact match sensitivity is preferred over k-mer-based classifiers like Kraken or Clark.

name: memory-and-throughput-profiling
description: Use when a tool's memory footprint (e.g. RawHash's large index for large genomes like the human genome) must be quantified and compared across seeding or preset modes, with peak RSS and indexing/mapping throughput tabulated side-by-side.

name: memory-footprint-comparison-across-amq-structures
description: Use when evaluating how a k-mer abundance index (fimpera vs raw counting Bloom filter) trades memory footprint in bits against false positive rate, e.g. to size a filter for a 2% FPR target.

name: memory-footprint-profiling
description: Use when comparing computational cost (peak RAM during database/index construction and classification runtime) of taxonomic classifiers on an identical simulated dataset such as setA2, mirroring Additional file 1 Table S3.

name: memory-scaling-performance-profiling
description: Decision support for sizing compute resources (CPUs/RAM) before running DIAMOND-based annotation of large FASTQ/FASTA metatranscriptome files against a local DIAMOND-indexed database such as NCBI nr Bacteria (~6 GB).

name: mesocosm-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when validating a source attribution tool against mesocosms of known fecal spike-in composition, or when reproducing the per-source sensitivity table showing which fecal sources (e.g., cow) yield false negatives.

name: metabat2-contig-binning
description: Use when you have multi-sample assembled metagenomic contigs (e.g. metaSPAdes/MegaHIT output from CAMI II GI/Air/PA mock communities) that must be grouped into per-sample MAGs before taxonomic classification.

name: metabolic-pathway-reconstruction
description: Use when the input is an ASV/OTU abundance table plus a study-sequence FASTA and the goal is a predicted metagenome functional profile (EC gene families and MetaCyc pathway abundances) without shotgun sequencing data.

name: metabolic-potential-recap-table-generation
description: Use when you have a genome or MAG FASTA plus KEGG KO annotations (eggNOG .emapper.annotations, KAAS, or KofamKoala format) and need tabular KEGG Module completeness/metabolic potential summaries without HMM-based annotation expansion.

name: metabolic-prediction-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when a sequence-based metabolic assignment tool must be validated against reference-labelled genomes, and comparative performance versus blast/reciprocal--hit baselines needs to be quantified.

name: metadata-column-mapping-for-classification
description: Use when a tab-separated metadata file accompanies a merged metaphlan/qiime abundance table for supervised model training in MegaR, and the columns holding sample IDs and class labels must be identified by column number.

name: metadata-sample-id-joining
description: Use when a header-present CSV metadata table must be aligned to a sample-by-sample SNP distance matrix (or selected subset of samples) before visualization or outbreak analysis, ensuring each genomic sample resolves to its patient metadata.

name: metagenome-assembled-genome-completeness-estimation
description: Use when analyzing genome sets of mixed or dubious quality (MAGs, SAGs, bins, SUBs) where completeness varies widely, and a completeness prior must feed into iterative Bayesian core/accessory partitioning.

name: metagenome-assembled-genome-phenotyping
description: Use when characterizing draft MAGs (e.g. biogas reactor bins like unClos_1 at ~91% or unFirm_1 at ~60% completeness) with present/absent phenotype calls, especially to verify a manual reconstruction.

name: metagenome-assembled-genome-quality-assessment
description: Use when binned contig FASTA files (MAG bins) have been produced by a binning step and per-bin completeness, contamination, and assembly statistics (N50, contig count, total length) must be estimated and summarized.

name: metagenome-assembled-genome-quality-assessment
description: Use when a collection of MAG FASTA files (e.g. 19,542 VMGC prokaryotic genomes from Zenodo record 10457006) must be scored for completeness/contamination and assigned MIMAG-revised quality tiers.

name: metagenome-assembly-accuracy-evaluation-with-metaquast
description: Use when contigs from a strain-aware metagenome assembler must be scored against known reference genomes to quantify reconstruction accuracy (genome fraction, misassemblies) across varying coverage levels or conditions.

name: metagenome-assembly-and-binning
description: Use when starting from raw paired-end FASTQ reads of a multi-sample shotgun metagenomics study (e.g. reads.csv sample index) and you need de novo MAGs plus VAMB clusters as upstream input for MAGinator profiling.

name: metagenome-assembly-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing metagenome assemblers on mock-community datasets (MP mock, GIS20) where reference genomes are known and NGA50, misassembly, and interspecies-misassembly metrics must be reproduced.

name: metagenome-assembly-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing hybrid vs. short-read-only assembly, or group-wise co-assembly vs. sample-wise assembly, using metrics like N50, assembly size, and MAG counts on simulated or real metagenomic time-series data.

name: metagenome-assembly-evaluation
description: Use when HiFi long-read FASTQ reads and a metagenome assembly (FASTA, built-in or user-provided under outputs/<sample>/<assembler>/assembly.fasta) are available and you need to quantify how representative the assembly is of the sequenced sample.

name: metagenome-assembly-iteration-management
description: Use when running Strainberry on a strain-oblivious long-read assembly (FASTA plus sorted, indexed BAM) and you need to control iteration count via the Hamming rate improvement stopping rule and --max-strains multiplicity cap.

name: metagenome-assembly-mapping-ratio-computation
description: Use when evaluating a HiFi long-read metagenome assembly by quantifying the proportion of raw reads and read bases that align to contigs, optionally stratified by bin quality (e.g. medium quality or higher).

name: metagenome-bin-quality-classification
description: Use when a set of binned metagenome contigs (e.g. MetaBAT2 bins from a HiFi co-assembly) needs to be assigned quality labels from CheckM2 completeness/contamination values for assembly comparison or reporting.

name: metagenome-binning-quality-assessment
description: Use when binning has produced MAG FASTA bins and you need BUSCO- or CheckM2-estimated completeness/contamination scores to gate which bins go to GTDB-Tk versus CAT/BAT, or to report MAG quality.

name: metagenome-community-composition-design
description: Use when you need simulated long-read metagenome communities of known strain composition (e.g. 2-5 conspecific E. coli strains, Mock3 downsampling at 5x-50x) to benchmark strain-separation tools like Strainberry.

name: metagenome-dataset-retrieval-sra
description: Use when a reproduction task requires the HiSeq, MiSeq or simBA-5 metagenomes referenced by NCBI SRA accessions (SRS019120, SRS014468, SRS015055) as classification-benchmark input.

name: metagenome-de-novo-assembly
description: Use when preprocessed metagenomic FASTQ reads (short-only, long-only, or hybrid short+long) per sample must be assembled de novo into contigs and per-assembler quality summaries are needed.

name: metagenome-de-novo-assembly-pipeline-execution
description: Use when you need to assemble individual strain-level genomes de novo from Illumina metagenomic short reads (interleaved FASTQ) and compare reconstruction quality against assemblers.

name: metagenome-functional-annotation-comparison
description: Use when you have paired MAG and complete reference genome FASTAs with KEGG KO annotations and need to quantify how faithfully HMM-recovered annotations on MAGs reproduce isolate-genome annotations.

name: metagenome-functional-prediction-from-16s
description: Use when the input is a closed-reference-picked 16S OTU table (e.g., Greengenes+IMG, QIIME 1.5.0-dev/uclust) and the goal is to infer KO/gene family abundances or pathway-level functional profiles without shotgun metagenome data.

name: metagenome-functional-profiling
description: Use when the input is an ASV/OTU abundance table plus study marker-gene sequences (e.g., 16S rDNA FASTA) and the goal is predicting functional content rather than sequencing a shotgun metagenome directly.

name: metagenome-overlap-graph-assembly
description: Use when assembling individual strain-level genomes de novo from Illumina-type metagenomic short reads without a reference, especially for high-complexity communities with many closely related strains.

name: metagenome-prediction-accuracy-correlation
description: Use when evaluating trustworthiness of PICRUSt metagenome predictions on 16S-only communities: compute per-sample NSTI on a marker gene tree and correlate it with prediction accuracy to detect accuracy decay across host-associated and environmental habitats.

name: metagenome-read-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking metagenomic gene prediction or sequence-analysis tools where nucleotide-level ground-truth gene coordinates are needed, i.e. reads must be simulated from annotated genomes at known error rates.

name: metagenome-scalability-runtime-profiling
description: Use when you must verify that Libra's all-vs-all k-mer scoring scales linearly with input volume, or when you need per-algorithm (COSINESIMILARITY, BRAYCURTIS, JENSENSHANNON) and per-run-mode (MAP vs REDUCE) runtime figures on Hadoop.

name: metagenome-short-read-assembly
description: Use when metagenomics short reads (not assembled genomes) are the genomic counterpart to GNPS mass spectrometry data and RiPP discovery requires contigs as input to 6-frame translation and motif-ORF/all-ORF precursor mining.

name: metagenome-short-read-assembly
description: Use when the input is interleaved paired-end Illumina FASTQ from a metagenome or mock community and the goal is de novo reconstruction of individual strain-level genomes without a reference.

name: metagenome-simulated-dataset-benchmarking
description: Use when validating a metagenome distance metric on simulated 454/PacBio mock-community datasets that vary sequencing depth, dominant-organism abundance, or genetic composition, to compare logarithmic vs natural k-mer weighting against Mash and Simka.

name: metagenome-wide-association-statistics
description: Use when running OMARU phylogenetic case-control MWAS and needing a multiple-testing threshold that controls type I error under the study's own clade count and sample structure, rather than a standard Bonferroni cutoff.

name: metagenomic-abundance-aggregation
description: Use when you have reconstructed SSU rRNA sequences with per-sequence read-count abundances from a metagenomic pipeline and need to deduplicate near-identical sequences at a 97% identity threshold while consolidating their abundances.

name: metagenomic-abundance-extraction-from-classifier-outputs
description: Use when benchmarking taxonomic abundance estimators on admixture/food-sequencing samples where cross-reactivity (false-positive signal) between closely related species, e.g. cattle/water buffalo or sheep/goat, must be quantified per classifier.

name: metagenomic-abundance-quantification
description: Use when raw FASTA/FASTQ reads from a sample must be classified against a reference genome collection and species-level abundances (or false-positive/deviation metrics like Σ FP and Σ Dev) are the target output.

name: metagenomic-all-vs-all-clustering
description: Use when you need to cluster many large whole-genome shotgun metagenomes (billions of reads, e.g., FASTQ/FASTA) all-vs-all by k-mer composition and abundance, where sketching, data reduction, or presence/absence metrics would diminish resolution.

name: metagenomic-alpha-diversity-estimation
description: Use when QCed metagenomic profiling tables (phylogenetic clades L2–L7 or gene abundance) from case–control shotgun data are available and the goal is to test whether within-sample diversity differs between cases and controls.

name: metagenomic-annotation-statistics-aggregation
description: Use when you have GeneMark-HM output on human microbiome metagenome assemblies and need to quantify how many contigs were assigned to species-level pan-genomes versus handled by the GeneMarkS-2 or MetaGeneMark fallback branches.

name: metagenomic-assembler-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing how many protein sequences different de novo assemblers recover from the same metagenomic reads, or when reproducing the Plass 2–10x recovery claim on complex metagenomes.

name: metagenomic-assembler-comparison
description: Use when short-read metagenomic data must be assembled and no single assembler is obviously appropriate; comparing SPAdes, metaSPAdes, and MEGAHIT by N50 lets contiguity decide the assembly carried forward.

name: metagenomic-assembly-based-gene-profiling
description: Use when building gene-level functional abundance profiles from shotgun metagenomic FASTQ reads via de novo assembly and UniRef90 gene annotation, e.g. as input to gene-level MWAS case-control tests.

name: metagenomic-assembly-benchmarking
description: Use when benchmarking multiple de novo assemblers on a known mock-community metagenomic sample with reference replicons available, to compare global metrics (Nx, contigs, mapped reads) and per-reference metrics (contiguity, multiplicity, validity, Lx, NAx, NGx).

name: metagenomic-assembly-evaluation
description: Use when multiple de novo assemblers have been run on the same recruited viral read set and you must rank their contigs against known haplotypes with MetaQUAST metrics such as N50 and genome coverage.

name: metagenomic-assembly-gene-calling
description: Use when building a body-site non-redundant gene catalog from vaginal metagenomic FASTQ read sets and isolate genomes, requiring per-sample assembly, CDS prediction, and all-vs-all BLASTP de-redundification.

name: metagenomic-assembly-homology-search
description: Use when you have a single reference genome (or per-species references) and per-sample metagenomic assemblies/genomes, and need to extract conserved homologous regions with flanking context before downstream strain-comparison analyses.

name: metagenomic-assembly-length-filtering
description: Use when a metagenomic or isolate assembly (e.g., SPAdes 3.9.1 scaffolds) contains many short contigs that are about to be classified by a kmer-based method (PlasFlow) and results for short sequences would otherwise be unreliable.

name: metagenomic-assembly-quality-assessment
description: Use when comparing metagenomic assemblers on the same Illumina read set (mock or simulated viral/bacterial communities) and you need genome fraction, misassembly, and per-100 kb error metrics against reference genomes.

name: metagenomic-assembly-retrieval
description: Use when reproducing plasmidome classification benchmarks that require downloading the four reference plasmidome assemblies and filtering contigs to >1000 bp before running kmer-based plasmid/chromosome classifiers.

name: metagenomic-assembly-scaffolding
description: Use when raw sequencing reads (FASTQ) must be turned into a filtered scaffold/contig FASTA before kmer-signature-based classification (e.g. PlasFlow plasmid prediction) on metagenomic or small-genome assemblies.

name: metagenomic-assembly-strain-comparison
description: Use when tracking shared or closely related strains between pairs of metagenomic assemblies (or genomes) of the same species, especially when structural variation, low-data contexts (phages/plasmids), or SNP-insensitivity is required rather than popANI/SNP counting.

name: metagenomic-bam-position-depth-profiling
description: Use when you have a sorted .bam mapped to a reference .fasta and need per-scaffold coverage, breadth, expected breadth, and nucleotide-diversity metrics for genome populations in a metagenome.

name: metagenomic-benchmark-result-comparison
description: Reference for evaluating whether a new k-mer/minhash-based read classifier beats established metagenomics tools (CLARK, Kraken2, Kraken2+Bracken) on FP rate and abundance estimation accuracy over the same reference genome database.

name: metagenomic-binning-and-scaffold-clustering
description: Use when a hybrid metagenome assembly (Illumina paired-end plus ONT/PacBio long reads or mate pairs) must be partitioned into species-specific scaffold clusters, or when near-complete genomes and biologically important elements must be detected per bin.

name: metagenomic-catalogue-construction
description: Use when short-read metagenomic (FASTQ.GZ) data from mixed microbial communities must be mined for novel insertion sequences and consolidated into a non-redundant FASTA catalogue for downstream annotation or genome querying.

name: metagenomic-cds-dereplication
description: Use when building a body-site non-redundant gene catalog from a large set of predicted CDSs (nucleotide FASTA) and redundant near-identical sequences across metagenomes must be collapsed into cluster representatives for downstream annotation and read mapping.

name: metagenomic-clade-association-testing
description: Use when QCed shotgun metagenomic FASTQ data from case and control cohorts are available and per-clade disease association statistics (p-values/FDR) are needed via phylogenetic profiling.

name: metagenomic-classifier-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating how a taxonomic classifier behaves on reads from species missing from its database, i.e. when quantifying false positives caused by similarity to the closest available relative rather than true species presence.

name: metagenomic-classifier-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing taxonomic classification accuracy (sensitivity/precision) of metagenomic classifiers on simulated read sets with known origins, e.g. Kraken vs BLAST-based or k-mer-based classifiers.

name: metagenomic-classifier-database-building
description: Use when building a custom Kraken taxonomy database from a set of reference genomes (e.g. NCBI RefSeq complete microbial genomes) so every k-mer maps to an LCA taxonomic label.

name: metagenomic-contamination-assessment
description: Use when validating that a custom marker-gene or reference database is specific to its target kingdom by measuring how many of its sequences align against a large out-group reference catalog (e.g., fungal markers vs. a bacterial gut genome catalog).

name: metagenomic-contig-binning
description: Use when starting from a metagenomic de Bruijn-graph assembly (FASTA contigs >=500 bp) plus the trimmed reads, and the goal is a bin-quality table of completeness and strain heterogeneity per bin.

name: metagenomic-contig-binning
description: Use when starting from paired-end metagenomic shotgun reads (e.g. FASTQ) and non-redundant MAG sets are needed as input for downstream MAG taxonomy classification, especially for benchmarking classifiers.

name: metagenomic-contig-classification
description: Use when a metagenomic or plasmidome assembly (FASTA contigs/scaffolds) needs plasmid-vs-chromosome assignment with initial phylum-level taxonomy, and kmer-signature classification without prior knowledge of sample composition is appropriate.

name: metagenomic-contig-clustering-by-organism
description: Use when metagenomic shotgun reads/contigs must be grouped by organism of origin before downstream per-group model fitting, e.g. to gate retraining of gene prediction IMMs within each cluster.

name: metagenomic-contig-depth-estimation
description: Use when you have assembled metagenomic contigs plus per-sample short-read FASTQs and need per-contig mean sequencing depths across samples to feed co-abundance-based binning (e.g., MetaBAT2) or to estimate MAG abundances.

name: metagenomic-contig-extension
description: Use when metaSPAdes or another de novo assembler has produced viral metagenomic seed contigs of only a few kb and the goal is to lengthen them with paired or unpaired FASTQ reads while checking accuracy against NCBI viral reference sequences.

name: metagenomic-contig-taxonomy-annotation
description: Use when you need to classify assembled metagenomic contigs as putative viral sequences and need a reproducible confidence label based on agreement across multiple detection tools rather than a single-tool call.

name: metagenomic-count-filtering
description: Use when a mapped gene frequency count table from a mapping-based metagenomic pipeline is sparse and compositional and must be filtered, length-corrected and CSS-normalized before taxonomic or functional (KO/EC/reaction) profiling.

name: metagenomic-count-normalization
description: Use when the input is a sparse, high-throughput marker-gene (OTU/species/taxon) count matrix with two or more sample groups, and per-feature differential abundance statistics must account for both normalization and under-sampling of microbial communities.

name: metagenomic-database-construction
description: Use when constructing a k-mer/minhash classification database from large multi-kingdom reference genome collections where full-database build exceeds workstation memory, or when benchmarking build time and peak RAM across partition/executor counts.

name: metagenomic-de-novo-assembly
description: Use when raw or preprocessed paired-end metagenome FASTQ reads must be assembled into contigs de novo as the first step toward building or reproducing a gene catalog such as VIRGO, and assembly statistics are the deliverable.

name: metagenomic-differential-abundance-analysis
description: Use when comparing metagenomic abundance profiles (taxon/gene/KO/EC/reaction tables) across phenotype groups (e.g. healthy vs adenoma vs carcinoma) to find significantly changed biomarker features while correcting compositional bias.

name: metagenomic-distance-behavior-validation
description: Use when you need to reproduce, reimplement, or validate scalable all-vs-all metagenome distance computation from k-mer frequency vectors, or sanity-check that a distance implementation yields near-zero self-distance.

name: metagenomic-fastq-accession-handling
description: Use when reproducing a k-mer abundance indexing/AMQ benchmark that requires concrete public metagenomic FASTQ runs — one dataset to build the index and an independent query dataset for FPR measurement.

name: metagenomic-fecal-source-tracking
description: Use when gzipped FASTQ shotgun metagenomes from water samples must be attributed to specific fecal source categories and apportioned by cell fraction, without sequencing the potential sources themselves.

name: metagenomic-flanking-region-extraction
description: Use when short-read metagenomic FASTQ data must yield the genomic context (flanking regions) around ARGs or other target genes, and full de novo assembly would be computationally prohibitive.

name: metagenomic-functional-annotation-level-comparison
description: Decision support for choosing between gene-level and functional-level (KO/EC/reaction) differential analysis of mapped metagenomic count data, when you have per-level significance ratios from a case-control dataset such as CAMAMED's colorectal adenoma/carcinoma (CAMAMED) run.

name: metagenomic-functional-annotation-pipeline-configuration
description: Use when installing MetaLAFFA or customizing its pipeline operation — choosing steps, per-step parameters, cluster submission settings, or reference databases (UniRef90, KEGG mappings, host decoys) — prior to annotating shotgun metagenomic FASTQ data.

name: metagenomic-functional-pathway-profiling
description: Use when shotgun metagenomic case-control data (e.g. SCZ n=344, T2D n=171) require pathway-level enrichment testing and integration with host GWAS summary statistics to evaluate pathway overlap.

name: metagenomic-functional-profiling
description: Use when metagenomic reads have already been mapped to a non-redundant gene catalog yielding per-sample gene frequencies, and the goal is to extend these into KO, EC number and reaction annotations with per-sample functional frequencies.

name: metagenomic-gene-catalogue-processing
description: Use when a metagenomic analysis needs gene clusters grouped by genomic adjacency (synteny) to associate functional content and shared pathways with MAG clusters or subspecies clades.

name: metagenomic-gene-cluster-functional-summarization
description: Use when you have MAGinator synteny_clusters.tab output plus a non-redundant gene catalogue and need to attach KEGG module assignments per synteny cluster and measure functional coherence.

name: metagenomic-gene-count-matrix-curation
description: Use when profiling de novo MAG clusters from shotgun metagenomics requires cluster-specific signature genes: you have a gene read-count matrix (small_gene_count_matrix.tsv) and MAG cluster assignments (metagenomicspecies.tab) and need abundance-grade gene sets.

name: metagenomic-gene-prediction
description: Use when input is unassembled metagenomic DNA reads (e.g. Sanger, 454, or Illumina shotgun reads) and the goal is nucleotide-level gene prediction with sensitivity/precision scoring against known gene coordinates.

name: metagenomic-gene-prediction
description: Use when input is a metagenome assembly FASTA (human microbiome contigs) needing gene prediction in GTF format, and near-complete-genome accuracy is required for short contigs without genomic context.

name: metagenomic-gene-prediction
description: Use when you have assembled genome FASTA files (MAGs, fungal genomes, viral genomes/vOTUs) and need translated protein-coding gene sequences as input for downstream gene clustering, annotation or gene catalogue construction.

name: metagenomic-gene-to-ortholog-mapping
description: Use when you have a gene-level (e.g. UniRef90-based, length-normalized) abundance table and a gene-to-KO mapping file, and need a KO-level functional profile per sample.

name: metagenomic-genome-assembly
description: Use when processing shotgun viral metagenomic FASTQ reads in ViroProfiler and you need per-sample assembled contigs plus a single species-level non-redundant contig library (nrclib.fasta) for downstream annotation, taxonomy assignment, and analysis.

name: metagenomic-genome-dereplication
description: Use when a genome set assembled/binned from metagenomes will be used as a concatenated mapping reference or for cross-tool strain-sharing benchmarks, and redundant near-identical genomes (e.g. >98% ANI) must be collapsed first.

name: metagenomic-genome-size-estimation
description: Use when metagenomic read-mapping results (per-genome sequence depth X from CoverM against source-associated genome databases) must be normalized to genome equivalents to express source signal as approximate cell fractions.

name: metagenomic-hic-binning-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing viral binning tools on metagenomic Hi-C datasets (shotgun + Hi-C FASTQ pairs from SRA/ENA) and evaluating recovered vMAGs by completeness categories.

name: metagenomic-hic-multi-dataset-quality-benchmarking
description: Use when you have cleaned Hi-C paired-end FASTQ reads from several metagenomic Hi-C datasets and need a reference-free, quantitative measure of ligation/library quality comparable across datasets.

name: metagenomic-hit-summarization
description: Use when you have filtered read-to-gene DIAMOND alignment hits ( e-value per read) from shotgun metagenomic data and need to compute per-gene abundance counts, including fractional assignment of multi-mapping reads.

name: metagenomic-is-candidate-screening
description: Use when paired-end short-read metagenomic reads have already been screened for inverted repeats by pal-MEM (LCoord/RCoord annotated FASTA) and sample assemblies exist, and you need proximity-filtered candidate ITR reads.

name: metagenomic-metadata-regression-modeling
description: Use when you have a microbial feature abundance table (taxonomic or functional profiles) plus sample metadata (e.g. geography, health status, extraction method) and need significant feature–variable associations from multivariable linear models.

name: metagenomic-mock-data-simulation
description: Use when a reproducible mock compositional abundance table (with matched control/disease phenotype data) is needed to test or benchmark metagenomic feature-enrichment or causality-inference methods such as VTwins.

name: metagenomic-pipeline-benchmarking
description: Use when you need to quantify wall-clock time, peak memory footprint, and CPU-hour usage of a Snakemake-based metagenomic pipeline (e.g. ARGprofiler with fastp, KMA, ARGextender, SPAdes, Mash rules) under its final parameter settings.

name: metagenomic-preprocessing
description: Use when raw shotgun metagenomic FASTQs must be cleaned before functional annotation — removing human/host reads, PCR or optical duplicates, and low-quality or too-short reads prior to gene mapping.

name: metagenomic-preprocessing-pipeline
description: Use when raw metagenomic samples arrive as SRA archives and must be converted to FASTQ/FASTA, quality-checked, and characterized with per-sample sequence statistics before taxonomic/functional mapping.

name: metagenomic-protein-assembly
description: Use when the goal is to maximize protein sequence recovery from complex metagenomic or metatranscriptomic short-read data (paired-end FASTQ or single-end FASTA/FASTQ) by assembling directly at the protein level.

name: metagenomic-protein-sequence-screening
description: Use when you need to identify and type-classify proteins (e.g. DsrA/DsrB and paralogous families) in thousands of (meta)genomic protein sequences in FASTA format, at scale, without phylogenetic reconstruction.

name: metagenomic-read-alignment
description: Use when shotgun metagenomic FASTQ reads (e.g., the 30-sample BIO-ML set from PRJNA544527 or a 121-sample H. pylori eradication cohort) must be mapped to a reference database to generate per-sample BAMs for downstream variant detection.

name: metagenomic-read-alignment
description: Use when paired-end shotgun metagenomic FASTQ reads must be mapped to a combined microbiome reference FASTA while preserving junction pairs mapping across different references, as the first stage of LEMON's HGT detection pipeline.

name: metagenomic-read-alignment-to-gene-catalog
description: Use when you have QC'd shotgun metagenomic FASTQ reads and a non-redundant gene catalog (e.g., the IGC catalog), and you need per-sample gene frequencies as input to compositional differential-abundance analysis.

name: metagenomic-read-alignment-to-genome-databases
description: Use when assigning shotgun metagenomic reads from water or mesocosm samples (e.g. FASTQ reads from PRJNA1161616) to individual genomes in a source-associated database to quantify per-genome and per-source-category signal.

name: metagenomic-read-alignment-to-viral-scaffolds
description: Use when predicted viral scaffolds (e.g., from VIBRANT or VirSorter) must be binned from metagenomes and per-sample coverage tables are needed as input to vRhyme's coverage variance / effect-size binning network.

name: metagenomic-read-classification
description: Use when classifying high-throughput sequencing reads (Illumina FASTQ, single- or paired-end) from metagenomic whole-genome sequencing to NCBI taxa, especially when reference genomes are incomplete or distant strains must still be classified.

name: metagenomic-read-classification
description: Use when classifying paired-end metagenomic reads (e.g. simulated setA2/setB2 or HMP metagenome SRR1804065) against a reference genome FASTA in alignment-free fashion, computing sensitivity/precision/F1/specificity.

name: metagenomic-read-classification
description: Use when assigning taxonomic labels to large sets of metagenomic reads (FASTQ/FASTA from SRA accessions such as SRS019120, SRS014468, SRS015055, or Mason-simulated reads), or when benchmarking classifier speed and accuracy against Megablast or MetaPhlAn.

name: metagenomic-read-classification
description: Use when classifying shotgun FASTQ/FASTA reads from complex biological samples (e.g., calibrator sausage mixtures) against large reference genome collections to detect ingredient/species composition and estimate abundances with low false-positive rates.

name: metagenomic-read-classification
description: Use when classifying fastq/fasta metagenomic reads at species or genus rank, especially gut microbiome reads from uncultured MAGs where k-mer/LCA tools miss species absent from reference databases.

name: metagenomic-read-clustering
description: Use when metagenomic Illumina short reads must be split into strain/species-coherent read groups before per-cluster assembly, e.g. as the preprocessing step of an overlap-layout-consensus strain-aware assembly pipeline.

name: metagenomic-read-coordinate-processing
description: Use when scanning metagenomic FASTA reads with pal-MEM for inverted terminal repeats and you need to encode read coordinates in two-bit space, apply edge-boundary conditions, or exclude MEMs near read ends that arise from amplification artifacts.

name: metagenomic-read-counting-per-taxon
description: Use when you already have per-read taxonomic assignments from a MetaCache/MetaCacheSpark query run and need organism-level read counts and abundance percentages at a chosen rank such as species.

name: metagenomic-read-digital-normalization
description: Use when raw paired-end virome FASTQ reads (e.g. SRA runs like SRR3458562 or SRR9875293) feed into VirMAP's mapping assembly, pileup rebuilding, or DIAMOND/BBMap alignment and read depth is uneven or redundant.

name: metagenomic-read-gene-annotation
description: Use when per-sample DIAMOND tabular hits against a gene catalog (e.g. UniRef90) need -e-value refinement and fractional gene counting to produce gene/orthology abundances from shotgun metagenomic FASTQs.

name: metagenomic-read-length-and-n-trimming
description: Use when raw or primer-trimmed amplicon FASTQ reads (454 or Illumina) show deteriorating 3'-end quality or embedded Ns and must be trimmed and length-filtered before dereplication and OTU clustering.

name: metagenomic-read-mapping
description: Use when metagenomic paired-end FASTQ reads need to be mapped to a multi-genome reference .fasta to quantify genome detection, coverage, microdiversity, or strain sharing (e.g., ZymoBIOMICS mock-community benchmarking).

name: metagenomic-read-mapping-and-counting
description: Use when shotgun metagenomic reads (FASTQ) must be quantified against de novo MAG clusters or signature gene sets to estimate organism/subspecies abundances per sample, e.g. tracking B. infantis and B. longum across the COPSAC2010 and CHILD infant cohorts.

name: metagenomic-read-mapping-quantification
description: Use when short-read shotgun metagenomes (FASTQ) must be converted from mapped-read counts into genome-equivalent relative abundances (cell fractions) against a source-associated genome database for source tracking.

name: metagenomic-read-mapping-to-gene-catalog
description: Use when you need to profile the taxonomic and/or functional composition of vaginal metagenomic or metatranscriptomic FASTQ samples against the VIRGO gene catalog instead of assembling reads de novo.

name: metagenomic-read-pair-filtering
description: Use when metagenomic reads have been mapped to representative sub-species genomes (e.g. concatenated .fasta) and per-scaffold or per-genome coverage, clonality, nucleotide diversity, or SNV calls must be computed without contamination from falsely mapped read pairs.

name: metagenomic-read-pooling-and-spike-in-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking a targeted assembly or annotation pipeline (e.g. CasCollect) against a complete metagenome assembly, and a simulated community with known CRISPR/Cas content and background host contamination is needed from raw FASTQ reads.

name: metagenomic-read-quality-control
description: Use when raw paired-end or single-end Illumina metagenomic FASTQ/fastq.gz reads must be adapter-trimmed and quality-trimmed before SSU rRNA read extraction or any 16S/18S-based taxonomic classification.

name: metagenomic-read-quality-control
description: Use when raw vaginal metagenomic or metatranscriptomic fastq reads must be cleaned (human/rRNA removal) and mapped to a reference gene catalog such as VIRGO before taxonomic or functional profiling.

name: metagenomic-read-quality-filtering
description: Use when quality-controlling shotgun metagenomic FASTQs as part of an end-to-end functional annotation pipeline, after host and duplicate read filtering and before mapping reads to a gene database.

name: metagenomic-read-quality-trimming
description: Use when raw paired-end Illumina shotgun metagenomic reads (e.g. SRA accession SRR606249, 2 x 100 bp) must be cleaned prior to meta-assembly with metaSPAdes or MegaHIT.

name: metagenomic-read-query-execution
description: Use when benchmarking fimpera-style amplified s-mer querying of a counting Bloom filter on metagenomic FASTQ reads, specifically to verify that query time stays flat or slightly decreases as z increases.

name: metagenomic-read-recruitment-analysis
description: Use when evaluating or benchmarking a reference gene catalogue's sequence-capture efficiency on shotgun metagenomic FASTQ samples, or comparing a new catalogue (e.g. VMGC-90) against an incumbent (e.g. VIRGO) via per-sample mapping rates.

name: metagenomic-read-recruitment-targeted-assembly
description: Use when you need genomic flanking regions around antimicrobial resistance genes (or other target genes) from short-read metagenomic FASTQ data, and full metagenomic de novo assembly is too computationally expensive.

name: metagenomic-read-simulation
description: Use when you need synthetic longitudinal metagenomic reads carrying within-strain SNVs and small InDels with configurable allele-frequency trajectories, to benchmark mutation-detection tools.

name: metagenomic-read-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking a taxonomic classifier needs simulated reads with known origin, e.g., ART-generated Illumina/Roche-454 FASTQ sets from genomes whose proteins are excluded from the reference database.

name: metagenomic-read-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking HGT breakpoint detection or local strain reconstruction pipelines against known ground truth, so sensitivity and FDR can be computed from simulated reads at defined coverages.

name: metagenomic-read-simulation-and-alignment
description: Use when benchmarking metagenome binners against curated ground-truth genomes: simulated/sampled per-sample reads must be converted into sorted BAM coverage files and ORF predictions before binning and F1/precision/specificity scoring.

name: metagenomic-read-subsampling
description: Use when a genome in a simulated community is assembled at extreme coverage (e.g. >1000x) and you need to confirm that coverage — not biology — drives the observed misassembled blocks.

name: metagenomic-read-subsampling-replication
description: Use when a user wants to quantify how classification sensitivity and reconstruction completeness degrade with sequencing depth, e.g. testing a pipeline on SRA mock-community reads (FASTQ) at 10/1/0.1% subsampling across replicate trials.

name: metagenomic-read-taxonomic-attribution
description: Use when disease-associated genes from MWAS must be assigned to taxa in a shotgun metagenome, e.g., tracing which organisms reads of a specific gene derive from.

name: metagenomic-read-taxonomic-classification
description: Use when you have FASTQ read fractions (mapped/unmapped from read-contig alignment) from a HiFi metagenome assembly and need to know whether low-representation taxa are missing from the assembly.

name: metagenomic-read-taxonomic-classification
description: Use when quality-assuring preprocessed short-read FASTQ metagenomic samples prior to assembly: to classify reads against a reference database, detect contamination, and visualize microbial community composition per sample with Krona charts and a MultiQC report.

name: metagenomic-read-to-protein-alignment
description: Use when quality-filtered (host-filtered, duplicate-filtered, quality-trimmed) shotgun metagenomic FASTQs must be mapped to a microbial protein gene database like UniRef90 to obtain read-to-gene matches for functional profiling.

name: metagenomic-read-type-gating
description: Use when a metagenomic run mixes short-read-only, long-read-only, and paired short+long-read samples, and each sample must be routed to the correct assembly path (MEGAHIT vs SPAdes vs hybridSPAdes) before QUAST-based quality comparison.

name: metagenomic-reference-catalog-retrieval
description: Use when a study needs large, publicly available, redundancy-filtered reference protein catalogs (e.g. as search database input for HH-suite3/BFD or for catalog size/provenance audits) and the input is metagenomic or metatranscriptomic protein sequence space.

name: metagenomic-reference-sequence-comparison
description: Use when candidate transferred segments reconstructed from shotgun metagenomics data must be scored against donor/receptor reference segment sequences to measure local alignment similarity and reconstruction accuracy.

name: metagenomic-sample-phenotype-classification
description: Use when you have a metagenomic taxonomic profile table (MetaPhlAn merged table or QIIME OTU/BIOM) plus sample metadata with class labels, and the goal is to train a classifier or predict the phenotype of unknown samples.

name: metagenomic-scaffolding-misjoin-detection
description: Use when scaffolding metagenomic contigs with paired long-range links and you must decide which contig-pair links are probable interspecies misjoins based on coverage depth and oligonucleotide composition.

name: metagenomic-sequence-clustering-and-retraining
description: Use when predicting genes in unassembled environmental shotgun reads (e.g. 454 reads from the human gut microbiome) where GC-content alone is a poor proxy for training model parameterization and an unsupervised organism-based grouping plus retraining step is needed.

name: metagenomic-sequence-phylogenetic-classification
description: Use when gene-predicting unassembled metagenomic reads where GC-content is a poor proxy for choosing training genomes, and phylogenetic classification is needed to parameterize per-organism gene prediction models.

name: metagenomic-sequence-preprocessing
description: Use when raw FASTA/FASTQ metagenomic reads or training genomes must be transformed into fixed-length k-mer token ID sequences (canonical k-mers, <unk> handling, padding index 0) before DNN embedding and training.

name: metagenomic-shared-variant-calling
description: Use when you have shotgun metagenomic BAM alignments from many samples and need to identify SNPs shared across the population (e.g., strain-tracking or ARG diversity analysis), not per-sample de novo calling.

name: metagenomic-short-read-assembly
description: Use when raw shotgun metagenomic or virome FASTQ reads must be converted into assembled contigs before viral contig mining, e.g. reproducing the Liang et al. 2020 infant stool 59-sample vOTU analysis with MetaPhage.

name: metagenomic-short-read-mapping
description: Use when you have reconstructed full-length SSU rRNA sequences (e.g. metagenome_SSU_sequences.fasta from EMIRGE/MetaRib assembly) and need per-sequence relative abundances before 97% VSEARCH clustering.

name: metagenomic-shotgun-read-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking strain-level metagenomic variant discovery tools (e.g., MetaQuad, MQuad) and you need simulated shotgun communities with known ground-truth strain mixtures, engineered variants, and per-sample mean depths spanning 3x-35.5x.

name: metagenomic-snv-pileup-analysis
description: Use when you have VAMB-binned MAGs plus original shotgun reads and need to quantify within-sample strain diversity — i.e. which MAG clusters contain multiple variants (mixed alleles) per sample across one or more environments.

name: metagenomic-source-attribution-scoring
description: Use when benchmarking metagenomic fecal source tracking predictions against samples with known source composition (e.

name: metagenomic-strain-phylogeny-reconstruction
description: Use when you have per-MAG-cluster signature genes and per-sample read mappings and need phylogenetic trees whose leaves are samples, to associate metadata with subspecies/strain-level differences.

name: metagenomic-subspecies-stratification
description: Use when sample-level gene content profiles mapped to VIRGO (summary.Count.txt restricted via 1.taxon.tbl.txt) are available and the goal is to partition samples into within-species MG-subspecies clusters.

name: metagenomic-taxa-gene-feature-extraction
description: Use when shotgun metagenome reads must be converted into taxon- and gene-level abundance tables and differentially abundant colorectal-cancer-style biomarkers must be identified while correcting compositional bias.

name: metagenomic-taxonomic-classification-benchmarking
description: Use when you need to quantitatively compare taxonomic classifiers on metagenomic reads with known community composition, computing per-tool F-measure at genus and species level and runtime.

name: metagenomic-taxonomic-profiling
description: Use when shotgun metagenome FASTQ reads (e.g., mesocosm samples from PRJNA1161616 and fecal spike-in slurries from PRJNA1092107) must be converted into Kraken2 taxonomic profiles or kmtricks k-mer count tables to serve as input for FEAST, metaSourceTracker, or decOM source tracking comparisons.

name: metagenomic-taxonomy-profiling-of-rna-seq-reads
description: Use when RNA-seq FASTQ reads must be screened for microbial (bacterial, archaeal, viral) content: host reads are filtered against a STAR reference index and the exogenous remainder is classified taxonomically with kraken2.

name: metagenomic-technical-replicate-separation-analysis
description: Decision support for choosing Mash sketch and k-mer sizes when k-mer distances must distinguish technical resequencings of one sample from other metagenomes in a large-scale pipeline.

name: metagenomic-variant-matrix-processing
description: Use when you have per-sample AD/DP allele counts from cellsnp-lite over shotgun metagenomic (e.g., ARG) loci and need to filter MetaQuad informative variants (num_of_clusters >= 2 in BIC_params.csv) into an AF matrix for Bray-Curtis PCoA and pairwise.adonis group comparison.

name: metagenomics-depth-of-coverage-import
description: Use when a tabular metagenomics depth-of-coverage time series (Example 1 / BWWTP data) must be loaded into MOVIS for time-series visualization, and the temporal feature must be confirmed during sanitizing.

name: metal-resistance-gene-collection-assembly
description: Use when building a merged, homology-reduced reference of metal-resistance (or stress-type) genes from versioned source databases, or when reproducing the PanRes curation counts of 14,078 unique sequences and 5,280 centroids.

name: metaproteomics-cluster-label-analysis
description: Use when validating or reproducing a clustering result on time-series metaproteomics data (e.g., MOVIS Example 1 embeddings) by cross-tabulating cluster labels against sampling-time periods and testing whether a majority of one cluster maps to a specific temporal segment.

name: metarib-targeted-assembly
description: Use when reconstructing SSU rRNA genes from metagenomic reads as part of the RiboTaxa pipeline: specifically, when MetaRib must assemble rRNA targets from the unfiltered high-quality (BBTools-trimmed) reads, complementary to the SortMeRNA-filtered EMIRGE branch.

name: metatranscriptome-abundance-estimation
description: Use when raw FASTQ metatranscriptome reads (paired-end or >100 bp) must be converted into organism abundance summaries, or when mRNA-derived abundance must be validated against rRNA-derived abundance in non-ribodepleted samples.

name: metatranscriptome-annotation-aggregation
description: Use when you have downloaded per-read annotation results files (e.g. from MG-RAST v3.6 or DIAMOND BLAST-like output) and need ranked abundance summaries of organisms or functions for statistical comparison.

name: metatranscriptome-diversity-index-computation
description: Use when SAMSA2 abundance summary tables (ranked feature counts per metatranscriptome, produced by DIAMOND_analysis_counter.py) are available and per-sample diversity (Shannon, Simpson) or downstream DESeq statistics are needed.

name: metatranscriptome-pipeline-benchmarking
description: Use when you need to quantify runtime or throughput of a standalone metatranscriptome analysis pipeline against a web-service baseline (e.g., SAMSA2 vs MG-RAST/SAMSA 1.0) on a fixed set of test files.

name: metatranscriptome-read-annotation
description: Use when raw metatranscriptome FASTQ reads have been preprocessed (PEAR-merged, Trimmomatic-trimmed, SortMeRNA rRNA-filtered) and must be assigned organism and function labels from a local protein database.

name: metatranscriptome-read-preprocessing
description: Use when raw paired-end FASTQ metatranscriptome reads must be converted into ribosome-filtered, quality- and adapter-trimmed input for DIAMOND annotation, e.g. as the first stage of the SAMSA2 master_script pipeline.

name: metatranscriptome-read-subsampling
description: Decision support for planning metatranscriptome sequencing depth, or when validating that a sample's annotated-read count suffices for accurate low-abundance transcript quantification.

name: metatranscriptomic-gene-fusion-breakpoint-validation
description: Use when DNA-derived HGT breakpoint candidates (e.g., from LEMON get_acc_bkp) exist for a metagenomic sample and a matched RNA-seq/metatranscriptome sample is available for independent validation.

name: metatranscriptomic-organism-abundance-testing
description: Use when you have MG-RAST (or DIAMOND) annotation results for multiple metatranscriptome samples in control vs. experimental groups and need to identify organisms whose mRNA abundance differs significantly between groups.

name: metatranscriptomic-read-quality-trimming
description: Use when starting from raw paired-end metatranscriptomic FASTQ files (e.g. ribodepleted or poly(A)-enriched stool RNA-seq) that need adapter trimming and quality cleaning before read joining and downstream annotation.

name: metavirome-database-management
description: Use when reproducing phage discovery on virome FASTQ/contigs with MetaPhage, e.g. running multiple miners (VirFinder, VirSorter, Phigaro, VIBRANT) and vOTU clustering on infant gut or similar shotgun/VLP metagenomes.

name: metavirome-pipeline-report-generation
description: Use when a paired-end virome/metagenome FASTQ dataset (e.g. VLP-enriched reads with a CSV metadata file) must be processed end-to-end and delivered as a single interactive HTML report comparing phage miners, taxonomy, and diversity.

name: metavirome-read-quality-control
description: Use when raw FASTQ reads from shotgun metagenome or virome sequencing must be quality-trimmed and decontaminated (e.g., phiX spike-in) before assembly and viral contig mining.

name: metavirome-votu-classification
description: Use when dereplicated vOTU FASTA sets from a virome or shotgun metagenome need phylum-to-genus taxonomic labels via protein-sharing clustering against curated phage references (INPHARED).

name: metrics-table-generation
description: Use when comparing abundance-call correctness of two counting-AMQ based indexes (e.g. fimpera z=3 vs original cBF of identical size) from true-positive query results with reported abundances and ground truth.

name: mg-rast-annotation-submission
description: Use when raw metatranscriptome reads have been cleaned (Trimmomatic) and optionally paired-end joined (FLASH), and organism/functional annotation via a public server is required before abundance aggregation.

name: mi-xs-package-membership-mapping
description: Use when a MIxS extension proposal designates terms for specific environmental packages and you must confirm the term-to-package mapping against the authoritative schema file mixs.yaml.

name: microbe-distance-matrix-construction
description: Use when you have a NEWICK-format phylogenetic tree (e.g. built by Mafft/FastTree from GreenGenes-matched OTU representative sequences) and need a pairwise cophenetic distance matrix between OTUs for downstream phylogeny-aware feature ordering.

name: microbe-snp-linear-regression-qtl-analysis
description: Use when taxa abundance and SNP genotype matrices over the same samples need taxa-SNP association testing via linear regression, and model-wide P value behavior must be checked with a QQ-plot.

name: microbial-genome-annotation-expansion
description: Use when a MAG or genome FASTA has partial KEGG KO annotations (e.g. from eggNOG-mapper, KAAS, or KofamKOALA) and the goal is to recover missing orthologs via HMM profile searches to expand KEGG Module completeness.

name: microbial-genome-detection-thresholding
description: Use when a mock community with known composition (e.g. ZymoBIOMICS Microbial Community Standard #D6300) and matched public reference genomes are available and you need to quantify how accurately a tool detects which genomes/strains are present.

name: microbial-network-algorithm-configuration
description: Use when configuring FlashWeave's learn_network call for OTU abundance data and you must decide between sensitive/fine-grained vs fast modes, or whether multi-habitat/multi-protocol data requires the heterogeneous (HE) variant.

name: microbial-phenotype-description-preprocessing
description: Use when raw microbial taxonomic description text files (e.g., the Part_One_111_final dataset) must be segmented and cleaned before character extraction with MicroPIE or a similar NLP pipeline.

name: microbial-phenotype-model-benchmarking
description: Use when a comparative-genomics phenotype prediction task must select an SVM kernel: input is a COG presence/absence feature matrix with binary trait labels, and the goal is kernel comparison via balanced accuracy to justify a default kernel choice.

name: microbial-phenotype-prediction-from-genome
description: Use when you have bacterial nucleotide FASTA assemblies or predicted genes (e.g. population genomes such as unClos_1/unFirm_1) and need phenotype calls for 67 traits to verify or complement a metabolic reconstruction.

name: microbial-phenotypic-character-prediction
description: Use when sentences from natural-language microbial taxonomic descriptions must be assigned to phenotypic characters (e.g., Gram stain, motility, NaCl optimum) prior to rule-based character-state extraction, or when reproducing MicroPIE's reported SVM cross-validation metrics.

name: microbial-qtl-association-analysis
description: Use when host genotype (SNP/SNV matrix) and 16S rRNA microbial abundance data are available and the goal is to find taxa-SNP associations and flag LD SNV blocks via rho estimation.

name: microbial-read-retention-quantification
description: Use when benchmarking host-depletion tools for precision on non-human reads: you need to measure microbial read retention (reads_out/reads_in) from DWGSIM/PBSIM2-simulated Illumina and ONT reads against Hostile, HRRT, or masked Hostile indexes.

name: microbial-sequence-characterization
description: Use when host-filtered paired-end FASTQ files from RNA-seq data must be assigned taxonomically to detect microbial (bacterial, archaeal, viral) content, e.g. in metagenomic analysis of SSc skin RNA-seq samples like SRR5074528.

name: microbial-source-tracking-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing fecal source tracking tools on shotgun metagenomes with ground-truth source compositions (e.g., spike-in mesocosms), or when deciding which FST tool and tuning parameters to adopt.

name: microbiome-abundance-table-model-evaluation
description: Use when you have a microbial abundance table (OTU or species table) plus sample disease/status labels and need to train and benchmark a phylogeny-aware deep-learning classifier for microbiome status or disease detection.

name: microbiome-alpha-diversity-marker-combination
description: Use when you have effect estimates and standard errors per study and marker (≥10 studies), want a global conclusion on 'α-diversity' across multiple related markers, and have no prior marker-by-marker correlation estimates.

name: microbiome-beta-diversity-jaccard-computation
description: Use when a processed microbiome OTU table (e.g., otu.tab.txt or a phyloseq object such as biom.Rdata) must be converted into a Jaccard dissimilarity matrix for beta-diversity analysis or survival association testing in the MiSurv/MiRKAT workflow.

name: microbiome-body-site-clustering
description: Use when you have paired-end WGS or simulated long-read metagenome samples with known body-site labels and need to compare how k-mer-based tools cluster them by origin.

name: microbiome-count-normalization-css-tmm-quantile
description: Use when a merged MetaPhlAn or QIIME OTU/BIOM taxonomy table needs rescaling across samples before GLM, Random Forest, or SVM model building, or when comparing how normalization choices affect classifier accuracy.

name: microbiome-count-normalization-undersampling-correction
description: Use when calling differentially abundant features (OTUs, species, or other taxa) across two or more sample groups from sparse, undersampled microbial count matrices where library-size normalization biases dominate.

name: microbiome-differential-abundance-testing
description: Use when a binary or continuous grouping factor and a microbiome feature table are available and you need to test differential abundance while quantifying robustness of individual features and the overall microbiome-group association.

name: microbiome-diversity-report-component-organization
description: Use when you have raw microbiome analysis outputs (e.g., EMP data, alpha diversity, Shannon entropy, network files) that must be assembled into a reproducible structured scientific report.

name: microbiome-effect-size-visualization
description: Use when progressive permutation has flagged robust microbiome features (observed -log10 p-values outside the 95% quantile intervals of the fully permuted scenario) and you need signed effect sizes and individual abundance plots.

name: microbiome-feature-ordering-for-cnn-input
description: Use when you have a cophenetic distance matrix from a phylogenetic tree (e.g., from the R ape package) of OTU features and need to reorder/group them phylogenetically before training a CNN-based microbiome classifier.

name: microbiome-feature-robustness-ranking
description: Use when binary-grouped microbiome count data has yielded significant differential features and you need to rank how robust each discovery is to progressive permutation of grouping labels.

name: microbiome-feature-screening
description: Use when a high-dimensional OTU/taxa count matrix (e.g. 856 OTUs x 60 samples) and an adjusted response vector must be reduced to a non-empty subset S of taxa likely associated with the outcome, prior to a data-adaptive multivariate association test under a generalized linear model.

name: microbiome-fragility-index-computation
description: Use when a set of differentially abundant microbiome features from a binary-group comparison must be ranked by robustness, by counting how many progressive label-permutation steps flip each feature to nonsignificance.

name: microbiome-functional-data-interpretation
description: Use when input is PICRUSt2 predicted functional output (e.g., KO abundance tables and sample metadata) and the goal is differential pathway abundance, pathway annotation, or GSEA between comparison groups.

name: microbiome-functional-profile-visualization
description: Use when you have a DA results table from pathway_daa() applied to PICRUSt2 KEGG pathway abundances and need a publication-quality figure showing which pathways differ between groups and by how much.

name: microbiome-genotype-association-analysis
description: Use when you have a SNP genotype matrix and a microbial taxa abundance matrix over the same sample cohort and need to identify significant taxa-SNP (mbQTL) relationships, including all-to-all R² estimates or a single specified rsID.

name: microbiome-group-comparison-design
description: Use when you have a PICRUSt2-predicted pathway-level abundance table (KO converted to KEGG pathway abundance) plus sample metadata with a grouping variable, and you must test which pathways differ significantly between groups.

name: microbiome-group-difference-analysis
description: Use when a microbiome OTU/feature count table has a binary grouping factor and you need to characterize overall association strength and the robustness of significant features across progressive label permutations.

name: microbiome-marker-gene-survey-analysis
description: Use when the input is a sparse high-throughput microbiome OTU/taxa count matrix with two or more sample groups and the goal is to identify features that are differentially abundant across populations.

name: microbiome-metadata-association-analysis
description: Use when you have per-sample inStrain profile objects (or equivalent strain calls) plus per-infant metadata (sibling/twin relationships, birth day, birth weight, gestational age) and need to test whether strain sharing correlates with these host properties.

name: microbiome-metadata-association-modeling
description: Use when comparing whether two sequence variant callers yield comparable microbiome-biological-variable association performance, or when building supervised classification models from a variant count table (e.g., SvTable.txt) merged with sample metadata.

name: microbiome-metadata-matching
description: Use when a merged MetaPhlAn or QIIME OTU/BIOM profile table must be paired with a tab-separated metadata file whose class column (e.g. column 7, T1D_Diagnosed with t/f labels) and sample ID column (e.g. column 2, Gid_shotgun) must be identified before MegaR model building.

name: microbiome-method-comparison-benchmarking
description: Use when benchmarking differential-abundance methods for zero-inflated microbiome relative abundance data, e.g. to quantify empirical power of GAMLSS-BEZI vs. transformed linear models across effect sizes.

name: microbiome-otu-compositional-normalization
description: Use when the input is a raw OTU abundance count matrix (e.g. 16S V1-V2 OTUs from QIIME) that must be compositional-normalized and OTU-wise standardized before feature screening or multivariate association testing in the AMAT framework.

name: microbiome-otu-data-simulation
description: Use when you must benchmark type I error calibration or statistical power of a microbiome multivariate association test against synthetic OTU count data generated to mimic a real community.

name: microbiome-phylogeny-aware-abundance-profiling
description: Use when you have feature/OTU tables from multiple denoising or clustering methods (e.g. vsearch open/closed-reference, de novo, DADA2, Deblur) and need to assess how similarly they resolve community composition using phylogeny-aware beta-diversity metrics.

name: microbiome-pvalue-trace-interpretation
description: Use when a progressive permutation run (bin_permute_all output on a binary grouping outcome) needs interpretation via U-curves and p-value traces to assess overall microbiome association strength.

name: microbiome-qtl-preprocessing
description: Use when a taxa-by-sample 16S abundance table (plus an optional SNP/covariate file) must be prepared for mbQTL rho estimation, and taxa–taxa R values need to be estimated as inputs to taxa–SNP association analysis.

name: microbiome-quality-control-filtering
description: Use when raw OTU count tables and taxonomy tables (e.g., otu.tab.txt / tax.tab.txt from phyloseq) must be quality-controlled before survival-microbiome analysis and you need MiSurv's default filtering criteria reproduced.

name: microbiome-relabundance-null-data-generation
description: Use when evaluating the false positive control of a differential abundance test on zero-inflated beta relative abundance data — e.g. simulating null data with mu1=mu2=0.5, alpha1=alpha2=0.5, phi=5 to reproduce Table 1 type I error rates at alpha=0.01/0.05/0.1.

name: microbiome-relative-abundance-modeling
description: Use when testing differential relative abundance of microbial taxa (phylum to genus, e.g. levels l2/l4/l5/l6) between groups in compositional, zero-inflated 16S microbiome data, especially longitudinal designs with covariate adjustment.

name: microbiome-sample-metadata-extraction
description: Use when a microbiome survival analysis needs clinical/design variables (survival time, event indicator, treatment group, covariates) pulled from a sample-data table such as MiSurv's sam.dat.txt or the phyloseq object biom.Rdata.

name: microbiome-simulation-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing power/type I error of multivariate microbiome association tests on simulated OTU count data with continuous or binary outcomes, e.g. Dirichlet-multinomial scenarios varying signal density.

name: microbiome-source-tracking-simulation
description: Use when evaluating or comparing source-tracking algorithms on compositional data with many candidate sources (e.g., M=50 environments, K=10 true contributors) and substantial unknown-source mixing (0–90%), or when validating that a new MST method actually reduces noise from noncontributing sources.

name: microbiome-time-series-trajectory-prediction
description: Use when longitudinal OTU count tables (taxa x samples with sequence IDs and sample times) have been denoised by LUMINATE 'estimate', and the goal is to infer cLV parameters (A, g, B) and predict future community trajectories under external perturbations.

name: microdiversity-profiling-of-mapped-reads
description: Use when you have coReads .bam files mapped to representative sub-species .fasta references and need per-genome SNV calling, nucleotide diversity, clonality, and breadth for population-genome comparisons across sample groups.

name: migration-edge-optimization-optm
description: Use when TreeMix has been run across multiple user-defined migration-edge values (optionally with bootstrapping) and you must choose the optimal number of migration edges for the inferred population tree from biallelic SNP data.

name: mimag-quality-class-thresholding
description: Use when a set of MAG FASTA files needs completeness/contamination estimation and assignment to revised-MIMAG quality tiers (e.g. retaining genomes with >=50% completeness and <5% contamination).

name: mimic-sequence-data-augmentation
description: Use when training iDeLUCS (or a DeLUCS-style contrastive network) on unlabeled DNA sequences in FASTA format and per-sequence augmented training pairs are needed to stabilize unsupervised clustering.

name: mind-compatible-network-export
description: Use when one or more network inference association matrices (interaction plus pvalue matrices) have been computed and qualifying consensus edges must be exported as a MIND-compatible JSON multigraph annotated with per-method interaction weights.

name: miner-agreement-visualization
description: Use when metagenomic/virome contigs must be mined with multiple phage predictors and the goal is a vOTU set plus a per-miner overlap visualization to assess cross-miner concordance.

name: miner-prediction-overlap-analysis
description: Use when a metagenomic (or virome) dataset has been mined by multiple phage-mining tools and you need to quantify per-miner prediction counts and overlap/difference in vOTU assignments across miners.

name: minhash-database-matching
description: Use when assembled plasmid contigs (e.g. Unicycler output FASTA from Plassembler) need to be matched against a known plasmid database to annotate similarity to PLSDB entries.

name: minhash-genome-sketching
description: Use when you have paired WGS/FASTQ read files for many metagenomic samples and need a fast MinHash-based all-vs-all distance matrix to test whether samples cluster by a known metadata attribute such as body site.

name: minhash-genome-sketching
description: Use when you have many genome assemblies (e.g. 3269 MAG FASTA files) and need to find each one's closest relative in a reference genome set (e.g. 2505 HGR genomes) to assign species labels.

name: minhash-kmer-read-classification
description: Use when shotgun reads (FASTA/FASTQ, short or long) from metagenomic or all-food-sequencing (AFS) samples must be taxonomically classified and quantified against massive multi-kingdom reference genome collections faster than alignment-based tools like BWA or MegaBLAST.

name: minhash-kmer-sketching
description: Use when building a large reference genome classification database (e.g. multi-kingdom food or RefSeq-scale collections) where storing all k-mers would exhaust memory and a minhash sketch must be computed into partitioned hash tables.

name: minhash-sketch-distance-estimation
description: Use when you need sample-level similarity/distance estimates from raw short-read FASTQ files — e.g. clustering metagenomes, identifying re-sequencings, or selecting Mash sketch/k-mer defaults.

name: minimal-primer-set-optimization
description: Use when a large pool of candidate qPCR primer pairs (e.g., nondegenerate forms expanded from degenerate EcoFunPrimer outputs) must be reduced to the smallest set still amplifying the maximum number of environmentally ranked reference genes.

name: minimap2-alignment-gold-standard-calling
description: Use when benchmarking a nanopore read classifier (e.g. SPUMONI) and you need a per-read truth label set: align the same read set with minimap2 against the same references and take confident alignments (MAPQ >= 30) as ground truth.

name: minimap2-ground-truth-generation
description: Use when evaluating raw nanopore signal mapping tools against a trusted reference: minimap2 alignments of basecalled reads serve as ground truth to compute per-dataset precision/recall/F1 for raw-signal mappers.

name: minimap2-long-read-alignment
description: Use when decontaminating Oxford Nanopore (ONT) long reads from (meta)genomic FASTQ input against a human reference index such as human-t2t-hla, or when benchmarking long-read host depletion against tools like NCBI's HRRT.

name: minimap2-reference-alignment
description: Use when assembler-generated contigs must be mapped to known reference replicons (multi-FASTA passed via --reference) to compute reference-based assembly quality metrics like LSA.

name: minimizer-index-database-query
description: Use when a metagenomic classifier must query each query-sequence k-mer against a large exact-match k-mer database (Jellyfish count spaces storing LCA taxon IDs) and per-k-mer alignment is too slow.

name: minimizer-partitioned-database-indexing
description: Use when implementing or reconstructing an exact k-mer lookup database (e.g., k-mer→LCA taxon maps) that must support fast per-k-mer queries without alignment, via minimizer grouping and indexed binary search.

name: minimum-allele-frequency-computation
description: Use when you have freebayes VCFs from wastewater NGS samples mapped to SARS-CoV-2 NC_045512 and need to reproduce or recompute lineage-specific AF statistics such as the non-zero minimum AF of B.1.1.7-unique mutations.

name: minimum-p-value-statistic-testing
description: Use when combining multiple studies across multiple related markers (e.g., 6 α-diversity indices) from summary statistics only (effect estimates and standard errors) and an omnibus hypothesis test is needed without a priori marker-by-marker correlations.

name: minimum-pvalue-adaptive-hypothesis-testing
description: Use when combining multiple studies (≥10) across multiple related markers (e.g., six α-diversity indices) from summary statistics alone, with no prior marker-by-marker correlations, and the goal is a single omnibus hypothesis test rather than a pooled effect estimate.

name: minor-allele-variant-detection
description: Use when input is Illumina FASTQ from samples suspected of containing low-frequency resistant alleles (mixed infections, heteroresistance, XDR-TB second-line drug testing) and Mykrobe predictor's major-clone calls alone miss resistance.

name: minpath-pathway-reconstruction
description: Use when you have a KO (KEGG Orthology) abundance table from 16S-based functional prediction and need MetaCyc pathway presence/abundance inferred by minimum-parsimony reconstruction.

name: misassembly-detection-from-alignment-breakpoints
description: Use when you have multiple FASTA assemblies of a model organism plus a reference genome (e.g. NC_000913.3) and read pairs, and you need to count extensive misassemblies, genome fraction, duplication ratio, NGA50, and mismatches/indels per 100 kb.

name: misassembly-edge-error-quantification
description: Use when validating that a metagenomic assembler's scaffold corresponds to a specific reference genome (e.g. B. longum 51A scaffold2094 in gut sample V06-T-0501-S07) and you need to quantify edge misassembly and fragmentation per assembler.

name: misclassification-count-quantification
description: Use when benchmarking taxonomic classifiers for false-positive behavior on reads whose true source species is missing from every tool's reference database (e.g. AQ<60%, ANI<95% novelty cutoffs).

name: missing-summary-data-handling
description: Use when the summary-statistics table has missing study-by-marker entries so the number of studies (Kj) varies by marker, and you need pooled estimates plus mMeta/aMeta p-values using all available data.

name: mitochondrial-genome-annotation-verification
description: Use when you need to transfer an existing linear-reference annotation (e.g., a GTF of mitochondrial gene coordinates) onto a graph pangenome and confirm each gene region resolves uniquely in graph coordinates.

name: mitogenome-panel-simulation
description: Use when you need simulated human mitogenome FASTA panels with known SNP/indel ground truth to benchmark graph-based variant detection (precision/recall) or to measure wall-clock time and memory scaling of VARI-merge + cSupB pipelines.

name: mixed-allele-frequency-statistics
description: Use when you have run (or plan to run) MAGinator on shotgun metagenomics data with VAMB MAG clusters and need to quantify within-cluster strain mixtures — i.e. which samples/MAG clusters carry more than one variant of a MAG.

name: mixed-effects-microbiome-statistics
description: Use when you have a feature-abundance matrix (e.g. fungal species from shotgun metagenomes) plus sample metadata and need significant taxon–metadata associations while controlling for repeated or nuisance covariates like age.

name: mixed-effects-model-fitting-region-random-effects
description: Use when repeated measures within a small number of study regions (e.g., five temperate forest regions) may inflate fixed-effects R², and you need to quantify the per-model loss of explained variance from adding region as a random intercept.

name: mixed-integer-linear-program-formulation
description: Use when assigning strain types to samples from per-locus allele sets and proportions (geneX_proportions.csv) against a known MLST strain database, and novel-strain detection under proportion constraints is required.

name: mixed-integer-linear-programming-solver-configuration
description: Use when deconvolving mixed MLST samples into strains via the paper's ILP/MILP formulations, or when configuring CPLEX runs whose NP-hard models need gap/time-limit stopping criteria and objective variants.

name: mixed-integer-linear-programming-strain-deconvolution
description: Use when WGS reads from heterogeneous samples must be decomposed into known MLST strain types plus novel strains, given a reference allele database (e.g. 8 housekeeping genes, 1726 alleles, 753 strain types) and mixed samples where strain proportions vary.

name: mixed-integer-program-solution-post-processing
description: Use when an ILP/MILP (e.g. the Allele Diversity Problem solved with CPLEX) returns multiple optimal solutions and you must (a) pick one biologically plausible solution and (b) derive fractional allele abundances from the selected solution.

name: mixed-sample-heteroresistance-interpretation
description: Use when calling resistance in M. tuberculosis samples with minor resistant allele populations, especially for capreomycin, amikacin or ofloxacin where major-clone-only calls miss phenotypic resistance.

name: mixing-proportion-accuracy-evaluation
description: Use when simulated sinks with known ground-truth source mixing proportions and unknown-source contributions (0–90%) are available and you must compare source tracking methods on estimation accuracy.

name: mixing-proportion-scaling-analysis
description: Use when you have a microbiome feature table with a binary grouping outcome and need to quantify overall association strength and discovery robustness by tracking significant-feature counts across progressive permutation mixing proportions (U-curve).

name: mkt-based-adaptive-evolution-estimation
description: Use when you have unfolded site frequency spectrum (DAF) data plus divergence counts for neutral (4-fold/0) and selected (0-fold/i) classes per gene and need to estimate α, or to compare α of a user-selected gene set (e.g. high-recombination bins) against the genome-wide distribution.

name: mkt-count-table-concatenation
description: Use when a user-selected set of protein-coding genes (e.g. selected by recombination rate bins or chromosome localization) must be analyzed jointly for a single selective regime rather than gene-by-gene, and per-gene MKT count tables are available.

name: mlst-allele-panel-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking whether a metagenomic allele/strain deconvolution pipeline recovers fractional allele composition per MLST locus from simulated WGS reads with known ground truth.

name: mlst-allele-proportion-normalization
description: Use when the ADP ILP has already identified the allele set for an MLST locus and you need fractional allele abundances per gene from the per-sample, per-gene read mapping files.

name: mlst-schema-input-preparation
