description: Use when you already possess a chewBBACA-created or adapted cgMLST/wgMLST schema (schema_seed folder) plus draft genome FASTA files, and must stage and validate these inputs before running chewBBACA.py AlleleCall.

name: mlst-strain-diversity-deconvolution
description: Use when per-locus allele sets and allele proportions are available for MLST samples and you must infer which known/novel strain types explain the observed within-host diversity.

name: mlst-strain-type-inference
description: Use when per-sample MLST allele sets and allele proportions (geneX_proportions.csv) are available and you need to jointly infer which known and novel strain types, with proportions, explain the samples.

name: mmseqs2-homology-search
description: Use when you need to quantify overlap between two protein/gene catalogues (e.g. VMGC-90 vs VIRGO-90) by all-vs-all similarity search at defined amino acid identity and coverage thresholds.

name: mock-community-benchmark-accuracy-evaluation
description: Use when a new strain- or genome-comparison method needs quantitative accuracy validation on community data with known ground-truth composition, e.g. reproducing the inStrain vs dRep/MIDAS/StrainPhlAn benchmark on ZymoBIOMICS.

name: mock-community-benchmark-analysis
description: Use when paired-end 2 × 250 bp 16S mock community datasets are available and you need to rank OTU-retrieval pipelines by read preservation, OTU-count accuracy, or runtime.

name: mock-community-benchmark-analysis
description: Use when a community of known composition (mock or synthetic gut) with sequenced shotgun reads is available and you must quantify which SSU extraction, reconstruction, or classification tool recovers the expected variants, taxa and runtimes.

name: mock-community-benchmark-data-analysis
description: Use when deposited LMAS metric tables (global and per-reference) from mock metagenomic communities are available and the goal is to test whether assembler branding (genomic vs metagenomic) predicts performance on complex samples.

name: mock-community-benchmark-datasets
description: Reference for validating or benchmarking a 16S rRNA gene sequence variant caller on data with known composition, or for reproducing runtime, memory, and variant-count comparisons between HashSeq and DADA2.

name: mock-community-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when comparing taxonomic classification tools on simulated mock communities with known ground-truth abundance profiles, to quantify genus/species identification, abundance estimation accuracy, and read classification rate.

name: mock-community-benchmark-metrics-computation
description: Use when you have simulated/metagenomic mock community samples with known taxonomic composition and need to quantify a profiler's precision, sensitivity or F1 per taxonomic rank and abundance threshold.

name: mock-community-benchmark-metrics-computation
description: Use when a newly generated strain-separated metagenome assembly must be quantitatively benchmarked per recovered strain against known reference genomes from a mock community (Mock3, Mock9).

name: mock-community-benchmark-reproduction
description: Use when benchmarking taxonomic classifiers on mock community Illumina reads and you need to reproduce genus/phylum sensitivity and precision comparisons between protein-level (Kaiju) and k-mer-based (Kraken) classifiers.

name: mock-community-composition-comparison
description: Use when a 16S rRNA amplicon profile has been CopyRighter-corrected and a known expected mock community composition (equal 16S rRNA gene copies per species) is available to quantify accuracy by Hellinger/euclidean distance.

name: mock-community-ground-truth-comparison
description: Use when classifying reads or reconstructed SSU sequences from a mock/synthetic community with a known expected taxonomy, and you need per-rank precision/recall/F-measure to compare classifiers.

name: mock-community-metagenome-analysis
description: Use when Illumina paired-end plus 4 kbp/8 kbp mate-pair reads from a known-composition mock metagenome (e.g. DDBJ PRJDB4377) must be assembled with several assemblers and compared by NGA50 contiguity.

name: mock-community-quality-assessment
description: Use when comparing de novo short-read assembler performance on a known mock community standard with reference genomes available, to judge which assemblers produce accurate, contiguous assemblies.

name: mock-community-read-simulation
description: Use when validating a taxonomic or functional profiling database against cross-kingdom false-positive mapping, by simulating mock-community FASTQ reads with ART and measuring mapping rates or specificity.

name: mock-community-reference-based-evaluation
description: Use when a known-composition mock metagenome (e.g. GIS20 bacteria with Illumina paired-end plus ONT or PacBio long reads) is being assembled and contiguity/accuracy must be compared across assemblers against reference genomes.

name: mock-community-scaffold-completeness-evaluation
description: Use when a strain-separated long-read metagenome assembly (e.g., assembly.scaffolds.fa from Strainberry on a mock community) must be evaluated for completeness and base-level accuracy against known reference strain genomes.

name: mock-community-species-benchmarking
description: Use when a target-detection tool must be quantitatively validated on a defined mock community, e.g. per-species read classification accuracy/F1 for 16S MinION reads under stratified 5-fold cross-validation.

name: mock-community-strain-count-comparison
description: Use when benchmarking OTU-count fidelity of 16S pipelines on mock communities with known strain composition, to judge which pipeline's OTU count deviates least from truth.

name: mock-community-validation-analysis
description: Use when you have predicted gene-family (KO) abundance tables from 16S data plus shotgun-derived KO annotations for the same or mock communities, and need to quantify prediction accuracy.

name: mock-dataset-graph-validation
description: Use when implementing or modifying the host proximity graph code in ViralCC and you need a reproducible check that the automatic k-selection rule (maximize |E_host| subject to |E_host| ≤ |E_hic|) behaves as published.

name: model-fit-mse-evaluation
description: Use when a signature-gene or marker-gene abundance model built in one cohort is applied to another cohort and you must quantify fit quality per cohort (e.g., reported MSE 103.95 for COPSAC2010 vs 878.09 for CHILD) to assess transferability.

name: model-parameter-count-verification
description: Use when a reimplementation of DeepTaxa's hybrid CNN-BERT classifier must be validated against published spec before training or inference reuse.

name: model-performance-metric-tabulation
description: Use when you have held-out test predictions from multiple classifiers trained on identical cross-validation splits of microbiome abundance data and need a model-by-metric comparison table mirroring Figs. 4-5.

name: model-serialization-rds
description: Use when a trained MegaR classification model (RF/GLM/SVM on merged MetaPhlAn or QIIME/OTU/BIOM tables) must be persisted to RDS and later reused to predict classes for unknown samples without repeating the training pipeline.

name: modification-enzyme-hmm-detection
description: Use when assembled contigs or RefSeq genomes paired with tandem mass spectra must be mined for RiPPs: after 6-frame translation, modification-enzyme HMM hits define which 10 kbp windows feed motif-ORF/all-ORF precursor prediction in MetaMiner.

name: monoculture-model-evaluation
description: Use when validating a Zebra genome cover recurrence fit with a known-composition control (e.g., a monoculture SAM alignment against the WoL database), to confirm predicted cover tracks observed cover and that true hits separate from low-coverage reference-overlap artifacts.

name: monte-carlo-power-comparison
description: Use when choosing a between-study heterogeneity variance estimator (SJ vs DL) for random effects meta-analysis across multiple related markers, or when validating empirical power/type I error of marker-set meta-analysis methods via simulations.

name: monte-carlo-type-i-error-estimation
description: Use when validating that a zero-inflated beta GAMLSS test controls false positives on simulated microbiome relative abundance data under the null hypothesis, e.g. reproducing Table 1 type I error comparisons at alpha = 0.01, 0.05, 0.1.

name: movis-workflow-driven-data-exploration
description: Use when input is a tabular (CSV/TSV) time-series multi-omics data set (e.g., metabolomics over sampling timestamps) and the goal is step-wise exploration to detect temporal trends, anomalies, or substrate shifts and export publication-ready visualizations.

name: mrf-graph-inclusion-prior-sampling
description: Use when compositional count data (e.g. taxa abundances) must be related to covariates that are believed to be correlated (block covariance structure), and the dependency graph among covariates is not known a priori and must be inferred jointly with variable selection.

name: msa-based-runtime-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing inference wall-clock time of a DNN contact-prediction pipeline against a classical ECA baseline (e.g., CCMpred precision-matrix optimization) over the same pre-computed MSAs on matched CPU and GPU hardware.

name: msa-covariance-feature-construction
description: Use when predicting protein residue contacts directly from an MSA with a DNN, or when replicating the DeepECA Baseline Model precision benchmarks on CASP11/CASP12 against PSICOV, CCMpred, DeepCov, and ResPRE.

name: msa-derived-feature-engineering
description: Use when building DNN input features for protein contact prediction from MSAs, particularly when MSAs are shallow (few homologous sequences) and raw coevolution signal alone underperforms on long-range contacts.

name: msa-input-feature-preparation-for-dnn
description: Use when a target protein sequence (FASTA) must be converted into the DNN input feature tensor (MSA-derived covariance matrices) for DeepECA/DeepCov-style contact prediction.

name: mtbc-lineage-typing
description: Use when raw mycobacterial (MTBC or NTM) sequencing reads need species/lineage calls, when reproducing the MTBC_A2/Myco_Retro classification benchmark, or when Mykrobe lineage calls must be checked for concordance against KvarQ.

name: multi-allelic-alt-allele-handling
description: Use when VCF variant calls from low-frequency wastewater sequencing (freebayes, allele frequency < 0.01) contain comma-separated multi-allelic ALT strings that must become one rule per ALT before lineage rule matching.

name: multi-assembler-benchmark-table-compilation
description: Use when comparing the assembly quality of several de novo assemblers across a common set of metagenome datasets and you need a single per-assembler x per-dataset table of Quast metrics.

name: multi-assembler-comparison
description: Use when the goal is to reproduce or extend a contiguity benchmark of metagenome assemblers on mock-community reads (Illumina paired-end plus 4 kbp/8 kbp mate-pair), reporting NGA50 per tool per sample.

name: multi-assembler-contig-generation
description: Use when input is paired-end short-read FASTQ from a mixed microbial/viral community (e.g., E. coli K12 + phage Lambda test reads) and you want contigs assembled by SPAdes, metaSPAdes, and MEGAHIT together to maximize recovery of viral genomes before gene-prediction-based viral scoring.

name: multi-classifier-performance-comparison
description: Use when you need to select a taxonomic classifier by benchmarking several (e.g. Centrifuge, Kraken2, SPINGO, BLCA, QIIME 2 Sklearn) on sequences with a known ground-truth taxonomy, such as a mock community.

name: multi-component-document-assembly
description: Use when a directory of mixed bioinformatics output files (plots, tables, networks, Markdown, HTML components) must be turned into a rendered report in a specified format, and the goal is automated, reproducible report generation.

name: multi-format-document-rendering
description: Use when a configuration-driven report must be emitted in multiple static document/presentation formats from one source file, e.g. converting a report.yaml + component directory into report.qmd and rendering it with Quarto.

name: multi-kingdom-genome-collection-processing
description: Use when you have a mixed FASTA collection of genomes (e.g. prokaryotic MAGs, fungal genomes, vOTUs) and need a non-redundant pan-genome gene catalogue at a defined amino acid identity threshold.

name: multi-kmer-de-bruijn-graph-assembly
description: Use when adaptor-preprocessed metagenomic FASTQ reads must be assembled de novo to produce fragmented seed contigs that feed a contig-extension step such as ContigExtender.

name: multi-level-taxonomic-diversity-analysis
description: Use when QCed2/QCed3 OMARU profiling tables (clade levels L2–L7 and gene abundance) are available for case-control metagenome cohorts and the goal is to test whether diversity differs between cases and controls.

name: multi-mapping-read-quality-resolution
description: Use when evaluating a HiFi metagenome assembly with reads that map to contigs belonging to multiple bins of different CheckM2 quality levels, and you need non-double-counted aligned read/base ratios split by bin quality.

name: multi-marker-covariance-weighted-pooling
description: Use when combining ≥10 studies across multiple related markers (e.g., six α-diversity indices: Richness, Shannon, Simpson, PD, PE, PQE) from summary statistics alone, with no priori marker-by-marker correlation estimates and possible missing data.

name: multi-marker-summary-statistics-meta-analysis
description: Use when combining ≥10 studies across multiple related markers with only summary statistics (effect estimates and their standard errors, possibly with matched NAs), and no prior marker-by-marker correlations, e.g., α-diversity indices across microbiome studies.

name: multi-method-bin-count-aggregation
description: Use when benchmarking a viral binning method against baselines on assembled metagenomic Hi-C data and you need per-method counts of high/medium-completion bins (CheckV) to quantify improvement percentages.

name: multi-module-pipeline-output-aggregation
description: Use when several conditionally-enabled analysis modules must be executed per configuration flags and their heterogeneous outputs merged into one summary table plus interactive HTML/PDF deliverables, as in QUAST-style assembly evaluation.

name: multi-omics-cross-tabulation-analysis
description: Use when a k-means clustering of time-series multi-omics samples (e.g., Example 1 BWWTP metaproteomics FASTA embeddings) needs verification that a cluster label correlates with a temporal sub-period of the sampling time series.

name: multi-panel-figure-visualization
description: Use when metagenomic samples (e.g., NICU infant stool) have been profiled with inStrain and compared pairwise, and you need to test and visualize whether shared strains are enriched between siblings, whether MZ twins share more than DZ twins, and whether similarity tracks physiological properties.

name: multi-path-convolutional-ensemble-classification
description: Use when classifying microbiome samples (OTU/species abundance table + sample metadata) into disease or control status categories and you want a phylogeny-aware deep learning classifier benchmarked against ML baselines.

name: multi-pipeline-comparison-evaluation
description: Use when comparing how competing amplicon-seq pipelines estimate OTU richness, especially when a synthetic dataset with a known number of true OTUs is available for validation.

name: multi-polarization-backscatter-characterization
description: Use when Sentinel-1 gamma_0 temporal stacks (e.g. VH/VV GeoTIFFs such as ALB_gamma0_VH.tif and ALB_gamma0_VV.tif) must be summarized into neighborhood texture variables representing habitat structural heterogeneity.

name: multi-population-metagenome-coverage-benchmarking
description: Use when you need to quantify what fraction of reads from independent, population-diverse metagenomes map to a reference gene catalog versus a smaller subset reference, to assess catalog comprehensiveness.

name: multi-sample-contig-pooling
description: Use when building a species-level non-redundant viral contig catalog from multiple shotgun viral metagenomic samples, requiring per-sample assembly followed by cross-sample dereplication.

name: multi-sample-coverage-profile-processing
description: Use when assembling metagenomic short reads into contigs and you need sample-wise read coverage per contig as input features for a binner such as CH-Bin.

name: multi-sequence-vector-averaging
description: Use when input is archived (raw) FASTA files from time-series multi-omics data (e.g., metaproteomics) and the goal is to convert sequences into a numeric feature table suitable for downstream clustering or visualization.

name: multi-task-protein-structure-prediction
description: Use when predicting secondary structure, solvent accessibility, or residue-residue contacts from a protein sequence via its MSA, or when benchmarking 1D/2D structure prediction against RaptorX-Property and SCRATCH-1D on CASP targets.

name: multi-threaded-performance-comparison
description: Use when you need to compare computational efficiency (wall-clock time and max memory) of Plassembler versus Unicycler across multiple thread counts on simulated or real hybrid (short+long read) bacterial read sets.

name: multi-tool-binning-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when a binning tool's relative performance on large, complex high-dimensional datasets must be quantified against baselines using standard AMBER metrics (purity, completeness, F1) on shared inputs.

name: multi-tool-result-harmonization
description: Use when multiple viral-detection tools (VirSorter2, VIBRANT, DeepVirFinder, CheckV, MMseqs2 taxonomy) have been run on the same assembled contig library and per-contig viral calls must be reconciled into a single confidence-scored table.

name: multiclass-classification-metric-computation
description: Use when a trained multiclass classifier (e.g., PM-CNN predicting Control/Periodontitis/Gingivitis or gut disease labels) must be scored on held-out samples with the five paper-standard metrics and reported to a metrics CSV.

name: multigraph-edge-weight-annotation
description: Use when multiple network inference association matrices (interaction + pvalue matrices) have been filtered and consensus edges must be assembled with per-method weights for export to the MIND database.

name: multiple-sample-group-statistical-testing
description: Use when you have a sparse high-throughput OTU/taxon count matrix with sample group labels and need to identify features differentially abundant between two or more groups.

name: multiple-sequence-alignment-construction-from-ngs-reads
description: Use when deep-sequencing reads from a mixed sample (shotgun or amplicon, e.g. 454 Titanium pyrosequencing or Illumina viral data) must be placed in a common reference coordinate frame before windowed error correction or haplotype reconstruction.

name: multiple-sequence-alignment-curation
description: Use when rRNA gene sequences contain large insertion sequences (≥10 bp) that must be stripped prior to multiple sequence alignment, or when building a phylogeny from divergent 16S sequences (e.g. CPR) where naive alignment would be unreliable.

name: multiple-sequence-alignment-of-mlst-alleles
description: Use when evaluating individual loci in a cg/wgMLST schema — i.e. when you have per-locus FASTA files of allelic diversity and want to inspect alignment/phylogenetic structure of alleles per locus.

name: multiple-sequence-alignment-of-ortholog-loci
description: Use when you have recovered homologous single-copy marker sequences (e.g. USCOs/near-USCOs) for multiple specimens and need per-locus multiple sequence alignments as input for trimming, concatenation, and tree inference.

name: multiple-sequence-alignment-of-viral-genes
description: Use when starting from PROKKA-annotated genome GFF files (e.g. 56 RefSeq coronavirus genomes) and homologous gene families must be aligned, tree-ordered, and collapsed into representative sequences for downstream LCA assignment.

name: multiple-sequence-alignment-of-viral-genes
description: Use when you need to type or classify viral genomes/OTUs from a conserved marker gene (e.g., L1) and place them on a phylogeny against reference sequences from RefSeq.

name: multiple-testing-bonferroni-correction
description: Use when many raw permutational ANOVA P-values are produced from pairwise treatment-group contrasts (e.g. LEVO vs OTHERS, CLA vs OTHERS across time points) and adjusted P-values must be reported to avoid false-positive group differences.

name: multiple-testing-fdr-correction
description: Use when a multivariable association analysis (e.g. MaAsLin2 on the FunOMIC-derived 2,679-sample abundance tables) tests many fungal taxa against many metadata variables and raw p-values must be corrected before calling significance.

name: multiple-testing-fdr-correction
description: Use when a taxa–SNP regression sweep (e.g., mbQTL linearTaxaSnp over microbeAbund × SnpFile) yields thousands of P values that must be corrected for multiple comparisons and diagnostic-checked before calling mbQTL associations.

name: multiple-testing-pvalue-adjustment
description: Use when DAA results on pathway-level KEGG abundance tables contain raw p_val columns and significance must be judged on p_adjust, because hundreds of pathways are tested at once.

name: multiple-testing-pvalue-correction
description: Use when a gene-level differential expression results table contains raw p-values from a negative-binomial or similar GLM fit and per-gene FDR-adjusted values (padj) are needed for downstream filtering or enrichment input.

name: multiqc-aggregation-of-qc-outputs
description: Use when a pipeline stage produces many scattered per-sample QC/classification outputs (Kraken2/Centrifuge reports, Krona charts, preprocessing QC) and a single aggregated HTML report is needed to assess contamination before assembly.

name: multiqc-report-aggregation
description: Use when a metagenomics QC stage has produced per-sample FastQC HTML/zip reports for raw and trimmed FASTQ pairs and you need one aggregated overview to verify adapter removal and Q20 trimming.

name: multiscale-cnn-sequence-feature-extraction
description: Use when building or reproducing a 16S rRNA taxonomic classifier that needs local motif features (e.g., k=3/5/7 convolution windows over BPE-tokenized DNA) fused with long-range transformer context.

name: multivariate-canonical-axis-interpretation
description: Use when two multivariate feature tables measured on the same plot/observation units (e.g. Sentinel-1 gamma_0 temporal-stack metrics vs ALS structural metrics) must be compared for shared variance and axis-level association.

name: multivariate-site-score-extraction
description: Use when ground-truth presence-absence community data (e.g. 463 monitoring plots across 12 taxa/functional groups) must be reduced to per-plot ordination axes (NMDS1/NMDS2) to model assemblage composition against remote-sensing predictors.

name: mutation-frequency-mixture-design
description: Use when benchmarking a hotspot mutation caller on nanopore data and you need simulated FASTQ mixtures with known truth sets across mutant frequencies, replicates, and negative controls.

name: mwas-gwas-pathway-overlap-testing
description: Use when both MWAS pathway enrichment results (e.g. sumstats_*_annot.txt from OMARU) and host GWAS pathway enrichment results (e.g. PASCAL output as <Phenotype>_GWAS_<Pathway_reference>.txt) are available and you need to assess their overlap significance.

name: mycobacterial-drug-resistance-prediction
description: Use when raw FASTQ reads from MTBC isolates need rapid per-drug resistance calls (e.g. rifampicin, isoniazid, ethambutol) without assembling genomes or variant calling, or when benchmarking against phenotypic DST or KvarQ.

name: mycobacterial-genome-read-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking host read-removal tools on known-composition microbial data: you need simulated bacterial reads with a ground truth so that false-removal (retention) percentages of Hostile versus HRRT can be measured exactly.

name: mycobacterial-species-identification
description: Use when raw FASTQ reads from suspected mycobacterial isolates (MTBC or NTM, e.g. MGIT culture positives or SRA downloads) need phylo_group/species/lineage calls, or when Mykrobe species calls must be compared against KvarQ lineage labels.

name: mycobiome-abundance-table-generation
description: Use when shotgun metagenomic FASTQ samples must be profiled for fungal species composition, e.g. building per-sample abundance/prevalence tables for gut, infant, or disease-cohort mycobiome analysis.

name: mycobiome-clinical-variable-mapping
description: Use when fungal taxonomic or functional abundance tables (e.g. from FunOMIC-T/FunOMIC-P profiling) must be tested for significant associations with metadata variables such as health status, country, body site, or DNA extraction method.

name: mykrobe-output-parsing
description: Use when you have raw Mykrobe predictor . outputs (e.g. from MTBC_A1 or St_B1 isolates run with --format ) and need per-mutation, per-genetic-region tabular data for per-drug error or concordance tables.

name: mysql-sample-record-querying
description: Use when sample metadata held in the MetaLIMS MySQL database must be queried through PHP's mysqli interface and mapped — including lab-specific custom fields — to build a Clarity LIMS-compatible sequencing submission form.

name: naive-overlap-baseline-comparison
description: Use when benchmarking sequence recovery of paired-end Illumina assembly against a naive perfect-overlap baseline on a control library (e.g. SRA024100), to reproduce reported 4-50% yield gains from relaxing quality thresholds 0.9 to 0.6.

name: naive-pileup-mapping-assembly-of-viral-genomes
description: Use when metagenomic paired-end reads must be reconstructed into virus-like super-scaffolds by mapping to Genbank viral/phage references (gbvrl, gbphage) with low-coverage or divergent viruses where de-novo assembly alone is insufficient.

name: naive-pileup-viral-contig-reconstruction
description: Use when refining VirMAP super-scaffolds/contigs so the final dual assembly consists solely of viral sequences, after viral filtering and contig merging, by rebuilding each genome's contigs from its assigned read set.

name: nanopore-adapter-trimming
description: Use when raw Nanopore FASTQ reads enter a metagenome assembly workflow and adapters must be removed before control-read decontamination (NanoLyse), quality filtering (Filtlong) and long-read assembly.

name: nanopore-long-read-to-short-read-conversion
description: Use when a nanopore FASTQ (e.g., .fq.gz from ONT) must be converted into NGS-liked short-read sets to run conventional NGS pipelines for hotspot mutation detection in a hotspot panel.

name: nanopore-raw-signal-mapping
description: Use when the input is raw nanopore signal data (FAST5, POD5, SLOW5, or BLOW5) from legacy r9.4 chemistry that must be mapped to a reference genome in real time, especially for large genomes such as human NA12878.

name: nanopore-raw-signal-seed-hash-matching
description: Use when mapping raw nanopore signal reads to a reference genome via hash-based seed matching, or when reproducing how RawHash converts matching seed hash values into a mapped genomic region through colinear chaining.

name: nanopore-read-classification
description: Use when base-called nanopore reads must be classified as target vs non-target (e.g., adaptive-sampling host/strain depletion) against one-genome or multi-strain pan-genome references where minimap2 alignment is too slow or memory-hungry.

name: nanopore-read-resistance-genotyping
description: Use when you have raw single-molecule nanopore (MinION) reads of a bacterial isolate and need antibiotic resistance predictions without prior error correction, ideally benchmarked against a second sequencing platform.

name: nanopore-read-simulation
description: Use when you need ground-truth nanopore read sets of known origin and adjustable accuracy to benchmark read classification or alignment accuracy (F1, precision, recall) and throughput.

name: nanopore-read-subsampling-coverage-normalization
description: Use when pooled Nanopore FASTQs of uneven depth must be subsampled to a fixed coverage (e.g. 50x or 60x) before assembly benchmarking or fair tool comparison.

name: nanopore-signal-inference-benchmarking
description: Use when you need to measure and compare inference/processing throughput (kbp/s) of raw MinION fast5 signal tools or basecalling pipelines across hardware tiers such as a 2GB Jetson Nano versus a high-end desktop.

name: nanopore-signal-read-classification
description: Use when input is raw ONT fast5 signal data (amplified or metagenomic 16S) and you need per-read target-species detection on inexpensive hardware without basecalling, e.g. MinION as a species detector.

name: ncbi-sra-dataset-retrieval
description: Use when reproducing the StrainXpress benchmark or any strain-aware metagenome assembly comparison that needs the original Bmock12 (SRX4901583), NWCs, or Gut Metagenome (PRJNA379884) short-read FASTQ inputs.

name: near-complete-genome-detection-in-assemblies
description: Use when comparing metagenome assembler outputs (FASTA scaffolds, e.g. MetaPlatanus out_final.fa) and you must count near-complete genomes, genes, gene clusters or viral sequences to rank assemblers on high-depth ONT/PromethION + Illumina data.

name: nearest-neighbor-sequence-identity-search
description: Use when you need to explain a classifier's per-sequence errors by distance to training data: bucket held-out 16S sequences by nearest-neighbor percent identity (>97%, 90–97%, <90%) to stratify F1 degradation.

name: negative-binomial-abundance-model-fitting
description: Use when estimating per-sample abundances of MAG clusters from shotgun metagenomics and you need to pick an optimal, statistically validated set of de novo signature genes from a gene count matrix.

name: negative-binomial-association-testing
description: Use when the input is a longitudinal microbiome count dataset (master table with samples x features over time) and the goal is to detect features changing significantly over time while comparing error control (TPR/FDR) across negative-binomial methods.

name: negative-binomial-glm-fitting
description: Use when raw gene-level RNA-seq count matrices plus sample metadata are available and per-gene log2 fold changes and Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p-values are needed for differential expression between conditions.

name: negative-control-microbiome-count-simulation
description: Use when validating a longitudinal microbiome method's type-I error control: you need simulated null (zero-effect) count data whose library sizes differ systematically across time points to expose normalization-induced false positives.

name: neighbour-joining-phylogenetic-tree-reconstruction
description: Use when you have per-locus allele FASTA files from a chewBBACA schema and want per-locus MSAs and neighbour-joining trees to assess allelic variability within individual schema loci.

name: neighbour-joining-tree-construction
description: Use when annotated (e.g., PROKKA GFF) gene sequences from multiple taxa must be grouped into homologous clusters with phylogenetic support before assigning representatives to taxonomic nodes for probe or pseudo-genome design.

name: nested-cross-validation-model-evaluation
description: Use when benchmarking Traitar phenotype classifiers on labeled bacterial genomes (e.g. GIDEON phenotypes) and you need unbiased accuracy estimates such as macroaccuracy over 67 traits via 10-fold nested cross-validation.

name: network-based-baseline-method-reproduction
description: Use when a new network-based association predictor must be benchmarked against published baselines on a known association matrix with precomputed similarity networks, and reported AUC/AUPR values must be reproduced to validate the comparison.
tools: Jie Ren's d2* oligonucleotide frequency tools

name: network-edgelist-static-rendering
description: Use when a VueGen report configuration declares a component with component_type: network, plot_type: interactive_network, and csv_network_format: EDGELIST, and the target report type is a static format such as PDF, DOCX, ODT, PPTX, or Reveal.js.

name: neural-network-architecture-coding
description: Use when coding or reproducing a DNN that maps variable-length short metagenomic sequencing reads to species/genus labels via k-mer embedding -> BiLSTM -> multi-head self-attention -> 3-layer MLP, per the DeepMicrobes Model Architectures specification.

name: neural-network-inference-genome-signatures
description: Use when you have metagenomic or genomic FASTA contigs longer than 1000 bp that must be labeled plasmid vs chromosome by k-mer signature, and uncertain predictions should be excluded via a probability threshold.

name: neural-network-probability-thresholding
description: Use when you need to classify contigs/scaffolds from a metagenomic or bacterial genome assembly as plasmid vs. chromosome, and want to discard low-confidence neural network predictions via probability thresholding.

name: neural-network-sequence-labeling
description: Use when you need to label contigs from a metagenomic or bacterial genome assembly as plasmid vs. chromosome without prior knowledge of sample taxonomic or functional composition, and want uncertain predictions flagged.

name: nextflow-channel-wiring
description: Use when implementing or extending an nf-core/DSL2 pipeline module and you must connect a tool's outputs into pipeline-level version tracking and MultiQC aggregation channels.

name: nextflow-pipeline-execution
description: Use when metagenomic FASTQ short and/or long reads must be processed end-to-end into assemblies and MAGs, or when benchmarking nf-core/mag assembly settings (hybrid, co-assembly) on simulated data such as CAMISIM mouse-gut time series.

name: nextflow-pipeline-execution
description: Use when shotgun virome FASTQ pairs must be processed end-to-end via 'nextflow run deng-lab/viroprofiler' with a container profile and a '-c' custom config, or when per-process CPU/memory limits must be tuned.

name: nextflow-pipeline-execution
description: Use when you must run the MiCoNE nextflow pipeline over all combinations of tools/parameters for 16S processing steps (DC, CC, TA, OP, NI) and export per-combination co-occurrence networks.

name: nextflow-pipeline-execution
description: Use when a multi-step bioinformatics workflow (e.g. RNA-seq host read filtering plus metagenomic classification) must be run reproducibly with Nextflow, Singularity containers, and a scheduler such as SLURM.

name: nextflow-pipeline-orchestration
description: Use when biallelic SNP data in VCF or PLINK binary format must be run through a full population-genomics workflow (filtering, PCA/ADMIXTURE, TreeMix, selection scans) reproducibly on a local machine or HPC cluster via Nextflow.

name: nextflow-workflow-execution
description: Use when benchmarking de novo short-read assembly of a defined mock community across multiple assemblers under identical conditions, or when reproducing global (Contigs, Nx, Mapped reads, Misassembled contigs) and per-reference (Contiguity, Multiplicity, Validity, Lx, NGx) assembly metrics from.

name: nf-core-module-scaffolding
description: Use when a pipeline's terminal step must collect upstream process outputs (plots, tables, Markdown, HTML components) from a directory and regenerate them as a report, and the tool is distributed as an nf-core module.

name: ngs-read-window-decomposition
description: Use when you have a sorted BAM/CRAM (or FASTA MSA) of reads from a genetically heterogeneous viral sample and need error-corrected reads plus local haplotype reconstruction before global haplotype assembly or SNV calling.

name: nhmmer-ortholog-search-against-genome
description: Use when KEGG module evaluation reports missing KOs in a MAG/genome and you want to recover unannotated or truncated gene sequences via profile HMM searches against the genome's proteins.

name: nitrate-reduction-pathway-gene-mapping
description: Use when bacterial genomes are being phenotyped with Traitar and you need to link the nitrate-to-nitrite conversion (nitrate reduction) phenotype to its supporting Pfam protein families and accessions.

name: nmds-ordination-response-modeling
description: Use when you have plot-level (1-ha) remote-sensing predictor tables (Sentinel-1 gamma_0 means or ALS metrics) plus ground-truth biodiversity responses (NMDS axes, richness, phylogenetic diversity) for multiple taxa and need to quantify and compare predictive power across predictor sets under.

name: noisy-msa-robustness-testing
description: Use when assessing whether a contact-prediction model is robust to noisy MSA input (e.g. metagenomic contamination), or when reproducing DeepECA's noise-reduction claim via E-value 1/3 HHblits MSAs.

name: nominal-alpha-rejection-rate-analysis
description: Use when validating that a differential abundance test controls false positive (type I) error on zero-inflated beta relative abundance data by simulating under the null and comparing empirical rejection rates at alpha=0.01/0.05/0.1 to nominal levels.

name: non-redundant-gene-catalog-construction
description: Use when you have millions of predicted CDSs pooled from several sources (e.g., metagenome assemblies plus isolate genomes) and need to collapse redundant sequences into a single non-redundant gene catalog with stable gene IDs.

name: non-redundant-gene-catalogue-construction
description: Use when you have a large collection of (meta)genomes — e.g. 33,804 VMGC prokaryotic/fungal/viral genomes — and need a non-redundant reference gene catalogue for read mapping or functional profiling.

name: noncoding-region-detection-in-protein-alignments
description: Use when stitched (hit-stitched) query-to-reference protein alignments contain putative noncoding stretches — many indels with occasional matches — that must be trimmed before concatenating phylogenetic markers.

name: nonparametric-effect-size-estimation
description: Use when analyzing longitudinal high-dimensional data with a continuous time variable (e.g. 'Day') and you need per-feature effect sizes and direction (increase/decrease over time) in addition to significance testing.

name: normal-loess-error-model-inference
description: Use when comparing the number of sequence variants called from 16S rRNA amplicon FASTQ data by HashSeq's normal/LOESS error model at 5% FDR versus DADA2 defaults, especially on mock communities of known taxa.

name: norta-count-table-generation
description: Use when you need ground-truth synthetic abundance tables to evaluate network inference or consensus (scaled_sum) precision/sensitivity, as in the MiCoNE NorTA and seqtime benchmarks.

name: noun-phrase-term-matching
description: Use when extracting phenotypic character values (e.g., cell shape, Gram stain type, NaCl/pH/temperature optima, aerophilicity) from natural-language taxonomic description sentences of prokaryotes without training data for supervised classification.

name: novel-species-genome-selection-by-ani-aq-thresholds
description: Use when building an absent-species false-positive benchmark: you have a genome set (e.g. PRJNA348753 human gut MAGs) and need to pick genomes whose closest RefSeq/training relative fails novelty cutoffs (AQ<60%, ANI<95%).

name: nsti-accuracy-assessment
description: Use when predicting metagenomes from 16S rRNA OTU tables with PICRUSt and you must quantify per-sample prediction reliability from reference-genome coverage, especially for host-associated or environmental communities with sparse reference genomes.

name: nsti-phylogenetic-distance-calculation
description: Use when predicting metagenomes from 16S data with PICRUSt and you need a per-sample confidence metric, or when testing whether prediction accuracy decays with phylogenetic distance to reference genomes.

name: nucleotide-composition-feature-extraction
description: Use when you need to compute nucleotide composition features (tetranucleotide/k-mer frequencies, GC, CpG, GC skew, codon usage) for viral scaffolds and build a length-7 pairwise scaffold-by-scaffold distance table for downstream binning or machine learning.

name: nucleotide-diversity-birth-mode-comparison
description: Use when you have coReads .bam files mapped to representative sub-species reference genomes and need to compare per-genome nucleotide diversity (microdiversity) across metadata groups such as birth mode.

name: nucleotide-diversity-calculation
description: Use when you have a cellsnp-lite VCF pile-up (e.g., cellSNP.cells_ARG.vcf.gz) plus MetaQuad BIC_params.csv and need per-gene, per-sample nucleotide diversity to detect polymorphism shifts such as ARG diversity changes after antibiotic treatment.

name: nucleotide-frequency-composition-analysis
description: Use when assembled contigs and multi-sample short-read data are available and contigs must be clustered into MAGs using sequence composition plus per-sample depth/co-abundance signals.

name: nucleotide-protein-alignment-integration
description: Use when metagenomic contigs (e.g. VirMAP improved dual assembly) must be taxonomically classified using both nucleotide and protein alignment evidence, independent of genome coverage or read overlap.

name: nucleotide-protein-super-scaffold-merging
description: Use when metagenomic paired-end reads must be reconstructed into virus-like super-scaffolds by combining nucleotide (BBMap) and translated-protein (DIAMOND) alignments against Genbank viral/phage references, especially for low-coverage or divergent viruses.

name: nucleotide-seed-read-expansion
description: Use when you have raw paired-end Illumina reads from isolate genomes or metagenomes and need to recover CRISPR arrays or a repeat-defined locus without complete genome assembly, especially when the target repeat sequence is known.

name: nucleotide-sequence-clustering
description: Use when a nucleotide FASTA of predicted coding sequences (e.g. ~5.5M CDSs from assembled vaginal metagenomes) must be de-replicated into a non-redundant gene catalog at ≥95% identity over ≥90% of the shorter gene length.

name: nucleotide-sequence-clustering-redundancy-removal
description: Use when you have per-sample FASTA sequences of putative elements (e.g. insertion sequences from many metagenomes) and need a non-redundant catalogue by clustering at ~95% nucleotide identity.

name: nucleotide-similarity-search
description: Use when annotating metagenomic contigs that are too short for self-training gene finding, and sequenced genomes of close relatives (species-level pan-genomes) are available to supply protein-coding region parameters via nucleotide similarity assignment.

name: nucmer-whole-genome-alignment
description: Use when a set of candidate duplicate viral scaffolds (already rough-grouped, e.g. by Mash dist) needs exact pairwise nucleotide alignment to compute percent identity and percent coverage before dereplication (longest or composite mode).

name: nuts-mcmc-posterior-inference
description: Use when a Bayesian compositional time-series model (e.g. TGP-CODA or MALLARD) must be fit by MCMC to longitudinal 16S count data to obtain posterior estimates of latent relative abundances for accuracy/runtime benchmarking.

name: ocean-virome-community-analysis
description: Use when the goal is all-vs-all comparison or clustering of many large metagenomes/viromes (billions of reads) by k-mer content at full read depth, e.g. reproducing Tara Ocean Virome temperature-structured clustering (Fig. 5).

name: offset-value-computation
description: Use when traversing a colored de Bruijn graph built from multiple sample haplotypes (e.g., 5000–20,000 simulated mitochondrial genomes) to assign positional coordinates to nodes and colored superbubbles (cSupBs), or to detect cycles during the traversal.

name: offset-value-coordinate-assignment
description: Use when you need per-node or per-base coordinates on a VARI-merge colored de Bruijn graph pangenome — e.g., for offset-based cycle detection, reference position determination (RPD), or projecting GTF gene annotations onto the graph as (position, bubid, basecolor) triples.

name: offset-value-cycle-identification
description: Use when building a colored de Bruijn graph over highly similar haplotypes (e.g., mitochondrial genomes) and the postorder-like traversal finishes with unvisited nodes, signaling cycles that block cSupB decomposition.

name: olc-assembly-pipeline-handling
description: Use when the input is interleaved FASTQ metagenomic short-read data (e.g. all_reads.fq from an Illumina MiSeq run) and the goal is de novo, strain-resolved assembly without a reference genome.

name: oligonucleotide-frequency-dissimilarity-computation
description: Use when whole-genome FASTA sequences of viruses or host organisms are available and you need an alignment-free, k-mer-frequency-based pairwise dissimilarity/similarity matrix to seed a network-based prediction method.

name: oligonucleotide-thermodynamic-stability-assessment
description: Use when designing degenerate or nondegenerate primers from aligned nucleotide sequences and candidate oligos must be filtered by hairpin/homodimer Tm, GC content bounds, and per-primer degeneracy limits before amplification testing.

name: oligonucleotide-tiling-probe-design
description: Use when you must design targeted-capture baits across many related genomes (e.g., 56 RefSeq coronaviruses) and need to compare tiling-only, hybridization-modeled (CATCH), and homology-hierarchy (HUBDesign) strategies by efficiency metric.

name: omics-clustering-dimensionality-reduction
description: Use when a filtered Pandas DataFrame time-series omics table needs unsupervised grouping via distance-based or density-based clustering plus embedding, before rendering an interactive time-series visualization.

name: on-the-fly-lcp-extraction-from-bwt
description: Use when the input is only the eBWT file of a raw-read collection (e.g. reads.fasta.bwt from BCR) and you need positional-clustering variant detection without the memory cost of explicit LCP/GSA arrays.

name: one-mismatch-child-variant-assignment
description: Use when processing 16S rRNA amplicon FASTQ data to form parent/one-mismatch-child clusters with HashSeq and you need a verified cluster table before LOESS-based error inference.

name: one-mismatch-children-statistics
description: Use when running HashSeq on Illumina 16S rRNA amplicon data and you need to check that the LOESS regression of one-mismatch children's mean/SD versus parent abundance fits well above the filtering threshold before trusting inferred variants.

name: one-mismatch-variant-enumeration
description: Use when you have pre-processed 16S rRNA gene fastq reads (primers removed, paired, trimmed to 250 bases) and need to enumerate one-mismatch children per parent and model their observation rate versus parent abundance.

name: ont-long-read-scaffolding
description: Use when a metagenome sample has both Illumina paired-end reads and ONT long reads (e.g. 28-75 Gbp PromethION) and the goal is highly contiguous scaffolds or near-complete genomes for high-abundance species.

name: ont-read-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking host-read-removal precision on Nanopore data: reference-grade bacterial or mycobacterial assemblies must be turned into simulated ONT FASTQ reads so read retention (reads_out/reads_in) can be measured against tools like Hostile and HRRT.

name: oob-error-convergence-assessment
description: Use when fitting a random survival forest on microbiome taxa for survival prediction (MiSurv Module 4) and you must verify OOB error stabilization at a chosen ntree (10,000) before ranking predictors by VIMP.

name: opal-output-metric-recomputation
description: Decision support for comparing metagenomic taxonomic profilers (KMA variants, MetaPhlAn, mOTUs, Bracken) on benchmark data with known ground truth, when per-level Purity/Completeness/F1 must be recomputed from profiler output files rather than trusted from published figures.

name: open-reading-frame-extraction
description: Use when you have assembled nucleotide contigs and need to enumerate every candidate short-ORF RiPP precursor inside modification-enzyme-flanked BGC windows, without relying on known RiPP sequence motifs.

name: open-reference-otu-picking-greengenes
description: Use when raw 16S rRNA amplicon reads (e.g., FASTQ from a QIITA study) must be converted into an OTU-level feature table, RDP taxonomy table, and FastTree phylogeny that are structurally consistent with a deposited phyloseq/biom dataset.

name: open-source-bioinformatics-pipeline-execution
description: Use when you have simulated or real metagenomic shotgun reads (454, Sanger, or Illumina) and need to run an open-source gene prediction pipeline end-to-end, from installation through prediction output for benchmarking.

name: optics-cluster-extraction
description: Use when per-sample AD/DP allele counts (cellsnp-lite output) are available for a shotgun metagenomic population and variants must be classified as shared/informative versus background noise by clustering sample allele frequencies.

name: oral-niche-differential-abundance-testing
description: Use when comparing predicted functional (KO/KEGG module) abundances between body sites or physiological states from 16S-only data, e.g. supragingival vs subgingival plaque or menses vs rest-of-cycle vaginal samples.

name: orf-coding-potential-classification
description: Use when working with six-frame-translated short-read assemblies (e.g. 'plass assemble' output FASTA) where short ORFs below 60 aa may be spurious and a coding-potential decision is needed per candidate protein.

name: orf-contig-coordinate-parsing
description: Use when you have VAMB gene clusters (all_genes_cluster.tsv) plus ORF FASTA sequences embedding per-contig gene order, and you need genomic adjacency information to build synteny clusters.

name: orf-depth-gene-abundance-quantification
description: Use when building gene-level functional abundance/profiling data from QCed shotgun metagenomic FASTQ reads (e.g. as part of OMARU's Step 2, OMARU_QCed1.sm), before gene-level MWAS association testing.

name: orf-frame-branching-error-correction
description: Use when predicting genes in raw metagenomic reads (454, Sanger, or Illumina) that carry indel or substitution sequencing errors, so that coding-frame tracking must tolerate insertions, deletions, and stop-codon-introducing substitutions.

name: orf-prediction-and-blast-annotation
description: Use when assembled contigs (from SPAdes/metaSPAdes/MEGAHIT inside virMine, or supplied via -A) must be gene-predicted and BLAST-annotated against viral and nonviral protein FASTA databases to classify contigs as viral.

name: orf-prediction-from-contigs
description: Use when you have per-sample QCed shotgun FASTQ files and need gene-level functional profiling: contigs are assembled de novo (MEGAHIT) and ORFs must be called on them before UniRef90 annotation.

name: orf-prediction-from-nucleotide-sequences
description: Use when input is raw nucleotide FASTA genome sequence(s) and gene prediction has not been performed externally, so ORF calling must precede protein family annotation and phenotype assignment.

name: orf-prediction-on-insertion-sequence-contigs
description: Use when candidate IS nucleotide sequences (e.g. FASTA of ISs from ITR-based discovery) must be annotated to decide which encode transposase-family proteins.

name: orf-six-frame-translation
description: Use when you need to enumerate all possible short peptide precursors from nucleotide FASTA genomes/contigs — e.g. estimating candidate short ORFs for RiPP precursor databases or benchmarking motif-ORF vs all-ORF search-space sizes.

name: organism-function-assignment-from-alignment
description: Use when preprocessed metatranscriptome reads (post-PEAR/Trimmomatic/SortMeRNA) need organism and functional annotations, and a local protein reference FASTA with informative headers is available or can be built.

name: organism-taxonomic-accuracy-assessment
description: Use when you need to quantify how accurately a metatranscriptome annotation pipeline recovers known organism identities (species/genus) and functions from reads with simulated ground-truth labels, e.g. to compare pipeline versions like SAMSA2 vs SAMSA 1.0.

name: ortholog-abundance-correction
description: Use when a KO-level abundance table from shotgun metagenomic read mapping needs normalization before pathway aggregation, and per-genome copy-number values (not raw relative abundances) are required.

name: ortholog-hmm-gene-prediction
description: Use when you have assembled fungal genomes (high-quality or draft) and need to extract single-copy marker gene sequences to build a taxonomic marker catalog or assess genome completeness across a strain collection.

name: ortholog-marker-accuracy-scoring
description: Use when recovered marker FASTA sequences from genome-skimming retrieval runs (e.g. Patchwork, ALiBaSeq, aTRAM 2 outputs) must be quantitatively scored against a curated USCO reference set to compare accuracy across programs or coverages.

name: ortholog-marker-retrieval-from-genomic-assemblies
description: Use when you need to mine (near-)universal single-copy ortholog markers from a de novo short-read assembly (e.g. SPAdes contigs) or raw WGS reads for phylogenomics, with DNA-to-protein similarity search against a curated OrthoDB-based USCO reference set.

name: orthologous-cluster-count-validation
description: Use when you have run (or are about to trust) all-vs-all BLASTP + modified Jaccard clustering on the VIRGO non-redundant gene catalog and must verify the resulting VOG cluster tables are complete and correctly merged.

name: otu-abundance-table-normalization
description: Use when an OTU abundance table (e.g. .tsv, .csv or BIOM, such as HMP_SRA_gut_tiny.tsv) must be normalized automatically before FlashWeave-style statistical co-occurrence network inference.

name: otu-clustering-against-annotated-database
description: Use when you have chimera-filtered paired-end 16S reads (never merged) plus an annotated 16S FASTA database and need annotated OTUs at species-level resolution without merging reads.

name: otu-copy-number-normalization
description: Use when a 16S rRNA OTU table must be converted to per-organism abundances (correcting 16S copy-number variation) before predicting gene family (KO) abundances with PICRUSt.

name: otu-pipeline-performance-comparison
description: Use when comparing how different quality-filtering strategies (MICCA's expected-error-based filtering vs UPARSE's truncation-based filtering) change retained-read and retained-chimera fractions on simulated 16S or ITS amplicon datasets.

name: otu-relative-abundance-computation
description: Use when comparing OTU-picking pipelines on data with a known composition (e.g. the 16S-R synthetic dataset of 500 OTUs and 100000 reads), and you need a quantitative abundance-accuracy metric rather than OTU-count or rarefaction curves.

name: otu-table-abundance-processing
description: Use when an OTU/amplicon abundance table with unaltered Greengenes taxonomic assignments (read counts, not percentages) must be corrected for 16S rRNA gene copy number bias, or when 16S qPCR totals need GCN correction.

name: otu-table-qc-and-formatting
description: Use when raw 16S amplicon data (e.g., mockrobiota mock4, mock12, mock16) must be converted into per-method feature tables that are QC-checked, formatted for qiime2, and compared to true community compositions via weighted UniFrac.

name: overdispersion-assessment-in-count-data
description: Use when evaluating whether per-cluster count data violate Poisson mean-variance assumptions, e.g., testing if one-mismatch children exceed the background sequencing-error rate estimated by LOESS.

name: overestimation-proportion-computation
description: Use when comparing abundance-call correctness of fimpera versus a same-size cAMQ/cBF: true-positive query results with reported abundances and ground truth are available and overestimation rates must be quantified.

name: overlap-extension-read-recruitment
description: Use when a small set of reads mapped to a partial or remotely related viral reference (SAM file) must be expanded to recover more reads of the same virus from a larger metagenomic read set (FASTA) for downstream haplotype assembly.

name: overlap-layout-consensus-graph-construction
description: Use when assembling individual strain genomes (haplotigs) from short-read metagenomic data that has already been split into per-cluster interleaved FASTQ read sets, and strain-resolved contigs are needed.

name: overlap-mismatch-correction-classification
description: Use when auditing PANDAseq-corrected overlap mismatches: you have per-correction records plus per-base PHRED/CASAVA quality characters and need to quantify corrections that are masked in both, one, or neither read.

name: overlap-score-threshold-filtering
description: Use when quality-controlled NGS reads must be linked by suffix-prefix overlaps for OLC assembly, and each Minimap2-derived overlap needs a weighted identity/length score plus a length and identity cutoff.

name: overlap-threshold-parameter-tuning
description: Use when running 'plass assemble' on short-read sequencing data and overlap-detection sensitivity/specificity must be adjusted via --min-seq-id and -e before judging assembled protein output.

name: overpopulated-feature-filtering
description: Use when building a large partitioned MetaCacheSpark reference database on a Spark/HDFS cluster and k-mer/minhash features are shared by so many sequences that they risk misclassification; enable via the -o build flag.

name: p-value-trace-visualization
description: Use when you have run progressive permutation of a binary grouping factor over a microbiome feature table and need to visually assess whether the most differential features from the original data retain signal strength (as -log10 p-values) as mixing approaches full permutation.

name: paf-mapping-output-generation
description: Use when converting matching seed hash values from raw nanopore signals into a mapped genomic region (e.g., D1 SARS-CoV-2 r9.4 FAST5 reads vs ref.ind/ref.fasta), or when validating mapping.paf against minimap2 ground truth.

name: paf-output-parsing
description: Use when you have PAF files in the UNCALLED-style template emitted by RawHash/UNCALLED/Sigmap and need to derive precision/recall, relative abundance, or read-prefix/chunk statistics from them.

name: pafstats-runtime-profiling
description: Use when comparing raw nanopore signal mappers (RawHash, UNCALLED, Sigmap) on D1–D5 FAST5 datasets and you need per-tool CPU/real-time and bases-per-second throughput ratios to test real-time feasibility.

name: paired-cohort-enrichment-testing
description: Use when you have a relative abundance feature table (species or pathways from metagenomic/16S sequencing) with a two-group phenotype (ctrl vs disease) and limited samples, and need sensitive phenotype-enriched feature identification.

name: paired-end-ambiguous-read-reexamination
description: Use when paired-end metagenomic reads (e.g. 100 bp Illumina mates) remain ambiguous after similarity scoring against reference genomes and mate-consistency should resolve them or reassign them to a higher taxonomic rank.

name: paired-end-fastq-mate-handling
description: Use when mapping paired-end shotgun metagenomic FASTQ reads to a protein-reference gene database (e.g., UniRef90) and you need per-mate alignment before downstream -hit filtering and gene counting.

name: paired-end-fastq-mate-synchronization
description: Use when raw paired-end shotgun viral metagenomic FASTQ files (R1/R2) need adapter removal, low-quality base trimming, and host/contaminant read removal before viral identification, and mates must stay in register.

name: paired-end-illumina-read-simulation
description: Use when building synthetic FASTQ benchmarks from known viral reference genomes (e.g. BASV, BKV, HIV-1) to evaluate contig extension or assembly accuracy under varied read length, error rate, and depth conditions.

name: paired-end-insert-size-distribution-filtering
description: Use when profiling metagenomic read mappings against reference genomes and needing to discard improperly paired or aberrant-insert-size reads before computing coverage, ANI, or SNVs.

name: paired-end-metagenomic-read-preprocessing
description: Use when reconstructing full-length SSU rRNA genes (16S/18S) from paired-end Illumina metagenomic FASTQ to enable species-level taxonomic profiling via RiboTaxa's dual-assembler strategy.

name: paired-end-overlap-graph-assembly
description: Use when you have a FASTA of mixed single- and paired-end viral reads (e.g. TAR-VIR recruited_reads.fa) and need to reconstruct strain-level haplotypes de novo, without a complete reference genome.

name: paired-end-overlap-match-probability-computation
description: Use when scoring overlapping paired-end FASTQ reads (e.g. 108-base Illumina reads) to decide which assembled sequences pass a quality threshold such as p = 0.9 or p = 0.6.

name: paired-end-overlap-scoring
description: Use when merging overlapping paired-end Illumina FASTQ reads (e.g. 16S rRNA amplicons) where naive perfect-match overlap fails due to uncalled (N) or miscalled bases, and error-correcting probabilistic assembly is needed.

name: paired-end-read-alignment
description: Use when metagenomic FASTQ (paired-end WGSIM-simulated or real shotgun) reads must be mapped to a bacterial reference set to produce unique/split read BAMs for HGT breakpoint detection.

name: paired-end-read-assembly
description: Use when Illumina paired-end FASTQ (or SAM/BAM) amplicon reads overlap and must be merged into full-length sequences with mismatch/uncalled-base correction, e.g., 16S rRNA libraries where naive assembly discards ~40% of reads.

name: paired-end-read-assembly
description: Use when raw paired-end Illumina reads (e.g. SRA FASTQ like ERR008613) must be converted into genome assembly contig FASTAs for comparison with QUAST/WebQUAST.

name: paired-end-read-local-reassembly
description: Use when a draft scaffold FASTA contains N-wildcard gap regions between contigs and a paired-end short-read dataset (e.g. Illumina GAGE PE reads) is available to fill those gaps by local reassembly.

name: paired-end-read-mapping-to-multi-genome-reference
description: Use when a metagenomic analysis needs paired-end shotgun reads mapped against many reference genomes simultaneously so junction read pairs spanning two different references can seed donor/receptor detection.

name: paired-end-read-merging
description: Use when raw paired-end FASTQ reads from stool metatranscriptomes must be joined into longer single fragments (longer than 100 bp) before annotation, as the SAMSA pipeline aligns paired-end files after Trimmomatic cleaning.

name: paired-end-read-merging
description: Use when raw paired-end metatranscriptome RNA-seq data in FASTQ form must be converted into a single merged, trimmed, rRNA-filtered FASTQ before DIAMOND annotation, as in the SAMSA2 preprocessing step.

name: paired-end-read-pair-integrity-checking
description: Use when a paired-end QC/trimming step (e.g. fastp) has produced cleaned_1.fastq.gz and cleaned_2.fastq.gz and you must confirm the pair is synchronized, non-empty, and valid gzip FASTQ before hybrid assembly.

name: paired-end-read-pairing-handling
description: Use when classifying paired-end FASTQ read pairs (e.g. simulated 2x250 nt Illumina reads) with Kaiju, or when benchmarking throughput where read-pair ordering and naming conventions must be preserved.

name: paired-end-read-quality-trimming
description: Use when raw paired-end FASTQ reads (e.g. from SRA accessions like ERR008613) must be quality-checked and low-quality ends removed before assembly, with surviving mate pairs kept as FASTQ.GZ.

name: paired-end-read-separate-clustering
description: Use when processing paired-end 16S FASTQ reads with highly overlapping mates where quality drops in the overlap region make read merging lossy, and you want annotated OTUs without a merging step.

name: paired-end-read-simulation-to-single-end
description: Use when deciding whether paired-end sequencing is necessary for metatranscriptome annotation, or when quantifying how much annotation information is lost by processing paired-end reads as single-end.

name: paired-end-reverse-complement-handling
description: Use when classifying paired-end reads (e.g., setB2_1/setB2_2 FASTA files) whose strand orientation is unknown, and classification quality depends on considering forward and reverse-complement strands.

name: paired-end-similarity-matrix-computation
description: Use when classifying paired-end metagenomic reads with LiME and you must build similarity matrices for all four collections (Reads1F, Reads1RC, Reads2F, Reads2RC) merged against the reference genomes.

name: paired-end-strand-and-mate-handling
description: Use when classifying paired-end metagenomic reads (e.g. 100 bp Illumina mates from SRR1804065 or setB2) with LiME, when strand direction is unknown and ambiguous reads must be resolved with mate information.

name: paired-read-concatenation-for-classification
description: Use when classifying paired-end reads from simulated or real metagenomes (e.g., HiSeq, MiSeq or simBA-5 read sets) with a k-mer LCA classifier that accepts single sequences, and you want both mates of a pair to vote together for one taxon.

name: paired-read-filtering-quality-control
description: Use when preparing .bam files for inStrain profile/compare so that genome coverage, SNV calls, and strain-level comparisons (ConANI/popANI) rest on correctly mapped read pairs rather than spurious single-end or mis-oriented alignments.

name: paired-read-taxonomic-classification
description: Use when paired-end read pairs (e.g. KAL_D, 26,114K read pairs) must be taxonomically assigned against multi-kingdom reference genome databases, especially when benchmarking MetaCache/AFS-MetaCache, CLARK, or Kraken2+Bracken classification quality or runtime.

name: pairwise-genome-ani-comparison
description: Use when you need sensitive strain-level comparison of microbial populations across metagenomic samples, e.g. testing whether related individuals share more strains than unrelated ones.

name: pairwise-instrain-profile-comparison
description: Use when pairwise genomic comparison of the same genome set across metagenomic samples must distinguish true shared strains from co-occurring but divergent populations, e.g. twin strain-sharing benchmarks.

name: pairwise-population-xpehh-comparison
description: Use when detecting recent selective sweeps by contrasting haplotype lengths between two populations from chromosome-split, tabix-indexed biallelic VCFs plus a sample-to-population .map file.

name: pairwise-scaffold-distance-matrix-construction
description: Use when you have a FASTA of predicted viral scaffolds and need a scaffold-by-scaffold nucleotide feature distance table (7 features per pair) to feed ML-based viral binning like vRhyme's.

name: pairwise-snp-indel-discovery-between-samples
description: Use when two raw FASTA/FASTQ read collections from related samples must be compared for SNP/INDEL discovery without aligning to a reference genome, and sensitivity against a de Bruijn graph baseline (DISCOSNP++) must be quantified.

name: pairwise-synteny-score-averaging
description: Use when you already have raw per-region synteny scores (e.g. synteny_scores_per_region.csv) and need a robust pairwise relatedness matrix over sample pairs, controlling for unequal region counts per pair.

name: pan-genome-index-construction
description: Use when you need to classify nanopore reads against one or many related reference genomes (e.g. one-genome vs multi-strain pan-genome FASTA) for targeted depletion, and must build MS and PML indexes plus a null index before running SPUMONI classification.

name: pan-genome-sequence-construction
description: Use when a reduced nucleotide reference of species-level gene space is needed to assign metagenomic contigs to close relatives or to select species-specific gene prediction models, as in the GeneMark-HM pipeline.

name: pan-genome-similarity-search-execution
description: Use when annotating short human-microbiome metagenomic contigs that cannot support de novo self-training, and species-specific parameters must be imported via pan-genome model selection.

name: pangenome-contig-assignment
description: Use when predicting protein-coding genes in assembled human microbiome metagenome contigs and you need species-level parameter selection via pan-genome assignment rather than generic metagenomic models.

name: pangenome-database-volume-reduction-analysis
description: Use when reproducing or benchmarking GeneMark-HM's efficiency claims, specifically the factor-15 database reduction and single-CPU run-time comparisons on metagenomic contigs.

name: pangenome-partitioning-quality-bootstrapping
description: Use when computing core-genome partitioning from presence/absence patterns of gene clusters or traits in genome sets of highly diverse completeness (e.g. MAGs/SAGs with CheckM completeness/contamination estimates), and when the quality of that partitioning must be quantified via bootstrapping.

name: pangenome-reference-repetitiveness-analysis
description: Use when comparing read-classification tool performance (bases/second throughput, index size, peak RSS) across references of differing repetitiveness, e.g. single-genome vs many-strain pan-genome indexes on mock-community reads.

name: pangenome-triplet-coordinate-annotation
description: Use when variants detected on a colored de Bruijn graph pangenome need graph coordinates (position, bubid, basecolor) transformed into locus-level annotations in VCF format for highly similar haplotype sequences.

name: pangolin-lineage-assignment-interpretation
description: Use when sample mutations in a VCF must be matched against SARS-CoV-2 lineage-defining rules (Pangolin or outbreak.info) to explain or validate a lineage assignment from wastewater NGS data.

name: parallel-command-line-pipeline-execution
description: Use when a pipeline step must be repeated independently over many input files (e.g. 4,472 vaginal metagenomic assemblies or ~26 million predicted genes) and each invocation is a standalone CLI tool that can be embarrassingly parallelized.

name: parallel-pipeline-execution-24-core
description: Use when a reference-free SNP-discovery job on a large read set (e.g. 30x Human chromosome 1) is too slow sequentially and a multi-core machine (24 cores) is available.

name: parallel-runtime-profiling-multi-cpu
description: Use when you need to reproduce or compare reported compute times for ShoRAH's error-correction or frequency-estimation steps on deep-sequencing (e.g. 40,000-read pyrosequencing) samples, or to document hardware requirements of a viral diversity workflow.

name: parameter-count-model-size-control
description: Use when training per-k-mer neural detectors from raw MinION squiggle reads and the resulting .h5 models must stay small enough to run in limited memory (e.g. baseLess with --mem 256 on a Jetson Nano).

name: parameter-sensitivity-sweep-analysis
description: Use when benchmarking LiME (or an eBWT-based classifier) across parameter grids: you need to measure how alpha-clusters of minimum length alpha and threshold beta jointly affect classification sensitivity, precision and F1 against known read provenances.

name: parameter-sweep-evaluation
description: Use when selecting the k-mer length k for baseLess salient-k-mer models: sweep candidate k values against non-target lengths (30/50 kb) and target lengths (0.6/1.5/30 kb) and pick the k minimizing FPR.

name: parameter-sweep-heatmap-visualization
description: Use when benchmarking Snekmer's unsupervised cluster mode across recoding alphabet (0-5 plus None/size-20) and kmer length combinations against known HMM-derived family labels, and rendering the AUC results as a summary heatmap.

name: parent-abundance-fit-curve-visualization
description: Use when you have HashSeq OneMismatchCluster.txt output from 16S rRNA amplicon data and need to show how one-mismatch child discovery scales with parent read abundance and fit a Poisson error model.

name: pathway-abundance-errorbar-visualization
description: Use when you already hold a KEGG pathway-level abundance table (e.g. ko_abundance), sample metadata, and a ggpicrust2 DA results table, and need a publication-quality error-bar figure of differential pathways.

name: pathway-algal-cover-correlation-analysis
description: Use when only 16S rRNA data are available along a continuous environmental gradient (e.g., algal cover in coral mucus) and functional shifts must be inferred by correlating predicted KEGG pathway abundances against that variable.

name: pathway-differential-abundance-analysis
description: Use when you have a PICRUSt2-derived KEGG pathway abundance table plus sample metadata with a grouping variable and need to test which predicted pathways differ in abundance between comparison groups.

name: pathway-significance-result-verification
description: Use when a PICRUSt2/ggpicrust2 differential abundance run must be validated against a published significant-pathway result (e.g., ko05016 and ko05012 under LinDA) before the output table is accepted.

name: pca-population-structure-analysis
description: Use when genome-wide biallelic SNP data (VCF or PLINK BED/BIM/FAM) need population structure inference via PCA and ADMIXTURE, including determining the optimal ancestral components K by CV error.

name: pcoa-ordination-of-variant-frequencies
description: Use when you have a sample-by-variant allele-frequency matrix (e.g., from cellSNP.cells_ARG.vcf.gz with MetaQuad num_of_clusters >= 2 variants) and need to test whether predefined sample groups (e.g., antibiotic treatments) differ in variant composition at a given time point.

name: pcr-amplification-criterion-application
description: Use when evaluating in silico whether a set of candidate primers (degenerate or expanded to nondegenerate forms) successfully amplifies reference gene sequences, and when comparing coverage of new primers against published primer sets.

name: pcr-concordance-validation
description: Use when sequence-based variant or gene-presence calls (e.g., Mykrobe PVL or resistance calls) must be checked for concordance against an existing PCR or phenotypic reference table on a defined isolate panel.

name: pe-se-organism-activity-correlation-analysis
description: Use when deciding whether paired-end sequencing is required for metatranscriptome read annotation, e.g. raw paired-end FASTQ files are available and the goal is to measure annotation loss from simulated single-end processing.

name: peak-memory-profiling
description: Use when comparing runtime and RAM footprint of taxonomic classifiers or similar read-processing tools on a fixed simulated read set, to decide which tool fits available hardware.

name: peak-memory-profiling
description: Use when benchmarking the peak memory and throughput of host-sequence decontamination of bacterial FASTQ reads with Hostile (Bowtie2/Minimap2, 8 threads) and comparing against the NCBI HRRT (sra-human-scrubber).

name: peak-memory-profiling-of-variant-callers
description: Use when benchmarking the disk/RAM footprint of reference-free variant discovery pipelines, e.g. comparing a BWT-only tool (ebwt2InDel, 7n bits expected working space) against GSA/LCP-based predecessors (ebwt2snp) on the same FASTQ/FASTA reads.

name: peak-memory-usage-measurement
description: Use when benchmarking reference-database build or read-classification runs of k-mer based classifiers (e.g. on AFS20/AFS31/AFS20RS90/AFS31RS90 databases) and you need a comparable peak-RAM metric per tool/database combination.

name: pearson-correlation-analysis
description: Use when organism abundance tables from two independent annotation sources (e.g., mRNA-based RefSeq hits vs. rRNA-based SILVA SSU hits) must be cross-validated by correlation at multiple taxonomic levels.

name: penalized-grouped-lasso-dtm-fitting
description: Use when comparing a penalized (non-Bayesian) DTM approach against Bayesian variable selection on compositional count data with phylogenetic tree structure and many covariates (e.g. 97 FFQ dietary factors), to benchmark the number of detected taxon-covariate associations.

name: peptide-sequence-shuffling-decoy-generation
description: Use when assigning tandem mass spectra (mzML/GNPS spectral datasets) to computationally predicted RiPP structures and you need an empirical FDR to set an acceptance threshold on peptide-spectrum matches.

name: peptide-spectrum-matching-scoring
description: Use when scoring peptide-spectrum matches between GNPS tandem MS spectra and a precursor peptide database derived from genomes/metagenomes, and when controlling identifications by target-decoy FDR.
tools: GNPS (Global Natural Products Social molecular networking)

name: peptide-spectrum-matching-with-blind-modifications
description: Use when tandem mass spectra are paired with genomic/metagenomic data and you need to identify RiPPs—including those with unknown or blind modifications—by peptidogenomic database search at controlled FDR.

name: peptidogenomics-spectrum-genome-searching
description: Use when you have tandem MS spectra (e.g. GNPS datasets) paired with producer genomes, RefSeq assemblies, or metagenomic/metatranscriptomic short reads, and want to identify RiPPs (lanthipeptides, lassopeptides, LAPs, linaridins, glycocins, cyanobactins, proteusins) at 1% FDR.

name: per-base-coverage-extraction-with-samtools-depth
description: Use when you have a BAM from mapping read subsets onto a specific reference FASTA and need the per-base covered fraction, gap identification, or coverage progression across iterative read-subset expansion cycles.

name: per-bin-summary-table-generation
description: Use when you have binned contig FASTA files from a metagenome assembly and need per-MAG quality metrics (contig count, N50, completeness, contamination) consolidated for bin selection.

name: per-family-roc-auc-evaluation
description: Use when you need to quantify agreement between de novo clustering results (e.g. Snekmer cluster output) and known ground-truth family labels, per family, across a parameter sweep.

name: per-filter-count-report-generation
description: Use when a read-filtering pipeline must account for exactly how each .bam read (pair) was removed — e.g. un-paired, insert size, mapQ, or nucleotide identity — and per-filter counts must be reported per sequence and validated.

name: per-fragment-read-subsampling-coverage-control
description: Use when multiple high-coverage 10x Chromium Linked-Read libraries must be compared at matched parameters, or when an experiment needs to fix read coverage per DNA fragment (CR) while varying fragment-level parameters such as physical coverage (CF) or fragment length (Mu_F).

name: per-genome-sequence-depth-quantification
