description: Use when short-read metagenomic FASTQ data must be quantified against a set of reference genomes to obtain per-genome mapped read counts and sequence depth, e.g. for read-mapping-based source attribution.

name: per-haplotype-read-coverage-quantification
description: Use when comparing read-recruitment strategies for viral metagenomic data and you need recruited-read counts plus per-haplotype genome coverage/fraction to judge which mapper parameters enrich the target virus .

name: per-lineage-viral-read-fraction-quantification
description: Use when a viral taxonomic classification run (e.g., VirMAP on a mock community such as the NetoVir control SRR3458562) must be converted into per-lineage read fractions and benchmarked against published relative abundance proportions.

name: per-position-nucleotide-diversity-calculation
description: Use when you have a sorted .bam of reads mapped to a reference .fasta and need per-position nucleotide diversity plus scaffold-level coverage, breadth, and expected-breadth metrics for microdiversity profiling.

name: per-rank-accuracy-tabulation
description: Use when a taxonomic classifier's predictions on the 69,335-sequence Greengenes2 2024.09 test set need per-rank top-1 accuracy (and optionally F1/ECE) tabulated, including Seen/Unseen or similarity-bucket subsets.

name: per-rank-classification-metrics-evaluation
description: Use when DeepTaxa (or comparable hierarchical 16S rRNA classifier) predictions on labeled test sequences must be scored per taxonomic rank, e.g. reproducing the Greengenes2 2024.09 species-level accuracy/F1/ECE benchmarks.

name: per-reference-assembly-metric-normalization
description: Use when comparing de novo assembler performance on mock metagenomic communities with known reference replicons, and per-reference metrics from LMAS global/per-reference tables must be placed on a comparable scale across assemblers.

name: per-replicon-metric-normalization
description: Use when benchmarking metagenomic de novo assemblers against a defined mock community and you need a per-reference-replicon completeness fraction (LSA) from contig-to-reference alignments.

name: per-sample-depth-calibration
description: Use when constructing simulated shotgun metagenomic benchmark datasets where each sample must hit a target mean depth, and per-sample read counts must be computed from depth, reference size, and read length.

name: per-sample-gene-count-aggregation
description: Use when shotgun metagenomic FASTQ reads must be converted into a sample-by-gene count/frequency matrix via alignment against a non-redundant gene catalog, prior to CSS normalization or KEGG-based functional annotation.

name: per-sample-gene-richness-quantification
description: Use when you need per-sample, per-species gene counts from vaginal metagenomic or metatranscriptomic FASTQ data to assess intraspecies gene-content diversity, such as testing whether multiple strains of a species co-occur in a community.

name: per-source-sensitivity-analysis
description: Use when benchmarking a metagenomic fecal source tracking tool against mesocosms of known composition and you need per-source accuracy, e.g. to detect under-performing sources like cow.

name: per-status-f1-variance-analysis
description: Use when comparing microbiome classification models on multi-class datasets (e.g. 3-class oral or 5-class gut status labels) and the question is whether per-class performance is balanced, not just whether overall Kappa or accuracy is higher.

name: per-taxon-accuracy-benchmarking
description: Use when benchmarking trajectory-reconstruction accuracy of denoised relative abundances per taxon across samples, e.g. comparing LUMINATE against TGP-CODA/MALLARD on simulated longitudinal count data.

name: per-taxon-probe-count-balancing
description: Use when building a hybridization-capture probe set from HUBDesign CandidateBaitRegions.tab and you need the final probe count capped and distributed fairly across all input taxa, e.g. tiling to 5x density with at most 13,500 baits.

name: percent-identity-variant-mapping
description: Use when inferred sequence variants (FASTA from a variant caller) need validation against a reference database such as SILVA132 to confirm they match previously observed sequences with high identity (>99%).

name: perl-bioinformatics-tool-configuration
description: Use when deploying CopyRighter from source in a Perl environment: setting up Makefile.PL-driven installation, resolving CPAN dependencies (Bio::Community, Getopt::Euclid >= 0.4.3, Method::Signatures, Scalar::Util), or handling non-administrator installation via local::lib.

name: perl-command-line-tool-execution
description: Use when you need to reproduce or verify the resource requirements (seconds and MB RAM per genome) of a Perl-based CLI genome-mining tool like DiSCo on FASTA protein inputs, or to demonstrate a tool runs on a personal computer without HPC.

name: perl-pipeline-configuration-and-execution
description: Use when predicting protein-coding genes in assembled metagenome contigs from shotgun sequencing of the human microbiome, especially short contigs where contig-specific parameter estimation is impossible and taxa-specific models are needed.

name: permanova-group-separation-testing
description: Use when you have a relative-abundance or compositional feature table (e.g. MetaPhlAn2 or MAGinator taxon-by-sample matrices) plus two-level metadata (IBD vs control) and need a statistical test of between-group beta-diversity separation.

name: permutation-based-discovery-selection
description: Use when a microbiome abundance table with a binary grouping variable is available and you must decide which top differential features are true discoveries rather than noise from label mixing, via full-permutation confidence intervals.

name: permutation-based-meta-analysis-pvalue-estimation
description: Use when combining ≥10 studies across multiple related markers (e.g., 6 α-diversity indices) using only effect estimates and standard errors, with no a priori marker-by-marker correlations, and p-values must be obtained via permutations.

name: permutation-based-pvalue-computation
description: Use when running mMeta.aMeta on study-by-marker summary statistics (regression coefficient estimates and standard errors) and hypothesis-testing p-values are needed across multiple related markers, particularly when marker-by-marker correlations are unknown.

name: permutation-based-pvalue-estimation
description: Use when a microbiome association test statistic (e.g. SPU/aSPU/AMAT T_AMAT) has no tractable analytic null distribution and an empirical P-value must be calibrated by permuting the phenotype vector.

name: permutation-based-threshold-testing
description: Use when screening high-dimensional OTU/count features for outcome association by permuting an adjusted response (B = 500) to build per-feature distance-correlation nulls and select a data-driven testing subset S.

name: permutation-null-significance-testing
description: Use when validating a longitudinal tool's false-positive control on semi-synthetic or real count/proportion data by shuffling the continuous time variable within each individual, as done for the fasting stool microbiome benchmark.

name: permutational-multivariate-anova-on-distance-matrices
description: Use when sample groupings must be tested for significant differences in multivariate dispersion (e.g. allele-frequency or community profiles) and only per-sample distance matrices — not raw feature tables — are available for group-wise hypothesis testing.

name: pfam-based-cluster-quality-scoring
description: Use when protein sequence clustering output must be quality-assessed against independent functional annotations (Pfam), e.g. to compare MMseqs2 easy-cluster runs across a sensitivity parameter sweep or to choose stable clustering settings.

name: pfam-domain-annotation-comparison
description: Use when evaluating the quality of protein sequence clusterings (e.g. from Linclust, UCLUST, CD-HIT at 90/70/50% identity) by measuring how often cluster members share identical Pfam domain annotations with their cluster representative.

name: pfam-protein-family-annotation
description: Use when nucleotide or protein FASTA sequences of bacterial genomes need Pfam protein family profiles as features for phenotype prediction or trait association analysis.

name: phage-host-network-crispr-validation
description: Use when you have Hi-C-inferred virus-host pairs from metagenomic Hi-C bins and want independent CRISPR spacer validation of those pairs, e.g. reproducing the wastewater phage-host network from ViralCC.

name: phage-host-prediction-interpretation
description: Use when you have quality-assessed viral contigs (e.g., identified by VirSorter2/DeepVirFinder/VIBRANT and checked with CheckV) and need to know which bacteria they infect, or when reproducing host-based findings such as phage–host links in UC vs healthy viromes.

name: phage-lambda-control-read-removal
description: Use when raw Nanopore metagenomic FASTQ reads contain phage-lambda sequencing control contamination and must be decontaminated after adapter trimming and before quality filtering and assembly.

name: phage-microdiversity-visualization
description: Use when metagenomic .bam mappings of multiple hosts/infants to the same phage or microbial genome are available and the goal is to classify biallelic SNV positions as within- vs between-host variants and visualize selection (dN/dS) per gene.

name: phage-mining-multi-tool-prediction
description: Use when FASTQ metagenomic or virome reads need viral contig identification and vOTU counting, and a single-miner prediction would miss phages detectable only by complementary k-mer, homology, or HMM-based approaches.

name: phage-replication-cycle-classification
description: Use when you have a set of predicted viral contigs (e.g. from VirSorter2/VIBRANT/DeepVirFinder + CheckV) and need to assign each contig a lytic, lysogenic, or chronic replication-cycle label plus candidate host.

name: phage-taxonomy-assignment-from-reference-clusters
description: Use when a dereplicated vOTU multifasta needs phylum-to-genus (and species-level) taxonomic labels by shared-protein-content similarity to curated INPHARED/GenBank phage reference genomes.

name: phage-taxonomy-composition-analysis
description: Use when shotgun viral metagenomic reads (FASTQ) must be turned into viral contigs with assigned taxonomy and family-level composition, e.g., comparing phage community structure between conditions such as UC vs healthy fecal viromes.

name: phage-taxonomy-conservatism-rules
description: Use when vConTACT2 has produced genome_by_genome_overview.csv and c1.ntw for vOTUs (e.g., from MetaPhage) and a direct taxonomic label per vOTU is needed instead of manual network inspection.

name: phenotype-associated-protein-family-ranking
description: Use when Traitar (Pfam 27.0-based, phypat or phypat+PGL models) has been applied to genomes and you need the ranked Pfam families underlying a specific phenotype prediction, e.g. to interpret a trait assignment mechanistically.

name: phenotype-classification-accuracy-evaluation
description: Use when you have Traitar cross-validation phenotype predictions with true phenotype labels and need per-taxonomic-rank accuracy (e.g. per-phylum) rather than only overall or per-phenotype accuracy.

name: phenotype-label-mapping
description: Use when evaluating genotype-to-phenotype classifiers: you have genome FASTAs plus externally curated phenotype labels (e.g., Bergey's Manual, GIDEON) and need to align predicted trait labels with the reference labels to compute accuracy.

name: phenotype-macroaccuracy-threshold-counting
description: Use when validating a published accuracy claim stated as a count of phenotypes above macroaccuracy thresholds (e.g. >80%, >=90%) and you have a per-phenotype, per-classifier cross-validation accuracy table.

name: phenotype-model-interpretation
description: Use when a trained linear-kernel phenotype model (e.g. PICA SVM on COG features) must be interpreted feature-wise, to test whether a trait is predicted by gene absence rather than gene presence.

name: phenotype-permutation-null-distribution-estimation
description: Use when the empirical null distribution of minimum P-values is needed for the phylogenetic (clade-level) MWAS after Step 4-1, to set a Psig threshold that controls type I error under the study's actual clade correlation structure.

name: phenotype-prediction-table-compilation
description: Use when a trained phenotypic trait model exists and you need to score every genome/species in a large database (e.g. eggNOG 4.0 core and periphery) and assemble the positives into a validated prediction table.

name: phenotypic-character-information-extraction
description: Use when the goal is to semi-automatically extract phenotypic characters (e.g., cell shape, Gram stain, NaCl/pH/temperature ranges, antibiotic sensitivity) from taxonomic description text into a taxon-by-character matrix for phylogenetic or phenomic analysis.

name: phenotypic-character-value-concatenation
description: Use when per-taxon extraction records from MicroPIE's character extractors must be pivoted into a structured taxon-by-character matrix, especially when a taxon has multiple extracted values for the same character that must be merged.

name: php-web-module-implementation
description: Use when building or modifying a web-based feature (e.g., a sequencing submission form or custom field handler) inside MetaLIMS, where PHP 5.5.25, the mysqli module, and MySQL 5.5.43 are the deployment stack.

name: phred-like-quality-score-computation
description: Use when you have per-alignment contig-to-reference-replicon identities (contigs above the --minLength threshold) from an assembly benchmark like LMAS and need a per-contig, Phred-like quality score comparable across assemblers.

name: phred-quality-probability-conversion
description: Use when FASTQ or SAM input from Illumina CASAVA pipelines contains ASCII quality values that must be turned into per-base error probabilities for probabilistic scoring, overlap alignment, or assembly quality filtering.

name: phred-score-mapping-matrix-construction
description: Use when short reads have been mapped to known MLST alleles and you need to encode read-allele mapping quality as a cost matrix (Phred-scaled mismatch scores) before solving the allele diversity ILP.

name: phylogenetic-abundance-profiling
description: Use when starting from shotgun metagenomic FASTQ files and you need clade-resolved (UHGG-based) phylogenetic abundance profiles with rigorous read, sample, and clade QC ahead of case-control MWAS testing.

name: phylogenetic-classification-based-model-parameterization
description: Use when training gene-prediction models on short metagenomic shotgun reads (e.g. 454 human gut microbiome reads) where GC-content-based genome selection is unreliable and organism-of-origin must be inferred per read.

name: phylogenetic-distance-transformation
description: Use when you have a cophenetic distance matrix (from ape's cophenetic function) over microbial features and need phylogeny-aware feature ordering/clustering before model training.

name: phylogenetic-distance-weighting
description: Use when 16S marker gene OTUs must be mapped to predicted gene families (KO/COG) for organisms without reference genomes, and a phylogenetic reference tree with annotated tips (e.g. Greengenes + IMG) is available.

name: phylogenetic-diversity-calculation
description: Use when you have an OTU/species count table per sample plus a phylogenetic tree and need per-sample phylogenetic α-diversity indices (PD, PE, PQE, or richness/Shannon/Simpson) as regression outcomes for downstream meta-analysis.

name: phylogenetic-gcn-correction
description: Use when 16S rRNA amplicon count tables (biom, QIIME, generic) need GCN-bias correction, or when qPCR-derived total abundance must be adjusted by average community GCN before downstream diversity or enterotype analyses.

name: phylogenetic-independent-contrasts-ancestral-state-estimation
description: Use when Greengenes OTUs or taxa lack sequenced genomes (hence no measured 16S rRNA copy number) and a phylogenetically-based GCN estimate is needed for CopyRighter correction.

name: phylogenetic-marker-benchmarking
description: Use when assessing whether DIAMOND's tantan masking suppresses alignments during Patchwork marker retrieval — especially for read-based query data — by A/B comparing --masking 0 against the default masking configuration.

name: phylogenetic-signal-estimation
description: Use when you need to test whether a quantitative trait estimated for OTUs or taxa (e.g., 16S rRNA GCN from CopyRighter's Greengenes data files) shows significant phylogenetic autocorrelation on a tree.

name: phylogenetic-tree-inference
description: Use when starting a PM-CNN analysis from an OTU/species feature table whose representative nucleotide sequences are available (e.g. from GreenGenes) and no phylogenetic tree in NEWICK format has yet been supplied.

name: phylogenetic-tree-inference
description: Use when you have a FASTA of de-novo clustered OTU representative sequences (e.g. from micca otu) and need a Newick phylogenetic tree with one leaf per OTU for downstream diversity or ecology analyses.

name: phylogenetic-tree-parsing-newick
description: Use when a phylogenetic tree exists in NEWICK format (from FastTree/Mafft or user-provided) and a pairwise tip-to-tip distance matrix is needed to encode phylogenetic relationships between OTUs/species.

name: phylogenetic-tree-rendering-and-polyphyletic-cluster-detection
description: Use when a population-genomics pipeline has produced IBS or FST distance matrices and TreeMix tree files, and you need interactive visual trees plus detection of populations that split across clades (polyphyly).

name: phylogenetic-tree-structured-compositional-modeling
description: Use when the input is compositional taxa/count abundance data (e.g., microbiome or diet-taxa tables) with a known phylogenetic tree, and the goal is to identify covariate-branch associations while respecting tree-like structure.

name: phylogenetic-tree-visualization-ete3
description: Use when running or reproducing the scalepopgen TreeMix phylogeny sub-workflow and you need to plot the inferred population trees, bootstrap-supported consensus trees, or migration-edge results from filtered biallelic SNP data.

name: phylogenetic-vs-taxonomic-abundance-correction
description: Use when 16S rRNA amplicon abundance profiles need GCN bias correction and a decision must be made between phylogenetic-level and taxonomic-level CopyRighter correction, or when validating corrected profiles against known community compositions.

name: phylogroup-clade-recapitulation-assessment
description: Use when you have pairwise synteny or strain-distance scores for genomes with a published phylogroup/phylogeny classification, and need to quantify whether the derived tree recovers those clades at statistical significance.

name: phyloseq-data-subsetting
description: Use when analysis must be restricted to a treatment-arm subgroup of a phyloseq microbiome dataset (e.g., control-group survival association in MiSurv Module 3) and metadata columns define the subgroup.

name: phyloseq-object-manipulation
description: Use when microbiome abundance, taxonomy, metadata, and/or tree data must be assembled into a phyloseq object (from biom.Rdata or otu.tab.txt/sam.dat.txt/tax.tab.txt/tree.tre) before rarefaction, diversity computation, or MiSurv Module 2-4 analysis.

name: phylum-level-taxonomic-aggregation
description: Use when a phyloseq object or OTU table with taxonomic annotations needs to be collapsed to phylum-level CLR-transformed abundances for survival-association modeling or treatment-group comparison.

name: phylum-relative-abundance-computation
description: Use when a 16S rRNA amplicon OTU table (biom/QIIME format with read counts) must be GCN-corrected and aggregated to phylum level to report median relative abundances and phylum shifts (e.g. Bacteroidetes, Firmicutes) across a cohort.

name: physical-coverage-parameter-optimization
description: Use when designing or simulating 10x Chromium Linked-Read libraries and you must choose CF, CR, or fragment length (Mu_F) at a fixed total coverage C to maximize contig N50 of a Supernova2 diploid assembly.

name: physico-chemical-time-series-visualization
description: Use when a tabular (CSV/TSV) time-series physico-chemical dataset must be explored in MOVIS to detect temporal trends, anomalies, or maxima in a single feature — e.g., locating when a temperature series reaches its peak value.

name: pica-flatfile-profile-manipulation
description: Use when you need to benchmark phenotypic trait prediction on partially complete genomes (e.g. metagenomic bins) by generating thinned COG presence/absence profiles at controlled completeness levels of 10-90%.

name: picrust-metagenome-prediction-from-otu-table
description: Use when only 16S marker-gene OTU tables (e.g. QIIME closed-reference picked with uclust against Greengenes+IMG) are available and KO-level functional profiles are needed without deep shotgun sequencing.

name: picrust2-pipeline-execution
description: Use when the input is an ASV/OTU abundance table plus marker-gene study sequences (FASTA) and the goal is to infer functional metagenome content (EC gene families and MetaCyc pathways) without shotgun sequencing.

name: pipeline-performance-comparison
description: Use when you need to empirically compare wall-clock runtime and peak memory of two amplicon sequence-variant pipelines (e.g., HashSeq vs DADA2) on the same 16S rRNA gene FASTQ data sets.

name: pipeline-performance-metric-reporting
description: Use when benchmarking or comparing the time performance of multiple OTU-retrieval pipelines (e.g. DADA2, deblur, CD-HIT-OTU-Miseq, CDSnake) across datasets, to populate a runtime comparison table in seconds.

name: pipeline-resource-configuration-tuning
description: Use when deploying the Mapler pipeline on HiFi metagenomic samples (e.g. Mock community, Gut microbiome, Deadwood) and you must set per-rule thread/memory allocations or compare measured wall-clock durations against reported reference times.

name: pipeline-run-report-verification
description: Use when a scalepopgen (nf-core-style Nextflow) run has finished and you must confirm the main script dispatched all sub-workflows successfully and that consolidated HTML execution/analysis reports document per-process resource usage.

name: pipeline-summary-statistics-generation
description: Use when running MetaLAFFA on shotgun metagenomic FASTQs and you need per-sample, per-step quality metrics (e.g. post-trim average base quality, average read length, number of reads) to audit QC and annotation quality.

name: plasmid-assembly-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing plasmid assembly tools on simulated or real (pooled, subsampled) Nanopore read sets against an independently curated plasmid ground truth, to quantify accuracy (QUAST) and plasmid recovery/missed-plasmid counts.

name: plasmid-chromosome-ratio-calculation
description: Use when you need to quantify and compare plasmid content across metagenomic/plasmidome assemblies by computing plasmid:chromosome contig ratios from kmer-signature-based classifiers such as PlasFlow and cBar.

name: plasmid-contig-classification
description: Use when you have metagenomic or bacterial genome assembly contigs (ideally >1000 bp) and need to label them as plasmid-derived versus chromosomal without prior knowledge of sample taxonomic composition.

name: plasmid-database-similarity-search
description: Use when assembled plasmid contigs (e.g. Unicycler output FASTA) need to be matched against a known-plasmid reference database such as PLSDB to annotate novelty or similarity.

name: plasmid-prediction-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when evaluating or reproducing plasmid prediction performance on assembled bacterial contigs, e.g. recovering plasmid recall/precision on the 42 plasmid-rich genomes of Arredondo-Alonso et al. and comparing against cBar and Recycler baselines.

name: plasmid-read-extraction
description: Use when a bacterial hybrid-assembly workflow needs to remove chromosomal reads from FASTQ inputs to speed up plasmid assembly, retaining unmapped reads and reads on putative plasmid contigs.

name: plink-binary-genotype-processing
description: Use when input genotype data are VCF or PLINK binary files that must be converted to PLINK BED format, chromosome IDs recoded to integers, and LD-pruned before PCA, ADMIXTURE, TreeMix, or selection-scan analyses.

name: ploidy-aware-haplotig-consensus-generation
description: Use when assembling strain-resolved haplotigs from pre-clustered metagenomic short reads (interleaved FASTQ per cluster), where co-occurring mutation patterns must be preserved per strain rather than collapsed into a consensus.

name: poisson-competing-model-genotyping
description: Use when you have per-mutation-site reference/alternate k-mer depths from a Mykrobe predictor JSON output (MTBC sample) and need to recompute or audit susceptible/minor/major genotype calls and drug resistance predictions.

name: poisson-error-model-fitting
description: Use when you have HashSeq's OneMismatchCluster.txt output (parents plus one-mismatch children from 16S rRNA amplicon data) and want to quantify the sequencing error rate or check whether child accumulation follows a Poisson process.

name: poisson-one-sided-significance-testing
description: Use when evaluating whether a Poisson error model with equal mean-variance assumption adequately controls one-mismatch child distributions in amplicon variant calling, or when reproducing the Fig. S1 anticonservativeness benchmark.

name: poisson-probability-modeling
description: Decision support for choosing the k-mer length k for a k-mer-detection model (e.g. baseLess composite networks) by computing expected false positive rates of salient k-mers occurring by chance in non-target sequences.

name: popani-strain-delineation
description: Use when pairwise isolate genomes or metagenomic assemblies of the same species must be classified as same vs. different strain, especially when structural variation may be missed by SNP-only comparisons.

name: population-allele-frequency-summary-statistics
description: Use when you have chromosome-split, tabix-indexed biallelic VCF files (or PLINK BED/BIM/FAM) plus a sample-to-population map and need QC filtering plus per-sample and per-window population statistics (MAF, Ho, He) before downstream population-genomic analyses.

name: population-genomic-data-retrieval
description: Use when building the polymorphism/divergence inputs for McDonald–Kreitman analyses, i.e. when DAF spectra and divergence counts must be pre-calculated from PopFly FASTA alignments or PopHuman 1000GP Phase III VCFs.

name: population-genomics-divergence-counting
description: Use when the goal is to produce per-gene polymorphism (DAF spectrum: Pi, P0) and divergence (mi, Di, m0, D0) count tables from FASTA alignments or VCF population data as input to MKT-based estimation of adaptive evolution (alpha).

name: population-genomics-mkt-estimation
description: Use when population-genomic polymorphism (DAF spectra for 0-fold and 4-fold classes) and divergence counts between D. melanogaster and D. simulans (or human-chimp) are available and you must estimate alpha, e.g. comparing gene sets such as high-recombination regions against the whole genome.

name: population-genomics-subworkflow-execution
description: Use when a genome-wide biallelic SNP dataset (VCF or PLINK binary) needs comprehensive population genomic analysis — filtering, PCA/ADMIXTURE structure, TreeMix phylogeny, and selection scans — in a single automated reproducible run.

name: population-phylogeny-inference-treemix
description: Reference for inferring population phylogenetic relationships and migration events from filtered genome-wide biallelic SNP genotype data (VCF or PLINK binary) using TreeMix within a Nextflow workflow.

name: positive-control-benchmark-validation
description: Use when a peptidogenomic or genome-vs-spectra search tool (e.g., MetaMiner/RiPPquest) must be benchmarked on known purified RiPP spectra before trusting identifications on novel microbial community datasets.

name: post-qc-data-reproducibility-verification
description: Use when reproducing or auditing MiSurv's default QC pipeline on 16S OTU data and checking that filtered outputs match the deposited post-QC tables (expected 294 features x 172 subjects).

name: post-translational-modification-application-to-precursors
description: Use when building a target/decoy RiPP database from precursor peptide ORFs whose biosynthetic gene cluster modification enzymes (lanthipeptide, lassopeptide, LAP, linaridin, glycocin, cyanobactin, proteusin) have already been identified.

name: posterior-edge-inclusion-thresholding
description: Use when you have MCMC posterior samples of inclusion indicators from a MicroBVS DM/DTM Bayesian variable selection run (e.g. prior='MRF_unknown' or Beta-Binomial a=0.1, b=0.9) and must convert them into a discrete selected graph or association set.

name: power-curve-visualization
description: Use when evaluating or visualizing statistical power of differential abundance methods on zero-inflated relative abundance data across effect sizes, e.g. comparing GAMLSS-BEZI against transformation-based linear models via simulation.

name: power-law-regression-fitting
description: Use when comparing algorithm scalability: runtime measurements exist for multiple input sizes N (e.g., UniProt subsets) and you need a fitted scaling exponent to distinguish linear (b≈1) from quadratic (b≈2) behavior.

name: precision-recall-benchmarking
description: Use when you have sequencing reads from communities with known ground-truth taxonomic profiles (e.g. ten HBC mock communities) and must quantify which classifier's read-level assignments and abundance estimates are most precise and sensitive.

name: precision-recall-fmeasure-calculation-per-taxonomic-rank
description: Use when comparing taxonomic classifiers (e.g. Centrifuge, Kraken2, mothur, RDP, SPINGO, BLCA, QIIME 2 Sklearn) on sequences with a known ground-truth community composition and you need rank-wise precision/recall/F-measure.

name: precision-recall-tvd-evaluation
description: Use when validating MLST allele- or strain-deconvolution results on simulated samples, comparing a pipeline against Kallisto or strainEST, or verifying recovery of true strain type distributions from ground-truth allele calls.

name: precision-recall-variant-benchmarking
description: Use when you need to quantify detection accuracy (precision, recall, stability) of a variant-calling method on simulated datasets with known SNP/insertion/deletion ground truth, varying variant counts and k.

name: precision-sensitivity-f1-per-rank-evaluation
description: Use when evaluating a viral metagenomic profiler on mock/simulated samples with known composition, and you need per-rank precision, sensitivity and F1 curves across abundance thresholds to compare tools.

name: presence-absence-matrix-construction
description: Use when you need to establish which ribosomal proteins (or other universal single-copy proteins) are present or absent across bacterial lineages from genome bins of mixed completeness, especially where sequence divergence defeats keyword-based gene calling.

name: prevalence-based-taxon-assignment
description: Use when assigning taxonomy to metagenome-assembled genome (MAG) FASTA bins at strain-level resolution with k-mer/minimizer counting against the kMetaShot HDF5 reference, and when a reliability ratio (ass2ref) is needed to filter questionable strain/species calls.

name: primer-degeneracy-expansion
description: Use when you have degenerate primer sequences (IUPAC ambiguity codes) from a primer-design tool like MetaFunPrimer or EcoFunPrimer and need nondegenerate variants to test 100% both-primer match coverage against reference gene sequences.

name: primer-mismatch-evasion-quantification
description: Use when you have curated 16S rRNA gene sequences (or a new primer pair) and need to estimate what fraction of a community or lineage amplicon surveys would fail to detect due to primer-binding-site mismatches.

name: primer-set-coverage-curve-analysis
description: Use when a designed primer set (e.g., 78 nondegenerate amoA-AOB pairs) must be pared down or evaluated: you need the minimal subset of primer pairs that captures maximum reference gene diversity, quantified as in silico PCR coverage.

name: primer-set-sensitivity-benchmarking
description: Use when you need to quantify how many genes from a curated reference set a primer pair (new or published) would detect, or to compare coverage of designed vs published primers before committing to qPCR.

name: principal-component-confounder-adjustment
description: Use when running an OMARU phylogenetic or gene case-control association test and you must decide how many PCs to add as covariates on top of metadata (e.g. sex, age, BMI) to control hidden confounders.

name: probabilistic-confidence-score-implementation
description: Use when implementing or reproducing supervised kmer-based family scoring/confidence scores that must penalize kmers shared between families and bound scores to (-1, 1), as in Snekmer's model/search scoring.

name: probability-threshold-classification-of-scaffolds
description: Use when a metagenomic or genome assembly in fasta form must be partitioned into plasmid-derived vs chromosomal scaffolds based on kmer genome signatures, with unreliable low-confidence calls filtered out.

name: probability-threshold-filtering
description: Use when classifying metagenomic contigs with PlasFlow and you need to control the accuracy/unclassified-fraction trade-off, or when reproducing the paper's reported accuracy at thresholds 0.7 (94.79%) and 0.8 (96.41%).

name: probe-cross-reactivity-efficiency-calculation
description: Use when comparing hybrid-capture probe design methods on the same target genome set and you need a quantitative cross-reactivity/coverage metric, i.e., the mean number of distinct target genomes hit per probe.

name: probe-genome-alignment-mapping
description: Reference for reanalyzing a published HUBDesign probe set: when you have probe sequences plus the annotated source genomes (e.g. GenomeInfo.tab listing 56 RefSeq coronavirus genomes) and need per-genome probe counts, specificity fractions, or comparison to reported extremes.

name: probe-hybridization-parameter-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing probe-design pipelines or hybridization parameter sets on a fixed multi-genome target set and you need a quantitative metric (probes per set, average distinct genomes hit per probe) to judge compactness vs coverage trade-offs.

name: profile-hmm-protein-search-for-seed-generation
description: Use when raw unassembled Illumina FASTQ reads must be screened for cas genes (or any specialty protein family) so matched reads can seed targeted assembly instead of whole-genome assembly.

name: progressive-permutation-label-exchange
description: Use when a microbiome feature table has a binary grouping factor and you need to assess the robustness/overall association of differential abundance discoveries by progressively permuting group labels and tracking significant-feature counts across mixing levels.

name: progressive-permutation-signal-analysis
description: Use when you have a feature-by-sample microbiome count table with a binary grouping factor and need to assess whether top differential features are robust to label permutation, or to rank them by fragility index.

name: prokaryotic-gene-prediction
description: Use when predicting genes in complete prokaryotic genomes or environmental shotgun/metagenomic sequences (e.g. 454/Illumina reads) with FASTA input and curated reference annotations, or when comparing Glimmer3.0/3.1/Glimmer-MG accuracy.

name: prokaryotic-genome-completeness-assessment
description: Use when you have prokaryotic MAG FASTA files (e.g. VMGC SGBs) and need to classify each universal single-copy ortholog as single-copy, duplicated, fragmented or missing, and detect pathway-level absences such as de novo purine biosynthesis genes.

name: prokaryotic-genome-dereplication
description: Use when a large set of assembled prokaryotic genomes (MAGs plus isolates, FASTA format) must be collapsed into nonredundant species-level bins at ~95% nucleotide similarity before taxonomy assignment or downstream cataloguing.

name: prokaryotic-orf-length-distribution-modeling
description: Use when reconstructing or validating the ORF length and adjacent-gene feature models behind a prokaryotic gene predictor's length-scoring term, or when an annotated genome's ORF lengths must be modeled as a blended empirical+parametric distribution.

name: prokaryotic-taxonomic-description-data-structuring
description: Use when free-text prokaryotic taxonomic descriptions must be converted into a structured taxon-by-character matrix (rows = taxa, columns = 42 designated phenotypic characters) for phylogenetic analysis.

name: proportional-read-redistribution-across-taxonomy
description: Use when per-read classifications from MetaCacheSpark/AFS-MetaCache must be converted into per-organism read counts and abundance percentages at a chosen taxonomic rank, and reads sitting on higher-level taxa need redistribution.

name: protein-accession-pathway-linking
description: Use when constructing a functional protein reference database where protein sequences must carry EC-number and pathway metadata (e.g., KEGG) so that downstream read-mapping yields interpretable functional profiles.

name: protein-alignment-output-parsing
description: Use when metatranscriptome reads (FASTQ, preprocessed) have been aligned with DIAMOND blastx against a local DIAMOND-indexed protein database and the tabular per-read output must be converted into organism/function annotation records.

name: protein-annotation-filtering
description: Use when building a reference protein database from multi-source fungal coding genes (NCBI, JGI, UniProt) where unannotated proteins must be removed and redundancy reduced before functional profiling.

name: protein-assembly-orf-length-distribution-analysis
description: Use when metagenomic short reads are six-frame-translated and assembled with Plass and you need to quantify ORF length retention (e.g. <60, 60-100, >100 aa bins) with the neural-network protein filter on versus off.

name: protein-cluster-consistency-scoring
description: Use when you have clusterings of a large protein sequence set (e.g., UniProt) produced by multiple tools at several identity thresholds and need to quantify which tool yields functionally most consistent clusters using GO/Pfam annotations.

name: protein-cluster-network-based-taxonomy-inference
description: Use when viral contigs (>10 kbp) identified from shotgun viral metagenomes need taxonomy, and both clustering-based (viral cluster) and homology-based (reference database) evidence should be combined into one lineage per contig.

name: protein-cluster-overlap-analysis
description: Use when two protein clustering results (e.g., Snekmer cluster and MMseqs2 outputs) on the same protein FASTA set must be compared via per-protein set operations, and combined coverage gain must be quantified.

name: protein-contact-accuracy-evaluation-by-msa-depth
description: Use when comparing contact-prediction models on CASP target domains and you need to know whether accuracy gains at top L/5, L/2, and L depend on how shallow (few homologous sequences) the input MSA is.

name: protein-contact-precision-evaluation-at-top-l-thresholds
description: Use when benchmarking a contact predictor on CASP target domains and you need precision at multiple top-k cutoffs (L/10 to L) and separation ranges to compare against PSICOV, CCMpred, DeepCov, or ResPRE.

name: protein-contact-prediction-inference
description: Use when you have an amino acid sequence (or FASTA) plus a generated MSA and need predicted contact residues and secondary structures from DeepECA's pre-trained models, e.g. as inputs to CONFOLD structure building.

name: protein-contact-probability-ensemble-averaging
description: Use when multiple DNN contact-prediction models trained on cross-validation splits of the same data (e.g. DeepECA multitask models) are available and the goal is to boost per-target contact accuracy by combining their probability outputs.

name: protein-database-shuffling-null-model
description: Use when calibrating a minimum match length or score cutoff for a protein-level metagenomic classifier: simulate/spurious match length distributions on a composition-preserving shuffled database to pick a threshold excluding random matches.

name: protein-domain-fasta-handling
description: Use when the input is a raw target protein amino-acid sequence (or set of sequences) that must be converted to FASTA and staged so HHblits-generated MSAs and covariance features can be computed for contact prediction.

name: protein-family-profile-generation
description: Use when nucleotide (or protein) FASTA genomes must be converted into Pfam protein-family profiles as input for phenotype classification, e.g. Traitar phypat/phypat+PGL workflows.

name: protein-family-profiling-with-pfam-hmms
description: Use when you need Pfam protein family presence/absence profiles for nucleotide or protein FASTAs (draft genomes, metagenome bins, SAGs) to feed phenotype prediction or comparative genotype-phenotype inference.

name: protein-family-signature-annotation
description: Use when candidate IS nucleotide sequences (FASTA) need protein family annotation — e.g. to decide whether an IS encodes a transposase via InterPro (IPR) / PANTHER (PTHR) accessions before reporting it.

name: protein-fasta-file-formatting
description: Use when preparing the -v (viral) and -nv (nonviral) protein FASTA databases required as input to virMine.py, or when rebuilding virMine 2.0 reference databases after a COG or RefSeq release update.

name: protein-guided-nucleotide-alignment-execution
description: Use when nucleotide query sequences (SPAdes contigs or raw short reads) must be searched against protein reference sequences (e.g., 957 H. robusta near-USCOs) to recover homologous phylogenetic markers from fragmented genome-skimming data.

name: protein-kmer-family-scoring
description: Use when implementing or reproducing supervised kmer-based protein family scoring from reduced-alphabet (AAR) kmer count matrices, needing family-specific kmer weights that penalize kmers present in out-group families.

name: protein-kmer-hash-selection
description: Use when clustering huge protein sequence sets (e.g. UniProt-sized FASTA) and you need a per-sequence subset of k-mers that still guarantees that homologous sequences share at least one exact k-mer match, without enumerating all k-mers.

name: protein-msa-generation
description: Use when starting from protein FASTA sequences that lack a supplied MSA and an MSA is required as input for DeepECA-style contact prediction, feature computation, or controlled noisy-MSA robustness tests.

name: protein-msa-sequence-weighting
description: Use when the goal is protein contact prediction from an MSA and MSA noise (e.g., metagenomic or noisy HHblits hits) may be degrading accuracy, and you want supervised, learned sequence weighting instead of fixed PSICOV-style weights.

name: protein-recovery-fold-change-analysis
description: Use when comparing protein sequence recovery of a protein-level assembler against nucleotide-level baselines on metagenomic reads, or when validating a manyfold recovery-improvement claim.

name: protein-redundancy-bin-scoring
description: Use when binning viral scaffolds into vMAGs from metagenomes and needing to pick the binning iteration among candidate weighted-network refinements based on protein redundancy rather than bacterial marker genes.

name: protein-redundancy-clustering
description: Use when constructing a reference protein database for functional annotation (e.g. DIAMOND/BLAST searches) from large multi-source FASTA sets where redundant near-identical sequences would inflate search space and ambiguity.

name: protein-redundancy-contamination-assessment
description: Use when scoring vRhyme bins for contamination: after running vRhyme on viral scaffolds, interpret vRhyme_bin_scoring.tsv redundant-protein counts per bin and select the iteration, then classify low- vs high-contamination vMAGs.

name: protein-secondary-structure-prediction-evaluation
description: Use when a protein secondary-structure/ASA predictor must be benchmarked against reference methods (e.g. RaptorX-Property, SCRATCH-1D) on CASP11/CASP12 target domains, or when training a multitask network that couples 2D contact feature maps with 1D structure predictions.

name: protein-sequence-backwards-search-implementation
description: Use when metagenomic reads must be classified at the protein level with inexact matching — e.g., when genera are underrepresented in the reference database and exact-match (MEM) classifiers miss too many reads.

name: protein-sequence-clustering
description: Use when given unannotated multi-FASTA protein input and the goal is de novo family determination via unsupervised clustering of AAR-kmer representations, e.g. reproducing nitrogen-cycle family separation at a 0.5 correlation threshold.

name: protein-sequence-clustering
description: Use when you have a set of assembled genomes (e.g. MAGs, fungal genomes, vOTUs) and need a non-redundant gene catalogue at a defined amino-acid identity threshold, or need to quantify catalogue-to-catalogue protein-space overlap.

name: protein-sequence-clustering
description: Use when a set of predicted viral proteins (e.g., from Prodigal on viral contigs) must be dereplicated into a non-redundant catalog prior to annotation with eggNOG-mapper, VOGDB, or DRAM-v.

name: protein-sequence-clustering
description: Use when a curated reference set of protein sequences for a functional gene (e.g., FunGene amoA-AOB) must be reduced to representative gene clusters before alignment to metagenomes or degenerate primer design.

name: protein-sequence-clustering-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing the runtime scalability, speed, or sensitivity of protein sequence clustering tools on large FASTA sets, or when reproducing power-law runtime exponents and false-negative rates at fixed sequence-identity thresholds (e.g. 50% or 90%).

name: protein-sequence-gene-clustering
description: Use when you have protein FASTA files (*.faa) for thousands of genomes (complete or MAGs/SAGs of mixed quality) and need gene clusters to feed a core/accessory genome analysis or other trait presence/absence computation.

name: protein-sequence-kmer-vectorization
description: Use when raw protein FASTA sequences must be converted to fixed-length feature representations for classification, clustering, or search, and you want to test whether amino acid recoding plus k-mering outperforms naive unencoded k-mer features.

name: protein-tertiary-structure-reconstruction-from-contacts
description: Use when you already have a per-domain list of predicted residue-pair contacts and predicted secondary structures and need to fold them into 3D models whose quality is measured by TMscore.

name: protein-to-metagenome-alignment
description: Use when you need to prioritize gene cluster representatives by environmental relevance — e.g., selecting which amoA-AOB clusters deserve primer design — from alignments of proteins against many metagenomes.

name: pseudo-genome-construction-from-representative-sequences
description: Use when you need to organize homologous genes from many annotated genomes into a taxonomy-aware set of pseudo-genomes before designing hybridization-capture probes at multiple taxonomic levels.

name: pseudomatching-length-computation
description: Use when classifying base-called sequencing reads against a large, repetitive pan-genome index in streaming mode, and per-position matching statistics (or the related PMLs) are needed faster than MONI's batch MS-finding allows.

name: pseudomatching-length-online-querying
description: Use when reads must be classified against a large, repetitive multi-strain reference in streaming/online fashion, and batch MS-finding (MONI) is too slow or unsuited to streaming input.

name: psicov-frequency-covariance-computation
description: Use when a target protein FASTA must be converted into the covariance-tensor feature representation (441 channels of LxL matrices) required as direct DNN input by DeepECA/DeepCov-style contact predictors.

name: publication-ready-figure-export
description: Use when a time-series multi-omics dataset (e.g., BWWTP Example 1 metagenomics depth-of-coverage or physico-chemical Processed data set 1) has been explored in MOVIS and a reproducible, publication-quality figure must be produced and exported.

name: purine-biosynthesis-gene-functional-annotation
description: Use when a clade of MAGs/SGBs (e.g. Saccharofermentanales SGB009, SGB034, SGB080) may lack a conserved set of universal single-copy orthologs and you need to identify which missing USCO genes map to a specific pathway such as de novo purine biosynthesis.

name: pvalue-inflation-qq-plot-assessment
description: Use when case-control metagenomic association summary statistics (sumstats_*.txt) must be checked for P-value inflation and the correct number of PC covariates (e.g. N_PC_PHYL = 2) must be chosen before final reporting.

name: python-report-generator-implementation
description: Use when a pipeline's bioinformatics outputs (plots, tables, networks, Markdown text, HTML components) must be turned into an interactive Streamlit web application driven by a structured YAML configuration of sections, subsections, and component objects.

name: python-script-based-alignment-filtering
description: Use when you have FASTA/FASTQ reads already flagged as containing inverted terminal repeats (with LCoord/RCoord ITR positions from pal-MEM) and need to keep only those whose flanking genomic context maps to assemblies within the expected IS length range (e.g. 500-3000 bp).

name: pytorch-model-training-and-testing
description: Use when a labeled microbial feature table (OTU/species abundance table plus sample metadata) must be classified with a phylogeny-aware deep learning model whose features are ordered by hierarchical clustering of phylogenetic distances.

name: pytorch-transformer-encoder-implementation
description: Use when a hybrid sequence classifier needs a from-scratch transformer pathway over BPE-tokenized DNA (512-token inputs) whose output is fused with CNN features, rather than fine-tuning a pre-trained language model.

name: q-matrix-interactive-visualization
description: Use when ADMIXTURE runs over a range of K values have produced per-run Q-matrix and log files, and you need to select the K with the lowest cross-validation error and interactively visualize ancestry proportions per sample.

name: qc3c-kmer-mode-ligation-quality-assessment
description: Use when you have cleaned Hi-C paired-end FASTQ reads (no reference assembly yet) and need a reference-free metric of Hi-C ligation/library quality, such as the inter-contig 3D ratio.

name: qiime2-artifact-format-conversion
description: Use when a reconstructed SSU sequences FASTA (e.g. metagenome_SSU_sequences.fasta from RiboTaxa's EMIRGE/MetaRib assembly) must be converted into a QIIME 2 .qza artifact before classify-sklearn classification.

name: qiime2-classifier-inference
description: Use when raw or denoised 16S rRNA amplicon representative sequences need taxonomic assignment under multiple reference databases (Greengenes, SILVA, NCBI RefSeq) to compare predicted vs. expected taxonomic compositions, e.g. on mock community benchmark data from Zenodo record 7051556.

name: qiime2-classify-sklearn-configuration
description: Use when reconstructed or clustered SSU rRNA FASTA sequences (e.g. EMIRGE/MetaRib output from metagenomics reads) must be assigned taxonomy down to genus/species level via a naive-Bayes trained classifier.

name: qiime2-feature-classifier-workflow
description: Use when full-length or near-full-length SSU rRNA sequences (e.g. 97%-clustered reconstructions in SSU_sequences.fasta) need taxonomic lineages plus per-sequence relative abundance from metagenomic reads.

name: qiime2-naive-bayes-classifier-training
description: Use when benchmarking 16S rRNA taxonomic classifiers on a common reference database (e.g. Greengenes2 2024.09 FASTA) and a held-out test set, to obtain a naive-Bayes baseline comparable to DADA2, SINTAX, and Kraken 2.

name: qiita-data-retrieval-and-comparison
description: Use when raw 16S rRNA reads for a QIITA-hosted study (e.g. ID 10508) must be retrieved, reprocessed into feature/taxonomy/tree files, and compared against deposited processed data.

name: qpcr-total-abundance-correction
description: Use when qPCR-derived total microbial abundance must be combined with a 16S rRNA amplicon profile and the qPCR numbers need correcting for lineage-specific 16S rRNA gene copy number bias.

name: qq-plot-pvalue-diagnostics-interpretation
description: Use when a user has run or plans mbQTL Approach A (linear regression taxa-SNP testing) and needs to assess overall model performance/inflation of the estimated P values before interpreting associations.

name: quadratic-baseline-runtime-benchmarking
description: Use when you have implemented an optimized sliding-window-minimum variant (e.g. fixed-window minL/minR in place) and need runtime comparisons against the naive per-window recomputation baseline over growing input arrays.

name: quadratic-programming-optimization
description: Use when computing convex hull distances for high-dimensional metagenomic contig feature vectors requires solving min_w (-2 Q^T P w + w^T P^T P w) s.t. e^T w = 1, w >= 0 via a QP solver.

name: quality-mask-region-annotation
description: Use when you have PANDAseq per-correction records plus original FASTQ quality strings and need to quantify how many mismatched bases were quality-masked by upstream (CASAVA) processing rather than genuinely conflicting.

name: quality-masked-region-scoring
description: Use when reproducing or auditing PANDAseq assembly quality scores from CASAVA FASTQ pairs, or when explaining why assemblies with mismatches in quality-masked overlap regions fail a quality-threshold accept/discard check.

name: quality-metric-aggregation-and-tabulation
description: Use when you have per-contig quality assessments (e.g., CheckV complete/high/medium/low/partial/provirus calls) for vOTU sets from two or more datasets and need aggregated tier counts to explain differences in predicted viral richness.

name: quality-metric-distribution-reproduction
description: Use when a paper reports counts of genomes in quality tiers (e.g. medium-quality/high-quality/near-complete) and you must independently recompute and verify those counts from the deposited genome FASTAs.

name: quality-profile-error-masking
description: Use when you need a controlled paired-end benchmark with known truth sequences but realistic, position-dependent Illumina error structure (e.g. to validate an assembler like PANDAseq).

name: quality-score-log-likelihood-scoring
description: Use when predicting genes on error-prone short reads (454/Sanger with indels, Illumina with substitutions) where per-base quality values are available and frame shifts must be tolerated rather than treated as true stop codons.

name: quality-stratified-mapping-visualization
description: Use when evaluating a HiFi metagenome assembly where bins have CheckM2 quality scores, and you need mapping ratios resolved to the highest bin quality level each read touches.

name: quantile-based-candidate-genome-filtering
description: Use when a MetaCacheSpark query yields a candidate genome list with spurious hits (e.g. shared conserved regions inflating hit counts) and reads must be assigned only to genuinely covered references, as in the all-food-sequencing KLyo_C sample.

name: quantitative-claim-verification-from-tables
description: Use when a paper asserts one pipeline outperforms others on a count-based metric (e.g. total reads retained) and the supporting numbers are available in a benchmark table that can be re-tabulated, ranked, and cross-checked row by row.

name: quartile-summary-statistics-verification
description: Use when a published benchmark summary statistic (e.g. mean or quartile gain over baselines) must be independently recomputed and verified from per-dataset evaluation tables such as Quast/metaQuast genome-fraction reports.

name: quarto-markdown-report-authoring
description: Use when a bioinformatics pipeline's output files (plots, tables, networks, Markdown text, HTML components) must be assembled into a static document or presentation whose structure is declared in a YAML configuration file.

name: quast-assembly-quality-metrics
description: Use when comparing contig sets from multiple metagenome assemblers against a known reference (strain genomes) and you need Quast metrics such as genome fraction, N50, NGA50 and Error Rate for benchmark tables.

name: quast-genome-fraction-metric-computation
description: Use when benchmarking plasmid (or bacterial) assemblies against a curated ground truth and you need QUAST accuracy metrics — genome fraction, mismatches/indels per 100 kbp — plus counts of missed and fragmented plasmids.

name: quast-metrics-table-parsing
description: Use when FASTA contig files from multiple genome assemblers (e.g. ABySS, Velvet, SPAdes, MEGAHIT) must be compared reference-free, and the QUAST report.tsv metrics table must be extracted and validated.

name: quast-tsv-report-parsing
description: Use when you have one or more genome assemblies (FASTA contigs) to evaluate against a reference genome (e.g., E. coli K-12 MG1655 NC_000913.3) and need machine-parseable metrics to compare assemblers.

name: query-coverage-accuracy-evaluation
description: Use when evaluating how completely Patchwork (or a DIAMOND-based pipeline) recovered reference markers, e.g. quantifying whether disabling tantan masking improves query coverage for read-based inputs.

name: query-throughput-calculation
description: Use when benchmarking read classifiers and you must normalize query wall-clock times into MR/m so that tools run on different databases or hardware can be compared fairly.

name: r-based-annotation-summary-analysis
description: Use when you have aggregated MG-RAST (or DIAMOND) annotation summary files (organism or functional) from one or more metatranscriptome samples and need statistical significance testing, abundance ranking, or graphical/tabular summaries in R.

name: r-based-genomic-report-generation
description: Use when you have one or more SARS-CoV-2 VCF files from NGS sequencing of wastewater (or clinical) samples and need to assign lineage-characteristic mutations and infer lineage distributions over sampling time periods.

name: r-bioconductor-figure-generation
description: Use when you have a trimmed taxa-SNP rho correlation table (e.g. taxa_SNP_Cor_lim) from mbQTL and need a heatmap figure to visually identify correlated SNV blocks such as LD regions.

name: r-bioconductor-package-execution
description: Use when a taxa-by-sample abundance table must be converted into a square taxa–taxa correlation (R) matrix with per-pair R² goodness-of-fit values as preprocessing for mbQTL rho estimation.

name: r-bioconductor-package-workflow
description: Use when analyzing sparse OTU/marker-gene count matrices from two or more sample groups to detect differentially abundant features while accounting for normalization and under-sampling of microbial communities.

name: r-bioconductor-package-workflow
description: Use when you have SARS-CoV-2 VCF files (e.g., from freebayes variant calling of ARTIC wastewater NGS data) and need to detect lineage-characteristic mutations and infer lineage abundances in R.

name: r-data-frame-annotation-wrangling
description: Use when you hold a DA results table (feature IDs are KO terms or KEGG pathway IDs) from ggpicrust2/PICRUSt2 output and need pathway name, description, class, and map fields joined onto each row.

name: r-example-data-loading-and-manipulation
description: Use when you have a PICRUSt2-format KO abundance table in R and need to load example data or aggregate KO ortholog-level abundances into KEGG pathway-level abundances for downstream analysis.

name: r-function-pipeline-execution
description: Use when the analysis plan is expressed as a sequence of named R package functions with specific parameters (e.g. MegaR's getLevelData/getGoodfeature) and the deliverables are per-run output files written from an R session.

name: r-package-example-data-execution
description: Use when verifying an R package installation with shipped example datasets, or reproducing the LongDat vignette workflow before applying the pipeline to new longitudinal count/proportion/binary/ordinal/continuous data.

name: r-package-plotting
description: Use when you have run ProgPermute's bin_permute_all on a binary grouping factor and need to visualize whether top hits from the original data show a decreasing -log10 p-value trend across permutation scenarios.

name: r-raster-stack-processing
description: Use when raster time-series stacks (e.g. multi-date Sentinel-1 gamma_0 GeoTIFFs) must be read in R and summarised into per-pixel statistics or neighborhood texture metrics (GLCM contrast/dissimilarity, orderliness/entropy) for habitat-structure mapping.

name: r-score-gene-prioritization
description: Use when a set of gene cluster representatives must be prioritized by how abundant and widespread they are across user-defined reference metagenomes, e.g. to select which gene clusters to target with primers.

name: r-statistical-programming
description: Use when implementing or reproducing the AMAT microbiome multivariate association pipeline (DC-based feature screening plus adaptive GLM-based testing) from simulated or real OTU count matrices with an outcome vector, in R.

name: r-statistical-programming-spatial-data
description: Use when computing plot-mean structural metrics (e.g. over 1-ha plots) from Sentinel-1 VH/VV gamma_0 temporal stacks in R, or when statistically comparing radar- and ALS-derived habitat structure via canonical correlation analysis.

name: r-visualization-of-accuracy-curves
description: Use when per-subsample accuracy results for high-, medium-, and low-abundance transcript classes have been computed across sequencing depths and need to be plotted to determine the minimum annotated-read depth (5-10M) exceeding 90% accuracy.

name: radar-fixed-effects-model-prediction
description: Use when you have a fitted radar biodiversity model and must predict assemblage composition (NMDS1) on plots outside the five training regions, then externally validate against observed ordination scores.

name: random-case-control-data-splitting
description: Use when validating that a differential abundance test on real microbiome relative abundance data (e.g. 16S taxa tables from the Bangladesh cohort) controls false positive rates by permuting artificial group labels under the null of no group effect.

name: random-effects-meta-analysis
description: Use when combining K>=10 studies across multiple related markers (e.g., 6 alpha-diversity indices) from summary statistics only — effect estimates and standard errors — with no prior correlation or full-data access.

name: random-effects-meta-analysis-of-taxa-estimates
description: Use when you have comparable per-study differential taxa comparison results (estimates + standard errors from GAMLSS-BEZI taxa.compare) from ≥2 microbiome studies and need pooled overall effects and heterogeneity across studies.

name: random-effects-meta-analysis-pvalue-computation
description: Use when you have study-specific regression coefficients and standard errors (effect estimates + SEs) for ≥10 studies across multiple related markers, and need p-values that avoid the over-conservatism of traditional random effects meta-analysis.

name: random-forest-model-training
description: Use when a two-class or multi-class phenotype classification model must be built from a merged MetaPhlAn table or QIIME/BIOM OTU table plus metadata (e.g. T1D t/f labels), and RF accuracy must be tuned and validated.

name: random-forest-phenotype-classification
description: Use when classifying metagenomic samples into phenotype classes (e.g., T2D, cirrhosis, T1D) from merged MetaPhlAn or QIIME/BIOM taxonomic profile tables with matching tab-separated metadata, and a robust RF-based accuracy estimate is needed.

name: random-genome-subset-sampling
description: Use when you need to validate whether a core-genome prediction quality estimate (e.g. mOTUpan --boots false-positive rate) reliably predicts true accuracy, especially for MAGs of varying completeness.

name: random-survival-forest-modeling
description: Use when the goal is to predict a survival (time-to-event) response from compositional microbiome predictors — e.g., ranking microbial genera by variable importance and verifying out-of-bag error convergence by 10,000 ensembled trees.

name: range-doppler-orthorectification
description: Reference for geolocating Sentinel-1 GRDH (IW) pixels: input is still in slant-range image coordinates after terrain flattening and must be orthorectified before analysis or compositing.

name: rank-based-inverse-normal-transformation
description: Use when gene-level (functional) abundance values from metagenomic shotgun profiling are skewed/non-normal and must be transformed before case-control MWAS association testing, as done in OMARU's profiling stage.

name: rank-wise-lowest-common-ancestor-assignment
description: Use when improved viral contigs must be taxonomically classified with per-contig scores and LCA ranks, especially for low-coverage or divergent viruses where single -hit assignment is unreliable.

name: ranked-abundance-summary-aggregation
description: Use when you have raw per-read DIAMOND annotation output from SAMSA2 (metatranscriptome reads annotated against local DIAMOND-indexed RefSeq or SEED Subsystems databases) and need ranked feature-abundance tables per sample.

name: ranked-list-comparison-to-supplementary-table
description: Use when a trained linear SVM phenotype model must be inspected or its feature ranking reproduced and checked against a published table, e.g. verifying that trait absence rather than gene presence drives prediction.

name: rare-species-prevalence-stratification
description: Use when per-sample shotgun sequencing is shallow and you need to verify that genome cover plateaus (saturates) for rare or low-prevalence taxa once coverage is composited across like samples from the same environment.

name: raster-stack-temporal-analysis-in-r
description: Use when you have temporal stacks of geocoded Sentinel-1 gamma_0 rasters (VH and VV) plus acquisition dates, and need per-pixel seasonal/temporal summary statistics for downstream ecological modelling.

name: raster-vector-plot-extraction
description: Use when Sentinel-1 gamma_0 summary rasters must be sampled at field-plot center locations (e.g. ALB_example_plots.* shapefile) to derive plot-level means or validate them against reference values such as S1_mean.csv.

name: raw-signal-adaptive-quantization
description: Use when you need to convert raw Oxford Nanopore electrical signals (FAST5, POD5, SLOW5, BLOW5) into deterministic hash values for real-time hash-based mapping or overlap search, and signal-to-signal variability must not change the hash for the same DNA content.

name: rdp-taxonomic-annotation-16s
description: Use when raw 16S rRNA amplicon reads need taxonomic annotation via RDP classification with ChimeraSlayer chimera removal, to yield a taxonomy table compatible with an OTU count table and Newick tree.

name: read-alignment-against-multiple-reference-genomes
description: Use when reproducing or benchmarking the original alignment-based AFS pipeline on food metagenomics samples (e.g. KAL_D, Kal/KLyo on the AFS10 reference set), or when establishing the runtime/accuracy baseline that AFS-MetaCache is compared to.

name: read-alignment-based-variant-writing
description: Use when simulating within-strain short-term evolutionary mutations in longitudinal (multi-time-point) simulated raw sequencing reads and a ground-truth mutation record (VCF) is needed for benchmarking.

name: read-alignment-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing read-classification accuracy (F1, precision, recall) of a fast classifier like SPUMONI against an aligner like minimap2 across reference index compositions (target strain present vs excluded) on simulated or real nanopore reads.

name: read-alignment-ground-truth-generation
description: Use when a simulated metagenomic dataset with known reference genomes (e.g. Sim50, Sim100, CAMI2 UG) has been assembled into contigs and you need per-contig truth labels to evaluate binning tools with AMBER.

name: read-alignment-statistics-computation
description: Use when preprocessing paired-end FASTQ metatranscriptome reads with Trimmomatic + FLASh and you need to quantify the merged-read fraction and average merged read length before annotation submission.

name: read-classification-hypothesis-testing
description: Use when you must decide, from a streaming read prefix (FASTQ/base-called nanopore reads), whether a read belongs to a target set versus random chance, and a compressed pan-genome index is preferable to full alignment.

name: read-count-quantification-per-sample
description: Use when raw paired-end FASTQ metatranscriptome reads must be reduced to per-sample counts of reads matching a reference genome (e.g., host/human) to test whether host transcriptomes are recoverable.

name: read-depth-normalization
description: Use when comparing case-control metagenomic diversity (alpha or beta) across samples whose read depths differ, e.g. T2D (n=171) or SCZ (n=344) fecal metagenomes, prior to Shannon/Bray-Curtis computation.

name: read-identity-filtered-coverage-quantification
description: Use when viral scaffolds (e.g., VIBRANT/VirSorter predictions) must be quantified from read alignment data to build the coverage table that vRhyme consumes for single- or multi-sample coverage effect size comparisons between scaffolds.

name: read-mapping-based-contaminant-screening
description: Use when retained reads after host decontamination show unexpectedly high human retention (e.g. NA12878 0.641% vs 0.406%) and a recurring contaminant such as EBV is suspected across a genome set.

name: read-mapping-based-genome-comparison
description: Use when you need accurate strain-level genome similarity (ANI) between genomes across metagenomic samples — e.g. benchmarking genome comparison accuracy or detecting shared strains — from read mappings rather than raw assemblies.

name: read-mapping-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when comparing mapping accuracy or throughput of raw-signal nanopore mappers against a reference genome, or when validating that a new mapper's precision/recall matches published orderings on datasets spanning small to large genomes.

name: read-mapping-coverage-calculation
description: Use when viral scaffolds (e.g. from VIBRANT or VirSorter prediction) from one or more metagenomes need coverage abundance features before binning scaffolds into vMAGs with vRhyme.

name: read-mapping-ratio-computation
description: Use when evaluating a metagenome assembly by measuring what fraction of HiFi reads and read bases align to contigs, especially when the breakdown should be stratified by bin quality (near complete/high/medium/low/unbinned).

name: read-mapping-statistics-qc
description: Use when shotgun reads have been mapped back to de novo MAG clusters (e.g. VAMB bins via MAGinator) and you must QC mapping depth/allele-frequency statistics to flag MAG clusters with mixed strains per sample or environment.

name: read-overlap-computation
description: Use when a short-read metagenome assembly or clustering pipeline needs pairwise read overlaps with identity and overlap-length scores, e.g. to build overlap graphs for strain-aware (haplotype-aware) OLC assembly.

name: read-pair-nucleotide-identity-calculation
description: Use when filtering mapped metagenomic reads before SNV calling or coverage profiling, and you must discard read pairs whose alignment to the reference .fasta falls below a user-defined minimum nucleotide identity.

name: read-pair-overlap-scoring
description: Use when a metagenomic assembly needs its initial divide step: you have interleaved Illumina FASTQ reads from a complex community and must partition them into small clusters that each correspond roughly to one species before local/global assembly.

name: read-prefix-length-quantification
description: Use when comparing adaptive/real-time nanopore signal mappers (RawHash, UNCALLED, Sigmap) on how early each stops sequencing a mapped read, i.e., estimating time and cost via read-prefix lengths and chunk counts from PAF records.

name: read-retention-benchmarking-across-tools
description: Use when comparing host read removal tools on the same human sequencing data (Illumina paired-end or ONT FASTQ) and you need a quantitative per-tool retained/removed read proportion table to benchmark decontamination stringency.

name: read-sequence-statistics-extraction
description: Use when raw metagenomic reads arrive as SRA archives and need conversion to FASTQ/FASTA plus per-sample QC reports and sequence statistics before mapping to gene catalogs.

name: read-simulation-with-hiseq-error-profile
description: Use when benchmarking a SNP/INDEL caller on synthetic data with a known ground truth: you need reads simulated from a bi-allelic genome (e.g. Human chromosome 1 at 30x, HiSeq error profile) instead of real reads with an approximated truth set.

name: read-subset-expansion-parameter-tuning
description: Use when running CasCollect on raw paired-end FASTQ data and you need to decide how many expansion cycles or what identity threshold will yield sufficient read coverage of a target CRISPR/Cas locus without redundant searching.

name: read-type-aware-tool-gating
description: Use when building or modifying an nf-core/mag (Nextflow DSL2) workflow that mixes short-read, long-read, and hybrid metagenomic data and each module must be routed only to the read types it supports.

name: real-time-mapping-behavior-analysis
description: Use when comparing how early competing real-time raw-signal mappers stop sequencing a read (bases sequenced per read) or how many signal chunks they consume per read, to estimate adaptive-sampling time/cost benefits.

name: real-time-mapping-stopping-evaluation
description: Use when a task asks to quantify estimation accuracy of relative abundance from truncated or subsampled nanopore signal read sets, or to measure the fraction of reads a real-time mapper consumes before safe early run termination (Sequence Until).

name: reciprocal-best-hit-ortholog-merging
description: Use when a non-redundant gene/protein catalog needs to be grouped into orthologous families using Jaccard similarity clustering followed by reciprocal--hit merging of clusters.

name: recombination-rate-stratified-gene-comparison
description: Use when testing complex hypotheses that require comparing selective regimes (α, adaptive/neutral/deleterious fractions) of a user-selected gene set — e.g. defined by recombination rate bins or chromosome localization — against the whole-genome distribution.

name: reconstruction-accuracy-delta-computation
description: Use when comparing HGT local-strain reconstruction methods (LEMON vs LUMPY) on simulated metagenomic reads at multiple coverage levels to verify that graph-based reconstruction outperforms split-read-only methods.

name: recursive-overlap-layout-candidate-assembly
description: Use when de novo metagenomic assembly (e.g., MetaSPAdes) yields seed contigs of only a few kb that need extension using raw sequencing reads, and contig accuracy must be preserved (e.g., >98% BLAST alignment to a reference viral genome).

name: reduced-amino-acid-alphabet-encoding
description: Use when building a k-mer prefilter for protein sequence clustering or search where alphabet reduction plus lowest-hash k-mer selection must keep the index linear in input size N.

name: redundancy-filtering-parameter-verification
description: Use when a downloaded or rebuilt Plass protein catalog (SRC or MERC FASTA) must be checked against published sequence counts, source-sample counts, and the 90%/90% redundancy-reduction parameters.

name: reference-based-assembly-evaluation
description: Use when benchmarking de novo metagenomic assembly performance on a defined mock community where complete reference genomes/replicons are known and per-reference accuracy, contiguity, and completeness metrics are required.

name: reference-based-contiguity-assessment
description: Use when benchmarking metagenomic de novo assemblies against a known mock community and you need a per-replicon measure of contig contiguity (single-alignment coverage of a reference, not NGA50/total coverage).

name: reference-based-genome-assembly-alignment
description: Use when a gold-standard or close reference genome (e.g., E. coli K-12 MG1655, NC_000913.3) is available and multiple assemblies must be compared on structural errors and per-base accuracy.

name: reference-based-misassembly-detection
description: Use when assembled contig FASTA files and a reference genome (true or close, e.g. W3110 for E. coli K-12) are available and you need misassembly counts, NGA50, genome fraction or duplication ratio to compare assemblies.

name: reference-based-vcf-generation
description: Use when reference-free variant calls exist as .snp files (ebwt2InDel output) and a reference genome assembly (e.g. hg38) is available, so variants must be converted to .vcf with reference coordinates.

name: reference-catalogue-benchmarking
description: Use when a new reference gene/genome catalogue (e.g. VMGC-90) must be quantitatively compared against a prior catalogue (e.g. VIRGO) using read-mapping rates over a shared, publicly available metagenomic sample set.

name: reference-database-indexing
description: Use when constructing taxonomic classification indices from large reference collections (e.g. NCBI RefSeq .fna/.faa sets) or when comparing the build cost of indexing tools across tool/database/parameter combinations.

name: reference-database-indexing
description: Use when preparing a local reference protein database (RefSeq, SEED Subsystems, or a custom FASTA) for DIAMOND-based read annotation in SAMSA2, with no external web service.

name: reference-database-integration
description: Use when viral or microbial genomes from a custom catalogue need taxonomic typing against an external reference database, and/or a combined catalogue+reference phylogeny of a marker gene (e.g., L1) is required.

name: reference-database-otu-sequence-retrieval
description: Use when PM-CNN input is an OTU abundance table lacking a phylogeny and you must obtain representative marker-gene (amplicon) sequences for each OTU before multiple sequence alignment and FastTree tree inference.

name: reference-database-preparation-for-viral-identification
