description: Reference for preparing the required -v (viral) and -nv (nonviral) protein FASTA databases before running virMine 2.0, when the inputFiles folder of the cloned repository lacks viral_aa.fasta and nonviral_aa.fasta.

name: reference-database-preprocessing-for-otu-annotation
description: Use when a 16S reference database FASTA (Greengenes or SILVA) must be prepared for CD-HIT-OTU-Miseq / CDSnake OTU assignment, or when cluster representatives must be matched to the most specific available taxonomy lineages.

name: reference-free-assembly-evaluation
description: Use when no reference genome is available and multiple assemblies (e.g., FASTA contigs from ABySS, Velvet, SPAdes, MEGAHIT) must be compared on contiguity and completeness metrics.

name: reference-genome-alignment-evaluation
description: Use when one or more genome assemblies (FASTA contigs) need reference-based quality assessment, or when quantifying how evaluation metrics change when a close-reference genome is substituted for the true reference.

name: reference-genome-database-preparation
description: Use when a pipeline step requires a pre-built reference index (e.g., Bowtie 2 index of hs37d5 for host read removal) and the reference FASTA/index must be downloaded and prepared before annotation can start.

name: reference-genome-fragmentation
description: Use when comparing conspecific microbial strains across metagenomic assemblies or genomes with SynTracker and you need homologous genomic regions binned per sample from a single reference genome.

name: reference-genome-selection
description: Use when building a reduced, non-redundant species-level reference gene database (pan-genomes) from thousands of complete genomes to support gene prediction model selection on metagenomic contigs.

name: reference-position-mapping
description: Use when variant calls or gene features exist in colored de Bruijn graph node coordinates (nodepos plus bubid/basecolor tri-tuples) and must be converted to reference-genome positions for comparison with linear annotations like GTF files or VCFs.

name: reference-replicon-alignment-analysis
description: Use when evaluating de novo metagenomic assemblies against defined mock communities: you have assembled contigs (FASTA) and reference replicons and need per-contig alignment identity plus a Phred-like Pls quality score per assembler.

name: region-grouped-cross-validation
description: Use when evaluating biodiversity or ecological predictive models fitted to spatially clustered plots from a few study regions, to prevent spatial leakage between training and test folds.

name: relative-abundance-accuracy-assessment
description: Use when planning metatranscriptome sequencing or judging whether a sample's depth suffices for accurate abundance measurement, especially of low-abundance transcripts in gut microbiome mRNA data.

name: relative-abundance-computation-metagenomics
description: Use when you need relative abundances for reconstructed full-length SSU rRNA sequences from metagenomics data: map reads with BBMap, sum counts within 97% VSEARCH clusters, and report percent abundances.

name: relative-abundance-estimation-from-read-mappings
description: Use when a mock community is pooled from FAST5 read sets and raw signals must be mapped to a combined multi-genome reference to obtain per-genome relative abundance estimates and compare their accuracy to ground truth.

name: relative-abundance-normalization
description: Use when you have reconstructed full-length SSU rRNA sequences (e.g. metagenome_SSU_sequences.fasta from EMIRGE/MetaRib) plus the original quality-controlled reads and need per-sequence relative abundances for taxonomic profiling.

name: relative-abundance-table-filtering
description: Use when a relative abundance table (taxonomy levels l2–l6, e.g. Bangladesh taxtab.rm[[5]]) contains rare taxa that would destabilize downstream GAMLSS-BEZI differential abundance testing or clutter phylum-level mean plots.

name: relative-percentage-gain-computation
description: Use when a benchmark table reports a per-dataset quality metric (e.g., genome fraction) for a new method and several baselines, and the goal is to quantify how much the new method exceeds the baseline per dataset and across all datasets.

name: relaxed-precision-recall-f1-evaluation
description: Use when a text-mining or information-extraction pipeline produces a character matrix (or equivalent structured extractions) that must be scored against a hand-curated gold standard, especially when per-character precision/recall/F1 and component ablations are needed.

name: repeated-cross-validation-accuracy-estimation
description: Use when a binary phenotypic trait model (e.g. obligate intracellular vs free-living) trained on COG presence/absence vectors must be validated with a robust, replicate-averaged accuracy estimate rather than a single train/test split.

name: repeated-kfold-cross-validation-evaluation
description: Use when two or more sequence variant calling methods (e.g., HashSeq vs. DADA2) must be compared for downstream association performance on the same microbiota data set, requiring cross-validated classifier metrics per caller per metadata variable.

name: repeated-timing-measurement-averaging
description: Use when quantifying the runtime scaling of CATHAI's graph-generation/plotting pipeline against sample count (n), e.g. to reproduce the timing-versus-sample-count benchmark table or to decide the maximum sample size for usable operation.

name: reported-count-verification
description: Use when a paper reports summary statistics (counts of items above thresholds) over a per-item results table — such as the Traitar Table S2 macroaccuracy table for 67 GIDEON phenotypes — and you must verify the reported numbers against the raw data.

name: reported-result-reproducibility-check
description: Use when a source card reports specific numeric findings (e.g. alpha mean 0.633 ± SD 0.028 for 475 high-recombination genes) that must be independently reproduced from pre-calculated polymorphism/divergence tables using a named tool.

name: reported-vs-computed-statistics-comparison
description: Use when a paper reports a concrete quantitative outcome (cluster count, runtime, input size) and the underlying dataset or pipeline is re-accessible, so the reported figure can be independently recomputed and compared.

name: representative-sequence-distribution-comparison
description: Use when comparing 16S DC methods (DADA2, Deblur, de novo, closed/open-reference) by measuring how accurately each predicted feature table recapitulates a known mock-community composition via weighted UniFrac.

name: representative-sequence-sampling
description: Use when you need to estimate how many clusterable sequence pairs a clustering tool misses (false-negative rate) on a protein set too large (e.g. 123M UniProt sequences) for exhaustive pairwise verification.

name: reproducible-random-seed-sampling
description: Use when averaging per-region pairwise synteny scores into APSS matrices over all sample pairs and runs must be reproducible despite random subsampling of regions.

name: residual-dnn-contact-prediction-training
description: Use when you need to train (or retrain) an end-to-end DNN contact predictor from an MSA, e.g. reproducing the DeepECA Baseline Model rows of the CASP11/CASP12 precision tables.

name: residual-sum-of-squares-accuracy-evaluation
description: Use when a synthetic dataset with known OTU composition is available and you need to score how faithfully different amplicon pipelines (MICCA, QIIME, UPARSE, mothur) reproduce true relative abundances.

name: resistance-genotype-concordance-assessment
description: Use when you have Mykrobe predictor JSON output for an M. tuberculosis sample and need to independently re-derive susceptible/minor/major genotype calls and measure per-site concordance with Mykrobe's emitted calls.

name: resource-usage-profiling
description: Use when you need to reproduce or verify reported computational resource requirements (wall-clock time, peak RAM) of running a tool like DiSCo per genome on a standard laptop rather than on HPC infrastructure.

name: resource-usage-profiling
description: Use when you need to quantify how a pipeline scales with input size, e.g. measuring wall-clock time and peak memory for graph construction and analysis at 5,000 vs 20,000 genomes.

name: retraining-delta-quantification
description: Use when comparing Glimmer-MG's initial gene predictions (models parameterized after Phymm phylogenetic classification) against its final predictions (after Scimm clustering and retraining) to measure the accuracy gain from the retraining step.

name: reverse-complement-verification-blastn
description: Use when converting Palidis candidate ITR pairs into predicted insertion sequences and you need cluster-concordance plus reverse-complement evidence that the flanking repeat pair is a genuine ITR.

name: ribodepletion-efficiency-comparison
description: Use when a pair of metatranscriptome samples (ribodepleted vs. non-ribodepleted, e.g. MG-RAST samples 4015 vs. 4012) must be compared to assess whether rRNA depletion is taxonomically unbiased, or when residual rRNA reads might distort organism abundance estimates.

name: ribonuclease-h-domain-recognition
description: Use when candidate IS nucleotide sequences (e.g. ITR-flanked contigs from Palidis) must be confirmed as encoding transposase-family proteins before inclusion in an insertion sequence catalogue.

name: ribosomal-protein-inventory-annotation
description: Use when inventorying ribosomal protein complements across many draft/complete genome bins to test whether a supposedly universal protein (e.g. rpL30, rpL9, rpL1, Der) is truly absent from specific lineages.

name: ribosomal-rna-filtering
description: Use when raw or quality-trimmed metatranscriptome RNA-seq FASTQ reads still contain rRNA sequences that would waste annotation compute and dilute mRNA functional profiles.

name: ripp-identification-mode-comparison
description: Decision support for choosing a MetaMiner database-construction mode when RiPPs must be identified from spectra with paired genomic data and the analyst must weigh sensitivity for novel RiPPs (motif-ORF) against broader ORF enumeration (all-ORF) at strict FDR.

name: ripp-peptidogenomics-search
description: Use when paired mass spectrometry spectra and genome or metagenome assemblies are available and the goal is RiPP discovery by searching spectra against precursor peptide databases, e.g. ACTI/GNPS datasets like MSV000078839.
tools: GNPS (Global Natural Products Social molecular networking)

name: ripp-precursor-candidate-generation
description: Use when you have microbial (or metagenomic, assembled into contigs) nucleotide FASTA and need to enumerate putative RiPP precursor ORFs — either a small, high-confidence set (motif-ORF) or an exhaustive set (all-ORF) — for downstream peptide-spectrum matching.

name: ripp-precursor-database-construction
description: Use when paired genomic/metagenomic contigs and GNPS tandem MS spectra must be searched for RiPPs and a putative precursor peptide database (target plus shuffled decoy) needs to be built first.

name: ripp-target-decoy-database-construction
description: Use when searching tandem mass spectra against predicted RiPP structures and a calibrated FDR (e.g., a 1% identification threshold) must be estimated via a target-decoy strategy.

name: rle-bwt-backward-search
description: Use when classifying sequencing reads (e.g., nanopore reads) against a large, repetitive pan-genome reference and you need per-position matching statistics or PMLs computed in O(r) space with a streaming one-pass algorithm.

name: rmse-trajectory-accuracy-evaluation
description: Use when comparing two dynamical-system parameterizations (e.g., trained on denoised vs raw/pseudo-count abundances) by measuring RMSE of predicted versus observed community trajectories over time.

name: rna-seq-count-matrix-import
description: Use when the input is a raw/normalized RNA-seq count matrix (csv/txt, genes in rows or first column, one column per sample) and the goal is to run differential expression via DESeq2, optionally with a metadata table of experimental factors.

name: rnaseq-preprocessing
description: Use when per-sample HTSeq gene count files or Cufflinks-style gene FPKM files must be merged into one CSV count/FPKM matrix so downstream bulk RNA-seq apps (e.g., DESeq2Shiny) can consume them.

name: roc-auc-evaluation
description: Use when you need to benchmark a differential abundance method's classification performance against a comparator on simulated taxa with known null/differential status, requiring ROC curves, AUC with 95% CI, and a DeLong test for correlated ROC curves.

name: roc-curve-analysis
description: Use when selecting or validating an overlap cutoff for read recruitment in TAR-VIR, or when you need an ROC/AUC justification that a sequence-similarity threshold separates within-quasispecies overlap from cross-species conservation.

name: roc-curve-performance-evaluation

name: rrna-alignment-gap-curation

name: rrna-insertion-prevalence-comparison

name: rrna-insertion-sequence-removal
description: Use when curating 16S rRNA genes that contain large insertion sequences (≥10 bp, up to 2,004 bp in this dataset) before multiple sequence alignment or phylogenetic tree building.

description: Use when working with publicly available non-ribodepleted metatranscriptomic data (e.

name: runtime-and-memory-measurement
description: Use when you must compare CPU time, memory peaks, and job runtimes of multiple MAG taxonomic classifiers on the same benchmark MAG sets and need a reproducible resource comparison table.

name: runtime-and-memory-profiling
description: Use when benchmarking a large reference database build or classification run — e.g. comparing partitioned vs. unpartitioned builds of the AFS31RS90 database across AFS-MetaCache partitions or MetaCacheSpark executor counts.

name: runtime-benchmark-tabulation
description: Use when comparing end-to-end or per-stage runtimes of two analysis pipelines on identical small input sets (e.g. five 50,000-sequence metatranscriptomes) to quantify a speed-up factor.

name: runtime-benchmarking-comparison
description: Use when a taxonomic classifier must be quantitatively validated against existing tools on mock or synthetic communities with known composition, requiring precision/recall/F-measure and runtime comparisons.

name: runtime-benchmarking-wallclock-timing
description: Use when a reproducibility task asks to confirm a published runtime claim for STEMSim, e.g. reproducing that one million reads are processed in approximately three minutes on a server with a 2.40 GHz CPU.

name: runtime-measurement-with-linux-time
description: Use when comparing the computational scalability or speed of clustering/search tools on large sequence sets, or when reproducing reported runtime scaling exponents and speedup factors.

name: runtime-memory-benchmark-profiling
description: Use when benchmarking taxonomic binning or profiling tools on the same read samples and databases and you need comparable per-tool runtime and peak-memory figures alongside F1-scores.

name: runtime-memory-profiling
description: Use when you need to verify that a machine-learning phenotype-prediction pipeline remains tractable in runtime and memory as training-set size and feature dimensionality (e.g. genomes x COGs) grow toward large-scale databases.

name: runtime-memory-profiling
description: Use when comparing the computational performance of two tools or implementations on identical inputs and settings, e.g. to verify a reported speedup or memory reduction for alignment-free dissimilarity calculation.

name: runtime-speedup-curve-visualization
description: Use when you need to determine the minimum CPU/RAM allocation at which an aligner or pipeline step reaches peak efficiency, e.g. before sizing cluster jobs for SAMSA2 DIAMOND annotation runs.

name: runtime-summary-statistics-aggregation
description: Use when benchmarking runs have recorded wall-clock time and max memory (e.g. from Zenodo-deposited run logs) and you need per-program, per-thread-count summary statistics and speedup ratios.

name: sam-bam-alignment-processing-and-sorting
description: Use when raw read alignments (SAM files from Bowtie2 or BWA-mem against a viral scaffold FASTA) must be converted, sorted, indexed, and parsed before computing per-scaffold coverage statistics.

name: sam-file-seed-read-processing
description: Use when you have a SAM file of reads already aligned to a partial or remotely related viral reference (seed reads) and need to recruit additional related reads from a larger metagenomic read set for strain reconstruction.

name: sam-to-vcf-variant-annotation
description: Use when a variant caller outputs reference-free calls (e.g. ebwt2InDel's .snp fasta) and a reference genome (e.g. hg38) is available, so calls must be expressed as coordinate-anchored .vcf entries for validation or downstream use.

name: sample-library-size-filtering
description: Use when a phyloseq OTU/feature table with uneven per-sample read depths must be QC-filtered before composition or survival analysis, and shallow samples (e.g., <3,000 reads) should be removed.

name: sample-metadata-schema-modeling
description: Use when building or restructuring a pre-sequencing sample metadata table (e.g. CSV of metagenomic samples) that must combine generic collection fields, DNA/RNA processing fields, and lab-specific custom fields, as MetaLIMS does.

name: sample-metadata-to-clarity-lims-field-mapping
description: Use when sample metadata is stored in MetaLIMS (MySQL/mysqli backend) and a sequencing facility requires a Clarity LIMS-compatible submission form derived from that metadata.

name: sample-pair-matrix-construction
description: Use when you have a raw per-region synteny score table (synteny_scores_per_region.csv) from SynTracker and need per-sample-pair APSS values at fixed subsampling lengths to build pairwise distance matrices or phylogenies.

name: sample-pca-visualization
description: Use when ranked abundance summary tables (organism or function counts) from SAMSA2's DIAMOND_analysis_counter.py step have been aggregated and you need a sample-level dimensionality-reduction plot to inspect control vs. experimental group separation.

name: samtools-bam-filtering
description: Use when raw FASTQ reads from shotgun metagenomic samples must be aligned to a reference database and sorted/filtered into .filtered.sorted.bam files before variant pileup with cellsnp-lite and MetaQuad.

name: sar-derived-habitat-structure-modelling
description: Use when modelling ground-truth alpha/beta diversity of forest taxa from per-plot Sentinel-1 gamma0 radar or ALS habitat-structure predictors, especially when comparing fixed-effects vs mixed-effects fits with the five forest regions as a random factor.

name: sar-gamma0-plot-summary-statistics
description: Use when you have Sentinel-1 gamma_0 temporal stacks (VH/VV GeoTIFFs), acquisition dates, and plot-center shapefiles and need per-plot radar structural metrics as predictors for ecological models (CCoA, NMDS composition models).

name: sar-gamma0-raster-analysis
description: Use when you have terrain-corrected Sentinel-1 gamma_0 backscatter stacks (e.g. GeoTIFFs such as ALB_gamma0_VH.tif / ALB_gamma0_VV.tif) and need raster variables describing horizontal (spatial) forest structure rather than per-pixel backscatter.

name: sar-radiometric-calibration-beta0
description: Use when Sentinel-1 GRDH IW data held as uncalibrated digital numbers (DN) must be converted to calibrated backscatter (beta_0) comparable across acquisitions and sensors, prior to terrain flattening to gamma_0.

name: sar-radiometric-terrain-flattening
description: Use when uncalibrated Sentinel-1 GRDH (IW) digital numbers have been radiometrically calibrated to beta_0 and must be normalized for terrain-induced backscatter distortion before orthorectification or time-series compositing.

name: sar-timeseries-median-compositing
description: Use when you have temporal stacks of Sentinel-1 gamma_0 VH/VV backscatter plus acquisition dates and need ecologically meaningful, speckle-reduced per-pixel summary rasters for habitat-structure analysis.

name: sars-cov-2-lineage-inference
description: Use when you have VCF files of low-frequency SARS-CoV-2 variants (e.g., from ARTIC-amplicon wastewater sequencing) and need to detect which lineages are present and estimate their relative abundance over time.

name: sars-cov-2-lineage-mutation-matching
description: Use when VCF variant calls from SARS-CoV-2 wastewater sequencing must be matched to a lineage's characteristic mutation set and summarized by allele-frequency metrics (e.g., minimum non-zero AF per time period).

name: sars-cov-2-vcf-variant-parsing
description: Use when input is one or more VCF variant-calling files from SARS-CoV-2 wastewater or clinical NGS data and the goal is to evaluate detected mutations against Pangolin/outbreak.info lineage-defining rules.

name: scaffold-breadth-metric-computation
description: Use when profiling genome populations from metagenomic read mappings and you need per-scaffold coverage, breadth (fraction of reference bases covered ≥1 read), and nucleotide diversity from sorted .bam files plus a reference .fasta.

name: scaffold-dereplication
description: Use when a viral scaffold FASTA contains redundant/duplicate sequences (e.g., multiple assemblies or fragmented genomes) and you need to collapse them pre-binning or investigate how vRhyme's composite merging joins scaffold pairs.

name: scaffold-gap-closing
description: Use when a draft scaffold FASTA contains unresolved N-wildcard gap regions and paired-end Illumina short reads are available to fill those gaps via local reassembly.

name: scaffold-pair-kmer-feature-distance-computation
description: Use when building labeled same/different scaffold-pair training data or reproducing vRhyme's supervised classifiers, which require nucleotide feature distance values (k-mer frequencies, GC content) as input features per pair.

name: scaled-weight-normalization-and-summing
description: Use when multiple network inference methods (e.g., 8 NI association matrices from correlation or direct-model tools) must be merged into one consensus co-occurrence network and edge weighting (not just vote counting) should drive edge selection.

name: scaling-exponent-analysis-of-clustering-tools
description: Use when benchmarking whether a sequence-clustering tool's wall-clock runtime grows linearly or quadratically with input set size N, or when reproducing published power-law runtime exponents at a fixed sequence-identity threshold.

name: scatterplot-visualization-of-cluster-properties
description: Use when you have run HashSeq's inferTrueSequences on 16S rRNA amplicon data and need to inspect childrenProperties.txt to set or validate an abundance threshold (e.g., 1,000 reads) above which the LOESS background error model fits well.

name: schizophrenia-mwas-target-gene-selection
description: Use when shotgun metagenome MWAS (e.g., SCZ vs. controls) has yielded significant disease-associated genes and you need a gene-to-taxon attribution by tracing sequencing reads back to their source organisms.

name: scientific-report-generation
description: Use when a pipeline or analysis has produced intermediate output files (plots, dataframes, networks, Markdown, HTML components) and a shareable report in a specific format must be generated from them with minimal coding.

name: scientific-table-reproduction
description: Reference for reproducing published benchmark/runtime tables (e.g., Table 2 of the CDSnake paper) when a task requires exact numeric values per pipeline per dataset, formatted as a machine-readable CSV with header and one row per dataset.

name: seasonal-backscatter-statistics-derivation
description: Use when temporal stacks of Sentinel-1 gamma_0 (VH and VV) plus an acquisition-dates table are available and you need pixel-based seasonal backscatter summaries (medians, differences, ratios) as forest-structure predictors.

name: seasonal-pattern-identification-in-omics-time-series
description: Use when a tabular time-series omics dataset with an embedded temporal feature (e.g., Herold et al. BWWTP metagenomics depth-of-coverage) should be screened for periodic or seasonal dynamics such as quartile envelopes tracing a sine-like curve.

name: secondary-structure-constraint-integration
description: Use when you have top-L residue contact lists and predicted secondary structures from a deep-learning contact predictor and need to build and score 3D protein models.

name: seed-based-read-subset-expansion
description: Use when raw Illumina paired-end FASTQ reads (isolate genomes or metagenomes) must be assembled around cas genes/CRISPR arrays without complete genome or metagenome assembly, e.g. when runtime or compute limits full metaSPAdes assembly.

name: seed-contig-generation-for-extension
description: Use when metagenomic reads need de novo-assembled seed contigs before a contig-extension step: input is adaptor-trimmed FASTQ and the downstream tool expects a FASTA seed contig set.

name: seed-read-subset-selection
description: Use when raw, unassembled Illumina sequencing reads must be reduced to a small seed-read subset matching cas proteins or CRISPR repeats before targeted assembly, especially for large or metagenomic datasets where full assembly is too slow.

name: seed-subsystems-hierarchy-parsing
description: Use when raw DIAMOND annotation output is line-by-line per-read text and you need condensed, descending-sorted organism or SEED Subsystems functional abundance tables for downstream statistics.

name: seen-unseen-sequence-stratification
description: Use when evaluating a taxonomic classifier's generalization to species not represented in its training label vocabulary, e.g. on Greengenes2 test sequences held out from training.

name: segmental-duplication-sequence-alignment

name: selection-trajectory-parameter-configuration

name: self-attention-mechanism-implementation
description: Use when implementing or reconstructing DeepMicrobes' Embed + LSTM + Attention species classifier: you have k-mer-embedded DNA reads and need a length-independent, attention-pooled representation for taxonomic classification.

name: sensitivity-fdr-computation
description: Use when evaluating breakpoint or structural-variant detection accuracy against known ground-truth positions from simulations, where sensitivity and FDR must be computed at multiple coverage levels (e.g. 2X, 5X, 70X).

name: sensitivity-precision-computation
description: Use when scoring gene-finder output (e.g. Glimmer-MG, FragGeneScan, MetaGeneMark predictions) on simulated metagenomic reads where true gene coordinates are known and per-condition sensitivity/precision must be tabulated by read technology and error rate.

name: sensitivity-specificity-benchmark-evaluation

name: sensitivity-specificity-calculation

name: sensitivity-specificity-threshold-optimization

name: sentinel-1-sar-preprocessing

name: sepsis-pathogen-probe-set-reanalysis

name: sequence-alignment-benchmarking

name: sequence-coverage-metrics-computation

name: sequence-length-distribution-statistics

name: sequence-yield-quantification

name: sequencing-background-noise-evaluation

name: sequencing-coverage-downsampling

name: sequencing-coverage-parameter-sweep
description: Use when planning or evaluating 10x Chromium Linked-Read library preparation/sequencing parameters (CF, CR, C, fragment length) and you need to know which combinations maximize contig/scaffold N50 and NA50 for diploid de novo assembly.

name: sequencing-depth-accuracy-convergence-analysis

name: sequencing-depth-saturation-analysis

name: sequencing-depth-sensitivity-analysis

name: sequencing-error-rate-estimation

name: sequencing-error-rate-quantification

name: set-union-coverage-calculation

name: sewage-metagenome-read-retrieval

name: sex-chromosome-hemizygosity-verification

name: shared-host-edge-threshold-optimization

name: short-read-alignment-parsing

name: short-read-alignment-to-host-reference

name: short-read-alignment-to-reference-catalog

name: short-read-alignment-to-reference-genome
description: Use when you have reference-free variant calls (KisSNP2-format fasta / .snp file from ebwt2InDel) and an available reference genome, and you need reference-coordinate .vcf entries for downstream validation or comparison.

name: short-read-alignment-to-reference-genome

name: short-read-alignment-to-scaffolds

name: short-read-alignment-with-bowtie2

name: short-read-and-long-read-mapping

name: short-read-clustering-benchmarking

name: short-read-coverage-subsampling
description: Use when you must benchmark a retrieval/assembly pipeline across sequencing depths and only full-coverage paired-end Illumina reads (e.g. D. gyrociliatus PRJEB37657) are available — subsample to simulate lower-coverage genome-skimming arms.

name: short-read-mapping-to-allele-database
description: Use when WGS read pairs must be aligned against known MLST allele sequences so per-read allele match/mismatch evidence (e.g., Phred-weighted mismatches) can be extracted as ILP input for strain deconvolution.

name: short-read-mapping-to-genome-databases
description: Use when paired-end shotgun metagenomic FASTQ reads from water samples must be attributed to competing fecal source categories (e.g., human, sewage, septage, cow, dog, goose) using a genome-to-source database without sequencing the sources themselves.

name: short-read-quality-filtering
description: Use when raw paired-end short-read (Illumina) FASTQ files must be cleaned of low-quality reads, adapters and poor-quality trailing bases before hybrid assembly or downstream polishing.

name: short-read-quality-trimming
description: Use when raw Illumina paired-end metagenomic FASTQ/fastq.gz reads must be stripped of Illumina adapters and low-quality bases before downstream SSU rRNA filtering, assembly, or classification.

name: short-read-quality-trimming
description: Use when raw Illumina paired-end FASTQ reads must be quality-trimmed and adapter-stripped to remove low-quality sequence and adapters before targeted assembly or seed-read searching.

name: short-read-quality-trimming
description: Use when raw paired-end Illumina FASTQ (e.g. CAMISIM simulated metagenomic test data) enters nf-core/mag and must be adapter/quality trimmed and decontaminated before assembly.

name: short-read-quality-trimming
description: Use when raw paired-end shotgun virome FASTQ reads need adapter removal, quality trimming, and contaminant filtering as the first stage of ViroProfiler before assembly or viral identification.

name: short-read-reference-mapping-with-bowtie2
description: Use when you need to quantify how completely a raw or subsetted set of short paired-end reads (FASTQ) covers a specific reference contig (FASTA), e.g. tracking cas operon coverage across read-subset expansion cycles.

name: short-read-simulation-and-mapping

name: short-read-to-assembly-mapping

name: short-read-variant-calling

description: Use when an analysis pipeline starts from a public NCBI SRA run accession (e.g. SRR6287056) and raw paired-end FASTQ files for both mates must be downloaded before preprocessing steps such as hg19 host-read depletion.

name: sra-metagenomic-data-retrieval
description: Use when a downstream variant-discovery or strain-analysis pipeline (e.g. cellsnp-lite + MetaQuad) needs raw sequencing reads from a publicly archived metagenomic study and only the BioProject accession is known.

name: sra-read-data-retrieval
description: Use when a task requires reproducing the MTBC_B (n=1,609) Mykrobe resistance-prediction validation and the raw isolate FASTQ reads must first be downloaded from ENA/NCBI SRA using accession codes in Supplementary Data.

name: sra-read-data-retrieval
description: Use when a benchmark or reproduction task requires downloading raw short-read and long-read FASTQ data for specific samples identified by archive accessions (e.g. BioProject PRJDB4377, Supplementary Table S7).

name: sra-read-retrieval
description: Use when a benchmark or tutorial pipeline requires the raw reads for a specific SRA accession (e.g. SRR961514 Mock B viral community) as FASTQ input for downstream trimming and metagenomic assembly.

name: sra-read-retrieval
description: Use when a task provides an SRA accession (e.g. SRR9875293, SRR3458562) or BioProject (PRJNA431646, PRJNA319556, PRJNA395784) and local FASTQ input is needed for downstream VirMAP or metagenomic classification.

name: sra-read-retrieval
description: Use when a benchmark workflow specifies an SRA accession (e.g. SRX6602475) as the real biological read input and the raw nanopore FASTQ/FASTA reads must be downloaded before classification or alignment.

name: ssu-fasta-output-processing
description: Use when you have full-length/nearly full-length 16S/18S SSU sequences reconstructed by EMIRGE and MetaRib (e.g. metagenome_SSU_sequences.fasta) plus per-sequence abundance counts, and need clustered representatives and consolidated abundances prior to taxonomic classification.

name: ssu-rna-sequence-abundance-quantification
description: Use when you have reconstructed SSU rRNA sequences (e.g. metagenome_SSU_sequences.fasta) and quality-controlled metagenomic reads, and need per-sequence relative abundance estimates before clustering or classification.

name: ssu-rna-sequence-clustering-vsearch
description: Use when you have full-length/nearly full-length 16S/18S SSU rRNA sequences reconstructed from metagenomic reads (e.g. metagenome_SSU_sequences.

name: ssu-rrna-read-filtering
description: Use when metagenomic Illumina (meta)genomic FASTQ reads need enrichment for SSU rRNA fragments before targeted full-length 16S/18S reconstruction, e.g. RiboTaxa-style extraction against SILVA SSU 138.1.

name: ssu-rrna-sequence-reconstruction
description: Use when input is Illumina paired-end or single-end (meta)genomic FASTQ and the goal is near-full-length SSU rRNA gene sequences (not short-read taxonomic classification), e.g. to enable species-level 16S/18S assignment or to recover novel rRNA variants.

name: ssu-rrna-taxonomic-classification
description: Use when reconstructed full-length SSU rRNA sequences (e.g. metagenome_SSU_sequences.fasta from RiboTaxa's EMIRGE/MetaRib reconstruction) must be taxonomically assigned down to species level with per-sequence confidence and relative abundance.

name: stacked-bar-trajectory-visualization
description: Use when you have a longitudinal OTU/count table (first row sequence IDs, second row sampling times) and need per-mouse/per-subject stacked bar trajectory plots, optionally with external-event indicators.

name: start-codon-position-comparison
description: Use when you need to quantify how accurately a gene caller predicts start codons (not just gene presence) by scoring exact and near-correct start-site calls against a curated annotation truth set.

name: state-space-model-variational-inference
description: Use when you have a longitudinal OTU table (taxa by samples with sequence IDs and sampling times) of noisy sequencing counts and need denoised relative abundances plus posterior probabilities that observed zeros are sampling zeros rather than absences.

name: statistical-power-comparison-across-meta-analysis-methods
description: Use when meta-analyzing summary statistics (effect estimates and standard errors) across multiple related markers and you need to decide between or verify that the group permutation p-value method outperforms asymptotic normality.

name: statistical-power-comparison-across-methods
description: Use when you must show whether a new statistical test is more than existing multivariate microbiome association tests across controlled simulation scenarios at a fixed significance level.

name: statistical-power-estimation-by-monte-carlo
description: Use when you must empirically compare detection power of two differential-abundance methods for zero-inflated relative abundance data across graded effect sizes, e.g. replicating the paper's Fig 1b simulation (mu1=0.5 vs mu2=0.4/0.3/0.2).

name: statistical-significance-testing-of-method-comparisons
description: Use when comparing competing source-tracking methods on identical simulated or benchmark inputs and you need significance levels for accuracy differences, e.g., testing MSE gaps against P < 1e-6 thresholds across varying unknown-source fractions.

name: statistical-significance-testing-students-ttest
description: Use when comparing per-character extraction performance (Relaxed precision/recall/F1) of two systems—e.g., an NLP tool vs. a human-curated matrix—scored against one shared gold standard and a significance verdict is needed.

name: stool-host-transcriptome-contamination-assessment
description: Use when raw paired-end stool metatranscriptome FASTQ files (ribodepleted or poly(A)-enriched) need screening for human/host read contamination, or when deciding if host transcriptomes are recoverable from a gut microbiome sequencing run.

name: strain-aware-assembly-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing de novo strain-aware metagenome assemblers on real short-read community datasets and need reproducible Quast genome-fraction, N50 and identity comparisons across assemblers.

name: strain-aware-haplotype-contig-merging
description: Use when assembling strain-aware metagenome contigs from cluster-specific haplotigs produced by a local assembly stage (StrainXpress stage-a output), needing global assembly into final master contigs.

name: strain-calling-accuracy-metrics-computation
description: Use when a deconvolution pipeline that infers allele distributions and strain types must be validated against ground truth from simulated samples, requiring both set-membership and proportion-based accuracy measures.

name: strain-classification-threshold-application
description: Use when pairwise genome or metagenome comparisons must be split into same-strain vs. different-strain calls, especially when SNP-based tools alone miss structurally divergent strains (e.g., clonal popANI but wide APSS range).

name: strain-clustering-average-linkage-popani
description: Use when you have inStrain profile objects for multiple samples (e.g., NICU infant metagenomes mapped to a dereplicated genome set) and need strain-level identities to test whether specific strains are shared between related individuals.

name: strain-composition-estimation
description: Use when WGS reads from a bacterial sample (e.g. B. burgdorferi ticks) must be decomposed into constituent MLST strain types and allele/strain proportions despite within-host heterogeneity.

name: strain-detection-benchmarking-across-tools
description: Use when the goal is to compare how many microbial strains are shared between samples (e.g., twin siblings) under different strain-comparison criteria, or to validate inStrain's popANI approach against dRep/MIDAS/StrainPhlAn on the same mappings.

name: strain-duplication-ratio-assessment
description: Use when a strain-separated metagenome assembly (e.g., Strainberry assembly.scaffolds.fa) must be quantitatively assessed per reference strain using ANI, NG50, and duplication-ratio metrics.

name: strain-genome-coverage-quantification
description: Use when you have a strain-oblivious long-read metagenome assembly, a strain-resolved assembly (e.g., Strainberry scaffolds), and closed strain reference genomes, and you need per-strain coverage fractions or recovered additional genomic material.

name: strain-genome-reference-construction
description: Use when a benchmark with known ground-truth strain composition and controlled mean sequencing depth is needed to evaluate strain-level variant detection (e.g. MetaQuad) on simulated shotgun metagenomic data.

name: strain-haplotype-separation
description: Use when long PacBio or Nanopore reads from a single low-complexity metagenomic sample must be separated into conspecific strain-level assemblies, rather than left collapsed in a strain-oblivious metagenome assembly.

name: strain-level-diversity-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing metagenomic assemblers on short-read viral/metagenomic data containing closely related strains, where assemblies must be scored against reference genomes for genome fraction, misassemblies and per-100 kb error rates.

name: strain-level-popani-comparison
description: Use when comparing microbial populations across metagenomic samples to quantify shared strains, needing pairwise popANI/ConANI and breadth-based detection against a concatenated reference genome set.

name: strain-level-variation-assembly
description: Use when assembling metagenomic or mock viral community FASTQ reads with high strain-level diversity (e.g. mixed HIV-1 strains at ~2.8% abundance in a host background) and you need intra-species diversity preserved instead of a single consensus per species.

name: strain-level-viral-community-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking metagenomic assemblers on communities with high strain-level diversity, where a simulated ground-truth community with known reference genomes is needed to compute per-genome fraction and misassembly counts.

name: strain-resolution-benchmark-tabulation
description: Use when a strain-oblivious long-read metagenome assembly has been strain-separated with Strainberry and you must quantify per-bin additional genomic material, scaffold-count gains, and halved coverage into a summary table.

name: strain-separated-assembly-evaluation
description: Reference for judging whether Strainberry correctly separated two or more conspecific strains from a long-read metagenome assembly, using ANI, reference coverage, and duplication-ratio metrics per recovered strain.

name: strain-specific-contig-reconstruction
description: Use when a metagenomic assembly graph (GFA sequence graph from MetaCortex MC mode) encodes intra-species/strain-level variation and you need to extract per-strain paths and quantify their accuracy against strain references.

name: strain-tracking-synteny-analysis
description: Use when comparing conspecific microbial strains from metagenomic assemblies or assembled genomes where SNP-based tools are insufficient (e.g., structural variation, phages, plasmids) and a per-region synteny-based relatedness score is needed.

name: strain-type-distribution-milp-deconvolution
description: Use when per-locus allele proportions have already been inferred for multiple samples and you need a global, multi-sample strain-type decomposition that can include strains not present in the MLST database.

name: strain-type-distribution-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking a strain-deconvolution or MLST strain-typing solver against known ground truth: you need simulated multi-strain samples with controlled novel-strain and recombination events, plus precision/recall/TVD/EMD evaluation of inferred strain type proportions.

name: strain-variant-haplotyping-interpretation
description: Use when a Strainberry run on a strain-oblivious long-read metagenome assembly (e.g., Lathe/metaFlye FASTA plus coordinate-sorted Nanopore BAM) has finished and you must quantify per-bin additional genomic material, coverage halving, and strain-level classifications of the separated scaffolds.

name: strainphylan-phylogenetic-stratification
description: Use when shotgun metagenomic MAG clusters must be resolved below species level — e.g. to separate B. infantis from B. longum — via SNV phylogenies from signature genes and abundance-based cluster validation.

name: stratified-cohort-analysis-by-breastfeeding-duration
description: Use when testing a binary exposure (e.g., diarrhea status) against microbiome relative abundances within an exclusive-breastfeeding-duration stratum in a longitudinal infant cohort, expecting log(odds ratio) estimates with FDR-adjusted p-values.

name: streamlit-multi-page-app-generation
description: Use when a YAML report configuration defines sections, subsections, and components (plot, dataframe, markdown, html, apicall, chatbot) and the desired output format is an interactive web application rather than a document, presentation, or notebook.

name: stress-based-dimensionality-selection
description: Use when quantifying β-diversity (assemblage composition) from a presence-absence species matrix per functional group and you must decide how many NMDS dimensions to retain before extracting site scores as response variables.

name: structural-variant-coordinate-overlap-analysis
description: Use when comparing multiple assemblies of one genome against a close-reference genome (e.g. a substrain rather than the true reference) and you need to determine whether reported misassemblies are shared true structural variants or assembler-specific errors.

name: structural-variant-detection
description: Decision support for choosing between reference-based and assembly-based variant calling when NA12878/NA24385-style Illumina or 10x Linked-Read data are available and GIAB truth sets can benchmark accuracy.

name: structural-variant-tool-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating or reproducing comparisons of HGT breakpoint detection or local strain reconstruction methods on simulated shotgun metagenomic reads, where ground-truth breakpoints and transferred segments are known.

name: subgroup-survival-response-analysis
description: Use when a survival (time-to-event) endpoint such as time-to-T1D-onset must be associated with microbiome features — CLR taxa via Cox models, Jaccard/unifrac beta-diversity via MiRKAT-S, or genus-level random survival forests — within one treatment subgroup of sample metadata.

name: subsampled-assembly-benchmark-comparison
description: Reference for reproducing or extending depth-benchmarking of viral genome reconstruction: subsample a large FASTQ cohort to lower read depths, rerun assembly-based reconstruction at each depth, and compare segment contiguity/length against a baseline method.

name: subspecies-detection-thresholding
description: Use when metagenomic reads have been mapped to concatenated representative sub-species FASTAs and you must decide which sub-species count as detected per sample before comparing metrics (e.g. nucleotide diversity) across groups such as birth mode.

name: substitution-error-orf-merging
description: Use when predicting genes in metagenomic reads with substitution errors (e.g. Illumina data), where a single base error can introduce a spurious stop codon that fragments an otherwise correct ORF prediction.

name: suffix-array-taxon-lookup
description: Use when implementing or verifying protein-level read classifiers in the Kaiju style, where MEM hits found via BWT backwards search must be mapped to NCBI taxon IDs and ambiguous hits collapsed to an LCA.

name: summary-statistics-aggregation-across-runs
description: Use when pooling per-contig results (seed length, final length, extension gain) from several ContigExtender runs into a single combined statistics table such as summary_statistics.csv.

name: supermatrix-concatenation-phylogenomics
description: Use when you already hold recovered marker sequences (e.g., FASTA per specimen per locus) for multiple specimens and need to align, trim, concatenate them into a supermatrix, and infer a maximum-likelihood phylogeny.

name: supervised-classifier-training-16s-variants
description: Use when comparing variant callers by association performance: variant count tables plus sample metadata are available and the goal is to test whether different callers yield comparable supervised classification performance.

name: supervised-pair-classifier-training
description: Use when reproducing or retraining vRhyme's supervised pair classifiers from fragment sequence features, or when validating that regenerated .sav model files behave like the reference models in vRhyme/models/.

name: supplementary-figure-reproduction
description: Use when deposited LMAS metric tables (global and per-reference) for mock metagenomic samples must be re-analyzed and re-plotted to test whether metagenomic-branded assemblers consistently outperform genomic assemblers.

name: supplementary-figure-reproduction-from-simulation
description: Use when a paper reports a simulation-based supplementary figure (negative-control FPR comparison) and the goal is to regenerate the simulated count tables, rerun both analysis modes, and confirm the reported qualitative pattern.

name: supplementary-table-data-retrieval
description: Use when a task asks to reproduce a study's reported genome counts or per-phylum breakdown, and the source is article tables/abstract rather than raw sequence data (e.g. 8 complete vs 789 draft CPR genomes).

name: supplementary-table-replication-verification
description: Use when a task asks to replicate or validate published per-species or per-genus probe coverage statistics from a probe design paper, e.g. checking that a sepsis probe FASTA covers all strains at genus level and 53.3% at species level.

name: survival-association-kernel-testing
description: Use when testing whether gut microbiome beta-diversity (e.g., Jaccard dissimilarity) associates with survival/time-to-event outcomes (e.g., time-to-T1D onset) in a study with treatment groups and covariates like sex.

name: svg-visualization-export
description: Use when a tabular time-series omics dataset (CSV/TSV or pickled DataFrame with a temporal feature column) has passed importing, sanitizing, filtering, and analyzing steps and a publication-ready, reproducible figure must be produced and exported as SVG.

name: svm-based-phenotype-classification
description: Use when bacterial nucleotide FASTA genomes (or already-predicted proteins) need trait/phenotype assignment — e.g. the 67 Traitar trait labels such as motility, nitrate reduction, or L-arabinose fermentation.

name: svm-character-prediction-inference
description: Use when extracting microbial phenotypic characters from natural-language prokaryote taxonomic descriptions and you need to filter which sentences are passed to rule-based character extractors before building a taxon-by-character matrix.

name: svm-classifier-training-on-cog-profiles
description: Use when training phenotype prediction models from comparative-genomics feature tables (e.g. eggNOG COG presence/absence profiles) and you need fast, accurate SVM-only classification without an explicit feature-selection step.

name: svm-feature-weight-ranking
description: Use when a trained linear SVM phenotype model (e.g. PICA intracellular model on 97 labelled species) must be inspected to determine whether a trait is predicted by gene presence or absence, and to compare the ranking against a published table.

name: svm-kernel-comparison
description: Use when choosing an SVM kernel for phenotype prediction from protein-family (COG) presence/absence feature matrices, or when verifying that a linear kernel matches or beats RBF, sigmoid, and polynomial alternatives under repeated cross-validation.

name: svm-phenotype-prediction
description: Use when predicting a binary microbial phenotypic trait (e.g. obligate intracellular lifestyle) from comparative-genomics feature matrices such as COG presence/absence vectors, or when screening whole genome databases like eggNOG for species carrying a trained trait.

name: sweep-results-tabulation
description: Use when a workflow sweeps a single tool parameter (e.g., MMseqs2 sensitivity 1–7.5) over identical inputs and per-run outputs (counts, quality scores) must be assembled into one tabular CSV for range-based validation.

name: synteny-based-strain-comparison
description: Use when comparing strains of the same microbial species from metagenomic assemblies or isolate genomes — especially when SNP-based tools (inStrain popANI, MIDAS, StrainPhlAn) call pairs clonal but structural differences may exist.

name: synteny-block-alignment-with-decipher
description: Use when you already have region-specific bins of homologous sequences (e.g., central 1-kbp regions plus 2-kbp flanks per BLAST hit) and need per-pair synteny scores based on synteny-block structure rather than SNPs.

name: synteny-cluster-tabulation
description: Use when you have MAGinator gene cluster assignments (all_genes_cluster.tsv) plus ORF nucleotide sequences carrying contig gene order (all_genes.fna) and need co-localized gene groups for pathway-level functional insight.

name: synteny-score-subsampling
description: Use when you have SynTracker's raw per-region synteny score table and need APSS matrices per subsampling length, or must decide how many regions (n) a pairwise comparison needs before it is usable.

name: synteny-score-threshold-sweep
description: Use when APSS tables from SynTracker runs must be turned into binary same/different-strain calls, when a cutoff must be calibrated for a new species or context, or when benchmarking SynTracker against SNP-based strain-comparison tools.

name: synthetic-benchmark-reproduction
description: Use when a paper reports average unsupervised clustering accuracy on a specific benchmark of synthetic FASTA datasets and the numbers must be independently reproduced from the original datasets and tool parameters.

name: synthetic-community-truth-comparison
description: Decision support for choosing an OTU-picking pipeline when a synthetic dataset with known OTU composition is available and abundance-accuracy (not just OTU richness) must be compared across tools.

name: synthetic-metagenome-dataset-generation
description: Use when you need to benchmark Libra's runtime scaling on synthetic metagenome inputs of known size, or to tabulate per-metric (Cosine Similarity, Bray-Curtis, Jensen-Shannon) runtime shares under MAP and REDUCE Hadoop modes.

name: synthetic-microbiome-abundance-simulation
description: Use when evaluating network inference or consensus algorithms against known ground truth: synthetic abundance tables with recorded interaction networks are needed to compute precision and sensitivity of inferred co-occurrence networks.

name: synthetic-mixture-generation-from-emp-samples
description: Use when you need simulated source-sink microbiome data with known ground-truth mixing proportions — e.g., testing whether a source tracking method can recover contributions when many nuisance candidate sources (M=50) and unknown fractions (0–90%) are present.

name: synthetic-otu-count-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking microbiome feature-screening or multivariate association tests on controlled synthetic data — specifically when OTU counts must mimic a real throat microbiome composition via multinomial sampling.

name: synthetic-reads-validation-with-10x-pipelines
description: Use when simulated 10x Chromium linked-read FASTQs (gzipped R1/R2 pairs from LRTK-SIM) must be checked for compatibility with 10x official pipelines such as Long Ranger or Supernova2 before assembly or benchmarking.

name: systemic-sclerosis-microbiome-interpretation
description: Use when kraken2 per-sample reports exist for paired SSc-patient and healthy-control RNA-seq samples and the goal is to compute SSc-exclusive taxa (set-difference presence/absence analysis) and confirm clinically relevant genera.

name: tabular-annotation-output-formatting
description: Use when writing the final output of an insertion-sequence discovery run: candidate IS nucleotide sequences have been ORF-predicted (Prodigal) and InterProScan-annotated, and each retained IS must be reported with its length, protein family accessions, positions, and genomic context in a.

name: tabular-csv-structuring
description: Reference for reproducing published benchmark/runtime tables as machine-readable CSV when a source table presents per-pipeline timings (here, seconds) in a dense concatenated layout across multiple datasets.

name: tabular-data-manipulation
description: Use when you have multiple per-sample HTSeq gene count files and need a single samples-by-gene count matrix (CSV) as input for downstream RNA-seq analysis such as DESeq2Shiny.

name: tabular-data-quality-sanitization
description: Use when a tabular time-series omics dataset (CSV, TSV, or pickled Pandas DataFrame with the temporal dimension as a feature column) has just been imported via MOVIS's importing step and must be quality-checked before the filtering or analyzing steps run.

name: tabular-record-serialization
description: Use when sample metadata for multiple metagenomic samples must be captured as structured one-row-per-sample records, including lab-specific custom text/dropdown or numeric fields beyond a generic collection and processing schema.

name: tabular-result-export
description: Use when per-dataset, per-method benchmark scores (e.g., Quast/metaQuast genome fraction percentages) have been computed and must be aggregated and persisted as a CSV with per-dataset rows plus summary statistics for verification.

name: tabular-result-summarization
description: Use when a paper's claims refer to numbers in a results table and you must verify them by loading the table, computing derived metrics (e.g. |OTUs − true strains|), and ranking pipelines per dataset.

name: tantan-masking-ablation-comparison
description: Use when a Patchwork/DIAMOND marker-retrieval run shows low query coverage and you need to decide whether disabling DIAMOND's tantan masking (--masking 0) recovers longer alignments, particularly with raw-read (FASTQ-derived) rather than assembly queries.

name: target-decoy-fdr-estimation
description: Use when validating RiPP peptide-spectrum matches produced by searching spectra against a putative precursor-peptide database (e.g., MetaMiner/Dereplicator output) and an acceptance threshold (e.g., 1% FDR per dataset) is needed before reporting identifications.

name: targeted-cas-gene-assembly-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating whether a targeted-assembly approach (e.g. CasCollect in protein mode with --trim --meta) outperforms full metaSPAdes assembly or PRICE for cas gene/operon recovery from pooled metagenomic FASTQ reads, with runtime and contig-count comparisons.

name: taxa-abundance-dotplot-rendering
description: Use when bin_permute_ has already produced a discoveries list ($goodpvname) and you need per-feature abundance dot plots of each recommended microbe relative to the binary grouping factor.

name: taxa-snp-correlation-analysis
description: Use when estimating rho correlations between SNPs and microbial taxa across a sample cohort while simultaneously controlling for taxa–taxa correlation (R) and goodness-of-fit (R²) to flag LD SNPs/regions, per mbQTL Approach B.

name: taxa-snp-linear-regression-qtl-mapping
description: Use when you have a microbial abundance matrix (taxa x samples), a genotype/SNP matrix (SNPs x samples), optional covariates, and you need to detect significant taxa–SNP host-genetic associations via linear regression.

name: taxa-taxa-correlation-product-analysis
description: Use when you have a SNP genotype matrix (SnpFile) and a microbial abundance matrix (microbeAbund, taxa rows x sample columns) and need SNP-taxa correlation (R2/rho) estimates plus taxa-taxa R values for mbQTL discovery.

name: taxon-count-vector-validation
description: Use when a reconstructed source or sink taxon profile has been derived by arithmetic on count vectors (e.g., residual subtraction after L1 sparse source selection) and must be verified before downstream use.

name: taxon-level-differential-abundance-analysis
description: Use when comparing taxonomic relative abundance between two treatment groups (e.g., control vs tylosin) from a processed 16S feature table, especially when Sex or other covariates must be adjusted and FDR-controlled taxon lists are required.

name: taxon-rank-abundance-summarization
description: Use when you have per-read classification output (Kaiju tabular output with C/U status and NCBI taxon IDs, or Kraken assignments) and need genus- or phylum-level counts, sensitivity, and precision summaries.

name: taxonomic-abundance-profiling
description: Use when raw trimmed .fq.gz metagenomic reads must be binned and profiled at a target taxonomic rank against a large reference database, e.g. reproducing genus-level abundance trajectories across a sample time series.

name: taxonomic-abundance-profiling
description: Use when raw metagenomic FASTQ reads (e.g., Illumina data from NCBI SRA accessions) must be assigned taxonomic labels and summarized as a genus-level distribution plus unclassified fraction.

name: taxonomic-classifier-sensitivity-precision-computation
description: Use when benchmarking metagenomic taxonomic classifiers via genome exclusion — i.e., simulating reads (ART, Illumina/Roche-454 read models), classifying them against databases that omit the source genome, and computing genus/phylum sensitivity and precision.

name: taxonomic-database-construction
description: Use when raw shotgun reads from complex biological samples (e.g., food) must be classified against a large multi-kingdom reference genome collection, and the k-mer/minhash database first has to be constructed at scale.

name: taxonomic-description-sentence-segmentation
description: Use when input is natural-language prokaryotic taxonomic description text (e.g., the Part_One_111_final dataset) that must be segmented into sentences and normalized before phenotypic character extraction.

name: taxonomic-description-text-mining
description: Use when you have a folder of unstructured prokaryote taxonomic description documents and need to populate a taxon-by-character matrix of phenotypic characters (e.g., cell dimensions, Gram stain, NaCl/pH/temperature optima) for downstream comparative analysis.

name: taxonomic-distribution-aggregation
description: Use when you have a filtered DiSCo hitlist (disco_hitlist.tsv) of DsrA/DsrB hits from (meta)genomic records and need to summarize which lineages and phyla carry the Dsr pathway.

name: taxonomic-distribution-grouping
description: Use when you have per-feature taxonomy assignments (e.g. QIIME2 Naive Bayes or BLAST predictions on 16S mock-community data) and need abundance profiles grouped at a chosen taxonomic level for composition comparison.

name: taxonomic-feature-extraction-by-level
description: Use when the input is a merged MetaPhlAn or QIIME OTU/BIOM table containing multiple taxonomic ranks and you need a feature matrix at a specific level (genus, species, or all) before filtering, normalization, or model building in MegaR.

name: taxonomic-group-aggregation
description: Use when a FASTA-derived per-sequence statistics table needs to be summarized by taxonomic labels (phylum) or molecule type (chromosome vs plasmid), e.g. to reproduce reported dataset statistics before model training.

name: taxonomic-hierarchy-tree-traversal
description: Use when GCN (or another trait) must be mapped onto the Greengenes phylogeny or taxonomic tree to test phylogenetic signal or infer trait values for taxa lacking sequenced relatives.

name: taxonomic-identifier-mapping
description: Use when building a k-mer-to-LCA taxonomy database from NCBI RefSeq genomes so each k-mer in a metagenomic classifier resolves to a specific NCBI taxon ID.

name: taxonomic-label-vocabulary-matching
description: Use when a hierarchical 16S rRNA classifier (e.g. DeepTaxa on Greengenes2 2024.09) must be evaluated on test sequences whose species labels are absent from the training vocabulary, to measure parent-rank robustness.

name: taxonomic-lineage-assignment
description: Use when similarity matrices between reads and reference genomes have been computed (e.g. by LiME's ClusterLCP/ClusterBWT_DA) and each read must be assigned to a TaxID at a specific rank such as species or phylum.

name: taxonomic-metadata-mapping
description: Use when genome-to-taxon mapping is needed to rank catalogue elements (e.g. ISC insertion sequences) by how many genera and species their hits span across an indexed genome database.

name: taxonomic-phylum-distribution-tabulation
description: Use when a metagenomic genome-reconstruction study reports draft/complete genome counts and per-phylum assignments (e.g. from 16S rRNA or SCG-binned genomes) that must be extracted, verified, and tabulated into a structured distribution table.

name: taxonomic-probe-count-tabulation
description: Use when you have a published probe/bait FASTA plus genome-to-taxon metadata and need to compute what fraction of strains are covered at genus vs. species level.

name: taxonomic-profile-generation
description: Use when metagenomic sequencing reads (fastq/fasta) must be converted into taxonomic profiles (relative abundances and per-read assignments) for benchmarking or abundance estimation of gut microbiome taxa.

name: taxonomic-profile-threshold-filtering
description: Use when a merged MetaPhlAn table (e.g. merged_metaphlan_t1d.txt) or QIIME OTU/BIOM table must be filtered to informative features before training GLM, SVM, or RF classifiers in MegaR.

name: taxonomic-profiler-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when choosing among candidate taxonomic profilers or reference databases for metagenomic profiling, and benchmark results (e.g. CAMI profiler outputs, KMA .mapstat files) need to be scored and compared.

name: taxonomic-profiling-with-marker-genes
description: Use when metagenomic sequencing reads (post quality-control) need organism-level phylogenetic characterization prior to or alongside gene-catalog mapping, as in the CAMAMED case-control colorectal cancer gut metagenome workflow.

name: taxonomic-rank-precision-evaluation
description: Use when benchmarking a taxonomic classifier's precision and sensitivity at species/genus/family/phylum ranks on simulated reads from organisms whose clades were excluded from the reference database.

name: taxonomic-rank-pruning-and-count-propagation
description: Use when you have per-read taxonomic assignments from a MetaCacheSpark/AFS-MetaCache query run and need read counts and abundance percentages per organism at a chosen rank via the -a/--abundance_per parameter.

name: taxonomic-rank-tally-validation
description: Use when reproducing or validating taxonomic classification counts of vOTUs from virome or shotgun metagenome assemblies, where expected per-rank tallies (phylum through genus/species) must be matched against published values.

name: taxonomic-read-mapping-validation
description: Use when a newly built taxonomic database (e.g. fungal marker genes) must be shown to reject reads from off-target organisms such as bacteria before deployment on real metagenomes.

name: taxonomic-specificity-classification
description: Use when you have a deposited probe set (e.g. from the HUBDesign probes/Coronavirus directory) plus the annotated source genomes, and need to determine what fraction of probes are genome-specific versus cross-reactive across multiple viruses.

name: taxonomic-tie-resolution-via-lca
description: Use when implementing or auditing k-mer-based taxonomic label assignment where root-to-leaf path scores can tie, and a deterministic, conservative label (the LCA of tied leaves) must be emitted.

name: technical-repeat-end-buffer-filtering
description: Use when MEMs computed from amplified metagenomic short reads (pal-MEM/E-MEM style output) must be filtered to remove edge-proximal technical repeats before ITR candidate selection.

name: temporal-feature-quality-checking
description: Use when importing a raw or pickled CSV/TSV time-series multi-omics table into MOVIS and you must confirm data quality and that the temporal feature is detected before filtering or plotting.

name: temporal-lineage-frequency-visualization
description: Use when NGS wastewater samples collected over successive time periods have been assigned lineages (e.g. via lineagespot/Pangolin rules) and the goal is to rank per-sample lineage abundances and plot a variant's temporal trajectory.

name: temporal-metadata-tabular-construction
description: Use when raw archived FASTA files must be converted into a numeric feature table with an embedded temporal column so downstream MOVIS clustering or visualization steps can operate on sequence data.

name: temporal-multi-omics-data-handling
description: Use when input is archived time-series multi-omics data (e.g. FASTA archives under Data/cached/example_1/) and the goal is to embed sequences and cluster them (KMeans or OPTICS) in the MOVIS pipeline.

name: temporal-trend-detection-in-metabolomics
description: Use when a tabular (CSV/TSV) time-series metabolomics dataset must be inspected for temporal substrate shifts or trend discontinuities in specific date windows, e.g., the November–December 2011 BWWTP sludge data.

name: temporal-window-filtering-of-tabular-data
description: Use when a tabular CSV/TSV dataset with a temporal feature has been imported and sanitized in MOVIS and the analysis targets a specific time-series period — e.g., isolating the early-April 2012 window of the BWWTP physico-chemical data to inspect the 29.62 °C temperature peak.

name: tenfold-cross-validation
description: Use when a machine learning model (e.g. Random Forest) has been trained in MegaR on taxonomic profiles (16S or WGS) and you need a variance-minimized, unbiased estimate of predictive accuracy before reporting or deployment.

name: tensorflow-1d-cnn-model-training
description: Use when generating custom k-mer detection networks for baseLess from corrected raw signal reads — i.e., you have training/test fast5 reads for a known species and a k-mer list, and no pre-generated network exists.

name: term-list-based-value-extraction
description: Use when natural-language taxonomic description sentences must be converted into taxon-by-character values using curated term lists, especially when term-list coverage is insufficient for coordinated noun phrases.

name: term-list-driven-output-formatting
description: Use when assembling per-taxon extraction records into a structured phenotypic character matrix for phylogenetic analysis software such as Mesquite or MacClade.

name: terminal-coverage-masking-of-scaffold-ends
description: Use when computing per-scaffold read coverage tables for viral scaffold binning from BAM/CRAM alignments, where terminal coverage on scaffold ends should be excluded before pairwise coverage effect-size comparisons.

name: test-set-generation-for-trait-prediction
description: Use when assessing SVM phenotypic trait prediction robustness on incomplete genomes or metagenomic bins by generating randomly thinned COG profiles at controlled completeness levels.

name: tetranucleotide-frequency-distance-computation
description: Use when scaffolding metagenomic contigs with paired long-range links and you must decide which links are within-species versus probable interspecies misjoins, using coverage depth ratios and 4-mer frequency distributions.

name: text-normalization-for-nlp
description: Use when raw taxonomic description files (e.g., from a folder like Part_One_111_final) must be segmented into sentences and cleaned before feeding NLP components such as an SVM character predictor.

name: tfidf-feature-normalization
description: Use when building genomic-signature features from kmer frequency counts of DNA sequences (e.g. plasmid vs. chromosome classification) and the downstream model expects TF-IDF-weighted, L2-normalized feature vectors rather than raw counts.

name: tga-codon-role-classification
description: Use when annotating human microbiome metagenomic contigs of unknown provenance where the genetic code is unknown, and correct interpretation of TGA (stop vs. sense/tryptophan) is needed before or during gene prediction.

name: three-phase-taxonomic-read-classification
description: Use when similarity matrices from ClusterBWT_DA (one per strand of both mates) must be converted into per-read-pair taxonomic assignments at species rank or higher, output as C/U/A/H,IdSeqRead,TaxID,maxSim lines.

name: throughput-metrics-extraction
description: Use when you need to quantify the computational efficiency of a multi-rule bioinformatics workflow — e.g. per-rule memory footprints, wall-clock times, and Gbp/h throughput across a sample set.

name: tiling-probe-selection
description: Use when annotated genomes (e.g., PROKKA GFFs) and a guide tree are available and you need a compact, balanced hybridization-capture probe set that captures known and related (up to ~20% divergent) sequences across multiple taxa.

name: time-period-lineage-trend-matching
description: Use when wastewater-derived mutation/lineage calls (e.g., lineagespot output from VCF files) must be validated against clinical genotype data sampled over the same area and multiple time periods, to judge whether the environmental surveillance signal aligns with clinical lineage dominance.

name: time-series-clustering-with-kmeans-and-optics
description: Use when a quality-controlled, filtered tabular time-series multi-omics dataset (CSV/TSV loaded into MOVIS) should be grouped by temporal behavior to expose substrate shifts or trends, e.g. the November–December 2011 metabolomics window.

name: time-series-data-sanitizing-quality-checks
description: Use when tabular CSV/TSV time-series data (e.g., the BWWTP physico-chemical Processed data set 1 loaded into MOVIS as a Pandas Data Frame) must be quality-checked and names/structures validated before downstream filtering or visualization.

name: time-series-omics-data-importing
description: Use when a tabular time-series omics data set (CSV/TSV or pickled Pandas DataFrame) or archived FASTA files must be brought into a Pandas DataFrame pipeline as the first of MOVIS's five sequential core steps.

name: time-series-period-filtering
description: Use when a tabular CSV/TSV time-series dataset (e.g., the BWWTP physico-chemical data with 2-h sampling) contains time ranges or features/rows outside the analytical scope and must be subset before clustering or visualization.

name: time-series-quartile-visualization
description: Use when a tabular (CSV/TSV) dataset has an embedded temporal feature and the goal is to detect periodic or envelope-level patterns in the population distribution — e.g., quartile traces cycling with ~one-month periodicity.

name: timing-pattern-verification-from-tables
description: Use when a publication claims a speed ordering across tools on multiple datasets and you hold a reproduced runtime table (seconds per pipeline per dataset) that must be checked against the claimed pattern.

name: tmscore-structural-similarity-evaluation
description: Use when you have per-domain predicted contact lists and secondary structures (e.g., from a multitask contact predictor) and need to build 3D models and quantify their similarity to native structures via TMscore.

name: top-k-consensus-host-prediction
description: Use when a scoring model (e.g., kernelized logistic matrix factorization on a virus-host heterogeneous network) outputs ranked host predictions per virus and you want a more robust species-level host call than the single top-ranked prediction provides.

name: top1-accuracy-multirank-evaluation
description: Use when a labeled 16S rRNA test FASTA with taxonomy TSV labels is available and per-rank top-1 accuracy, weighted F1, and calibration (ECE) of a classifier must be reproduced or benchmarked across all seven taxonomic ranks.

name: toy-graph-validation-testing
description: Use when implementing or porting the cSupB traversal/tree algorithm and you need a small, fully known colored DAG (the Fig. 1 toy graph, k=3) to verify correctness of superbubble detection, offsets, and tree levels.

name: trait-presence-absence-pattern-modeling
description: Use when computing core genomes from MAGs/SAGs of varying completeness: presence/absence patterns of gene clusters or traits across genomes must be partitioned into core vs accessory while accounting for incompleteness.

name: transcript-abundance-stratification
description: Decision support for sequencing depth planning: when designing a metatranscriptome study and needing to know how many annotated reads are required for accurate low-abundance transcript quantification.

name: transferred-segment-similarity-scoring
description: Use when reconstructed local HGT strain segments (from a sample.acc.txt breakpoints file) must be quantitatively compared to true/reference segments to measure reconstruction accuracy.

name: transitive-and-weak-edge-trimming
description: Use when strain-separated metagenome contigs must be joined into scaffolds using long-read dovetail alignments, requiring removal of transitive and weakly supported edges from a string graph before path tracing.

name: transitive-edge-and-branch-removal-in-overlap-graphs
description: Use when haplotigs produced by local assembly of each read cluster must be merged into master contigs via a master overlap graph, and the graph contains transitive edges or branch (bifurcation) nodes that block unique-path contig extension.

name: translated-nucleotide-protein-coordinate-handling
description: Use when reconstructing how adjacent or overlapping DIAMOND BLASTX hits against protein references are stitched into a single continuous amino acid sequence per reference, as in Patchwork.

name: translated-nucleotide-protein-homology-search
description: Use when the query data are unassembled or fragmented nucleotide sequences (contigs, raw reads) and homologs must be found against protein reference sequences, tolerating frameshifts in fragmented assemblies.

name: translated-nucleotide-to-protein-alignment-scoring
description: Use when nucleotide query contigs or raw reads from genome-skimming (LC-WGS) assemblies must be aligned against protein reference markers to obtain homologous, scored regions for downstream stitching and trimming.

name: translated-read-gene-screening
description: Use when you have raw short DNA sequencing reads (FASTQ) and need to find reads encoding a known protein family without assembling the dataset first.

name: translation-initiation-signal-classification
description: Use when benchmarking gene start prediction tools (e.g., GeneMark-HM vs MetaProdigal) on complete genomes and you need to stratify results by translation initiation signal type — canonical RBS, non-canonical RBS, or leaderless.

name: transposable-element-annotation
description: Use when you have a FASTA catalogue of candidate insertion sequences (e.g. from Palidis/ISC) and need to determine which have known homologs in ISfinder and at what stringency.

name: transposase-integrase-annotation-filtering
description: Use when candidate insertion sequences (putative IS nucleotide contigs with ITRs, 500-3000 bp) must be validated as bona fide transposase-family elements before inclusion in an IS catalogue or output table.

name: treatment-group-comparison-statistics
description: Use when comparing a survival outcome (time-to-event with censoring) between pre-defined treatment groups and the comparison must be adjusted for covariates such as Sex via Cox regression.

name: true-positive-rate-computation
description: Use when validating an annotation-expansion method by removing known KO annotations from eggNOG (.emapper.annotations) results and scoring whether an HMM search correctly recovers the removed gene and annotation.

name: true-positive-recovery-assessment
description: Use when a simulated metagenomic benchmark has a known ground-truth mutation list and you must quantify how many true shared variants a caller (e.g. MetaQuad) recovers and whether it introduces false positives.

name: tsne-dimensionality-reduction-of-sequence-embeddings
