description: Use when you have per-sequence embeddings from a trained classifier checkpoint and need to test whether the representation space is taxonomically structured at a given rank (e.g., species or phylum).

name: tsv-summary-reporting
description: Use when running Plassembler hybrid plasmid assembly and you need a machine-readable per-contig table capturing circularity and PLSDB mash-screening matches for downstream validation or reporting.

name: twin-cohort-metagenome-strain-sharing-quantification
description: Use when quantifying microbial strains shared between related individuals (e.g., twin pairs) from metagenomic read mappings, or when benchmarking a strain-comparison method's accuracy against existing ANI-based tools.

name: twin-cohort-microbiome-reanalysis
description: Use when re-analyzing the 280-sample twin/mother gut V1-V2 amplicon cohort (samples with >=1,000 reads) to test whether GCN correction changes enterotype classification or phylum-level profiles.

name: twin-strain-sharing-enrichment-testing
description: Use when metagenomic samples from related and unrelated individuals (e.g. NICU infant stool) have inStrain compare popANI profiles and you need to test sibling enrichment and MZ-vs-DZ strain-sharing patterns.

name: two-bit-nucleotide-sequence-encoding
description: Use when implementing k-mer hashing or maximal exact match (MEM) detection over FASTA reads/genomes where memory-efficient nucleotide representation and bit-space coordinate thresholds are needed, as in the pal-MEM repeat-detection step of Palidis.

name: two-dimensional-coordinate-transform-of-mapped-read-pairs
description: Use when paired-end shotgun reads mapped with BWA yield junction pairs whose two sides map to different references, and the discordant pairs must be converted into 2D points for density-based clustering of HGT breakpoint candidates.

name: type-i-error-simulation-analysis
description: Use when you need to demonstrate that a differential abundance testing method controls false positives at nominal alpha (e.g. 0.01, 0.05, 0.1) on real 16S relative abundance data with known null group labels.

name: u-curve-area-under-mixing-curve-calculation
description: Use when multiple binary grouping factors (e.g. location vs gender) are available and you need a single quantitative value per factor to rank which factor better explains microbiome community differences.

name: u-curve-visualization
description: Use when progressive permutation results (bin_permute_all output) are available and you need to visualize significant-feature counts across mixing proportions to assess overall microbiome–group association.

name: ultrafast-bootstrap-support-assessment
description: Use when a trimmed concatenated alignment and gene partition file (e.g., FASconCAT-G output from 957 Patchwork-recovered USCO loci) are ready and node-support statistics are needed for a maximum-likelihood tree.

name: ungapped-local-alignment-filtering
description: Use when implementing a linear-time sequence clustering pipeline and needing to prune center-vs-member candidate pairs after Hamming pre-clustering but before expensive gapped alignment, to cut gapped-alignment workload while keeping ~1% false negatives.

name: unique-coverage-aggregation-across-samples
description: Use when shotgun metagenomic alignments (.sam from bowtie2 or SHOGUN) show taxonomic hits against Web of Life reference genomes but per-sample sequencing is too shallow for coverage-based presence calls.

name: unique-path-contig-extension
description: Use when assembling strain-resolved master contigs from cluster-specific haplotigs produced by local assembly, e.g. merging per-cluster contigs into final_contigs.fasta in a de novo strain-aware metagenome assembly pipeline.

name: uniref90-homology-alignment
description: Use when constructing gene-level functional abundance profiles from shotgun metagenomic FASTQ within the OMARU workflow, or when reproducing assembly-based gene annotation with UniRef90 via DIAMOND.

name: unit-normalization-of-measurements
description: Use when free-text taxonomic description sentences yield numeric measurements for characters like Cell Diameter, Cell Width, or Cell Length whose units vary in surface form and must be standardized before building a matrix.

name: universal-marker-cog-selection
description: Use when scoring every prokaryotic species in a COG-annotated genome database with a trained phenotype model whose feature space is limited to universal marker COGs, or when building prediction inputs for incomplete genomes where a full COG profile would be inconsistent.

name: unknown-sample-phenotype-prediction
description: Use when a trained MegaR model exists as an RDS file and an unknown-sample abundance table (merged MetaPhlAn table or BIOM) must be assigned class labels (e.g. f/t) without re-running model training.

name: unknown-source-initialization-inference
description: Use when a sink community cannot be fully explained by candidate sources — i.e., residual taxa remain after sparse Lasso-based source selection, and the fraction of an unobserved source environment must be estimated.

name: unknown-source-profile-residual-reconstruction
description: Use when a STENSL L1-regularized sparse selection output (sink vector x, source matrix Y, sparse alphahat) is available and an explicit profile for the unknown/unobserved source must be derived, not just its mixing proportion.

name: unsupervised-clustering-accuracy-evaluation
description: Use when you have predicted cluster assignments for DNA sequences and a ground-truth TSV with sequence_id and cluster_id columns, and need to quantify clustering quality without training on labels.

name: unsupervised-dna-sequence-clustering
description: Use when clustering unlabeled DNA sequences from a single FASTA file into known or estimated clusters without alignment or taxonomic identifiers, e.g. mitochondrial genomes, bacterial, or viral datasets with 2-199 expected clusters.

name: unsupervised-gene-model-retraining-per-cluster
description: Use when predicting genes in fragmented metagenomic reads where no reference genomes for training are available, and sequences should first be grouped by likely organism of origin so models can be retrained unsupervised per cluster.

name: unsupervised-protein-family-clustering
description: Use when you have protein FASTA families with pre-existing HMM-based labels and want to test whether AAR-kmer-based unsupervised clustering recovers that family structure, or to sweep recoding alphabets and kmer lengths for de novo family determination.

name: upgma-hierarchical-clustering
description: Use when a lower-triangular pairwise distance matrix in PHYLIP format (e.g. d2S from CAFE with -K 14, -M 1) must be converted into a hierarchical clustering topology to test whether predefined groups form monophyletic clades.

name: upgma-phylogeny-construction
description: Use when you have a pairwise APSS (average pairwise synteny score) matrix from SynTracker and need a hierarchical strain phylogeny, or when validating a synteny-based tree against a reference tree (e.g., a Mash-based phylogroup tree).

name: upset-set-intersection-analysis
description: Use when several co-occurrence networks have been inferred from the same counts table by different methods (e.g., SparCC, propr, SpiecEasi, FlashWeave, COZINE, HARMONIES, SPRING, mLDM) and you need to quantify which nodes/edges they share.

name: usco-presence-absence-matrix-construction
description: Use when a set of related MAGs/species-level genome bins (e.g. SGB009, SGB034, SGB080) must be screened for shared absence of universal single-copy orthologs to infer lineage-specific metabolic gene loss.

name: usco-retrieval-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when you need to quantify how accurately a fragmented or assembled genome-skimming query recovers a known set of universal single-copy ortholog (USCO) references, producing reproducible accuracy statistics.

name: usearch-sequence-clustering-de-redundancy
description: Use when a curated set of near-full-length 16S rRNA gene sequences (or similar amplicon/marker sequences) contains redundant variants and downstream per-sequence analyses (e.g. 515F/806R primer binding) should be counted once per ~species-level cluster rather than once per assembled copy.

name: usearch-sequence-deduplication-and-clustering
description: Use when merging multiple gene reference collections (e.g. ResFinder, CARD, MegaRes, AMRFinderPlus, ARGANNOT) into one catalog and you need unique sequences plus homology-reduced centroids.

name: utf8-text-cleaning
description: Use when raw natural-language taxonomic or scientific prose contains XML entities, non-UTF-8 symbols, or punctuation that would break sentence splitting or downstream NLP parsing before character extraction.

name: variant-call-coverage-filtering
description: Use when you have a .snp file of KisSNP2-format variant calls produced by ebwt2InDel (or ebwt2snp) and need to retain only SNP/INDEL events supported by a minimum number of reads before VCF conversion.

name: variant-call-file-generation
description: Use when simulated longitudinal metagenomic reads must carry ground-truth variants: STEMSIM writes mutated reads plus a VCF detailing the exact mutations it introduced.

name: variant-call-validation-against-ground-truth-vcf
description: Use when a variant caller emits fasta/KisSNP2-format variant contexts that must be converted to VCF and benchmarked for SNP/INDEL sensitivity and precision against a known truth set (e.g., NCBI GIAB NA12878_HG001).

name: variant-call-validation-with-happy
description: Use when two or more variant-calling outputs (VCF) must be compared against a trusted truth VCF to quantify SNP/INDEL sensitivity and precision, e.g. benchmarking a new caller against a baseline.

name: variant-caller-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when you need to empirically compare shared-variant callers on shotgun metagenomic data with known ground truth, especially to quantify false positive reduction and F1 trends across mean sequencing depths.

name: variant-caller-benchmark-comparison
description: Decision support for choosing a variant caller for low-frequency (<0.01) SARS-CoV-2 mutation detection in wastewater FASTQ data when lineages must be inferred per variant caller before committing to one VCF source.

name: variant-calling-low-frequency-variants
description: Use when calling variants from SARS-CoV-2 wastewater or other mixed viral populations where mutations occur at very low allele frequencies (<0.01) and a caller comparison or freebayes-based VCF is needed.

name: variant-insertion-reference-generation
description: Use when simulating diploid linked-read data from a reference genome plus a variant call set (VCF), where two haploid FASTA inputs with inserted SNVs are needed as LRTK-SIM source sequences.

name: vcf-ancestral-state-variant-processing
description: Use when population-genomic variation data are provided as VCF (e.g. 1000GP Phase III via PopHuman) and per-gene polymorphism/divergence counts for an unfolded SFS are needed to run MK-derived tests such as the eMKT.

name: vcf-lineage-mutation-annotation
description: Use when the input is one or more VCF files from SARS-CoV-2 wastewater NGS data (e.g., freebayes calls against NC_045512) and the goal is to list detected mutations and identify which lineages (e.g., B.1.177, B.1.1.7, B.1.351) are present.

name: vcf-to-plink-bed-conversion
description: Use when downstream population-genomic tools require PLINK binary (BED) input but the available genotype data are VCF files split by chromosome and indexed with tabix, e.g. before running ADMIXTURE in scalepopgen.

name: vcf-to-treemix-input-conversion
description: Use when inferring population trees and migration events from filtered biallelic SNP genotype data (VCF or PLINK binary) that must be transformed into TreeMix-compatible input, especially when bootstrapping and optimal migration-edge selection are needed.

name: vcf-variant-table-processing
description: Use when input consists of single or multiple SARS-CoV-2 VCF files (e.g., from freebayes variant calling of wastewater or ARTIC NGS samples) and the goal is to detect lineage-characteristic mutations and quantify per-lineage abundance.

name: vcontact2-custom-reference-database-configuration
description: Use when classified viral contigs (vOTUs) from a metagenomic/virome assembly need phage taxonomy assignments (phylum–genus), and a curated protein-sharing clustering against INPHARED reference genomes is required instead of a generic vConTACT2 reference.

name: vcontact2-network-taxonomy-inference
description: Use when vOTU contigs have been clustered against INPHARED references with vConTACT2 (producing genome_by_genome_overview.csv and c1.ntw) and you need automated per-vOTU taxonomy plus supporting network views.

name: vega-lite-visualization-authoring
description: Use when a tabular time-series omic data set (CSV/TSV or pickled Pandas DataFrame with a temporal feature column) needs a reproducible, publication-ready chart exported as SVG, e.g. from Data/cached/example_1.

name: viral-base-retention-quantification
description: Use when measuring how much viral sequence information a reconstruction pipeline retains as sequencing depth decreases — e.g., subsampled paired-end FASTQ from a viral mock community at 10%, 1%, and 0.1% depth with replicate trials per depth.

name: viral-bin-clustering-metric-evaluation
description: Use when multiple Hi-C or composition-based binners have been run on a mock metagenomic dataset with known ground-truth genome labels and you must quantify binning accuracy via clustering metrics and vMAG completeness counts.

name: viral-contig-binning-evaluation
description: Use when a metagenomic Hi-C dataset has assembled contigs, a name-sorted filtered BAM, and an identified viral contig list, and you need to bin viral contigs and quantify whether graph integration improves vMAG recovery.

name: viral-contig-binning-hic-data
description: Use when metagenomic Hi-C data (assembled contig FASTA, read-pair-sorted BAM, viral contig list) must be binned into viral genomes and compared against other binning tools using clustering metrics and completeness-based vMAG counts.

name: viral-contig-classification-by-gene-content
description: Use when assembled metagenomic contigs (SPAdes/metaSPAdes/MEGAHIT assemblies or supplied long-read/contig FASTA via -A) must be classified as viral without relying solely on direct homology to known viral sequences.

name: viral-contig-graph-clustering
description: Use when you have assembled contigs (FASTA), a name-sorted Hi-C alignment BAM, and a viral contig list, and need to bin viral contigs into draft genomes using Hi-C linkages plus virus-host proximity.

name: viral-contig-identification
description: Use when you have a non-redundant contig library (e.g. metaSPAdes --meta output) from viral metagenomic data and need to decide which contigs are viral and how confident those calls are.

name: viral-contig-identification-virsorter
description: Use when you have assembled metagenomic contigs (MEGAHIT, --min-contig-len 1000) from shotgun data and need to flag viral contigs as input for Hi-C-based viral genome binning with ViralCC.

name: viral-contig-megabase-quantification
description: Use when comparing viral recovery across tools or pipelines on metagenomic (virome) FASTQ samples, e.g. to express recovered viral sequence as contig megabases and taxa-per-sample counts under matched filtering.

name: viral-contig-quality-assessment
description: Use when long assembled contigs from viral metagenomic samples must be evaluated for viral quality and completeness before dereplication into a non-redundant contig library.

name: viral-contig-taxonomic-filtering
description: Use when improving or finalizing a viral metagenomic assembly and you need to drop non-viral contigs based on reference-alignment taxonomy before LCA-based classification.

name: viral-family-taxonomic-annotation
description: Use when draft vMAGs (e.g., from ViralCC's VIRAL_BIN output directories) need family-level taxonomic labels to compute bin purity, or when reproducing the Caudovirales-family purity fractions reported for the human gut, cow fecal, and wastewater Hi-C datasets.

name: viral-gene-function-annotation
description: Use when input is a set of predicted viral contigs (from VirSorter2/VIBRANT etc.) and the goal is gene prediction, functional annotation (KEGG/PFAM/COG/VOG hits), and AMG identification.

name: viral-gene-prediction
description: Use when you have a set of identified viral contigs (e.g., from VirSorter2/VIBRANT/DeepVirFinder/CheckV in ViroProfiler) and need gene predictions, KEGG/PFAM/VOGDB functional hits, or AMG identification.

name: viral-genome-annotation-with-prokka
description: Use when raw (unannotated) viral genome files must be prepared as input for HUBDesign's clustering phase, which takes annotated genomes plus a GenomeInfo.tab mapping annotated-genome paths to NCBI taxon-ids.

name: viral-genome-benchmark-dataset-preparation
description: Use when building simulated virome benchmarks with fragmented complete viral genomes as ground truth to evaluate viral binners such as vRhyme, MetaBat2, VAMB, CONCOCT, BinSanity, or CoCoNet.

name: viral-genome-clustering-dereplication
description: Use when you have a set of quality-filtered viral genomes (e.g. CheckV >=50% completeness) and need to dereplicate them into species-level vOTUs and/or test their novelty against existing virome catalogues.

name: viral-genome-completeness-estimation-checkv
description: Use when you have recovered draft viral bins (FASTA) from metagenomic Hi-C or shotgun binning and need to quantify completeness (e.g., to compare ViralCC vs VAMB, CoCoNet, vRhyme, bin3C, MetaTOR) rather than using marker-gene tools like CheckM.

name: viral-genome-completeness-evaluation
description: Use when viral scaffolds have been binned into vMAGs (e.g., by vRhyme) and you need to classify bins as low- vs. high-redundancy and estimate completeness/contamination per bin.

name: viral-genome-fragmentation-simulation
description: Use when you need labeled training data for viral scaffold binning models: complete viral genomes must be converted into metagenome-like fragments and paired as 'same' vs 'different' genome origin.

name: viral-genome-quality-assessment
description: Use when a virome/metagenome pipeline (e.g. MetaPhage) yields unexpectedly many vOTUs and you must classify each contig as complete, high/medium/low-quality, partial, or provirus to validate the excess predictions.

name: viral-genome-quality-filtering
description: Use when metagenome-assembled viral contigs/genomes need completeness and quality assessment (CheckV) so that only genomes passing a completeness threshold feed downstream vOTU clustering or database comparison.

name: viral-genome-sequence-homology-mapping
description: Use when comparing oligonucleotide probe sets designed across multiple related viral genomes (e.g., 56 RefSeq coronaviruses) and you need a quantitative efficiency metric — mean distinct-genome hits per probe — to rank competing design strategies.

name: viral-haplotype-error-correction
description: Use when error-prone NGS reads (e.g. 454 Titanium pyrosequencing) from a genetically heterogeneous viral sample are aligned to a reference (e.g. HIV-1 subtype B pol) and low-frequency variants (~0.1%) must be separated from sequencing errors.

name: viral-haplotype-reconstruction
description: Use when a viral metagenomic read set (e.g. ART-illumina MiSeq 250 bp paired-end reads) must be classified against a partial or remotely related reference and resolved into strain-level haplotype contigs without a high-quality reference genome.

name: viral-mag-binning-execution
description: Use when input is predicted viral scaffolds (e.g., from VIBRANT or VirSorter) plus per-sample sorted BAM alignments, and the goal is to assemble fragmented viral genomes into near-complete vMAGs.

name: viral-metagenome-assembly
description: Use when assembling low-abundance viral genomes (e.g. mock viral communities or strain mixes spiked into host reads) from FASTQ reads and you need strain-level genome fraction, misassembly, and mismatch/indel metrics per assembler.

name: viral-metagenome-genome-binning
description: Use when you have predicted viral scaffolds (e.g., from VIBRANT or VirSorter) plus multi-sample metagenomic read coverage and need to cluster scaffolds into vMAGs while controlling contamination.

name: viral-metagenome-pipeline-execution
description: Use when analyzing raw shotgun virome reads (e.g., FASTQ from SRA) to identify viral contigs, assess their quality, assign taxonomy, and predict phage hosts — as in the UC fecal virome validation with 20 samples.

name: viral-metagenomic-read-abundance-quantification
description: Use when you have FASTQ reads and VirMAP-reconstructed viral contigs/super-scaffolds and need per-genome read abundance, read sets, and taxonomic classifications from metagenomic virome data.

name: viral-metagenomic-read-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking a viral read-recruitment or haplotype-assembly pipeline and a ground-truth simulated metagenome with known haplotype counts and coverage is needed.

name: viral-metagenomic-taxonomic-profiling
description: Use when you have shotgun Illumina paired-end virome FASTQ data and need viral contig identification, taxonomic assignment and abundance profiling, or when benchmarking a profiler against ground-truth mock community composition.

name: viral-metagenomics-annotation
description: Use when shotgun metagenomic reads or assembled contigs must be classified as viral, annotated for taxonomy/function, binned into vMAGs, or assigned hosts and lytic/lysogenic/chronic replication cycles.

name: viral-mock-community-benchmarking
description: Use when a taxonomic classifier (read-, contig-, or marker-gene-based) must be validated on sequencing data with a known ground-truth viral composition, or when robustness to reduced sequencing depth must be quantified.

name: viral-orf-prediction-codon-usage
description: Use when binning viral scaffolds (e.g., ≥2000 bp candidates from VIBRANT/VirSorter) and you need gene/protein calls to compute codon usage as a sequence-composition feature for scaffold-pair similarity.

name: viral-protein-database-construction
description: Use when preparing inputs for virMine 2.0: you must supply viral and nonviral protein FASTA databases (-v and -nv arguments) and need to construct them from current COG and NCBI RefSeq releases.

name: viral-protein-sharing-network-analysis
description: Use when dereplicated vOTU multifasta sets need genus-to-phylum taxonomic labels and network-based classification against curated phage references (e.g., INPHARED) is acceptable, since vConTACT2 alone leaves classification to manual network inspection.

name: viral-quasispecies-assembly
description: Use when deep-sequencing reads from a genetically heterogeneous viral sample must be assembled into full-length haplotypes with maximum-likelihood frequency estimates after local error correction.

name: viral-quasispecies-diversity-estimation
description: Use when deep sequencing reads from a genetically heterogeneous viral sample must be error-corrected, clustered into local/global haplotypes, and their frequencies estimated, especially to detect rare variants.

name: viral-read-alignment-to-genbank-nucleotide-protein-databases
description: Use when metagenomic FASTQ reads must be assigned to known viruses by both nucleotide and translated protein alignments to build per-genome read sets for mapping assembly.

name: viral-read-detection-and-subtraction
description: Use when retained reads from host read removal show anomalously high retention (e.g. NA12878 0.641% vs 0.406% after correction) and viral contamination such as EBV is suspected in 1000 Genomes or similar Illumina data.

name: viral-read-recruitment-and-genome-assignment
description: Use when paired-end viral metagenomic FASTQ data (e.g., SRA clinical respiratory samples) must have reads assigned to specific viral genomes and genomes reconstructed as super-scaffolds, especially with low coverage or divergent viruses.

name: viral-reference-database-preparation
description: Use when installing or rebuilding the VirMAP pipeline's reference databases before processing metagenomic samples, or when Genbank gbvrl/gbphage content has grown and the prebuilt viral nucleotide/protein databases must be regenerated.

name: viral-scaffold-network-binning
description: Use when predicted viral scaffolds (e.g., VIBRANT/VirSorter output) plus single- or multi-sample coverage data must be binned into vMAGs, and you need weighted-network construction, KMeans/Label Propagation refinement, and redundancy-based iteration selection.

name: viral-sequence-identification-in-assemblies
description: Use when benchmarking metagenome assemblies — e.g. 18 human gut nanopore samples assembled with hybrid ONT + Illumina paired-end tools — for near-complete viral sequence recovery as a biological evaluation criterion.

name: viral-sequence-read-normalization
description: Use when raw paired-end virome reads with uneven genome coverage must be dereplicated and digitally normalized to default parameters prior to de-novo and mapping assembly in a VirMAP classification run.

name: viral-taxonomic-annotation
description: Use when assembled viral contigs or vOTUs (e.g. from MAG-derived metagenomic assemblies) need family-, genus-, species- or type-level taxonomic labels, or when viral OTU clusters must be typed against a reference set such as NCBI RefSeq.

name: viral-taxonomic-classification
description: Use when improved dual-assembly viral contigs need taxonomic labels and read-level or simple BLAST--hit classification is expected to fail due to low coverage, divergent viruses, or ambiguous mapping.

name: viral-taxonomic-classification-pipeline-execution
description: Use when metagenomic paired-end FASTQ data must be classified to viral taxa and reconstructed into virus-like super-scaffolds, especially with low-coverage or highly divergent viruses that defeat read-only classifiers.

name: viral-taxonomy-annotation
description: Use when viral contigs predicted from shotgun viral metagenomes (VirSorter2/VIBRANT/DeepVirFinder output) need genus- or family-level taxonomic labels in a ViroProfiler run.

name: virome-assembly-contig-analysis
description: Use when the input is quality-controlled shotgun/VLP virome FASTQ reads (e.g., infant gut metagenomes) and the goal is assembled contigs, vOTU counts, per-miner overlap comparison, or vOTU-level ORF statistics.

name: virtual-species-genome-simulation
description: Use when you need to benchmark the computational tractability (wall-clock runtime and peak memory) of a trait-prediction pipeline at training-set sizes beyond your real labeled data, by simulating genomes with realistic feature-matrix dimensions.

name: virus-host-adjacency-matrix-processing
description: Use when a binary virus-host association matrix Y is available and you need interaction-profile-based host-host (or virus-virus) kernel similarity to feed into similarity network fusion or kernelized matrix factorization.

name: virus-host-association-prediction
description: Use when you need to rank candidate hosts for uncultured phage/virus genomes from sequence data alone, given a known virus-host association matrix plus virus-virus and host-host similarity networks.

name: virus-host-linkage-detection-from-hi-c
description: Use when you have metagenomic Hi-C data (name-sorted BAM aligned to assembled contigs), identified viral contigs and host MAGs, and need to determine which phages infect which host MAGs and validate those pairings independently.

name: virus-host-proximity-graph-construction
description: Use when binning viral contigs from metagenomic Hi-C data and you need to build a virus-host proximity graph from shared host contacts to complement the sparse Hi-C interaction graph.

name: virus-similarity-network-augmentation
description: Use when a newly sequenced phage genome (e.g., an NCBI accession not in the 820-virus RefSeq benchmark) must be added as a node to an existing virus similarity network before virus-host association prediction.

name: vlp-vs-shotgun-dataset-comparison
description: Use when comparing phage predictions from paired VLP-enriched and shotgun metagenome assemblies and you need to explain differences in vOTU counts via genome-quality stratification rather than raw counts.

name: vmag-completeness-assessment
description: Use when you need to evaluate the quality of draft viral bins (e.g., from ViralCC, VAMB, CoCoNet, vRhyme, bin3C, MetaTOR) against ground-truth or reference genomes, specifically counting near-complete and high-quality vMAGs.

name: vocabulary-index-mapping-construction
description: Use when preparing a deep-learning taxonomic classifier (e.g. DeepMicrobes Embed+LSTM+Attention) that needs a k-mer-to-integer vocabulary file feeding an embedding layer, or when building a canonical k-mer lexicon from FASTA training genomes.

name: votu-definition-at-nucleotide-identity-thresholds
description: Use when you have a set of quality-filtered viral contigs/genomes (e.g. CheckV-screened FASTA) and need to dereplicate them into species-level vOTUs and quantify overlap with reference virome catalogues.

name: votu-dereplication-clustering
description: Use when you have multi-FASTA viral scaffolds merged from several phage miners (e.g. VirFinder, VirSorter, Phigaro, VIBRANT) and need to reduce redundancy to species-level vOTUs before counting, overlap analysis, or classification.

name: vsearch-read-identity-recruitment
description: Use when raw FASTQ/Illumina reads contain a small set of seed reads of interest (e.g. HMM-derived cas-gene hits or CRISPR array repeats) and neighboring reads must be recruited to enable targeted assembly without assembling the full dataset.

name: vsearch-read-subset-expansion
description: Use when running CasCollect's read subset expansion step to grow seed reads (matching cas gene HMM profiles or CRISPR array repeats) into a larger read subset prior to targeted SPAdes assembly.

name: wall-clock-performance-tabulation
description: Use when comparing computational cost of two contact-prediction pipelines on the same pre-computed MSAs, needing measured runtimes per hardware configuration (CPU vs GPU) rather than accuracy metrics.

name: wall-clock-runtime-benchmarking
description: Use when reproducing or benchmarking reported execution times of a Snakemake/SBATCH pipeline per dataset, e.g. to validate Mapler's 2h4m/3h46m/5h3m figures under a 48-thread, 200G allocation.

name: wallclock-speedup-quantification
description: Use when reproducing or re-verifying runtime benchmark claims for Plassembler vs Unicycler, e.g. from run logs/timing records in Zenodo record 7996690, or when measuring assembler speedup across thread counts.

name: wastewater-lineage-time-series-analysis
description: Use when you have variant calls (VCFs) from multiple sequenced wastewater time-point samples and need to infer per-sample lineage distributions and visualize how one lineage's abundance changes over time.

name: wastewater-ngs-read-alignment
description: Use when raw paired-end FASTQ reads from SARS-CoV-2 wastewater sequencing (e.g., ENA study PRJEB44141) must be mapped to the SARS-CoV-2 Wuhan reference NC_045512 before low-frequency variant calling.

name: wastewater-surveillance-variant-analysis
description: Use when analyzing NGS wastewater sequencing reads to detect SARS-CoV-2 mutations below 0.01 frequency and infer the distribution of lineages (e.g., Alpha/B.1.1.7) across sampling periods.

name: wastewater-vs-clinical-lineage-agreement-quantification
description: Use when wastewater-inferred lineage calls (e.g., from lineagespot on VCF inputs) must be compared against clinical WGS lineage assignments from the same area and time windows to assess surveillance agreement.

name: web-service-metatranscriptome-annotation
description: Use when a metatranscriptome analysis pipeline depends on an external web annotation service (e.g., MG-RAST as in SAMSA 1.0), or when a web-service runtime/accuracy baseline is needed to compare against a standalone pipeline.

name: weighted-hotspot-mutation-result-integration
description: Use when Nano2NGS-Muta has produced per-set mutation detection results from N extracted short-read sets and final target hotspot mutation calls must be integrated and checked against a complete check-hotspot.list.

name: weighted-unifrac-distance-computation
description: Use when comparing feature/OTU tables generated by alternative DC methods (vsearch closed/open/de novo at 0.97, DADA2, Deblur) on 16S data, or benchmarking a method against a known mock-community composition on a reference phylogeny.

name: welch-t-test-statistical-comparison
description: Use when two independent groups of per-pair scores (e.g., APSS from SNP-only vs indel-only Bacmeta simulations) must be compared statistically, and per-point variances or sample sizes may be unequal.

name: wgmlst-schema-construction
description: Use when the input is a collection of draft or complete genome FASTA assemblies and the goal is to define a new wgMLST or cgMLST schema seed from the distinct loci present in those genomes, prior to allele calling.

name: wgs-distance-matrix-metadata-coupling
description: Use when a sample-keyed WGS SNP distance matrix must be joined to a header-present clinical/epidemiological metadata CSV so downstream cluster visualization and analysis retain per-sample metadata.

name: whole-genome-alignment-variant-comparison
description: Use when you need to quantitatively validate metagenomic strain-specific contigs (e.g. walked from a MetaCortex GFA sequence graph) against per-strain references by comparing identity and variant counts against a baseline contig.

name: wilcoxon-discovery-replication-differential-abundance
description: Use when comparing taxon abundances between two cohorts (e.g. IBD patients vs controls) across a discovery and an independent replication cohort to identify validated differentially abundant taxa from MAGinator-derived abundance tables.

name: wilcoxon-rank-sum-group-comparison
description: Use when comparing a continuous per-gene metric (e.g., nucleotide diversity) between two independent patient groups — such as pre-treatment vs post-antibiotic time points — without assuming normality.

name: wilcoxon-rank-sum-testing
description: Use when comparing microbial feature abundances between two binary groups from a 267-feature OTU/count table (e.g., testdata1) and you need robust nonparametric p-values per scenario of progressive permutation.

name: wilcoxon-signed-rank-testing
description: Use when comparing two methods' error metrics (e.g., MSE of estimated source mixing proportions) measured on the same paired benchmark instances — such as in vitro gut-mixture sinks with known ground-truth proportions — and a nonparametric paired significance test is needed.

name: windowed-multiple-sequence-alignment-construction
description: Use when deep-sequencing reads of a genetically heterogeneous viral sample must be aligned to a reference and split into overlapping windows to support local haplotype reconstruction and error correction.

name: within-host-pathogen-strain-diversity-analysis
description: Use when WGS read pairs from mixed-infected samples must be typed at MLST loci (e.g. the 8-gene B. burgdorferi scheme with 1726 alleles and 753 strain types) to infer per-sample allele proportions and strain-type mixtures, including novel strains.

name: within-strain-mutation-injection
description: Use when you have simulated longitudinal metagenomic reads (e.g. CAMISIM output directory or ART-simulated FASTQ reads) and need ground-truth within-strain SNV/InDel mutations injected across time points.

name: word2vec-vector-averaging-across-multisequence-files
description: Use when archived raw FASTA files (e.g., Example 1 BWWTP metaproteomics) must be converted into fixed-length numeric vectors for clustering, and no taxa linking or physico-chemical feature extraction is available.

name: xml-entity-decoding
description: Use when raw taxonomic description text (e.g., files like the Part_One_111_final dataset) contains XML entities or characters incompatible with UTF-8 that must be normalized into clean alphanumeric sentences before NLP sentence parsing and SVM character prediction.

name: yaml-config-report-parsing
description: Use when a user supplies a VueGen YAML config (e.g. Earth_microbiome_vuegen_demo_notebook_config.yaml) and needs the report/section/subsection/component tree materialized as Python objects before rendering a report in any supported format.

name: yaml-configuration-file-authoring
description: Use when generating a VueGen report: the practitioner has a directory of bioinformatics output components (plots, tables, networks, Markdown text, HTML components) and must describe their report organization in YAML before invoking the vuegen CLI.

name: yaml-configuration-of-genomic-workflows
description: Use when a Nextflow population-genomic analysis on biallelic SNP data (VCF or PLINK binary input) requires a validated YAML params file specifying which sub-workflows and tool options to run, or when launching scalepopgen with test/test_full profiles.

name: zero-depth-position-filtering
description: Use when building per-lineage rule vectors from SARS-CoV-2 VCF calls against NC_045512 in lineagespot, where positions in the reference-base portion of the rule vector must be dropped if no reads cover that reference position.

name: zero-inflated-beta-distribution-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking differential abundance methods on zero-inflated relative abundance data — e.g., estimating empirical type I error rates at alpha 0.01/0.05/0.1 or power across effect sizes via Monte Carlo replicates.

name: zero-inflated-beta-gamlss-modeling
description: Use when testing differential relative abundance of microbial taxa between comparison groups on compositional, zero-inflated proportion data (e.g., case/control taxa tables), where t-tests or transformed linear models would mishandle excess zeros.

name: zero-inflation-correction-sparse-count-data
description: Use when analyzing sparse metagenomic taxa or gene abundance count tables for case-control differential abundance, where compositional bias and zero inflation must be corrected before calling marker taxa, genes, KOs, EC numbers, or reactions.
